fact: GB111-NH2 binds to reactive cysteine residues on GAPDH and α-enolase, competing with cysteine-reactive probes.
source_span: GB111-NH2 also competed for IAF labeling, indicating that it covalently binds these same reactive cysteines.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the biochemical basis of GB111-NH2 binding, important for mechanistic insight.

fact: Binding of GB111-NH2 to GAPDH and α-enolase inhibits their enzymatic activity in vitro in a dose- and time-dependent manner.
source_span: We performed substrate assays with recombinant GAPDH and α-enolase and found that GB111-NH2 dose-dependently inhibited turnover of the respective substrates... GB111-NH2 also showed time-dependent inhibition of GAPDH and α-enolase activity.
selection_reasoning: Demonstrating functional inhibition of enzyme activity is key to linking binding to biological effect.

fact: Modification of the active-site cysteine of GAPDH and the active site-proximal cysteine of α-enolase potently impairs their enzyme activity.
source_span: Modification of the active-site cysteine of GAPDH and the active site-proximal Cys 388 of α-enolase have both been shown to potently impair enzyme activity.
selection_reasoning: This background fact supports the significance of cysteine targeting by GB111-NH2.

fact: Inhibitors that do not induce IL-1β secretion do not compete for binding to GAPDH and α-enolase.
source_span: The analogs that did not induce IL-1β secretion in BMDM... did not compete for az-GB binding to GAPDH and α-enolase.
selection_reasoning: This fact links enzyme binding specificity to the biological outcome of inflammasome activation.

fact: GAPDH activity determines flux through aerobic glycolysis, which involves NAD+ to NADH conversion, lactate secretion, and ATP production.
source_span: Because GAPDH activity was recently shown to determine flux through aerobic glycolysis... Productive glycolysis results in conversion of NAD+ to NADH, secretion of lactate, and ATP production.
selection_reasoning: This background fact provides context for the hypothesis that enzyme inhibition disrupts glycolysis to activate NLRP3.

fact: GB111-NH2 binds covalently to reactive cysteine residues in both GAPDH and α-enolase and inhibits their enzyme activity.
source_span: Taken together , these data indicate that GB111-NH2 binds covalently to reactive cysteine residues in both GAPDH and α-enolase and that binding to these cysteine residues inhibits enzyme activity .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies the molecular target and mechanism of the compound, which is central to understanding how it affects glycolysis and inflammasome activation.

fact: GAPDH activity determines flux through aerobic glycolysis in macrophages.
source_span: Because GAPDH activity was recently shown to determine flux through aerobic glycolysis ( Pietzke et al . , 2014 ) , we hypothesized that our compounds were activating NLRP3 by disrupting glycolytic flux .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why targeting GAPDH is relevant to glycolytic flux and inflammasome activation.

fact: GB111-NH2 treatment blocks LPS-induced glycolytic flux in bone marrow-derived macrophages by preventing NADH production, lactate secretion, and ATP production.
source_span: GB111-NH2 treatment completely blocked the lactate and NADH production induced by LPS stimulation , indicating that it directly impaired LPS-induced glycolytic flux ( Figure 5B–D ) . ATP production was also significantly impaired in LPS-primed BMDM upon GB111-NH2 treatment ( Figure 5E ) .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding showing that GB111-NH2 disrupts glycolysis in macrophages, linking metabolic disruption to inflammasome activation.

fact: Treatment with the NLRP3 activator nigericin does not reduce NADH levels, indicating that metabolic disruption is not a general feature of inflammasome activation and cell death.
source_span: Notably , treatment with the NLRP3 activator nigericin did not reduce NADH levels ( Figure 5B , Figure 5—figure supplement 1 ) , indicating that the metabolic disruption that we observed with GB111-NH2 is not a general feature of inflammasome activation and cell death .
selection_reasoning: This fact distinguishes the metabolic effects of GB111-NH2 from other inflammasome activators, highlighting a unique mechanism.

fact: Inhibitors of GAPDH and α-enolase, such as KA and EB, also impair glycolytic flux metrics in macrophages.
source_span: The GAPDH and α-enolase inhibitors KA and EB also affected metrics of glycolytic flux ( Figure 5B–D ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the conclusion that inhibition of these enzymes disrupts glycolysis and is linked to inflammasome activation.

fact: Severe limitation of glycolytic flux is required to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, as shown by the lack of inflammasome induction by the hexokinase inhibitor 2-deoxyglucose (2DG).
source_span: 2DG , a glycolytic inhibitor that targets hexokinase , did not dramatically impair glycolytic flux ( as measured by NADH production and lactate secretion ) and did not induce inflammasome formation ( Figure 5—figure supplement 2 ) . This indicates that severe limitation of glycolytic flux is required to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome .
selection_reasoning: This finding clarifies that only strong disruption of glycolysis, not partial inhibition, triggers inflammasome activation.

fact: Inhibitors of the TCA cycle and pentose-phosphate pathways do not affect lactate secretion or NADH production in LPS-primed macrophages and do not induce IL-1β secretion.
source_span: Inhibitors of the TCA cycle and pentose-phosphate pathways ( AA5 and 6-AN , respectively ) , carbohydrate metabolism pathways that are closely tied to glycolysis , also had no effect on lactate secretion or NADH production in LPS-primed BMDM and did not induce IL-1β secretion ( Figure 3A , Figure 5C ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact shows that disruption of glycolysis specifically, rather than related metabolic pathways, is critical for inflammasome activation.

fact: Disruption of glycolysis in macrophages creates a metabolic signal that activates the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source_span: We hypothesized that , due to the dependence of macrophages on glycolytic metabolism ( Tavakoli et al . , 2013 ) , disruption of this pathway would create a metabolic signal that is responsible for activating NLRP3 .
selection_reasoning: This statement frames the main research question and rationale for the study.

fact: Supplementation with downstream metabolites of glycolysis, such as pyruvate and succinate, reduces NLRP3 inflammasome formation induced by glycolytic disruption in macrophages.
source_span: When we cultured GB111-NH2-treated BMDMs with cell-permeable versions of the terminal metabolite of glycolysis , pyruvate , or the TCA cycle metabolite succinate , we observed a dramatic reduction in the number of inflammasome foci that formed ( Figure 6A ) .
selection_reasoning: This key finding links metabolic rescue to suppression of inflammasome activation, supporting the mechanism.

fact: Lactate, a structurally related metabolite that does not fuel the TCA cycle, does not reduce GB111-NH2-induced NLRP3 inflammasome formation.
source_span: A structurally related metabolite , lactate , which does not fuel the TCA cycle , did not reduce GB111-NH2-induced NLRP3 inflammasome formation ( Figure 6A ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact helps specify which metabolites can counteract inflammasome activation, refining the metabolic mechanism.

fact: Increasing L-glutamine concentration reduces inflammasome formation induced by glycolytic disruption, while removing L-glutamine sensitizes macrophages to inflammasome activation.
source_span: Doubling the media concentration of L-glutamine , a metabolite that can be converted into succinate via anaplerosis ( Tannahill et al . , 2013 ) , significantly reduced the number of inflammasomes that formed . Complete removal of L-glutamine from media sensitized BMDM to GB111-NH2-induced inflammasome formation ( Figure 6B ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding further supports the role of downstream metabolites in modulating inflammasome activation.

fact: Addition of metabolites downstream of glycolysis, such as pyruvate, lactate, and succinate, prevents NLRP3 inflammasome activation induced by glycolytic disruption in LPS-primed bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM).
source_span: Addition of metabolites downstream of glycolysis prevents NLRP3 inflammasome activation induced by glycolytic disruption . ( A ) LPS-primed BMDM were treated with GB111-NH2 for 2 hr in the presence of pyruvate ( pyr; 1 mM ) or cell-permeable esters of lactate ( lac; 1 mM ) and succinate ( succ; 10 mM ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key experimental finding linking glycolytic metabolites to inhibition of inflammasome activation, central to the study's main question and findings.

fact: Supplementation with pyruvate significantly reduces caspase-1 activation, IL-1β secretion, and cell death induced by glycolytic disruption in LPS-primed BMDM.
source_span: In addition to preventing inflammasome formation , supplementation of the glycolytic product pyruvate resulted in significant reductions in caspase-1 activation , IL-1β secretion , and cell death induced by GB111-NH2 .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the functional consequences of pyruvate supplementation on inflammasome-related inflammatory responses, a principal finding.

fact: Pyruvate supplementation does not impair NLRP3 inflammasome signaling induced by canonical activators ATP and nigericin, indicating a specific effect on glycolytic disruption-induced inflammasome activation.
source_span: Pyruvate supplementation had no effect on inflammasome signaling induced by the NLRP3 activators ATP and nigericin ( Figure 6C–E ) , indicating that pyruvate does not impair NLRP3 inflammasome signaling by a nonspecific mechanism .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the specificity of pyruvate's protective effect, important for understanding the mechanism and significance.

fact: Pyruvate treatment blocks inflammasome formation induced by glycolytic enzyme inhibitors KA and EB and restores NADH and ATP production in treated cells.
source_span: Pyruvate treatment also blocked inflammasome formation induced by KA and EB ( Figure 6F ) and restored NADH and ATP production in the treated cells ( Figure 6G–H ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact connects pyruvate's metabolic effects to inflammasome inhibition, supporting the mechanistic insight.

fact: Changes in the NAD+/NADH ratio, but not ATP concentration, correlate with NLRP3 inflammasome formation upon glycolytic disruption in LPS-primed BMDM.
source_span: The number of inflammasomes positively correlated with a drop in NADH production ( an increase in NAD+/NADH ratio ) ( Figure 7D ) , while ATP concentration exhibited no correlation with the numbers of inflammasomes ( Figure 7—figure supplement 1 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies a key metabolic signal (NAD+/NADH ratio) linking glycolytic disruption to inflammasome activation, central to the study's mechanistic conclusions.

fact: Inhibition of mitochondrial Complex I by rotenone decreases the NAD+/NADH ratio and completely suppresses inflammasome formation induced by glycolytic disruption in LPS-primed BMDM.
source_span: Interestingly , rotenone treatment was sufficient to completely abrogate inflammasome formation induced by GB111-NH2 ( Figure 7E ) , conditions under which we also observed a significant decrease in the NAD+/NADH ratio ( Figure 7F ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates a causal link between mitochondrial metabolism, NAD+/NADH ratio, and inflammasome activation, a principal mechanistic finding.

fact: The inability to produce NADH, rather than ATP depletion, predicts NLRP3 inflammasome formation upon glycolytic disruption by GB111-NH2 in LPS-primed BMDM.
source_span: These data suggest that the inability to produce NADH , and not ATP , is predictive of NLRP3 inflammasome formation upon glycolytic disruption by GB111-NH2 .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a key conclusion about the metabolic signal responsible for inflammasome activation.

fact: The α-enolase inhibitor EB does not induce a significant NAD+/NADH ratio defect, suggesting that inflammasome activation by EB may occur through a distinct mechanism or additional signals downstream of glycolytic disruption exist.
source_span: It should be noted , however , that the α-enolase inhibitor EB did not induce a significant NAD+/NADH ratio defect ( Figure 5 ) , suggesting that either EB induces inflammasome activation through a distinct mechanism from GB111-NH2 and KA , or that there are additional universal signals responsible for inflammasome activation downstream of glycolytic disruption .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights complexity in the mechanism and the possibility of multiple pathways leading to inflammasome activation, important for interpretation.

fact: Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and elevation of the NAD+/NADH ratio act as signals for NLRP3 inflammasome formation downstream of glycolytic disruption.
source_span: NAD+/NADH ratio elevation and mitochondrial ROS accumulation are signals for NLRP3 inflammasome formation downstream of glycolytic disruption .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies key signaling events linking metabolic disruption to inflammasome activation, central to the study's significance.

fact: Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) are required for NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis induced by disruption of glycolysis in bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs).
source_span: We stained BMDM with MitoSOX , a dye that reports accumulation of mitochondrial ROS , and observed that GB111-NH2 induced an increase in cellular MitoSOX fluorescence that was abrogated by addition of pyruvate ... selection_reasoning: This identifies a key mechanism linking mitochondrial ROS to inflammasome activation and cell death, central to the study's main findings.

fact: Potassium (K+) efflux is not required for NLRP3 inflammasome activation or pyroptotic cell death induced by GB111-NH2 in bone marrow-derived macrophages.
source_span: Addition of extracellular K+ , in contrast , did not reduce the number of inflammasome foci in GB111-NH2-treated BMDMs ... or impair GB111-NH2-induced cell death ... indicating that mitochondrial ROS , but not K+ efflux , is required for GB111-NH2-induced NLRP3 activation and pyroptosis.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies that K+ efflux, previously proposed as a unifying signal, is not involved in this specific inflammasome activation pathway.

fact: Salmonella typhimurium requires glucose and its own glycolytic enzymes for intracellular replication within host macrophages.
source_span: We and others have shown that the intracellular pathogen Salmonella typhimurium ( S . typhimurium ) requires glucose and its own glycolytic enzymes for intracellular replication.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the metabolic dependency of the pathogen, motivating the study of host-pathogen metabolic interactions.

fact: Host defense against Salmonella typhimurium infection requires activation of the NLRC4 and NLRP3 inflammasomes.
source_span: In addition , host defense against S . typhimurium requires the NLRC4 and NLRP3 inflammasomes.
selection_reasoning: This establishes the immunological relevance of inflammasomes in controlling this infection.

fact: Salmonella typhimurium infection activates the NLRP3 inflammasome in bone marrow-derived macrophages, even when the SPI-1 secretion system is genetically disabled.
source_span: We confirmed that infection with either wildtype S . typhimurium or S . typhimurium lacking the SPI-1 secretion system ( which genetically limits S . typhimurium to activate NLRP3 ) induced inflammasome formation.
selection_reasoning: This finding addresses the mechanism of inflammasome activation during infection, a core question of the study.

fact: Intracellular Salmonella typhimurium take up glucose derived from host macrophages, reducing host cell glucose availability.
source_span: We observed fluorescent signal that was dependent on infection in 2-NBDG-treated macrophages , indicating that the bacterial fraction took up the fluorescent glucose analog from the host cell ... we quantified ... and observed a significant decrease in 2-NDBG fluorescence in the cytosol of infected BMDM compared to uninfected BMDM ... These data indicate that intracellular S . typhimurium derive glucose from host macrophages and reduce host glucose availability.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates a key metabolic interaction between pathogen and host, linking infection to host glycolysis disruption.

fact: Disruption of host cell glycolysis by Salmonella typhimurium infection may stimulate NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

fact: Infection with Salmonella typhimurium reduces glycolytic flux in bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), as shown by decreased NADH and lactate production.
source_span: We measured glycolytic flux in infected BMDM to assess the effect of limited glucose availability on the host macrophages. selection_reasoning: This fact links infection to a key metabolic change in host immune cells, central to the study's main question and findings.

selection_reasoning: This temporal relationship supports a mechanistic link between metabolism and inflammasome activation, a core scientific claim.

fact: Supplementation of infected BMDMs with pyruvate, the end product of glycolysis, significantly reduces NLRP3 inflammasome formation, IL-1β secretion, and cell death induced by Salmonella typhimurium infection.
source_span: Consistent with our findings using glycolytic inhibitors, we also observed that supplementation of cells with the glycolytic end product pyruvate significantly reduced inflammasome formation, IL-1β secretion, and cell death induced by S. typhimurium infection (Figure 9A–D).
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates a potential therapeutic or modulatory intervention relevant to the study's significance.

fact: Pyruvate reduces inflammasome formation in BMDMs infected with both wildtype Salmonella typhimurium and SPI-1 secretion system-deficient strains.
source_span: Pyruvate was effective at blocking inflammasome formation in BMDMs infected with both wildtype S. typhimurium and S. typhimurium defective for the SPI-1 secretion system (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the broad applicability of pyruvate's effect across bacterial strains, important for translational relevance.

fact: Pyruvate does not completely block inflammasome formation, IL-1β secretion, and cell death induced by Salmonella typhimurium infection, possibly due to activation of other inflammasomes or bacterial utilization of pyruvate.
source_span: Notably, pyruvate did not completely block ASC focus formation, IL-1β secretion, and death induced by S. typhimurium infection, which could be due to compensatory activation of other inflammasomes such as the non-canonical caspase-11 inflammasome (Broz et al., 2012), or because S. typhimurium could also partially co-opt host pyruvate.
selection_reasoning: This nuance is important for understanding the limits of pyruvate's protective effect and the complexity of inflammasome activation.

fact: NLRP3-deficient BMDMs do not form inflammasome foci upon infection with stationary phase Salmonella typhimurium, whereas NLRC4-deficient BMDMs form inflammasome foci similarly to wildtype cells.
source_span: We did not observe inflammasome focus formation in Nlrp3-/- BMDMs upon infection with stationary phase S. typhimurium. In contrast, Nlrc4-/- BMDMs had a similar number of inflammasome foci upon infection as wildtype macrophages (Figure 9E).
selection_reasoning: This genetic evidence identifies NLRP3 as the key inflammasome activated by stationary phase S. typhimurium, central to the study's mechanistic claims.

fact: Pyruvate does not prevent inflammasome formation or cell death induced by Salmonella typhimurium grown to log phase, which activates the NLRC4 inflammasome.
source_span: Pyruvate did not prevent inflammasome formation or cell death induced by infection with S. typhimurium in log phase growth (Figure 9—figure supplement 2), an infection model that activates the NLRC4 inflammasome.
selection_reasoning: This fact distinguishes the inflammasome activation pathways affected by pyruvate, refining the study's conclusions.

fact: Pyruvate does not inhibit intracellular replication of Salmonella typhimurium in BMDMs.
source_span: We also verified that pyruvate was not blocking inflammasome formation by inhibition of bacterial replication using both an intracellular replication reporter plasmid (Helaine et al., 2010) and by monitoring bacterial replication by microscopy (Figure 9F–G). Reporter plasmid expression over the course of the intracellular replication assay indicates that intracellular S. typhimurium are viable in BMDM cultured in DMEM with or without pyruvate (Helaine et al., 2010).
selection_reasoning: This fact rules out a confounding explanation for pyruvate's effect, supporting the conclusion that pyruvate modulates host inflammasome activation rather than bacterial growth.

fact: Salmonella typhimurium grows at a similar rate in minimal media containing glucose or pyruvate as the sole carbon source.

selection_reasoning: This supports that pyruvate does not impair bacterial growth directly, relevant for interpreting pyruvate's effects on host-pathogen interactions.

fact: The inflammasome is a multiprotein complex that forms in response to pathogen- and danger-associated signals and leads to secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines to activate the immune system.
source_span: The inflammasome is a multiprotein complex that forms in response to various pathogen- and danger-associated signals . Formation of the inflammasome leads to processing and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines to activate the immune system ( Lamkanfi and Dixit , 2014; Biswas and Mantovani , 2012 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological role of inflammasomes, which is central to understanding the study's focus on inflammasome activation.

fact: Inflammasome formation and pyroptotic cell death are critical for fighting infection and contribute to inflammation in diseases such as type II diabetes, obesity, and atherosclerosis.
source_span: While inflammasome formation and pyroptotic cell death are critical for fighting infection and also contribute to inflammation in diseases including type II diabetes , obesity , and atherosclerosis ( Kuemmerle-Deschner et al . , 2011; Wen et al . , 2011; 2012 ) , the signals that trigger caspase-1 activation remain poorly understood .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides clinical and disease relevance for inflammasome activation, motivating the study.

fact: The signals that trigger caspase-1 activation during inflammasome formation remain poorly understood.
source_span: the signals that trigger caspase-1 activation remain poorly understood .
selection_reasoning: This knowledge gap motivates the research question addressed in the study.

fact: Disrupting glycolytic flux in innate immune cells triggers inflammasome formation, caspase-1 activation, and cytokine secretion.
source_span: When functionally blocked , innate immune cells sense metabolic perturbation as a danger signal , resulting in inflammasome formation , caspase-1 activation , and cytokine secretion . Our results using this molecule and other established inhibitors of these enzymes suggest that disrupting glycolytic flux serves as a trigger for inflammation and cell death in macrophages .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal mechanistic finding linking glycolytic disruption to inflammasome activation.

fact: The intracellular pathogen Salmonella typhimurium disrupts host cell glycolytic metabolism, resulting in NLRP3 inflammasome formation and pyroptotic cell death.
source_span: Disturbance of glycolytic flux by the intracellular pathogen S . typhimurium similarly results in inflammasome formation and pyroptotic cell death in an effort to clear the pathogen .
selection_reasoning: This connects the pathogen infection model to the metabolic mechanism and immune response studied.

fact: Restoring metabolism downstream of glycolytic disruption by chemical inhibitors or S. typhimurium infection prevents inflammasome activation by restoring NADH production and preventing mitochondrial ROS production.
source_span: Restoration of metabolism downstream of glycolytic disruption by GB111-NH2 or S . typhimurium infection was sufficient to abrogate the inflammasome response by restoring NADH production and preventing mitochondrial ROS production .
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights the metabolic basis of inflammasome activation and its reversibility.

fact: Disruption of glycolytic flux leads to an NAD+/NADH imbalance and induces mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which activates the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source_span: Disruption of glycolytic flux led to an NAD+/NADH imbalance and induced mitochondrial ROS accumulation , which has been shown here and elsewhere ( Tschopp and Schroder , 2010; Zhou et al . , 2010 ) to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome ( Figure 10 ) .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key biochemical mechanism linking metabolism to inflammasome activation.

fact: During S. typhimurium infection, inflammasome activation is important because it kills infected host cells and initiates inflammatory signals that activate the immune system to combat infection.
source_span: During infection with S . typhimurium , inflammasome activation is an especially important mechanism of host response because , though it kills the host cell , it initiates inflammatory signals that activate the immune system and combat infection ( Storek and Monack , 2015 ) .
selection_reasoning: This explains the biological significance of inflammasome activation in infection control.

fact: Two inflammasome complexes, NLRP3 and NLRC4, are required to fully combat S. typhimurium infection.
source_span: Two inflammasome complexes , NLRP3 and NLRC4 , are required to fully combat infection ( Broz et al . , 2010 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the inflammasome components involved in the host defense against this pathogen.

fact: The NLRC4 inflammasome responds to cytosolic flagellin and type 3 secretion system components of S. typhimurium, which are clear pathogen-associated molecular patterns.
source_span: The NLRC4 inflammasome responds to a clear pathogen-associated molecular pattern presented by S . typhimurium—cytosolic flagellin and type 3 secretion system components ( Zhao et al . , 2011 ) .
selection_reasoning: This provides contrast to NLRP3 activation and explains the known trigger for NLRC4.

fact: NLRP3 inflammasome activation results from disruption of host cell glycolytic metabolism caused by S. typhimurium colonization.
source_span: Here , we provide evidence that NLRP3 activation results in response to another effect of S . typhimurium colonization of the host cell , namely disruption of host cell glycolytic metabolism .
selection_reasoning: This is a central novel finding linking metabolic disruption to NLRP3 activation.

fact: S. typhimurium mutants defective in the TCA cycle enzyme aconitase induce a more rapid NLRP3-dependent immune response in vivo, likely due to increased reliance on glycolysis and faster disruption of host glycolysis.
source_span: This could explain a recent study showing that mutants of S . typhimurium defective for the TCA cycle enzyme aconitase induce a more rapid NLRP3-dependent immune response in vivo ( Wynosky-Dolfi et al . , 2014 ) . We reason that aconitase deficiency would force S . typhimurium to rely even more heavily on glycolysis to survive within the host . These S . typhimurium mutants would likely disrupt cellular glycolysis more quickly and thus activate NLRP3 more rapidly .
selection_reasoning: This supports the metabolic disruption hypothesis with in vivo evidence.

fact: In long-term S. typhimurium infection models, the bacteria preferentially reside within alternatively activated (M2) macrophages that primarily use oxidative metabolism rather than glycolysis, enabling prolonged infection without inflammasome activation.
source_span: It is also interesting that , in long-term models of S . typhimurium infection , the bacteria preferentially resides within alternatively activated or ‘M2’ macrophages , which primarily utilize oxidative metabolism rather than glycolysis ( Eisele et al . , 2013 ) . Thus , the macrophages in which Salmonella survives the longest are those in which host metabolic pathways are minimally perturbed , enabling prolonged infection without invoking an inflammasome response .
selection_reasoning: This fact links host cell metabolic state to bacterial survival and inflammasome activation.

fact: Metabolic sensing by immune cells drives NLRP3-dependent IL-1β release and inflammation in diseases such as type II diabetes, obesity, and Muckle-Wells syndrome.

For example , metabolic sensing by immune cells has been recently shown to drive NLRP3-dependent IL-1β release and inflammation in diseases ranging from type II diabetes and obesity to Muckle-Wells syndrome ( Kuemmerle-Deschner et al . , 2011; Strowig et al . , 2012 ) ,
selection_reasoning: This fact connects the study’s findings to broader disease contexts and significance.
