fact: Embryonic ventral nerve cord neuroblasts undergo a temporal transcription factor cascade from Hunchback to Krüppel to Nubbin/Pdm2 to Castor.
source_span: Embryonic ventral nerve cord ( VNC ) neuroblasts undergo a TTF cascade that progresses from Hunchback ( Hb; Ikaros zinc finger family ) to Krüppel ( zinc finger family ) to the redundant Nubbin/Pdm2 ( Pdm ) to Castor ( Cas; Casz1 zinc finger family )
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key temporal transcription factor cascade studied, foundational for understanding the experimental system.

fact: Each temporal transcription factor in the Hb-Kr-Pdm-Cas cascade is necessary and sufficient to specify the neuronal identity produced during its expression window.
source_span: The Hb-Kr-Pdm-Cas TTF cascade has been particularly well-characterized , with each factor being necessary and sufficient to specify the neuronal identity produced during its window of expression
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the functional importance of the TTF cascade in neuronal identity specification, a core scientific claim.

fact: Loss of Hunchback results in the absence of first-born neuron identities in all neuroblast lineages tested.
source_span: Loss of Hb results in absence of the first-born neuron identities in all neuroblast lineages assayed to date
selection_reasoning: This fact establishes the critical role of Hunchback in early neuronal identity, a principal finding relevant to the study.

fact: Prolonged expression of Hunchback in neuroblasts produces ectopic first-born neurons specific to each neuroblast lineage.
source_span: Conversely , driving prolonged Hb expression in neuroblasts results in ectopic first-born neurons in all lineages tested ... prolonged expression of Hb in NB7-1 produces ectopic U1 motor neurons , whereas prolonged expression of Hb in NB7-3 produces ectopic EW1 serotonergic interneurons
selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates the neuroblast-specific effect of Hunchback, key to understanding spatial-temporal integration.

fact: Hunchback can induce early-born neuronal identity only during a competence window of about five neuroblast divisions from embryonic stage 9 to 12.
source_span: Hb can induce early-born neuronal identity throughout a ‘competence window’ of ~5 neuroblast divisions ( from embryonic stage 9–12 )
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the temporal window critical for Hunchback function, important for experimental design and interpretation.

fact: The competence window for Hunchback is closed by downregulation of Distal antenna, a nuclear protein expressed in neuroblasts until stage 12.
source_span: The length of the competence window is defined by expression of Distal antenna ( Dan ) , a nuclear Pipsqueak domain protein present in all neuroblast nuclei until stage 12 ... Dan is downregulated in all neuroblasts at the end of stage 12 , and this closes the Hb competence window
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the molecular mechanism controlling the temporal competence window, relevant to the study's biological context.

fact: Spatial and temporal cues are integrated to generate lineage-specific neuronal diversity in Drosophila neuroblasts and likely in mammalian progenitor lineages.
source_span: It is clear that spatial and temporal cues are integrated to generate lineage-specific neuronal diversity , both in Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts and optic lobe neuroblasts ... and likely in mammalian progenitor lineages
selection_reasoning: This fact states the broader biological significance and motivation for studying spatial-temporal integration.

fact: Two models are hypothesized for integration of spatial and temporal transcription factors: independent specification and sequential specification.
source_span: Here we hypothesise two mechanisms by which this integration could occur . ( 1 ) Independent specification ... ( 2 ) Sequential specification ...
selection_reasoning: This fact outlines the main research question and conceptual framework guiding the experiments.

fact: In the independent specification model, temporal transcription factor binding is identical in all neuroblasts, whereas in the sequential specification model, temporal transcription factor binding differs between neuroblasts.
source_span: while in the independent specification model , TTF binding will be identical in all neuroblasts whereas in the sequential specification model , TTF binding will occur at different loci in each neuroblast
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the key experimental prediction distinguishing the two models, central to the study's approach.

fact: The study used Targeted DamID (TaDa) to identify Hunchback genomic binding sites and open chromatin regions in two specific neuroblast lineages, NB5-6 and NB7-4, during the competence window.
source_span: To identify Hb occupancy in these two neuroblast lineages , we adapted the previously described Targeted DamID ( TaDa ) method ... We use these lines to obtain NB-specific expression of Dam:Hb ( to identify Hb genomic occupancy ) and Dam alone ( to detect open chromatin )
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key method used to address the research question at a high level.

fact: Hunchback has different genomic targets in NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages, corresponding to differentially open chromatin in each lineage.
source_span: We demonstrate that Hb has differential targets in NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages , which correspond to differentially open chromatin in each lineage
selection_reasoning: This fact presents a principal finding supporting the sequential specification model.

fact: Hunchback binding occurs only at neuroblast-specific open chromatin domains and is not sufficient to create open chromatin.
source_span: Hb-bound loci specific to NB5-6 have open chromatin , but the same loci in NB7-4 have closed chromatin , shows that Hb is not sufficient to create open chromatin . Rather , Hb binding in each neuroblast is likely restricted to a subset of neuroblast-specific open chromatin domains
selection_reasoning: This fact reveals a key mechanistic insight about how spatial identity influences temporal factor binding.

fact: Hunchback (Hb) has different genomic targets in the NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages, corresponding to lineage-specific open chromatin regions.
source_span: We demonstrate that Hb has differential targets in NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages, which correspond to differentially open chromatin in each lineage.
selection_reasoning: This is a core finding linking Hb binding specificity to chromatin state differences between neuroblast lineages.

fact: Hb binding is restricted to neuroblast-specific open chromatin domains and is not sufficient to open chromatin by itself.
source_span: Importantly, our observation that Hb-bound loci specific to NB5-6 have open chromatin, but the same loci in NB7-4 have closed chromatin, shows that Hb is not sufficient to create open chromatin.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the mechanism of Hb binding and chromatin accessibility, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: The spatial transcription factor Gsb is required to specify the NB5-6 lineage and is enriched at open chromatin and Hb-bound loci in NB5-6 but not in NB7-4.
source_span: In support of this model, the Gsb STF, required to specify NB5-6 but not NB7-4, shows enriched occupancy at open chromatin and Hb enriched loci in NB5-6, but not in NB7-4, consistent with a role for Gsb in generating neuroblast-specific open chromatin organization.
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key upstream factor shaping chromatin and Hb binding specificity, important for understanding lineage specification.

fact: A sequential specification model is supported in which spatial transcription factors create neuroblast-specific chromatin organization that leads to neuroblast-specific Hb DNA binding.
source_span: Our findings support a sequential specification model in which STFs create neuroblast-specific chromatin organization, leading to neuroblast-specific Hb DNA-binding.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main conceptual advance and significance of the study.

fact: Two Gal4 lines, NB5-6-Gal4 and NB7-4-Gal4, were characterized to specifically label the NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages respectively during the Hb competence window.
source_span: Here we characterize two Gal4 lines that label either the NB5-6 or the NB7-4 lineages, which is a prerequisite for profiling neuroblast-specific Hb binding sites... Henceforth we call this line ‘NB5-6-Gal4.’ ... Henceforth we call this line ‘NB7-4-Gal4.’ ... We conclude that NB5-6-Gal4 and NB7-4-Gal4 lines are each expressed in a single neuroblast and its progeny during the Hb competence window and thus are ideal tools for expressing Dam or Dam:Hb in specific neuroblast lineages.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key methodological tool enabling lineage-specific profiling of Hb binding.

fact: NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages produce different Hb-positive early-born neurons during the Hb expression window.
source_span: Thus, we conclude that NB5-6 and NB7-4 produce different neurons during the Hb expression window.
selection_reasoning: This establishes the biological relevance of studying these two lineages and their distinct neuronal outputs.

fact: A functional, non-toxic Dam:Hb fusion protein was generated to map Hb occupancy using the TaDa method in NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages.
source_span: The first step in using the TaDa method to map Hb occupancy in the NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages is to generate a functional, non-toxic Dam:Hb fusion protein... To determine if Dam:Hb is toxic, we expressed the fusion protein throughout the nervous system... and observed no effect on embryonic viability.
selection_reasoning: This is a key methodological advance enabling the main experimental approach.

fact: Placing the Dam fusion protein in the second ORF keeps both Dam and Hb levels extremely low, reducing toxicity and increasing specificity of DNA binding.
source_span: placing the Dam fusion protein in the second ORF is important to keep both Dam and Hb levels extremely low , which reduces toxicity and increases specificity of DNA binding ( Southall et al . , 2013 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the rationale for the experimental design to reduce toxicity and improve specificity, which is important for understanding the study methods and validity.

fact: Expression of the Dam:Hb fusion protein throughout the nervous system or ubiquitously in embryos does not affect embryonic viability, indicating that Dam:Hb is non-toxic.
source_span: To determine if Dam:Hb is toxic , we expressed the fusion protein throughout the nervous system ( sca-Gal4 UAS-Dam:Hb ) and ubiquitously ( Da-Gal4 UAS-Dam:Hb ) , and observed no effect on embryonic viability ( Figure 3A ) .
selection_reasoning: Demonstrating non-toxicity of the fusion protein is critical to validate the experimental approach and ensure observed effects are not due to toxicity.

fact: The Hb portion of the Dam:Hb fusion protein is functional, as it can induce ectopic early-born Eve+ U neurons despite being expressed at very low levels.
source_span: We observed that expression of Dam:Hb was capable of inducing a small number of ectopic Eve+ neurons ( Figure 3B ) , despite the low levels of Dam:Hb , showing that Dam:Hb is functional .
selection_reasoning: Showing that the fusion protein retains functional activity is essential to justify its use for mapping Hb genomic binding.

fact: Dam:Hb fusion protein can bind the same genomic targets as endogenous Hb, as shown by similar genomic occupancy profiles and overlap with published Hb ChIP data.
source_span: A comparison over 700 kb of genomic DNA on chromosome 3R showed qualitatively similar Dam:Hb and Hb ChIP binding profiles ( Figure 3D ) . Indeed , enriched Dam:Hb binding was detected at eight of the nine known Hb target genes ( Lyne et al . , 2007 ) ( Figure 3E , Figure 3—figure supplement 1 ) .
selection_reasoning: This key finding validates the Dam:Hb fusion as a reliable proxy for endogenous Hb binding, supporting the main experimental approach.

fact: Dam:Hb and Hb ChIP datasets share a highly significant overlap in binding regions, confirming the specificity and accuracy of Dam:Hb binding.
source_span: We found that 1972 regions were shared between the two ( 29 . 89% of ChIP peaks and 29 . 62% of Dam:Hb peaks ) ... A Monte Carlo analysis on the narrow peak overlap showed this was highly significant , detecting only 6 . 16% overlap with a set of random peaks ( 100 iterations , p-value < 1 e−300 , see Materials and methods ) .
selection_reasoning: Quantitative overlap and statistical significance demonstrate that Dam:Hb binding faithfully represents Hb binding sites genome-wide.

fact: The known Hb DNA-binding motif is the most enriched motif at Dam:Hb binding sites, further supporting the specificity of Dam:Hb binding.
source_span: Additional support for the accuracy of Dam:Hb binding is that the known Hb DNA-binding motif is the most enriched motif at Dam:Hb binding sites ( Figure 3—figure supplement 3 ) .
selection_reasoning: Motif enrichment analysis confirms that Dam:Hb binds specifically to Hb target sequences, reinforcing the validity of the method.

fact: Dam:Hb binding data can be reproducibly obtained from small pools of cells, such as single neuroblast lineages, with shorter exposure times than previously reported.
source_span: We expressed Dam:Hb in a single neuroblast lineage in each hemisegment ( about 200 cells in the ~50 , 000 cell embryo ) and for five hours ( from embryonic stage 9–12 ) ... We performed three biological replicates for each neuroblast and observed excellent reproducibility across all replicates ( Figure 4A ) .
selection_reasoning: This methodological advance enables studying Hb binding in specific cell lineages, which is central to testing spatial and temporal integration models.

fact: Dam:Hb binds to different genomic loci in the two spatially distinct neuroblast lineages NB5-6 and NB7-4, indicating lineage-specific Hb binding profiles.
source_span: The high correlation between biological replicates for each neuroblast , plus the lack of correlation between the two neuroblasts , provided a gross indication that Dam:Hb has unique binding sites in each neuroblast lineage ( Figure 4A ) .
selection_reasoning: This principal finding addresses the main question of whether Hb binding differs between neuroblast lineages, which is key to understanding spatial regulation.

fact: Dam:Hb binds to different genomic loci in the two distinct neuroblast lineages NB5-6 and NB7-4.
source_span: Based on these results, we conclude that Dam:Hb binds different loci in different neuroblasts.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding that shows lineage-specific binding of a key transcription factor, central to the study's main question.

fact: There are 4224 loci differentially bound by Dam:Hb between NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages, with roughly equal numbers enriched in each lineage.
source_span: We used the R Bioconductor package DiffBind to identify 4224 differentially bound loci in the two NB lineages: 2007 that were enriched for Dam:Hb binding in the NB5-6 lineage, and 2217 that were enriched for Dam:Hb binding in the NB7-4 lineage.
selection_reasoning: Quantifying differential binding supports the claim of distinct binding profiles and is key to understanding the molecular differences between neuroblast lineages.

fact: Dam only binding (CaTaDa) can be used to detect open chromatin domains in Drosophila embryos, correlating well with DNase I hypersensitive sites.
source_span: We analysed the Dam only signal around the DNase I hypersensitive sites... and found enriched Dam signals around the DNaseI peaks... These data suggest that Dam only can be used to detect open chromatin in embryos.
selection_reasoning: This validates the method used to profile chromatin accessibility, which is critical for interpreting transcription factor binding differences.

fact: There are global differences in chromatin accessibility between the NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages, with thousands of loci showing differential open chromatin states.
source_span: We identified a total of 8,740 Dam only differentially bound loci, including 3656 loci in the NB5-6 lineage and 5084 loci in the NB7-4 lineage... We conclude that there are global differences in the open chromatin landscape between the NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages.
selection_reasoning: This finding links chromatin state differences to lineage identity and provides a mechanistic basis for differential transcription factor binding.

fact: The study tests the hypothesis that spatial transcription factors (STFs) acting early in neuroectoderm create distinct chromatin landscapes that influence later temporal transcription factor (TTF) binding in neuroblasts.
source_span: Given the order of their action – STFs acting early in the neuroectoderm, and TTFs acting later in the delaminated NB – one possibility is that STFs generate different open/closed chromatin landscapes in each neuroblast such that TTFs have access to different loci in each neuroblast.
selection_reasoning: This background and hypothesis provide the motivation and conceptual framework for the study.

fact: Dam:Hb binding sites are reproducible within each neuroblast lineage but differ significantly between NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages.
source_span: The high correlation between biological replicates for each neuroblast, plus the lack of correlation between the two neuroblasts, provided a gross indication that Dam:Hb has unique binding sites in each neuroblast lineage.
selection_reasoning: This supports the reliability of the data and the conclusion that binding differences are biologically meaningful.

fact: There are global differences in the open chromatin landscape between the NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages.
source_span: We conclude that there are global differences in the open chromatin landscape between the NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages.
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes the fundamental chromatin differences underlying lineage-specific gene regulation, central to the study.

fact: Dam:Hb binding correlates with chromatin accessibility domains in both NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages.
source_span: We found that Dam:Hb-bound loci in the NB5-6 lineage were enriched for open chromatin in that lineage, and similarly, Dam:Hb-bound loci in the NB7-4 lineage were enriched for open chromatin in that lineage.
selection_reasoning: This key finding links transcription factor binding to chromatin state, a principal mechanistic insight.

fact: Neuroblast-specific Dam:Hb binding occurs within neuroblast-specific accessible chromatin domains.
source_span: We conclude that neuroblast-specific Dam:Hb binding occurs within neuroblast-specific accessible chromatin domains.
selection_reasoning: This conclusion supports the idea that chromatin accessibility directs lineage-specific transcription factor occupancy.

fact: The model favored is that spatial transcription factors generate neuroblast-specific open chromatin domains, which then lead to neuroblast-specific Hb occupancy.
source_span: We favor a model in which STFs generate neuroblast-specific open chromatin domains, leading to neuroblast-specific Hb occupancy.
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic model is central to the study's interpretation and significance.

fact: Gsb is a spatial transcription factor necessary and sufficient to determine the identity of row 5 neuroblasts, including NB5-6.
source_span: Gsb has been shown to be both necessary and sufficient to determine the identity of the row 5 NBs.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological relevance of Gsb in the studied neuroblast lineage.

fact: Gsb occupancy is enriched at regions of accessible chromatin specifically in the NB5-6 lineage but not in the NB7-4 lineage.
source_span: We found an enrichment of Gsb signal specifically around NB5-6 open chromatin and not NB7-4 open chromatin.
selection_reasoning: This finding supports the hypothesis that spatial transcription factors shape lineage-specific chromatin landscapes.

fact: Lineage-specific Hb occupancy in NB5-6 correlates with lineage-specific Gsb occupancy at those loci.
source_span: We plotted Gsb signal around NB5-6-enriched Hb loci and found a corresponding enrichment of Gsb occupancy at these regions.
selection_reasoning: This key relationship links spatial transcription factor binding to subsequent Hb binding, supporting the sequential specification model.

fact: The sequential specification model proposes that transiently expressed spatial transcription factors sculpt lineage-specific chromatin landscapes in neuroblast lineages.
source_span: Taken together, these data support the sequential specification model, where a transiently expressed STF (e.g. Gsb) sculpts a lineage-specific chromatin landscape in NB lineages.
selection_reasoning: This statement summarizes the main conceptual advance and significance of the study.

fact: The spatial transcription factor Gsb is enriched at genomic loci differentially bound by the temporal transcription factor Hb in the NB5-6 neuroblast lineage but not in the NB7-4 lineage.
source_span: We conclude that loci differentially bound by Hb in NB5-6 are enriched for Gsb occupancy ... A Fisher’s exact test on these data found this spatial relationship to be highly significant for NB5-6 ( p = 8 . 78e-19 ) , but not for NB7-4 ( p = 0 . 078 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the core claim that spatial factors influence lineage-specific transcription factor binding, a key mechanistic insight central to the study.

fact: The sequential specification model proposes that transiently expressed spatial transcription factors like Gsb shape lineage-specific chromatin landscapes, which then determine the binding of temporal transcription factors like Hb to specify different neural fates.
source_span: Taken together , these data support the sequential specification model , where a transiently expressed STF ( e . g . Gsb ) sculpts a lineage-specific chromatin landscape in NB lineages ( eg . NB5-6 ) , this determines lineage-specific binding of TTFs ( e . g . Hb ) , which can in turn specify different neural fates in different NB lineages ( Figure 8 ) .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main conceptual framework and biological significance of the study.

fact: This study used Targeted DamID to analyze transcription factor binding in very small subsets of cells, specifically 8–12 cells per hemisegment in Drosophila embryos, which is a smaller scale than previous studies.
source_span: In our study we analyze the smallest percentage of cells to date - we calculate that there are between 8–12 cells in each hemisegment expressing Dam constructs; with a total of 11 segments that would give a maximum of 264 cells per embryo , or about 0 . 5% of the estimated 50 , 000 cells per embryo .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the methodological advance and precision of the study relevant to the main question.

fact: The ability to query transcription factor occupancy in small subsets of cells over short time periods enables new studies of cellular identity determination during development, reprogramming, or response to stimuli.
source_span: The ability to query transcription factor occupancy in such a precise manner – in a small subsets of cells over short periods of time – will encourage new uses of the method , such as studying the determination of cellular identities during development , upon reprogramming , or even in response to stimuli .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the broader significance and potential applications of the methodological approach.

fact: Gsb likely acts to open chromatin loci in the NB5-6 lineage, allowing Hb to bind loci that are not accessible in the adjacent Gsb-negative NB7-4 lineage.
source_span: We propose that the spatial factor Gsb opens genomic loci in NB5-6 , allowing the temporal factor Hb to bind loci that are not available in the adjacent Gsb-negative NB7-4 .
selection_reasoning: This is a key mechanistic claim explaining how spatial and temporal factors interact to specify lineage differences.

fact: The mammalian homologs of Gsb, Pax3 and Pax7, can recruit histone methyltransferases to promote open chromatin and increase gene expression, suggesting a possible similar role for Gsb in chromatin regulation.
source_span: Although nothing is currently known about the role of Gsb in chromatin regulation , the closely related mammalian Pax3 and Pax7 transcription factors can recruit histone methyltransferase to promote open chromatin and increase gene expression ... Moreover , Pax7 is a pioneer factor during pituitary development , opening ~2500 loci .
selection_reasoning: This background fact supports the biological plausibility and significance of the proposed role of Gsb.

fact: NB5-6 and NB7-4 neuroblast lineages develop adjacent to each other, share some common neuronal and glial properties, but differ in their anterior/posterior spatial identity and early-born neuron types.
source_span: NB5-6 and NB7-4 develop adjacent to each other during neuroblast formation ... they share a common lateral Msh+ spatial column , but are in different anterior/posterior spatial domains ( NB5-6 is Gsb+ , NB7-4 is En+ ) ... Although NB5-6 and NB7-4 make different early-born neurons , they share a common ability to make subperineurial glia and neurons that project through the posterior commissure .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides necessary biological context for understanding the lineage-specific differences studied.

fact: Approximately 1200 Hb-bound loci differ between NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages, and these loci are preferentially located in open chromatin regions specific to each lineage.
source_span: We show that ~1200 Hb-bound loci are different in NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages , and that the chromatin at these sites is preferentially open .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking chromatin accessibility to lineage-specific transcription factor binding.

fact: Hb is unlikely to act as a pioneer factor opening chromatin in these neuroblast lineages because it binds some sites in NB5-6 but not in NB7-4, indicating it is not sufficient to open chromatin on its own.
source_span: We do not favor the latter mechanism because Hb binds some sites in NB5-6 but not in NB7-4 ( and vice versa ) showing that it is not sufficient to open chromatin .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the role of Hb in chromatin binding and supports the model that spatial factors prime chromatin accessibility.

fact: The Drosophila model allows rigorous testing of the causal relationships between spatial transcription factors, chromatin accessibility, and temporal transcription factor binding through genetic manipulation and chromatin assays.
source_span: The advantage of the Drosophila model is that these relationships can be rigorously tested . For example , mutational inactivation of the relevant STF , while assaying chromatin accessibility or Hb occupancy in a lineage-specific way could reveal a causal link ... Similarly , targeting chromatin modifiers to select loci while assaying Hb occupancy could demonstrate a causal link ...
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the significance and future potential of the model system used.

fact: Hunchback (Hb) binds to many genomic loci in individual neuroblast lineages in vivo, including loci commonly occupied in multiple lineages and loci differentially bound in specific lineages.
source_span: Here we’ve reported the first description of Hb occupancy in vivo within the genome of individual neuroblast lineages . Our study identified many loci that were similarly occupied in the two lineages ... Apart from the commonly regulated loci , we identified over 100 loci that are differentially bound by Hb in NB5-6 or NB7-4 .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding describing Hb binding patterns that underlie lineage-specific neuronal identity, central to the study's main question.

fact: Hb directly activates the gene Krüppel (Kr) and represses the gene pdm2 in multiple neuroblast lineages.
source_span: The latter example consists of Hb activating Kr and repressing pdm2 in most neuroblast lineages . Indeed we find that Hb binds to both loci in NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages , confirming previous observations that Hb directly represses pdm2 and activates Kr in multiple neuroblast lineages ( Kambadur et al . , 1998; Tran et al . , 2010 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key mechanism by which Hb regulates temporal patterning genes, important for understanding neuroblast lineage specification.

fact: Hb likely directly represses the gene zfh2 in most neuroblast lineages, with equivalent binding observed in NB5-6 and NB7-4 lineages.
source_span: Hb is also likely to directly repress zfh2 in most neuroblast lineages ( CQD , unpublished results ) and our data show that the zfh2 locus is indeed equivalently occupied in both neuroblast lineages .
selection_reasoning: This adds to the understanding of Hb's regulatory role in neuroblast lineages, relevant to the study's conclusions.

fact: DNA accessibility, rather than cooperative or competitive interactions with other factors, has the strongest impact on Hunchback binding to genomic loci.
source_span: Our conclusions are in agreement with studies showing that DNA accessibility , not cooperative or competitive interactions , have the strongest impact on transcription factor binding ( Li et al . , 2008; Kaplan et al . , 2011 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the mechanism influencing Hb binding, important for interpreting the study's findings.

fact: Little was previously known about Hunchback's direct targets in the central nervous system or about neuroblast lineage-specific targets specifying neuronal identity.
source_span: Using traditional methods of studying protein-DNA interactions , Hb targets in early embryogenesis have been well-characterized ... yet little is known about Hb direct targets in the CNS , and nothing is known about neuroblast lineage-specific targets that specify lineage-specific neuronal identity .
selection_reasoning: This motivates the study by identifying a knowledge gap addressed by the research.

fact: This study is the first to describe Hunchback occupancy in vivo within the genome of individual neuroblast lineages, enabling exploration of how spatial and temporal factors integrate to generate neuroblast-specific neuronal progeny.
source_span: Here we’ve reported the first description of Hb occupancy in vivo within the genome of individual neuroblast lineages ... has for the first time explored the mechanism by which spatial and temporal factors could be integrated to generate neuroblast-specific neuronal progeny .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main methodological advance and research question addressed.

fact: The study identified over 100 genomic loci differentially bound by Hunchback in NB5-6 or NB7-4 neuroblast lineages, which are strong candidates for lineage-specific neuronal specification.
source_span: Apart from the commonly regulated loci , we identified over 100 loci that are differentially bound by Hb in NB5-6 or NB7-4 . These are excellent candidates for lineage-specific neuronal specification .
selection_reasoning: This is a key principal finding with implications for understanding neuronal diversity.

fact: Advances in genetic tools, functional genomics, and genome manipulation have recently made it possible to probe temporal transcription factor DNA-binding and chromatin landscapes within distinct neuroblast lineages.
source_span: Only recently has it been possible to probe TTF DNA-binding and chromatin landscapes within two distinct neuroblast lineages – due to the parallel advances in genetic tools , functional genomics , and our ability to manipulate the genome .
selection_reasoning: This provides important context for why the study was feasible and timely.

fact: Mechanisms generating neural diversity are conserved between vertebrates and invertebrates, suggesting that findings in Drosophila neuroblasts may inform vertebrate neurogenesis.
source_span: Given the conservation of mechanisms in generating neural diversity in vertebrates and invertebrates , and exquisite ways in which the genome can now be manipulated in different organisms , it is now possible to determine if similar mechanisms generate diversity during vertebrate neurogenesis .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the broader significance and translational relevance of the study.

fact: Transgenic flies with the Dam:Hb construct integrated at the attP2 landing site were generated to study gene regulation in Drosophila embryos.
source_span: Transgenic flies with the construct integrated at the attP2 landing site were generated by BestGene Inc .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the generation of a key experimental model used to investigate gene regulation, which is central to the study.

fact: Embryos from crosses of UAS-LT3-Dam and UAS-LT3-Dam:hb flies with Da-Gal4 males were collected and aged to obtain material for DamID experiments.
source_span: For verifying the Dam:Hb flies , about 1500 females of UAS-LT3-Dam and UAS-LT3-Dam:hb flies were crossed to about 500 males of Da-Gal4 in egg collection cages placed at 25°C . Embryos were collected every two hours and aged for 16 hr at 25°C ...
selection_reasoning: This fact outlines the experimental setup for obtaining embryos used in the key DamID experiments, which is important for understanding the methods.

fact: The TaDa experimental pipeline was optimized for small cell numbers and short duration of Dam expression to profile transcription factor binding in specific neuroblast lineages.
source_span: The TaDa experimental pipeline was followed according to Marshall et al . ( 2016 ) , with a few alterations to optimize for small cell numbers and short duration of Dam expression .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the methodological adaptation critical for the study's ability to profile transcription factor binding in limited cell populations.

fact: Genomic DNA was carefully extracted and processed from embryos to preserve integrity for DamID sequencing.
source_span: Embryos were homogenized with an electric pestle and gDNA was extracted using the DNA Micro Kit ( Qiagen , cat . no . 56304 ) . Extreme care was taken to ensure that the gDNA remained intact – this was done by using wide bore tips to avoid fragmenting the DNA , pipetting deliberately , and avoiding any rough shaking/tipping .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a critical step ensuring data quality in the sequencing-based method used to map protein-DNA interactions.

fact: Sequencing libraries were prepared from DamID samples and sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq4000 platform to generate high-depth single-end reads.
source_span: Sequencing libraries were prepared according to the Illumina TruSeq DNA library protocol . The samples were sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq4000 at 100 base pairs and about 20–60 million single end reads per sample .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key sequencing approach used to generate data for identifying transcription factor binding sites.

fact: P2X receptors open a transmembrane pore in response to extracellular ATP to allow ion flow.
source_span: P2X receptors function by opening a transmembrane pore in response to extracellular ATP.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the fundamental function of P2X receptors, essential for understanding the study's focus.

fact: P2X receptors are trimeric ion channels widely expressed in many mammalian cells, including neurons.
source_span: The family of P2X receptors encompasses seven subtypes in mammals ( termed P2X1-7 ) that are widely expressed in many cells , including neurons.
selection_reasoning: This provides biological context and relevance of P2X receptors in mammals and nervous system.

fact: ATP binding to P2X receptors triggers channel opening by inducing conformational changes in the extracellular domain.
source_span: Recent X-ray structures of the zebrafish P2X4 ( zfP2X4 ) receptor in its apo and ATP-bound states have provided a molecular understanding of how ATP binding triggers channel opening.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key activation mechanism relevant to the study's main question.

fact: The transmembrane domain of P2X receptors contains six α-helices, with TM2 helices lining the pore and forming a gate in the closed state.
source_span: The transmembrane domain ( TMD ) comprises six TM spanning α-helices , two from each subunit termed TM1 and TM2 , which are arranged around the threefold axis of symmetry , with TM1 positioned peripheral to TM2 . The pore-lining TM2 helices are steeply angled nearly 45° from the membrane plane and they form , in the apo state , a gate in the middle of the membrane that is thought to control the flux of ions.
selection_reasoning: This structural detail is necessary to understand the gating mechanism investigated.

fact: The ATP-bound crystal structure shows an iris-like opening of the pore by lateral displacement of the transmembrane helices, creating a wide entryway for ion flow.
source_span: This lateral displacement , in turn , enlarges through an iris-like opening the narrowest part of the channel , creating a wide entryway of 7 Å in diameter , which allows ions to flow through the open pore.
selection_reasoning: This describes the previously proposed gating mechanism that the study aims to test or refine.

fact: There is controversy about whether the ATP-bound crystal structure accurately represents the native open-channel pore of P2X receptors.

fact: GS-Elong controls the elongation of the methionine side chain in glucosinolates by methylthioalkylmalate synthase enzymes, with MAM2 adding one carbon, MAM1 adding two carbons, and MAM3 adding up to six carbons.
source_span: GS-Elong differentially elongates the methionine side chain by the methylthioalkylmalate synthase enzymes ( MAM ) . ... In Arabidopsis , MAM2 catalyzes the addition of one carbon to the side chain , creating GSLs with three carbon side chains . MAM1 catalyzes the addition of two carbons to make GSLs with four carbon side chains ... MAM3 ( also known as MAM-L ) catalyzes the additions up to six carbons ( Kliebenstein et al . , 2001c; Kroymann et al . , 2003; Mithen et al . , 1995; Textor et al . , 2007 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key enzymatic mechanism underlying glucosinolate structural variation.

fact: The GS-Elong locus in Arabidopsis thaliana shows allelic diversity that influences glucosinolate chemotypes through the presence or absence of functional MAM1 and MAM2 genes.

fact: Certain GS-Elong haplotypes, such as clade 4, can mutate to create either C3 or C4 glucosinolate chemotypes, while others like clade 3 have lost genes limiting their chemotypic potential.
source_span: For example, the clade 4 haplotype of GS-Elong can equally mutate to create a C3 or C4 chemotype because it has both MAM1 and MAM2. However, the remaining clades like clade 3 have lost one or the other gene limiting their ability to create alternative chemotypes.
selection_reasoning: This highlights evolutionary constraints and potential trajectories of glucosinolate variation, a principal finding about genetic diversity.

fact: Glucosinolate chemotypic variation similar to that in Arabidopsis thaliana is also found in related Brassica species and Arabidopsis sister species, but the underlying genetic events occurred independently in each species.
source_span: Brassica ssp. have genetic variation at GS-Elong and GS-AOP creating the exact same chemotypic variation found in Arabidopsis... the underlying genetic basis is independent events at the AOP and MAM loci showing that the variation did not go through the speciation boundary.
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses the evolutionary significance and convergent nature of glucosinolate variation across species.

fact: The genetic architecture of glucosinolate loci differs from that of pathogen resistance genes, with glucosinolate loci showing numerous young alleles and a blend of structural and SNP-based variation.
source_span: In contrast to R-gene loci characterized by old/stable biallelic variation, the GSL loci are characterized by a blend of structural and SNP-based variation with numerous alleles that appear young.
selection_reasoning: This comparison provides important context about the uniqueness of glucosinolate genetic variation relevant to the study's evolutionary insights.

fact: Geographic patterns of glucosinolate chemotype diversity in Europe show low variability in the Iberian Peninsula and Mediterranean Basin but high diversity in Central and Northern Europe.
source_span: For example, the Iberian Peninsula and the Mediterranean Basin had low variability in aliphatic GSL chemotypes, which show strong geographic structure. By contrast, Central/North Europe had high aliphatic GSL diversity with chemotypes showing overlapping geographic distributions.
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a key finding about the geographic distribution of trait variation, important for understanding evolutionary and ecological dynamics.

fact: The GS-AOP locus is largely fixed as the Alkenyl allele in the Iberian Peninsula and Mediterranean Basin, while alternative GS-AOP alleles are enriched in Central Europe, driving chemotypic divergence.

fact: Communication through body gestures is a fundamental part of daily social interactions and reflects social cognitive competency.
source_span: Communication through body gestures permeates our daily life . Efficient perception of the message therein reflects one’s social cognitive competency .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the importance of body gestures in social cognition, setting the stage for the study's focus.

fact: Motion sequences showing agents acting communicatively are perceived to be significantly shorter in duration than those showing noncommunicative actions.
source_span: Here we report that such competency is manifested temporally as shortened subjective duration of social interactions: motion sequences showing agents acting communicatively are perceived to be significantly shorter in duration as compared with those acting noncommunicatively .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding directly linking social interaction perception to subjective time compression.

fact: The strength of the subjective time compression effect for social interactions is negatively correlated with an individual’s autistic-like tendency.
source_span: The strength of this effect is negatively correlated with one’s autistic-like tendency .
selection_reasoning: This finding connects individual differences in social proficiency to the temporal perception effect, highlighting clinical relevance.

fact: Intranasal oxytocin administration restores the temporal compression effect in individuals with lower social proficiency.
source_span: Critically , intranasal oxytocin administration restores the temporal compression effect in socially less proficient individuals ,
selection_reasoning: This key experimental manipulation shows oxytocin’s role in modulating social time perception, supporting its involvement in social cognition.

fact: Perceived time during social interactions is not a faithful representation of physical time but is influenced by individual personality traits.
source_span: These findings indicate that perceived time , rather than being a faithful representation of physical time , is highly idiosyncratic and ingrained with one’s personality trait .

source_span: Moreover , they suggest that oxytocin is involved in mediating time perception of social interaction , further supporting the role of oxytocin in human social cognition .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the study’s significance linking oxytocin to social cognitive processes via time perception.

fact: Biological motion perception, such as recognizing body gestures from point-light displays, is an evolutionarily endowed ability important for social perception.
source_span: An important medium of social interaction is body gestures , from which most humans efficiently extract others’ attitudes and intentions even when the gestures are portrayed by only a handful of point lights attached to the head and major joints ( Johansson , 1973 ) . Such efficacy is considered evolutionarily endowed –– Human newborns and infants exhibit a predisposition to attend to the motions of biological entities ( i . e . biological motion ) ( Fox and McDaniel , 1982; Simion et al . , 2008 ) ; and the perception of biological motion engages a specific network of distributed neural areas , particularly the superior temporal sulcus ( STS ) ( Grossman et al . , 2005; Grossman and Blake , 2002; Vaina et al . , 2001 ) that plays an important role in social perception in both monkeys and humans ( Allison et al . , 2000 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why biological motion is a relevant and valid stimulus for studying social perception.

fact: People with autism spectrum disorder show deficits in biological motion perception and abnormalities in the superior temporal sulcus.
source_span: People with autism characterized by impaired social interaction and communication show both a deficit of biological motion perception ( Blake et al . , 2003; Klin et al . , 2009 ) and abnormalities in the STS ( Zilbovicius et al . , 2006 ) .
selection_reasoning: This clinical background supports the link between social proficiency, biological motion perception, and neural mechanisms.

fact: Social proficiency varies widely among neurotypical individuals and is associated with plasma oxytocin levels and oxytocin receptor gene polymorphisms.
source_span: Social proficiency varies widely even among neurotypical individuals , and is manifested behaviorally as a stable personality trait ( Digman , 1990 ) . This inter-individual variance has been associated with plasma concentrations of oxytocin , a well-documented prosocial neuropeptide , as well as polymorphisms of its receptor gene OXTR ( Andari et al . , 2014; Donaldson and Young , 2008; Modahl et al . , 1998; Parker et al . , 2014; Skuse et al . , 2014; Tost et al . , 2010 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides motivation and biological basis for studying oxytocin’s role in social time perception.

fact: Intranasal oxytocin administration alters the processing of social stimuli including biological motion, depending on an individual’s social proficiency and blood oxytocin concentration.
source_span: Likely through interactions with endogenous oxytocin , intranasally administered oxytocin ( Dal Monte et al . , 2014; Freeman et al . , 2016; Lee and Weerts , 2016; Striepens et al . , 2013 ) is found to alter the processing of social stimuli including biological motion in manners that depend on one’s social proficiency ( Bartz et al . , 2011; Kéri and Benedek , 2009 ) as well as blood oxytocin concentration ( Parker et al . , 2017 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the rationale for using oxytocin administration to modulate social perception in the study.

fact: The study used point-light displays of two agents engaging in communicative or noncommunicative interactions to assess subjective time perception.
source_span: As an initial step to qualify the influence of perceived social interaction on subjective duration , we selected 10 point-light displays of motion sequences from the Communicative Interaction Database ( Manera et al . , 2010 ) , each portraying two agents engaging in a communicative interaction that usually involved an object ( triadic interaction , see Materials and methods ) , and made from them an essentially physically matched set of 10 noncommunicative motion sequences by cross-pairing the agents from different interactions ( see Supplementary file 1 ) .
selection_reasoning: This high-level method description is central to understanding how the study tested social interaction effects on time perception.

fact: Observers perceived communicative motion sequences as shorter in duration than noncommunicative ones when the agents were shown upright.
source_span: In the upright condition , the mean PSE was 69 . 3 ms , significantly above 0 ( t23 = 5 . 60 , p<0 . 001 , Cohen’s d = 1 . 14 , Figure 2A ) . In other words , an upright communicative motion sequence compressed subjective duration such that it needed to be 69 . 3 ms longer to be perceived as equal in duration to an upright noncommunicative motion sequence .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding showing that social interaction perception affects time perception, a core scientific claim.

fact: Inverting the agents eliminated the temporal compression effect of communicative motion sequences on perceived duration.
source_span: In the inverted condition , by contrast , the mean PSE was significantly smaller ( t23 = −5 . 82 , p<0 . 001 , Cohen’s d = −1 . 19 ) and not different from 0 ( t23 = −1 . 51 , p=0 . 15 ) ( Figure 2A ) . Inversion is known to impair the perception of biological motion and thereby social interactions mediated by biological motion , yet does not affect low-level visual features ( Troje and Westhoff , 2006 ) . This result hence verified that the temporal compression effect of perceived social interactions could not be due to low-level non-biological visual features .
selection_reasoning: This finding supports the conclusion that the temporal compression depends on perceiving social interaction, not low-level visual features.

fact: Temporal sensitivity in duration judgments did not differ between upright and inverted conditions.
source_span: Their temporal sensitivities remained unchanged between the two conditions , as indicated by a comparison of the difference limens ( t23 = 0 . 70 , p=0 . 49 ) .
selection_reasoning: This shows that the effect is specific to perceived duration bias, not general temporal sensitivity.

fact: Temporal compression of perceived duration was not observed when the social aspect of communicative motion sequences was disrupted by temporal lag or spatial swapping of agents.
source_span: Analyses of the results from 48 observers ( 24 in each of Experiments 2 and 3; 27 females ) indicated that neither the temporally delayed ‘communicative’ motion sequences nor the spatially swapped ones altered temporal perception relative to their ‘noncommunicative’ counterparts ( Figure 2B and C ) . The PSEs were not significantly different from 0 regardless of whether the motion sequences were presented upright ( t23s = 1 . 39 and 0 . 34 , ps = 0 . 18 and 0 . 74 , for Experiments 2 and 3 , respectively ) or upside down ( t23s = 0 . 01 and −0 . 14 , ps = 0 . 99 and 0 . 89 , respectively ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding clarifies that spatial-temporal correlation alone does not cause temporal compression; social meaning is necessary.

fact: The study used point-light displays of two agents performing communicative or noncommunicative actions to investigate how social interaction affects time perception.
source_span: Observers were shown two motion sequences in each trial –– one communicative , the other noncommunicative , one after the other in random order –– and were asked to report via button press which ( the first or the second ) appeared longer in duration ... The duration difference corresponding to a probability of 50% marks the point of subjective equality ( PSE ) ... Twenty-four observers ( 12 females ) performed the duration judgment task in Experiment 1 .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key method and experimental design central to the study's main question.

fact: Inversion of biological motion impairs perception of social interactions but does not affect low-level visual features.
source_span: Inversion is known to impair the perception of biological motion and thereby social interactions mediated by biological motion , yet does not affect low-level visual features ( Troje and Westhoff , 2006 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why inversion was used to test the role of social perception in temporal compression.

fact: The temporal compression effect depends on recognizing communicative intention between agents rather than just spatial-temporal correlation of their movements.
source_span: We hence concluded that the temporal compression effect observed in Experiment 1 was absent in Experiments 2 and 3 . The mere spatial-temporal correlation between the moves of two agents , without a recognizable communicative intention ( disrupted by the temporal and spatial manipulations in Experiments 2 and 3 ) , was insufficient to affect temporal perception .
selection_reasoning: This is a key mechanistic conclusion about what drives the temporal compression effect.

fact: The temporal compression effect observed in Experiment 1 was absent in Experiments 2 and 3, indicating that mere spatial-temporal correlation without recognizable communicative intention does not affect temporal perception.

fact: Recognition of communicative intention varies among individuals and is linked to social proficiency, which exists on a continuum including autistic traits.
source_span: Social communicative ability has been shown to be a continuum that extends from patients with autism into the neurotypical population ( Baron-Cohen , 1995; Frith , 1991; Nummenmaa et al . , 2012; von dem Hagen et al . , 2011 ) . fact: Experiment 4 replicated the temporal compression effect in a larger sample of 90 male observers and found that individuals with higher autistic traits showed less temporal compression when perceiving social interactions.

fact: The social interaction-induced temporal compression effect was significant in individuals with low autistic traits but was weak or absent in those with high autistic traits.
source_span: A median split of the observers by AQ score showed that the social interaction-induced temporal compression effect was evident in the low AQ group ( AQ scores < 20 , mean PSE = 58 . 9 ms , significantly above 0; t45 = 7 . 06 , p<0 . 001 , Cohen’s d = 1 . 04 ) , yet barely reached statistical significance in the high AQ group ( AQ scores ≥ 20 , mean PSE = 17 . 1 ms , t43 = 2 . 00 , p=0 . 052 ) , with a significant group difference in PSE ( t88 = 3 . 51 , p=0 . 001 , Cohen’s d = 0 . 74 ) , but not difference limen ( t88 = 0 . 53 , p=0 . 60 ) .

fact: The study developed a method to infer directional genetic interactions by analyzing multivariate phenotypes of single and double gene knockdowns, determining which gene modifies the phenotype of the other.
source_span: We leveraged the multivariate nature of our data to identify the direction of genetic interactions by testing each pair of genes ( A and B ) for one of two directional relationship models: A modifies the phenotype of B , or B modifies the phenotype of A . Moreover , we assigned a sign to the relationship , which indicates whether the modification is of an alleviating or aggravating nature . For each gene pair , we analysed the multivariate phenotypes of both single as well as double perturbations .
selection_reasoning: This is a key methodological advance enabling the study to move beyond symmetric interactions to directional, signed genetic interactions.

fact: Directional genetic interactions are identified when the genetic interaction phenotype is parallel or antiparallel to one of the single gene knockdown phenotypes, indicating which gene modifies the other and whether the effect is alleviating or aggravating.
source_span: If the double knockdown phenotype is an amplified or dampened version of one of the single gene knockdown phenotypes , then the genetic interaction ( black arrow ) is parallel or antiparallel to the phenotype of either one of the single knockdowns ( blue or orange arrow: Figure 4A ) . Together , this geometric information indicates the directionality of the interaction ( i . e . , which gene modifies which ) , and whether it is alleviating ( antiparallel ) or aggravating ( parallel ) .
selection_reasoning: This explains the conceptual basis for determining direction and sign of genetic interactions, central to the study's main analytical approach.

fact: An example directional genetic interaction was detected where Cdc23 alleviates the phenotype of sti, indicating that functional Cdc23 is required for the phenotype of sti.

selection_reasoning: This concrete example illustrates the application and biological insight gained from the directional genetic interaction method.

fact: Directional genetic interactions can be identified by comparing double gene knockdown phenotypes to single knockdowns, revealing which gene functionally modifies the other.
source_span: Together , this geometric information indicates the directionality of the interaction ( i . e . , which gene modifies which ) , and whether it is alleviating ( antiparallel ) or aggravating ( parallel ) . For example , if the double knockdown phenotype of gene A and gene B is similar to the single knockdown of gene A , we call this an alleviating interaction from A to B ( A → B ) . This indicates that a functional gene A is required for the phenotype of gene B ( i . e . , gene A is functionally upstream of gene B ) , while the absence or presence of B has a limited effect on the phenotype of A .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the core concept of directional genetic interactions, which is central to the study's approach and findings.

fact: Using a conservative threshold, directional epistatic interactions were found between 1,344 gene pairs, with 1,040 alleviating and 304 aggravating interactions.

fact: The directional genetic interaction network reveals regulatory, causal, and temporal relationships between genes involved in cell cycle processes.

This directional alleviating interaction between the genes reflects the known , consecutive functions of the encoded proteins .
selection_reasoning: This example illustrates how directional interactions correspond to biological pathways, supporting the study's conclusions.

selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight explains the biological basis of a key directional genetic interaction.

fact: Key cell cycle regulators such as polo, γTuRC, SAC, APC/C, dynein/dynactin, and cytokinesis genes form a network of directional epistatic interactions that reflect their temporal and functional relationships during mitosis.

selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight explains how CYP734A50 influences style length, linking gene function to hormone levels, a key biological mechanism.

fact: Exogenous treatment with brassinolide increases style length in S-morph flowers of Primula vulgaris and Primula forbesii by promoting cell elongation.
source_span: When treating developing P. vulgaris and P. forbesii flowers with brassinolide, treated S-morphs developed significantly longer styles in a concentration-dependent manner... This effect was entirely due to increased cell elongation after brassinolide treatment.
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates the hormonal regulation of style length and validates the role of brassinosteroids, a principal experimental result.

fact: CYP734A50 arose via a gene duplication event specific to the Primula lineage and is closely related to the paralogue CYP734A51 found in both morphs.
source_span: A molecular phylogeny of angiosperm CYP734A proteins found in sequenced genomes indicated that CYP734A50 arose via a gene duplication specific to the Primula lineage.
selection_reasoning: This evolutionary background provides context for the gene's origin and uniqueness, important for understanding its role in heterostyly.

fact: CYP734A50 shows a higher rate of non-synonymous substitutions and relaxed purifying selection compared to its paralogue CYP734A51, consistent with its location in a non-recombining region of the genome.
source_span: Comparing P. veris and P. forbesii CYP734A50 gave a Ka/Ks ratio of 0.56... This difference was entirely due to a higher rate of non-synonymous substitutions... relaxed constraints were supported for the PfoCYP734A50 branch... we favour the explanation that the faster rate of molecular evolution of CYP734A50 proteins is due to a reduced efficacy of purifying selection as predicted by theory.
selection_reasoning: This genetic and evolutionary analysis explains the molecular evolution of CYP734A50, linking gene function to genomic context, a key insight.

fact: The presence or absence of CYP734A50 strictly cosegregates with the floral morph type in all heterostylous Primula species sampled.
source_span: Thus, the CYP734A50 presence/absence polymorphism strictly cosegregates with the morph type in all heterostylous species sampled across the Primula phylogeny.
selection_reasoning: This genetic association is fundamental to the study's conclusion that CYP734A50 is the G locus controlling style-length polymorphism.

fact: CYP734A50 represents the G locus in the Primula heterostyly supergene, and its expression in S-morph styles causes brassinosteroid degradation, limiting cell expansion and style elongation.
source_span: Thus , our combined evidence indicates that CYP734A50 represents the G locus in the Primula heterostyly supergene , whose expression in S-morph styles causes brassinosteroid degradation , limiting cell expansion and style elongation ( Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ) .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking a specific gene to the biological mechanism underlying style length differences in Primula, central to the study's main question.

fact: CYP734A50 arose via a lineage-specific gene duplication and presumably gained style-specific expression in the ancestor of the Primulaceae.
source_span: Evolutionarily , CYP734A50 arose via a lineage-specific gene duplication and presumably gain of style-specific expression .
selection_reasoning: This provides key evolutionary context explaining the origin of the gene and its role in style length variation.

fact: The duplication and gain of style-specific expression of CYP734A50 likely represents the dominant style-shortening mutation proposed in models explaining the evolutionary origin of distyly.
source_span: The proposed duplication and gain of style-specific expression of CYP734A50 in the ancestor of the Primulaceae likely represents this dominant style-shortening mutation .
selection_reasoning: This connects the gene's evolution to established theoretical models of distyly evolution, highlighting its significance.

fact: Two main models explain the evolutionary origin of distyly, both postulating that the first morphological change was the reduction of style length by a dominant mutation.
source_span: Two main models have been proposed to explain the evolutionary origin of distyly . While they differ in the sequence of events , assuming either that morphological features evolved first ( Lloyd and Webb , 1992 ) or that intra-morph incompatibility arose first ( Charlesworth and Charlesworth , 1979 ) , they both postulate that the first morphological change was the reduction of style length by a dominant mutation .
selection_reasoning: This background is necessary to understand the biological and evolutionary context motivating the study.

fact: The faster rate of molecular evolution of CYP734A50 proteins is likely due to a reduced efficacy of purifying selection rather than positive selection.
source_span: While rigorously ruling out positive selection would likely require sequences of the paralogues from more Primula species , based on the above results we favour the explanation that the faster rate of molecular evolution of CYP734A50 proteins is due to a reduced efficacy of purifying selection as predicted by theory .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the evolutionary forces acting on CYP734A50, which is important for interpreting its molecular evolution.

fact: CYP734A7 causes brassinosteroid-deficient phenotypes when overexpressed.
source_span: CYP734A7 causes BR-deficient phenotypes when overexpressed ( Ohnishi et al . , 2006 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides functional context for related genes in the CYP734A family, supporting the role of CYP734A50 in brassinosteroid metabolism.

fact: The long homostyle mutant of Primula vulgaris carrying the exon-4 deletion arose spontaneously as a single plant in a large P. vulgaris population in Germany.
source_span: The long homostyle mutant of P . vulgaris carrying the exon-4 deletion was provided by Gartenbau Ebbing-Lohaus , Heiden , Germany , where it arose spontaneously as a single plant in a large P . vulgaris population;
selection_reasoning: This fact provides key background on the genetic mutation studied, relevant to understanding the origin of the mutant used in the research.

fact: The exon-4 deletion mutant of Primula x pruhoniciana, a hybrid of P. juliae and P. vulgaris, was found independently in a local garden center in Berlin.
source_span: the exon-4 deletion mutant of P . x pruhoniciana ( a hybrid of P . juliae and P . vulgaris ) was found in a local garden center in Berlin . Therefore , both mutants were considered to be independently arisen .

fact: Primula forbesii seeds were grown under controlled short-day and long-day conditions to stimulate flowering for experimental analysis.
source_span: Primula forbesii seeds were obtained from the Botanical Garden at the University of Zurich ( accession 20050032 ) and grown in a growth room at 18°C , initially under short-day conditions ( 8 hr light , 16 hr dark ) to stimulate flowering , then under long-day conditions ( 16 hr light , 8 hr dark ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the experimental setup for growing a key species used in the study, relevant to the methods.

fact: Styles and petal tubes with attached anthers of L- and S-morph flowers of Primula veris were sampled at a developmental stage when differences in style length and anther position develop.
source_span: Styles and petal tubes with attached anthers of L- and S-morph flowers of P . veris were sampled when petals were between 4 and 10 mm long , corresponding to the time when the difference in style length and anther position develops ( Stirling , 1932; Webster and Gilmartin , 2006 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the timing of tissue sampling critical for studying morphological differences central to the research question.

fact: RNA sequencing was performed on Primula veris and Primula forbesii samples to analyze gene expression differences between floral morphs.
source_span: TruSeq RNA libraries were generated according to the manufacturer’s instructions ( Illumina ) and sequenced using the Illumina HiSeq2500 instrument ( 2 × 100 cycles ) , essentially as described ( Mascher et al . , 2013 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a key method used to identify gene expression differences relevant to the study's main question.

fact: Genes with higher expression in S-morph styles compared to other samples were considered candidates for the G locus controlling floral morph differences.
source_span: Genes with higher expression in S-morph styles for all three comparisons having a p-value below 0 . 05 were considered as G locus candidates .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies the main genetic target of the study, linking gene expression to floral morph determination.

fact: The gene CYP734A50 was identified and named as a candidate gene involved in floral morph differences in Primula veris and Primula forbesii.
source_span: The CYP734A50 gene was named as such after consultation with Dr . David Nelson ( http://drnelson . uthsc . edu/CytochromeP450 . html ) .

fact: The coding sequences of PveCYP734A50 and PfoCYP734A50 were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and are publicly available in GenBank.
source_span: PveCYP734A50 and PfoCYP734A50 coding sequences were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and are included in Supplementary file 2 . They are also available in GenBank under accession numbers KX589238 , KX589239 , KX589240 and KX589241 .
selection_reasoning: This fact confirms the validation and availability of key genetic sequences supporting the study's conclusions.

fact: The CYP734A50 gene was identified and named in Primula species after consultation with an expert in cytochrome P450 genes.
source_span: The CYP734A50 gene was named as such after consultation with Dr . David Nelson ( http://drnelson . uthsc . edu/CytochromeP450 . html ) .
