fact: TNF-induced apoptosis in keratinocytes can initiate inflammatory skin disease, indicating that defects in keratinocytes themselves can trigger both TNF-dependent and TNF-independent inflammation.
source_span: Moreover , our findings provide further evidence that TNF-induced apoptosis can play a role in inflammatory skin disease and indicate that defects in keratinocytes themselves can initiate TNF-dependent and -independent inflammation .
selection_reasoning: This fact connects cell death mechanisms in keratinocytes to the initiation of skin inflammation.

fact: Non-canonical NF-κB signalling can be a driver of inflammation in epithelial cells, which may be relevant to human psoriasis.
source_span: Importantly , we have shown that non-canonical NF-κB signalling can be the driver of inflammation in epithelial cells . This observation might be relevant to human psoriasis because it has been reported that the levels of TWEAK and its receptor Fn-14 are elevated in human psoriatic lesions ( Cheng et al . , 2015 ) , and it is well established that TWEAK/Fn14 signalling induces degradation of TRAF2 and activation of non-canonical NF-κB signalling ( Saitoh et al . , 2003; Vince et al . , 2008 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact links the mouse model findings to human disease relevance and potential mechanisms.

fact: Inhibition of non-canonical NF-κB signalling might be beneficial in chronic inflammatory diseases such as psoriasis, especially when combined with TNF inhibitors.
source_span: Thus , our results suggest that inhibition of non-canonical NF-κB signalling might be beneficial in chronic inflammatory disease together with TNF inhibitors .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the translational significance and therapeutic implication of the findings.

fact: In normal skin, TNF signalling induced by bacterial penetration activates canonical NF-κB signalling and inflammatory cytokine production to maintain skin homeostasis.
source_span: ( A ) In normal wild-type skin TNF signalling might be activated by local penetration of bacteria into the epidermis . This will induce TNF , presumably by keratinocytes themselves or other resident cells such as Langerhans cells , and promotes canonical NF-κB signalling , inflammatory cytokine production and expression of prosurvival genes . If this response nullifies the threat , TNF signalling is turned off and homeostasis of the skin is maintained .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the normal physiological role of TNF signalling in skin immunity.

fact: Loss of TRAF2 in keratinocytes leads to TNF-induced apoptotic cell death that recruits inflammatory cells and causes epidermal hyperplasia, creating a vicious cycle of inflammation.
source_span: ( B ) In the absence of TRAF2 in keratinocytes , TNF production can induce apoptotic cell death . This cell death , possibly because of the release of DAMPs , recruits neutrophils and other inflammatory cells to the skin and causes epidermal hyperplasia . Loss of TRAF2 also causes constitutive non-canonical NF-κB activation in viable keratinocytes , which increases the production and release of inflammatory cytokines , including TNF . Thus , TRAF2-deficient keratinocytes do not need to be stimulated by bacteria to produce TNF , and TNF-induced death sets up a potentially vicious cycle of inflammation .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the pathological mechanism by which TRAF2 loss causes skin inflammation.

fact: Deleting Tnf in Traf2-deficient mice prevents keratinocyte apoptosis and early onset of psoriasis-like skin inflammation.
source_span: ( C ) Concomitant deletion of Tnf in mice with Traf2-deficient keratinocytes breaks this vicious cycle and prevents apoptosis of keratinocytes and early onset of the psoriasis-like phenotype .
selection_reasoning: This experimental fact shows the critical role of TNF in initiating early inflammation.

fact: In the absence of TNF, Traf2-deficient keratinocytes still produce inflammatory cytokines via non-canonical NF-κB signalling, leading to psoriasis-like skin inflammation with slower onset.
source_span: ( D ) In the absence of TNF , Traf2-deficient keratinocytes still produce inflammatory cytokines via the non-canonical NF-κB pathway that ultimately generate the same psoriasis-like phenotype in mice but with slower onset . These cytokines recruit inflammatory immune cells to the skin , including neutrophils and IFNγ+ T cells .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the TNF-independent inflammatory pathway contributing to disease progression.

fact: Wild-type, Traf2-deficient, and Sphk1-deficient mouse dermal fibroblasts were treated with tumor necrosis factor (TNF) to study their cellular responses.
source_span: Wild–type , Traf2-/- and Sphk1-/- immortalised MDFs were treated with TNF ( 100 ng/ml ) in the absence or presence of Q-VD-OPh ( QVD; 10μM; SM Biochemicals , Anaheim , CA ) and Necrostatin ( Nec; 50μM; Biomol , Farmingdale , NY ) for the times indicated and lysed in ice-cold DISC buffer .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key experimental model and treatment used to investigate the cellular mechanisms relevant to the study.

fact: Keratinocytes and mouse dermal fibroblasts were isolated from adult mouse skin to analyze cell-specific responses.
source_span: Skin was separated from the tail of an adult mouse and incubated in dispase II ( 20 mg/ml ) at 4°C for 24 hr and keratinocytes and MDFs were isolated from the epidermal and dermal layers respectively as described before ( Etemadi et al . , 2013; Rickard et al . , 2014a ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on the biological system used to study skin cell types relevant to the disease or mechanism.

fact: Keratinocyte viability and cell death were measured after treatment with TNF and Smac-mimetic compounds using flow cytometry and viability assays.
source_span: Cells were harvested after 24-hr treatment with human Fc-TNF ( made in-house , referred as 'TNF' in the manuscript ) and Smac-mimetic ( TetraLogic ) , and cell death was measured by Propidium Iodide ( PI ) staining and flow cytometry performed on a FACSCalibur flow cytometer ( BD Biosciences , San Jose , CA ) and analysed using Weasel ( WEHI ) . Keratinocyte viability was assayed using CellTiter 96 ( Promega , Madison , WI ) according to the manufacturer’s instructions .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the key methods used to assess the effects of treatments on keratinocyte survival, central to understanding the study's findings.

fact: Gene expression in keratinocytes was analyzed using quantitative PCR with a mouse inflammation panel to compare Traf2-deficient and control cells.
source_span: cDNA was made with SuperScript VILO cDNA Synthesis kit ( Invitrogen ) and qPCR was performed using TaqMan Open Array mouse inflammation panel ( Applied Biosystems , Carlsbad , CA ) on a QuantStudio 12K Flex machine ( Life Technologies ) following the manufacturer protocols . Comparisons were made between Traf2-/-Tnf-/- and Traf2+/-Tnf-/- keratinocytes using empirical Bayes t-statistics ( Smyth , 2004 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key molecular method and comparison used to identify gene expression changes relevant to the study question.

fact: Skin tissue sections were analyzed by immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry to detect markers such as keratin 6, keratin 14, cleaved caspase-3, and immune cell markers.
source_span: For skin immunofluorescence , parafin sections were de-waxed , subjected to heat-induced epitope retrieval ( HIER ) with citrate buffer , blocked in 3% goat serum , then permeabilised with 0 . 3% Triton X-100 , and stained with keratin 6 ( Covance ) or keratin 14 , and goat anti-rabbit Alexa 594 ( Invitrogen , Carlsbad , CA ) antibodies . For tissue immunohistochemistry , sections were dewaxed and subjected to antigen retrieval in trypsin buffer or HIER with citrate buffer and stained with anti-CC3 ( 9691; Cell Signaling Technology , Danvers , MA ) , anti-CD45 ( BD , San Jose , CA ) and goat anti-rabbit biotinylated antibodies .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes key histological analyses used to assess skin pathology and immune involvement, important for understanding disease mechanisms.

fact: Dermal T cells were isolated from mouse skin and stimulated ex vivo to analyze cytokine production and immune responses.
source_span: Dermal T cells were isolated from the skin and resuspended in RPMI-1640 supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated fetal calf serum , 2 mM L-Glutamine ( GIBCO ) , 50 μM 2-mercaptoethanol ( Sigma , St . Louis , MO ) 100 U/ml penicillin/streptomycin ( GIBCO ) . Cells were stimulated for 4 hr in presence of PMA ( 20 ng/ml ) and Ionomycin ( 1 μg/ml ) in presence of the GolgiPlug ( BD Biosciences ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key immunological assay to evaluate T cell function relevant to the study's investigation of immune mechanisms.

fact: Bone marrow transplantation was performed to study the role of immune cells in Traf2-deficient mice.
source_span: Approximately 5 million cells from the bone marrow of C57/BL6 or IFNγ mice were injected by tail i . v . to Traf2EKO . Mice were maintained on 2 mg/ml neomycin in drinking water for three weeks post irradiation .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights an in vivo experimental approach to dissect immune contributions to the phenotype in Traf2-deficient mice.

fact: Glucocorticoids are among the most commonly prescribed drugs and play a key role in metabolic, vascular, and immunological responses to stress.
source_span: Glucocorticoids ( GCs ) have a key role in the metabolic , vascular , and immunological response to stress ( Cain and Cidlowski , 2017; Oster et al . , 2017 ) . GCs are among the most commonly prescribed drugs , and GC treatment remains a cornerstone in the management of many rheumatic and inflammatory diseases despite the introduction of modern disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs and biological immunomodulatory treatment ( Smolen et al . , 2017 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the clinical importance and widespread use of glucocorticoids, motivating the study.

fact: There is currently no biomarker that can accurately quantify glucocorticoid action in tissues.
source_span: Glucocorticoids are among the most commonly prescribed drugs , but there is no biomarker that can quantify their action . As a result of this complexity , circulating levels of cortisol relate poorly to tissue action of cortisol , and serum cortisol therefore has limited value as a biomarker for GC action ( Karssen et al . , 2001 ) .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the key knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

fact: Unphysiological glucocorticoid exposure has been implicated in the development of common diseases such as type 2 diabetes, hypertension, abdominal obesity, and cardiovascular disease.
source_span: Unphysiological GC exposure has been implicated in the etiology of several common diseases such as type 2 diabetes mellitus , hypertension , abdominal obesity , and cardiovascular disease ( Ragnarsson et al . , 2019 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the clinical significance of measuring glucocorticoid action for disease understanding and management.

fact: The study aimed to identify and validate circulating biomarkers of glucocorticoid action using an integrated multi-omic analysis approach.
source_span: The aim of the study was to identify and validate circulating biomarkers of glucocorticoid action . The transcriptome in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and adipose tissue , plasma miRNAomic , and serum metabolomics were compared between the interventions using integrated multi-omic analysis .
selection_reasoning: This states the main research question and the high-level methodological approach.

fact: The study used a randomized, crossover, single-blind design involving 10 subjects with primary adrenal insufficiency to compare physiological glucocorticoid exposure and withdrawal.
source_span: In a randomized , crossover , single-blind , discovery study , 10 subjects with primary adrenal insufficiency ( and no other endocrinopathies ) were admitted at the in-patient clinic and studied during physiological glucocorticoid exposure and withdrawal .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key experimental design and model used to study glucocorticoid action.

fact: Subjects with primary adrenal insufficiency, who lack glucocorticoid production, serve as a human glucocorticoid 'knock-down' model for studying glucocorticoid action.
source_span: Subjects with primary adrenal insufficiency , Addison’s disease , lack GC production from the adrenal cortex and can therefore be considered a human GC ‘knock-down’ model ( Figure 1A ) .
selection_reasoning: This explains the rationale for the chosen study population as a model system.

fact: The study identified a transcriptomic profile from peripheral blood mononuclear cells and adipose tissue, as well as a multi-omic cluster, that were predictive of glucocorticoid exposure.

selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding demonstrating successful identification of molecular signatures of glucocorticoid action.

fact: A circulating microRNA, miR-122-5p, was found to correlate with genes and metabolites regulated by glucocorticoid exposure and was replicated in independent studies with varying glucocorticoid exposure.

selection_reasoning: This identifies a specific circulating biomarker candidate validated across studies.

fact: Integrated multi-omic analysis combining gene expression, circulating microRNAs, and metabolites provides increased robustness for identifying biomarkers of glucocorticoid action compared to single-omic analyses.
source_span: Integrated multi-omic analysis provides increased robustness over analysis of individual ‘omic data sets ( Ideker et al . , 2011 ) . In particular , the identification of groups within one ‘omic ‘layer’ with shared co-regulation within another ‘omic layer implies a functional relationship that can be used both to assess the mechanistical relevance and to support the identification of biomarkers ( Karczewski and Snyder , 2018; Misra et al . , 2018 ) .

fact: The results provide a basis for developing biomarkers to measure glucocorticoid effects, which could help individualize and optimize glucocorticoid therapy and improve understanding of diseases related to abnormal glucocorticoid exposure.

selection_reasoning: This states the significance and potential clinical impact of the study findings.

fact: Glucocorticoid (GC)-responsive genes have higher connectivity in the human interactome than expected by chance.
source_span: GC-responsive genes were shown to have higher connectivity in the human interactome than expected by chance , demonstrated using 10 , 000 permutations of this network model ( Appendix 2 ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights a key network property of GC-responsive genes, relevant to understanding their biological impact.

fact: Despite limited overlap in differentially expressed genes, common pathways related to GC action are active in both PBMC and adipose tissue transcriptomes.
source_span: The greatest number of correlations shared was between PBMC and adipose tissue transcriptome ( 525 genes , Figure 3C ) , reinforcing the observation that , while the gene-level overlap of differential expression was limited , common pathways are active in both tissues related to GC action , which involve similar networks of co-expressed genes .
selection_reasoning: This explains the shared biological mechanisms of GC action across different tissues, a core study conclusion.

fact: A set of 59 genes was identified that perfectly classified glucocorticoid-treated versus saline-treated groups in both PBMC and adipose tissue transcriptomes.
source_span: This identified a set of 59 genes as variables of importance with fold changes in the same directions in both transcriptomic data sets that perfectly classified HC from saline treatment ( Supplementary file 1e ) .
selection_reasoning: This gene set is a principal finding demonstrating a molecular signature of GC exposure.

fact: Six of nine genes significantly differentially expressed in both PBMC and adipose tissue transcriptomes are associated with glucocorticoid response via gene ontology.
source_span: Nine of these genes were significantly differentially expressed in both PBMC and adipose tissue transcriptomes ( Figure 4C ) , and , of these nine genes , six were associated with GC response via gene ontology ( IL18RAP , JAK2 , MTSS1 , RIN2 , KIF1B , and BCL9L ) ( Figure 4D ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact links specific genes to GC response, supporting mechanistic insights.

source_span: The gene set ( n = 59 ) that we identified , which classified both PBMC and adipose tissue transcriptomes in relation to GC exposure , was validated ( area under the curve [AUC] 0 . 70–0 . 96 ) by further testing in five other previous studies of GC action by other research groups in cellular models ( Table 3 ) .
selection_reasoning: Validation across multiple studies confirms the robustness and translational relevance of the gene signature.

fact: A hypernetwork model integrating transcriptomic, miRNAomic, and metabolomic data identified a core group of 139 highly connected multi-omic elements related to glucocorticoid exposure.
source_span: We then quantified the number of correlations between all the circulating ‘omic data associated with GC exposure ( n = 336 ) using a hypernetwork . This approach was used to define a group of highly connected multi-omic elements with a relationship to GC exposure ( Figure 5A ) . A hypernetwork model of the core group of 139 highly connected elements was generated ( Figure 5B ) .
selection_reasoning: This multi-omic integration reveals complex molecular relationships underlying GC effects.

fact: The gene DCK was the only gene shared between the GC-dependent adipose tissue transcriptome and the multi-omic hypernetwork that also had predictive value for GC exposure.

selection_reasoning: Identifying DCK as a key predictive gene links transcriptomic and multi-omic findings with functional relevance.

source_span: Deletion of the DCK gene region has been shown to be associated with increased sensitivity to GCs ( Malani et al . , 2017 ) , an observation in alignment with the reduction in expression we found in both PBMC and adipose tissue transcriptomes in association with GC exposure ( Figure 4C ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact connects gene expression changes to known functional effects on GC sensitivity.

fact: miR-122-5p was identified as the only miRNA present in higher order modules of the multi-omic network and was correlated with cortisol exposure and FKBP5 expression, a regulator of glucocorticoid sensitivity.
source_span: These modules revealed multi-omic relationships and demonstrated that miR-122-5p was the only miRNA present in higher order modules as measured by network centrality . miR-122-5p was correlated with cortisol exposure and the expression of FKBP5 , a regulator of GC sensitivity ( cluster 11 in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1f ) .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a specific miRNA linked to GC regulation and sensitivity, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Plasma miR-122-5p was markedly down-regulated in subjects with Addison’s disease, replicating findings from the experimental glucocorticoid exposure study.

selection_reasoning: This clinical replication supports the translational relevance of miR-122-5p as a biomarker of GC exposure.

fact: Addison’s disease is a rare disorder characterized by absent or very low endogenous glucocorticoid production, making it a unique clinical model for glucocorticoid biomarker discovery.
source_span: Addison’s disease or primary adrenal insufficiency is a rare disorder, but a unique clinical model for GC biomarker discovery due to absent or very low endogenous GC production (Gan et al., 2014; Sævik et al., 2020).
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the disease context and rationale for using Addison’s disease patients to study glucocorticoid biomarkers.

fact: A clinical experimental study generated two profoundly different states of glucocorticoid exposure within the physiological range in the same individual to identify biomarkers of glucocorticoid action.

selection_reasoning: This describes the main experimental approach used to study glucocorticoid action and biomarker identification.

fact: Integrated multi-omic analysis of gene expression, metabolome, and circulating microRNAs from two independent tissues identified pathways related to glucocorticoid response and putative biomarkers of glucocorticoid action.
source_span: The novelty of this study is the identification of pathways related to GC response and putative biomarkers of GC action in gene expression, metabolome, and miRNAs derived from integrated multi-omic analysis in two independent tissues.

source_span: Increased exposure to GCs impairs glucose tolerance and may induce type 2 diabetes. source_span: In other organisms including Pectobacterium atrosepticum (Liu et al., 2008), P. aeruginosa (Lesic et al., 2009), Aeromonas hydrophila (Khajanchi et al., 2009), Yersinia pseudotuberculosis (Zhang et al., 2011), Chromobacterium violaceum (Stauff and Bassler, 2011), Vibrio cholerae (Zheng et al., 2010), Vibrio alginolyticus (Sheng et al., 2012), and Vibrio parahaemolyticus (Wang et al., 2013), QS regulates genes for the T6S apparatus (not the effector and immunity factors as we describe for B. thailandensis).
selection_reasoning: This fact situates the study in a broader context of QS regulation of T6S, highlighting the novelty of the mechanism described for B. thailandensis.

fact: The BtaR1-BtaI1 quorum sensing system in B. thailandensis carries a metabolic cost under experimental conditions, unlike the BtaR2-BtaI2 and BtaR3-BtaI3 systems.
source_span: Under the conditions of our experiments the BtaR1-BtaI1 QS system carries with it a metabolic cost, which is evident in broth culture competition experiments and to a lesser extent in pure broth culture grow curves. The BtaR2-BtaI2 and BtaR3-BtaI3 QS systems do not appear to carry this large cost.
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies a key biological cost associated with a specific QS system, which is central to the study's investigation of policing mechanisms.

fact: B. thailandensis wild-type populations mitigate the cost of BtaR1-BtaI1 gene regulation by limiting the growth of quorum sensing mutants through regulation of cell-contact-dependent toxin and immunity proteins.
source_span: We describe a mechanism by which wild-type populations can mitigate the cost of BtaR1-BtaI1 gene regulation by hindering the growth of QS mutants via regulation of cell-contact-dependent toxin and immunity proteins.
selection_reasoning: This fact states the principal finding of the study, describing the novel policing mechanism that enforces cooperation.

fact: This policing mechanism involves quorum sensing control of type VI secretion system (T6S) effector and immunity proteins that enforce cooperation by limiting the proliferation of QS mutants.
source_span: A policing model where QS control of T6S contact-dependent killing (effector and immunity proteins) enforces cooperation. QS-proficient bacteria (cooperators) limit the proliferation of a QS mutant (potential cheater) in a population.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the key mechanism by which cooperation is maintained, central to the study's main claim.

fact: Without quorum sensing co-regulation of the T6S killing mechanism, quorum sensing mutants outcompete wild-type cooperators.
source_span: Without co-regulation of the killing mechanism, QS mutants (potential cheaters) outcompete the wild type cooperators.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the significance of QS regulation of T6S in preventing cheating, a core conclusion of the study.

fact: BtaR1 promotes aggregation of B. thailandensis cells under some conditions, which may help cells resist infiltration by other strains and protect against social cheaters.
source_span: It is interesting that BtaR1 also promotes aggregation of cells under some conditions (Chandler et al., 2009). One can imagine that this system brings cells into close proximity where they can resist infiltration by other strains and species while at the same time protect themselves against social deviant BtaR1 mutant bacteria.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a plausible biological significance and context for the policing mechanism, relevant to the study's implications.

fact: Long-range coupling within prefrontal-hippocampal networks that supports cognitive performance emerges early in life.
source_span: The long-range coupling within prefrontal-hippocampal networks that account for cognitive performance emerges early in life.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the developmental timing and relevance of the studied brain network, setting the stage for the research question.

fact: Neonatal hippocampal theta bursts have been proposed to drive the generation of prefrontal oscillations, but the cellular basis of these early interactions was previously unresolved.
source_span: The discontinuous hippocampal theta bursts have been proposed to drive the generation of neonatal prefrontal oscillations, yet the cellular substrate of these early interactions is still unresolved.
selection_reasoning: This states the main knowledge gap motivating the study.

fact: The study used optogenetic manipulation of glutamatergic projection neurons in the CA1 area of dorsal or intermediate/ventral hippocampus in neonatal mice to investigate their role in prefrontal oscillatory entrainment.
source_span: Here, we selectively target optogenetic manipulation of glutamatergic projection neurons in the CA1 area of either dorsal or intermediate/ventral hippocampus at neonatal age to elucidate their contribution to the emergence of prefrontal oscillatory entrainment.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key experimental approach used to address the research question.

fact: Despite stronger theta and ripple power in dorsal hippocampus, the prefrontal cortex is mainly coupled with intermediate/ventral hippocampus through phase-locking of neuronal firing via dense direct axonal projections.
source_span: We show that despite stronger theta and ripples power in dorsal hippocampus, the prefrontal cortex is mainly coupled with intermediate/ventral hippocampus by phase-locking of neuronal firing via dense direct axonal projections.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding identifying the specific hippocampal subregion driving prefrontal coupling.

fact: Theta band-specific optogenetic activation of pyramidal neurons in intermediate/ventral CA1, but not dorsal CA1, enhances prefrontal oscillations in neonatal mice.
source_span: Theta band-confined activation by light of pyramidal neurons in intermediate/ventral but not dorsal CA1 that were transfected by in utero electroporation with high-efficiency channelrhodopsin boosts prefrontal oscillations.
selection_reasoning: This causal evidence directly links intermediate/ventral CA1 activity to prefrontal oscillatory entrainment, a core experimental result.

fact: The data provide causal evidence for the cellular origin of long-range coupling between hippocampus and prefrontal cortex in the developing brain.
source_span: Our data causally elucidate the cellular origin of the long-range coupling in the developing brain.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the significance and main conclusion of the study.

fact: In adult rodents, coordinated oscillatory activity in specific frequency bands, especially theta (4–12 Hz), functionally couples medial prefrontal cortex and hippocampus and is critical for learning and memory.
source_span: In the adult rodent brain, coordinated patterns of oscillatory activity code in a frequency-specific manner for sensory and cognitive performance. For example, learning and memory critically depend on oscillations within theta frequency band (4–12 Hz) that functionally couple the medial prefrontal cortex (PFC) and hippocampus (HP).
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the functional importance of theta oscillations and prefrontal-hippocampal coupling.

fact: Frequency-tuned brain oscillations coupling prefrontal cortex and hippocampus are present during early development, before memory and attention abilities mature.
source_span: These frequency-tuned brain states are present already during early development, long before the memory and attentional abilities have fully matured.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the developmental relevance of the studied oscillations.

fact: Network oscillations during development have a discontinuous and fragmented structure with bursts of activity alternating with silent periods.
source_span: Network oscillations during development have a highly discontinuous and fragmented structure with bursts of activity alternating with ‘silent’ periods.
selection_reasoning: This describes the nature of early brain oscillations relevant to the study.

fact: Spindle bursts are the most common oscillatory pattern during development, synchronizing large cortical and subcortical networks within the theta-alpha frequency range.
source_span: The most common oscillatory pattern, spindle bursts, synchronizes large cortical and subcortical networks within theta-alpha frequency range.
selection_reasoning: This background fact contextualizes the types of oscillations present in early development.

fact: In sensory systems, early oscillations like spindle bursts and gamma oscillations have been proposed to facilitate cortical map formation and thalamocortical topography organization, but the role of early oscillations in limbic systems is less understood.
source_span: In sensory systems, spindle bursts have been proposed to act as a template facilitating the formation of cortical maps, whereas early gamma oscillations seem to control the organization of thalamocortical topography. In limbic systems dedicated to mnemonic and executive abilities, the knowledge on the relevance of early network oscillations is even sparser.
selection_reasoning: This motivates the study by highlighting the gap in understanding limbic system oscillations.

fact: Previous lesion studies suggested that prefrontal-hippocampal communication during development might be necessary for episodic memory maturation, but lacked selectivity for specific activity patterns.
source_span: Few lesion studies, yet without selectivity for specific activity patterns, suggested that prefrontal-hippocampal communication during development might be necessary for the maturation of episodic memory.
selection_reasoning: This provides clinical and developmental relevance and motivates the need for selective causal studies.

fact: Direct causal evidence for the contribution of early oscillations to circuit maturation in prefrontal-hippocampal networks was previously missing due to methodological challenges.
source_span: While most of this correlative evidence put forward the relevance of early oscillations beyond a simple epiphenomenal signature of developing networks, direct evidence for their causal contribution to circuit maturation is still missing. This is mainly due to the absence of a causal interrogation of developing networks, similarly to the investigations done in adult ones.
selection_reasoning: This states the methodological gap the study addresses.

fact: Recent advances in area-, layer-, and cell type-specific manipulations at neonatal age have enabled causal interrogation of developing prefrontal-hippocampal networks.
source_span: Only recently the methodological difficulties related to area-, layer- and cell type-specific manipulations at neonatal age have been overcome.
selection_reasoning: This explains the feasibility and novelty of the study's approach.

fact: The study examined network oscillatory and firing activity in CA1 of dorsal and intermediate/ventral hippocampus in neonatal mice at postnatal days 8–10, the age when hippocampal-prefrontal coupling initiates.
source_span: To fill this knowledge gap, we firstly examined the network oscillatory and firing activity of CA1 area of either dHP or i/vHP by performing extracellular recordings... The entire investigation was performed at the age of initiation of coupling between HP and PFC, that is, P8-10.
selection_reasoning: This describes the developmental timing and experimental focus relevant to the main findings.

fact: The CA1 area in neonatal mice shows discontinuous oscillations mainly in the theta band (4–12 Hz) accompanied by sharp waves and strong neuronal firing.
source_span: Independent of the position along the dorsal-ventral axis, the CA1 area was characterized by discontinuous oscillations with main frequency in theta band (4–12 Hz)... They were accompanied by prominent sharp-waves (SPWs) reversing across the pyramidal layer and by strong MUA discharge.
selection_reasoning: This characterizes the physiological activity underlying the studied coupling.

fact: The CA1 area of the neonatal mouse hippocampus exhibits discontinuous theta oscillations accompanied by sharp-waves and multi-unit activity.
source_span: Independent of the position along the dorsal-ventral axis , the CA1 area was characterized by discontinuous oscillations with main frequency in theta band ( 4–12 Hz ) and irregular low amplitude beta-gamma band components , which have been previously categorized as theta oscillations ( Brockmann et al . , 2011 ) . They were accompanied by prominent sharp-waves ( SPWs ) reversing across the pyramidal layer ( str . pyr . ) and by strong MUA discharge
selection_reasoning: This describes the fundamental neural activity pattern in the hippocampus at neonatal age, providing essential background for the study.

fact: Theta bursts in the intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) occur more frequently, have larger amplitude, and shorter duration compared to the dorsal hippocampus (dHP) in neonatal mice.
source_span: The theta bursts in i/vHP had significantly higher occurrence ( i/vHP: 8 . 1 ± 0 . 2 oscillations/min , n = 103 mice vs . dHP: 5 . 2 ± 0 . 3 oscillations/min , n = 41 mice; p<0 . 001 ) , larger amplitude ( i/vHP:110 . 6 ± 5 . 6 µV vs . dHP: 92 . 9 ± 2 . 6 µV; p=0 . 015 ) , and shorter duration ( i/vHP: 3 . 5 ± 0 . 1 s vs . dHP: 4 . 3 ± 0 . 1 s , p<0 . 001 ) when compared with dHP
selection_reasoning: This key finding highlights functional differences in hippocampal subregions relevant to the study's focus on network activity.

fact: Pyramidal neurons in the intermediate/ventral hippocampus fire at higher rates than those in the dorsal hippocampus in neonatal mice.
source_span: Overall , pyramidal neurons in i/vHP fired at higher rates ( 0 . 45 ± 0 . 01 Hz , n = 557 units from 103 mice ) than in the dHP ( 0 . 35 ± 0 . 02 Hz , n = 158 units from 41 mice; p=0 . 025 )
selection_reasoning: This neuronal firing rate difference supports the functional distinction between hippocampal subregions.

fact: Sharp-waves (SPWs) in the neonatal hippocampus are more prominent in the dorsal hippocampus but occur more frequently in the intermediate/ventral hippocampus.
source_span: SPW in neonatal HP were more prominent in the dHP ( 712 . 8 ± 31 . 5 µV , n = 41 mice ) when compared with those occurring in the i/vHP ( 223 . 8 ± 6 . 3 µV , n = 103 mice , p<0 . 001 ) , yet their occurrence increased along the septo-temporal axis ( dHP: 6 . 6 ± 0 . 5 , n = 41 mice; i/vHP: 8 . 6 ± 0 . 2 , n = 103 mice , p<0 . 001 )
selection_reasoning: This finding reveals important differences in network event characteristics along the hippocampal axis.

fact: The power of hippocampal ripples and ripple-related neuronal firing is stronger in the dorsal hippocampus compared to the intermediate/ventral hippocampus in neonatal mice.
source_span: The power of ripples decreased along the septo-temporal axis ( relative power: dHP , 24 . 4 ± 3 . 3 , n = 41 mice; i/vHP , 6 . 1 ± 0 . 60 , n = 103 mice , p<0 . 001 ) . Similarly , the ripple-related spiking was stronger in dHP when compared with i/vHP ( peak firing: dHP: 1 . 13 ± 0 . 09 Hz , n = 232 units; i/vHP 0 . 84 ± 0 . 03 , n = 670 , p<0 . 001 )
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key difference in hippocampal network oscillations relevant to developmental coupling.

fact: The activity patterns and spectral structure differ between the dorsal and intermediate/ventral CA1 hippocampal areas in neonatal mice.
source_span: These data show that the activity patterns in the dorsal and intermediate/ventral CA1 area differ in their properties and spectral structure
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main comparative finding about hippocampal subregion activity.

fact: Tight interactions between the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex emerge already at neonatal age and support memory in adulthood.
source_span: Past studies identified tight interactions between HP and PFC , which emerge already at neonatal age ( Brockmann et al . , 2011; Hartung et al . , 2016 ) and are in support of memory at adulthood ( Krüger et al . , 2012; Spellman et al . , 2015; Place et al . , 2016 )
selection_reasoning: This provides important background and motivation for studying hippocampal-prefrontal coupling in neonates.

fact: Discontinuous theta oscillations in the hippocampus have been proposed to drive activation of local circuits in the prefrontal cortex.
source_span: The discontinuous theta oscillations in HP have been proposed to drive the activation of local circuits in the PFC
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic hypothesis underpins the study's investigation of hippocampal-prefrontal coupling.

fact: Simultaneous recordings of local field potentials and multi-unit activity were performed in the hippocampal CA1 area and prelimbic subdivision of the prefrontal cortex in P8-10 mice to assess coupling.
source_span: To assess the coupling of dHP and i/vHP with PFC , we recorded simultaneously LFP and MUA in the corresponding hippocampal CA1 area and the prelimbic subdivision ( PL ) of the PFC of P8-10 mice
selection_reasoning: This describes the key experimental approach used to investigate neonatal hippocampal-prefrontal interactions.

fact: The prelimbic subdivision of the prefrontal cortex was chosen for investigation because it is the prefrontal area with the densest hippocampal innervation in adults.
source_span: The entire investigation focused on PL , since in adults it is the prefrontal subdivision with the most dense innervation from HP ( Jay and Witter , 1991; Vertes et al . , 2007 )
selection_reasoning: This justifies the anatomical focus of the study relevant to interpreting results.

fact: Prelimbic and hippocampal oscillations co-occur within a narrow time window in neonatal mice, indicating temporal synchrony.
source_span: The majority of prelimbic and hippocampal oscillations co-occurred within a narrow time window
selection_reasoning: This finding supports the presence of functional coupling between hippocampus and prefrontal cortex.

fact: Spectral coherence analysis revealed stronger coupling between the prelimbic cortex and intermediate/ventral hippocampus than between prelimbic cortex and dorsal hippocampus in neonatal mice across theta, beta, and gamma frequency bands.
source_span: The results revealed a stronger coupling for PL-i/vHP ( 4–12 Hz: 0 . 17 ± 0 . 0069; 12–30 Hz: 0 . 31 ± 0 . 011; 30–100 Hz: 0 . 11 ± 0 . 0069 , n = 103 mice ) when compared with PL-dHP ( 4–12 Hz: 0 . 12 ± 0 . 0081; 12–30 Hz: 0 . 18 ± 0 . 0094; 30–100 Hz: 0 . 084 ± 0 . 004 , n = 41 mice )
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding about differential hippocampal-prefrontal connectivity relevant to the study's main question.

fact: Neonatal prelimbic cortex (PL) activity is more strongly driven by oscillations from the intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) than from the dorsal hippocampus (dHP).
source_span: Independent of the position along the septo-temporal axis, the information flow in theta or beta frequency band from either dorsal or intermediate/ventral HP to PL was significantly stronger than in the opposite direction. However, mean gPDC values for i/vHP → PL were significantly (p<0.001) higher (0.069 ± 0.003, n = 103 mice) when compared with those for dHP → PL (0.053 ± 0.003, n = 41 mice).
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the main finding about differential hippocampal subregion influence on neonatal prefrontal activity, a core scientific claim relevant to the study's focus on early brain network interactions.

fact: Theta oscillations in the dorsal hippocampus (dHP) do not substantially contribute to prelimbic cortex (PL) activity despite their higher power.
source_span: Despite higher power, theta oscillations in dHP do not substantially account for prelimbic activity.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the distinct functional roles of hippocampal subregions in driving prefrontal activity, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Sharp wave-ripples (SPWs-ripples) originating in the intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) induce stronger oscillatory activity and neuronal firing in the neonatal prelimbic cortex (PL) than those from the dorsal hippocampus (dHP).
source_span: This prelimbic activation is significantly stronger when induced by SPWs-ripples emerging in i/vHP than in dHP as reflected by the significantly higher power of oscillatory activity in theta, beta, and gamma frequency band... The SPWs-ripple-induced oscillatory activity in the PL of neonatal mice was accompanied by augmentation of firing rates... a less prominent peak was observed following SPW-ripples in dHP.
selection_reasoning: This finding identifies a key functional difference in how hippocampal subregions influence prefrontal network activity during development.

fact: A larger proportion of pyramidal neurons in the CA1 area of the intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) project directly to the prelimbic cortex (PL) in neonatal mice compared to the dorsal hippocampus (dHP).
source_span: Whereas in dHP very few cells were retrogradely labeled (0.15*10^3 ± 0.074*10^3 cells/mm2), a large proportion of pyramidal-shaped cells in the CA1 area of i/vHP projects to PL (3.29*10^3 ± 0.19*10^3 cells/mm2).
selection_reasoning: This anatomical evidence supports the functional findings of stronger i/vHP influence on PL, linking structure to function.

fact: Direct unilateral projections from hippocampal CA1 area to prelimbic cortex (PL) are present already at neonatal age in mice.
source_span: The direct unilateral projections from hippocampal CA1 area to PL have been extensively investigated in adult brain... and are present already at neonatal age.
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes the developmental presence of hippocampal-prefrontal connectivity, justifying the study's focus on neonatal networks.

fact: The study used generalized partial directed coherence (gPDC) to estimate the strength and direction of information flow between hippocampal subregions and prelimbic cortex in neonatal mice.
source_span: Therefore, in a second step, we estimated the strength of directed interactions between PL and HP by calculating the generalized partial directed coherence (gPDC)... The method bases on the notion of Granger causality and avoids distorted connectivity results due to different scaling of data in HP and PL.
selection_reasoning: This high-level methodological fact explains how the study assessed directional connectivity, a key approach underlying the main findings.

fact: Prefrontal oscillations in neonatal mice are generated shortly (~100 ms) after hippocampal sharp wave-ripples (SPWs-ripples).
source_span: Simultaneous recordings from neonatal CA1 area either in dHP or i/vHP and PL showed that already at neonatal age, prefrontal oscillations are generated shortly (~100 ms) after hippocampal SPWs-ripples.
selection_reasoning: This temporal relationship is central to understanding the functional coupling between hippocampus and prefrontal cortex during development.

fact: The CA1 area of the intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) sends dense axonal projections to the prelimbic cortex (PL), especially to its deep layers V and VI.
source_span: In 7 out of 9 mice anterogradely-labeled axons were found in the PL , preferentially within its deep layers V and VI . Thus , the dense axonal projections from CA1 area of i/vHP might represent the substrate of HP-induced oscillatory entrainment of prelimbic circuits .
selection_reasoning: This fact establishes the anatomical basis for hippocampal influence on prelimbic cortex activity, a core background and mechanistic claim.

fact: The hippocampus acts as a drive for prelimbic cortex activation already at neonatal age through direct axonal projections from CA1 to PL.
source_span: The tight coupling by synchrony and the directed information flow from hippocampal CA1 area to PL via direct axonal projections suggest that the HP acts already at neonatal age as a drive for prelimbic activation .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the developmental significance and functional role of hippocampal-prelimbic connectivity, a key conceptual claim.

fact: There are differences in communication between dorsal hippocampus (dHP) to PL and intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) to PL, with stronger driving force along the septo-temporal hippocampal axis.
source_span: Moreover , the differences identified between the dHP – PL and i/vHP – PL communication argue for prominent augmentation of driving force along the septo-temporal hippocampal axis .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the spatial specificity of hippocampal influence on PL, important for understanding the main question.

fact: Selective activation of pyramidal neurons in CA1 of either dHP or i/vHP was achieved by in utero electroporation of a fast-kinetics channelrhodopsin variant (ChR2 ET/TC) and a fluorescent marker.
source_span: To causally confirm these correlative evidences , we selectively activated by light the pyramidal neurons in the CA1 area of either dHP or i/vHP that had been transfected with a highly efficient fast-kinetics double mutant ChR2E123T/T159C ( ET/TC ) and the red fluorescent protein tDimer2 by in utero electroporation ( IUE ) .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key experimental method used to test hippocampal influence on prelimbic circuits.

fact: In utero electroporation transfected a substantial proportion of pyramidal neurons in CA1 of both dHP and i/vHP without affecting overall somatic development or reflexes in mice.
source_span: Staining with NeuN showed that a substantial proportion of neurons in str . pyr . of CA1 area ( dHP: 18 . 3 ± 1 . 0%; ... i/vHP: 14 . 5 ± 1 . 5% ) were transfected by IUE . ... Vibrissa placing , surface righting and cliff aversion reflexes were also not affected by IUE or transfection of neurons with opsins . These data indicate that the overall somatic development during embryonic and postnatal stage of ChR2 ( ET/TC ) -transfected mice is unaltered .
selection_reasoning: This supports the validity of the optogenetic approach and excludes confounding developmental effects.

fact: Blue light pulses at 4, 8, and 16 Hz evoked precisely timed firing of transfected hippocampal pyramidal neurons in vivo, with firing efficiency decreasing at higher frequencies.
source_span: Blue light pulses ( 473 nm , 20–40 mW/mm2 ) at different frequencies ( 4 , 8 , 16 Hz ) led shortly ( <10 ms ) after the stimulus to precisely timed firing of transfected neurons in both dHP and i/vHP . ... For both hippocampal sub-divisions the efficiency of firing similarly decreased with augmenting frequency .
selection_reasoning: This fact confirms the functional activation of targeted neurons, essential for interpreting stimulation results.

fact: Light stimulation of CA1 area of i/vHP at 8 Hz significantly increased oscillatory activity in the prelimbic cortex across theta, beta, and gamma frequency bands.
source_span: The firing in i/vHP timed by light at 8 Hz , but not at 4 Hz or 16 Hz , caused significant ( theta: p=0 . 039 , beta: p=0 . 030 , gamma: p=0 . 0036 ) augmentation of oscillatory activity in all frequency bands as reflected by the higher power in the PL during the stimulation when compared with the time window before the train of pulses .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding demonstrating the functional impact of i/vHP activation on prelimbic oscillations.

fact: Light stimulation of CA1 area of dHP did not affect prelimbic cortex oscillatory activity.
source_span: In contrast , stimulation by light of dHP left the prelimbic activity unaffected .
selection_reasoning: This contrast highlights the spatial specificity of hippocampal influence on PL activity.

fact: In control animals without opsin expression, light stimulation of dHP or i/vHP did not change prelimbic oscillatory activity.
source_span: In opsin-free animals , stimulation of dHP and i/vHP led to no significant changes in the oscillatory activity .
selection_reasoning: This fact controls for non-specific effects of light stimulation, supporting causal interpretation.

fact: Activation of Dlx5/6-positive interneurons in i/vHP reduced oscillatory power in both hippocampus and prelimbic cortex.
source_span: Blue light stimulation ( 473 nm ) confined to i/vHP of Dlx5/6–ChETA mice ( n = 19 ) led to a significant reduction of hippocampal power in all frequency bands ... Correspondingly , the oscillatory activity in PL diminished .
selection_reasoning: This finding identifies interneurons as modulators of hippocampal-prelimbic oscillatory coupling.

fact: Silencing of Dlx5/6-positive interneurons in i/vHP increased oscillatory activity in both hippocampus and prelimbic cortex.
source_span: Silencing of interneurons in Dlx5/6-ArchT mice ( n = 13 ) by yellow light ( 600 nm ) had an opposite effect and caused augmentation of oscillatory activity both within i/vHP ... and PL .
selection_reasoning: This complementary manipulation confirms the regulatory role of interneurons on hippocampal-prelimbic oscillations.

fact: Pyramidal neurons in CA1 of the hippocampus play a critical role in driving oscillatory entrainment of the prelimbic cortex.
source_span: Taken together , these data reveal the critical role of hippocampal activity for the oscillatory entrainment of PL and identify pyramidal neurons in CA1 .
selection_reasoning: This is the principal conclusion linking hippocampal pyramidal neuron activity to prelimbic oscillatory dynamics.

fact: The dorsal hippocampus (dHP) is mainly involved in spatial navigation due to its dense projections from the entorhinal cortex.
source_span: For example , the dHP , which receives dense projections from the entorhinal cortex ( Witter and Amaral , 2004 ) , is mainly involved in spatial navigation ( O'Keefe and Nadel , 1978; Moser et al . , 1995; Moser et al . , 1998 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the functional specialization of hippocampal subregions relevant to the study.

fact: The intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) receives strong cholinergic and dopaminergic innervation and contributes to processing non-spatial information.
source_span: In contrast , the ventral part receives strong cholinergic and dopaminergic innervation ( Witter et al . , 1989; Pitkänen et al . , 2000 ) and contributes to processing of non-spatial information ( Bannerman et al . , 2003; Bast et al . , 2009 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important context about the distinct roles of hippocampal subregions.

fact: Theta oscillation power is higher in the dorsal hippocampus than in the intermediate/ventral hippocampus in both adult and neonatal rodents.
source_span: Similar to findings from adult rodents , the power of theta bursts at neonatal age was higher in dHP than in i/vHP .
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights a key developmental and functional difference in hippocampal activity patterns.

fact: Sharp wave-ripples (SPWs and ripples) occur more frequently and with higher amplitude in the intermediate/ventral hippocampus than in the dorsal hippocampus in neonatal mice.
source_span: Quantification along the septo-temporal axis revealed that , similar to adults , the occurrence of SPWs was higher in the i/vHP and their amplitude was larger in the neonatal dHP ( Patel et al . , 2013 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes important electrophysiological differences along the hippocampal axis relevant to early development.

fact: The prelimbic cortex (PL) firing and oscillatory activity at neonatal age are timed by sharp wave-ripples originating in the hippocampus, especially from the intermediate/ventral hippocampus.
source_span: Already at neonatal age , the prelimbic firing and oscillatory entrainment is timed by SPWs-ripples . Of note , the degree of timing varies along the septo-temporal axis and is much higher for the i/vHP .
selection_reasoning: This fact links hippocampal activity to prefrontal cortex function early in development, central to the study's main question.

fact: Optogenetic silencing of interneurons in Dlx5/6-ArchT mice increases oscillatory activity in both the intermediate/ventral hippocampus and prelimbic cortex.
source_span: Silencing of interneurons in Dlx5/6-ArchT mice ( n = 13 ) by yellow light ( 600 nm ) had an opposite effect and caused augmentation of oscillatory activity both within i/vHP ( theta: p<0 . 001 , beta: p=0 . 0012 , gamma: p<0 . 001 ) and PL ( theta: p<0 . 001 , beta: p<0 . 001 , gamma: p<0 . 001 ) ( Figure 6A , C ) .
selection_reasoning: This experimental finding demonstrates the causal role of interneurons in modulating hippocampal-prefrontal oscillations.

fact: Pyramidal neurons in the CA1 area of the intermediate/ventral hippocampus, but not the dorsal hippocampus, drive broad activation of local prelimbic circuits.
source_span: Taken together , these data reveal the critical role of hippocampal activity for the oscillatory entrainment of PL and identify pyramidal neurons in CA1 area of of i/vHP but not dHP as drivers for the broad activation of local prelimbic circuits .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal mechanistic finding central to the study's conclusions.

fact: Prelimbic circuits are effectively entrained when pyramidal neurons in the intermediate/ventral hippocampus are stimulated at 8 Hz but not at 4 Hz or 16 Hz.
source_span: We observed that prelimbic circuits were effectively entrained when the stimulation of paramidal neurons in i/vHP occurred at 8 Hz but not at 4 Hz or 16 Hz .
selection_reasoning: This finding identifies a frequency-specific mechanism of hippocampal-prefrontal communication.

fact: The directionality of information flow between the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex at neonatal age suggests that hippocampal theta oscillations drive the oscillatory entrainment of local prefrontal circuits.
source_span: Moreover , the temporal delay of 10–20 ms between prefrontal and hippocampal spike trains as well as the estimated directionality of information flow between the two areas suggested that hippocampal theta drives the oscillatory entrainment of the local circuits in the PFC .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the main hypothesis about hippocampal influence on prefrontal activity early in development.

fact: Optogenetic manipulation of neuronal networks at neonatal age allows direct causal assessment of prefrontal-hippocampal coupling.
source_span: The present data directly prove this hypothesis , taking advantage of the recently developed protocol for optogenetic manipulation of neuronal networks at neonatal age ( Bitzenhofer et al . , 2017a , 2017b ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key methodological advance enabling the study's main conclusions.

fact: Hippocampal theta oscillations drive the oscillatory entrainment of local circuits in the prefrontal cortex (PFC).
source_span: Moreover , the temporal delay of 10–20 ms between prefrontal and hippocampal spike trains as well as the estimated directionality of information flow between the two areas suggested that hippocampal theta drives the oscillatory entrainment of the local circuits in the PFC .
selection_reasoning: This is a core mechanistic claim about the directionality and influence of hippocampal theta on PFC activity, central to the study's main hypothesis.

fact: Optogenetic manipulation of neonatal neuronal networks was used to directly test the hypothesis that hippocampal theta drives prefrontal oscillatory entrainment.
source_span: The present data directly prove this hypothesis , taking advantage of the recently developed protocol for optogenetic manipulation of neuronal networks at neonatal age ( Bitzenhofer et al . , 2017a , 2017b ) .
selection_reasoning: Describes the key method used to test the main scientific question.

fact: Prelimbic circuits in the PFC were effectively entrained when paramidal neurons in intermediate/ventral hippocampus (i/vHP) were stimulated at 8 Hz but not at 4 Hz or 16 Hz.
source_span: We observed that prelimbic circuits were effectively entrained when the stimulation of paramidal neurons in i/vHP occurred at 8 Hz but not at 4 Hz or 16 Hz .
