source_span: The loss of both connexins results in a phenotype that is as strong as the one seen in homozygous mutants for the dominant alleles of leo or luc.
selection_reasoning: This finding establishes the combined importance of both connexins in pigment pattern formation, a key result.

fact: The leo mutant phenotype varies from irregular, wavy stripes to complete loss of pigment pattern, depending on allele strength and combination.
source_span: The leo phenotype varies, depending on the strength and combination of different alleles, from irregular, wavy stripes that are occasionally interrupted, over rows of spots to a complete loss of the pigment pattern.
selection_reasoning: This describes the phenotypic spectrum caused by leo mutations, important for understanding the gene's functional impact.

fact: The dominant leotK3 allele produces a stronger phenotype than the leot1 null allele, suggesting a dominant negative effect of the mutant Cx41.8 protein.
source_span: The homozygous leotK3 phenotype is considerably stronger than this, indicating that the mutant Cx41.8 protein present in leotK3 cells has a dominant negative effect on some further component(s) involved in pigment pattern formation.
selection_reasoning: This insight into allele-specific effects informs the molecular mechanism underlying the phenotype.

fact: Cx39.4 is a fish-specific connexin closely related to mammalian Cx37, with unique structural features including an extended N-terminal cytoplasmic domain.
source_span: Cx39.4 is a fish specific connexin ... it shares 54% amino acid similarity with mammalian Cx37 ... Cx39.4 is the only α-Connexin where the N-terminal cytoplasmic domain of 23 amino acids is extended by two residues.
selection_reasoning: This provides important molecular characterization of luc/Cx39.4 relevant to understanding its function.

fact: The conductivity of gap junctions formed by Cx39.4 and Cx41.8 may be regulated by polyamines due to the presence of an ExxE motif in their N-terminal cytoplasmic domains.
source_span: As in the case of Cx41.8, the N-terminal cytoplasmic domain in Cx39.4 also contains an ExxE motif, therefore the conductivity of gap junctions formed by Cx39.4 could also be regulated by polyamines.
selection_reasoning: This suggests a potential regulatory mechanism for the connexins involved, relevant to their biological function.

fact: Neither Cx41.8 nor Cx39.4 contain sequence motifs that predict heteromeric compatibility, so their ability to form heteromeric gap junctions cannot be predicted from sequence alone.
source_span: Both, Cx41.8 and Cx39.4, have neither an R type nor a W type sequence motifs regulating heteromeric compatibility, so that no sequence based predictions about their ability to form heteromeric complexes are possible.
selection_reasoning: This highlights a limitation in predicting connexin interactions, relevant to understanding their molecular assembly.

fact: Mutant melanophores in chimeric animals are influenced by neighboring wild-type xanthophores, forming larger meandering patches rather than normal stripes.
source_span: Mutant melanophores, in chimeric animals, seem to be influenced by wild-type xanthophores in their neighbourhood, as they form continuous meandering patches larger than the spots found in leo or luc mutants.
selection_reasoning: This finding reveals cell-cell interaction effects important for pigment pattern formation.

fact: There is no contribution of non-pigment cells to the leo and luc mutant phenotypes in zebrafish pigment pattern formation.
source_span: The results of our transplantation experiments also show that there is no contribution of non-pigment cells to the leo and luc phenotypes.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies that the phenotype is due to pigment cell-autonomous effects, important for interpreting the genetic mechanism.

fact: The leo and luc genes are required in melanophores for the formation of a wild-type pigment pattern in zebrafish.
source_span: Unlike wild-type melanophores when transplanted into nac hosts (Maderspacher and Nusslein-Volhard, 2003), they do not form normal stripes, so clearly leo and luc are required in melanophores for the formation of a wild-type pattern.
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies the essential role of leo and luc genes in melanophores for normal pigment pattern formation, a core biological finding relevant to the study.

fact: Mutant xanthophores lacking leo or luc function fail to generate a wild-type pigment pattern when interacting with wild-type melanophores.
source_span: The function of both genes is also required in xanthophores; mutant xanthophores, when confronted with wild-type melanophores in the chimeras, do not generate a wild-type pattern but spot or disperse melanophores in large dense iridophore regions.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the importance of leo and luc genes in xanthophores for normal pigment patterning, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Iridophores do not require leo or luc gene function to contribute to a wild-type pigment pattern if adjacent to wild-type cells.
source_span: When we tested iridophores we found that they require neither leo nor luc function, as the mutant cells can contribute to a completely wild-type pattern if they are next to other wild-type cells.
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the cell-type specificity of leo and luc gene function, important for understanding pigment pattern formation.

fact: The expansion of dense iridophores in leo and luc mutants is an indirect effect likely caused by mutant xanthophores covering the iridophores.
source_span: This is surprising and indicates that the dramatic expansion of the dense iridophores that is associated with the mutant phenotypes is an indirect effect, possibly caused by mutant xanthophores covering the iridophores.
selection_reasoning: This explains a key phenotype mechanism in the mutants, relevant for interpreting mutant effects on pigment patterns.

fact: Cx41.8 and Cx39.4 proteins encoded by leo and luc interact to form heteromeric gap junction channels responsible for chromatophore interactions during pigment pattern formation.
source_span: Taken together our data suggest that Cx41.8 and Cx39.4 interact to form heteromeric gap junctions and that these channels are responsible for some of the interactions that take place among chromatophores while the pigment pattern is established.
selection_reasoning: This identifies the molecular mechanism underlying chromatophore communication, central to the study's main claim.

fact: In the absence of xanthophores, melanophores cluster together, but this clustering is lost when leo and luc function is also lost, indicating gap junction channels mediate homotypic melanophore interactions.
source_span: In the absence of xanthophores, in pfe mutants, melanophores cluster together; this clustering is lost in double mutants with leotK3, where leo and luc function are affected, indicating that the channels are responsible for homotypic interactions among melanophores.
selection_reasoning: This fact shows the functional role of gap junctions in melanophore behavior, a key finding about cell-cell interactions.

fact: Mutant xanthophores lacking leo or luc function cannot confine light stripe regions in the absence of melanophores, suggesting an instructive interaction between xanthophores and iridophores during normal development.
source_span: In the double mutants of leotK3 with nac, where melanophores are missing, mutant xanthophores are unable to confine the light stripe regions, suggesting an instructive interaction between xanthophores and iridophores during normal development.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the role of gap junctions in xanthophore-iridophore interactions, important for pigment pattern formation.

fact: In double mutants lacking iridophores and with leo or luc mutations, melanophore numbers are further reduced and xanthophores are evenly distributed, indicating a positive interaction between melanophores and xanthophores via gap junctions in wild-type fish.
source_span: In double mutants with shd or tra, where iridophores are lacking, the number of melanophores is further reduced and xanthophores are evenly distributed, indicating that in wild-type there might be a positive interaction between melanophores and xanthophores via gap junctions.
selection_reasoning: This fact reveals the interdependence of pigment cell types mediated by gap junctions, a key biological insight.

fact: Heteromeric gap junction channels formed by leo and luc connexins are more effective than homomeric channels, as loss-of-function mutants show weaker phenotypes than dominant-negative mutants blocking all channel activity.
source_span: The phenotypes of the double mutants with the leo or luc loss-of-function alleles are generally a bit weaker than with leotK3. This indicates that in the absence of one of the connexins, when heteromeric channels cannot form, homomeric channels retain some functionality.
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the functional importance of heteromeric versus homomeric gap junction channels in pigment patterning.

fact: The leo and luc mutant phenotypes are caused by iridophores failing to transition from a dense to a loose form at the correct time and place during pigment pattern development.
source_span: The leo and luc mutant phenotypes seem to be caused by iridophores not behaving appropriately and failing to undergo the transition from the dense to the loose form at the correct time and place.
selection_reasoning: This identifies a cellular mechanism underlying mutant pigment pattern defects, central to understanding the phenotype.

fact: During zebrafish metamorphosis, iridophore proliferation and dispersal outline light and dark stripe regions, while larval xanthophores proliferate and reorganize to cover light stripe regions densely and dark stripes loosely.
source_span: Recently it was shown that proliferation and dispersal of iridophores during metamorphosis, the time when the adult pigment pattern is generated, outline the light and dark stripe regions in the trunk of zebrafish (Singh et al., 2014); at the same time the larval xanthophores also start to proliferate, they re-organize and change their shapes to densely cover the light stripe regions and loosely the dark melanophore stripes (Mahalwar et al., 2014).
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the developmental dynamics of pigment cells relevant to the study's focus on pattern formation.

fact: Xanthophores covering iridophores may induce the transition of iridophores to a loose form in regions destined to form dark stripes during normal development.
source_span: This raises the possibility that in normal development the xanthophores, which cover the iridophores, induce the transition to the loose form when they reach the regions destined to form dark stripes.
selection_reasoning: This hypothesis links cell interactions to pigment pattern formation, a key conceptual advance.

fact: Gap junctions formed by leo and luc connexins mediate homotypic interactions among melanophores and xanthophores and may also be involved in heterotypic interactions between pigment cell types during zebrafish pigment pattern formation.
source_span: Our data suggest that Cx41.8 and Cx39.4 interact to form heteromeric gap junctions and that these channels are responsible for some of the interactions that take place among chromatophores while the pigment pattern is established.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main mechanistic conclusion about gap junction roles in pigment patterning.

fact: In luc mutants, fins retain striped patterns, suggesting that homomeric leo channels are sufficient for fin pigment patterning where iridophores are absent.
source_span: Interestingly, in luc mutants the fins are striped, suggesting that homomeric leo channels suffice for patterning the fins, where stripes can be formed in the absence of iridophores.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides insight into tissue-specific roles of connexins and pigment pattern formation.

fact: The global malaria burden has decreased over the last decade, and many nations are attempting malaria elimination.
source_span: The global malaria burden has decreased over the last decade and many nations are attempting elimination .
selection_reasoning: This provides essential background on the current status and motivation for malaria elimination efforts.

fact: Asymptomatic malaria infections are not normally diagnosed or treated, posing a major hurdle for malaria elimination efforts.
source_span: Asymptomatic malaria infections are not normally diagnosed or treated , posing a major hurdle for elimination efforts .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key challenge that motivates the study and the use of mass drug administration.

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) involves providing medications to entire target populations and has been used for several infectious diseases including malaria.
source_span: Mass drug administration ( MDA ) is the provision of medications to entire target populations and the approach has been used for many infectious diseases , including lymphatic filariasis , soil-transmitted helminths , onchocerciasis , schistosomiasis , and trachoma ... MDA has historically been used for P . falciparum malaria ...
selection_reasoning: This defines MDA and situates it as a relevant intervention for malaria elimination.

fact: MDA is being considered by several nations as a tool to be used alongside other interventions for malaria elimination.
source_span: It is being considered by several nations as a tool ( to be used in unison with other interventions ) for elimination ...
selection_reasoning: This explains the current policy relevance and rationale for studying MDA.

fact: There has been hesitance to use MDA for malaria due to concerns that drug pressure may promote parasite resistance.
source_span: Given that drug pressure ( through provision of antimalarial drugs ) provides a survival advantage for resistant parasites , there has been some hesitance in using MDA for malaria .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key limitation and concern motivating careful evaluation of MDA.

fact: MDA should ideally be used in settings with strong public health infrastructure, including easy access to diagnosis and treatment, responsive surveillance, and effective community engagement.
source_span: MDA should ideally be used in settings with strong public health infrastructure , including easy access to diagnosis and treatment; an up-to-date and responsive surveillance system; and effective community engagement .
selection_reasoning: This contextualizes the conditions under which MDA is expected to be effective.

fact: Used appropriately, MDA can quickly reduce or eliminate parasite reservoirs and act as a catalyst for subregional elimination of P. falciparum malaria.
source_span: Used appropriately , MDA can quickly reduce or eliminate parasite reservoirs and can act as a catalyst for subregional elimination of P . falciparum malaria .
selection_reasoning: This states the principal intended effect and significance of MDA.

fact: The rationale for MDA is to remove a sufficient amount of the parasite reservoir to disrupt malaria transmission through a population-level 'herd effect'.
source_span: The rationale is that the transmission potential or reproductive rate of malaria is so high that a sufficient amount of the parasite reservoir needs to be removed in order to disrupt transmission . This group-level effect is also referred to as a ‘herd effect’ ...
selection_reasoning: This explains the key mechanism underlying MDA's population-level impact.

fact: If a sufficient proportion of the population participates in MDA, malaria transmission chains cannot be sustained, leading to reduced morbidity and mortality.
source_span: If a sufficient amount of the population participates in MDA , transmission chains cannot be sustained and transmission will cease , ultimately leading to a reduction in malaria morbidity and mortality .
selection_reasoning: This describes the expected outcome of successful MDA at the population level.

fact: There is likely a context-specific critical threshold for MDA coverage, with some literature suggesting at least 80% coverage and adherence is necessary for success.
source_span: There is likely to be a context-specific critical threshold for MDA coverage , below which the reduction of the parasite reservoir is not sufficient to halt ongoing transmission . Some literature has suggested that at least 80% coverage and adherence of MDA in the targeted population is necessary in order for the MDA to be successful .
selection_reasoning: This highlights an important operational consideration for MDA effectiveness.

fact: The concept of a herd effect providing additional population protection from malaria through MDA is plausible but had not been empirically examined prior to this study.
source_span: If the aim for antimalarial MDA is to interrupt transmission , the notion of a herd effect providing additional levels of population protection is plausible but has not been examined empirically .
selection_reasoning: This states the main research gap addressed by the study.

fact: This study presents a detailed spatial and temporal analysis of malaria episodes and asymptomatic infections in four villages undergoing MDA in Myanmar.
source_span: Here , we present a detailed spatial and temporal analysis of malaria episodes and asymptomatic infections in four villages undergoing MDA in Myanmar .
selection_reasoning: This describes the main study design and setting.

fact: Individuals from neighborhoods with low MDA adherence had 2.85 times the odds of having a malaria episode post-MDA compared to those from high adherence neighborhoods, regardless of individual participation, suggesting a herd effect.
source_span: In this study , individuals from neighborhoods with low MDA adherence had 2 . 85 times the odds of having a malaria episode post-MDA in comparison to those from high adherence neighborhoods , regardless of individual participation , suggesting a herd effect .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal empirical finding demonstrating indirect protection from MDA.

fact: High mosquito biting rates, living in a house with someone else with malaria, or having an asymptomatic malaria infection were predictors of clinical malaria episodes.
source_span: High mosquito biting rates , living in a house with someone else with malaria , or having an asymptomatic malaria infection were also predictors of clinical episodes .
selection_reasoning: This identifies key risk factors relevant to malaria transmission and clinical disease.

fact: Spatial clustering of non-adherence to MDA, even in villages with high overall participation, may frustrate malaria elimination efforts.
source_span: Spatial clustering of non-adherence to MDA , even in villages with high overall participation , may frustrate elimination efforts .
selection_reasoning: This finding has important implications for MDA implementation and effectiveness.

fact: uPCR-detected P. falciparum infections were widespread in all villages at baseline and were significantly reduced following MDA.
source_span: uPCR-detected P . falciparum infections were widespread in all villages at baseline ... These infections were significantly reduced following MDA in all villages .
selection_reasoning: This documents the impact of MDA on parasite prevalence.

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) for Plasmodium falciparum malaria showed evidence of a herd protection effect at the community level.
source_span: The primary objective of this research was to look for a potential herd effect and at the impact of non-adherence with regard to MDA for P. falciparum malaria. There was an apparent group level effect from MDA adherence, suggesting herd protection and evident from three lines of evidence.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding and significance claim central to the study's main question and conclusions.

fact: Clinical episodes of P. falciparum malaria decreased among all groups for a longer period than the prophylactic effect of the administered antimalarials, indicating a group-level protective effect from MDA.
source_span: First, clinical episodes decreased among all groups for a longer period than the prophylactic effect (approximately 1 month) of the administered antimalarials. This group level protective effect from MDA was also evident in the rainy season following MDA.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the evidence for herd protection and is a key finding about the duration and impact of MDA.

fact: Neighborhoods with high MDA adherence experienced lower levels of P. falciparum infection compared to neighborhoods with mid or low MDA adherence.
source_span: Second, neighborhoods with high MDA adherence never experienced the same levels of infection as those with mid or low MDA adherence.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the spatial relationship between adherence and infection risk, a core finding relevant to the study's conclusions.

fact: Individuals who participated in MDA but lived in neighborhoods with low adherence had the highest risk of clinical P. falciparum episodes, while those who did not participate but lived in high adherence neighborhoods had the lowest risk.
source_span: Individuals who participated in MDA but lived in a neighborhood with low adherence had the highest risk of having a clinical episode whereas those who did not participate in MDA but lived in a neighborhood with high adherence had the lowest risk of having a clinical P. falciparum episode.
selection_reasoning: This fact illustrates the interaction between individual and neighborhood adherence, a key mechanism underlying herd protection.

fact: Living in a neighborhood with a high proportion of people who did not adhere to MDA was a significant risk factor for acquiring a clinical P. falciparum episode, independent of individual MDA adherence.
source_span: The results from the multivariable logistic regression also suggest that living in a neighborhood with a high proportion of people who did not adhere to MDA was a significant risk factor for acquiring a clinical P. falciparum episode, after adjusting for individual MDA adherence and other important predictors of having a clinical episode.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides statistical evidence for the importance of community-level adherence, supporting the herd effect claim.

fact: The increase in clinical P. falciparum episodes after MDA coincided with an increase in the human biting rate (HBR) of malaria vectors in the village.
source_span: The increase in clinical P. falciparum episodes post-MDA also corresponded to an increase in village HBR.
selection_reasoning: This fact links vector activity to malaria incidence, important for understanding transmission dynamics post-MDA.

fact: Clinical P. falciparum episodes after MDA were most likely to occur among children aged 5 to 14 years and among individuals living in a house with another person who had a clinical episode during the same month.
source_span: After MDA, clinical P. falciparum episodes in village TOT were most likely to occur among 5 to 14 year olds (AOR: 3.41; CI: 1.33–8.77, compared to 0 to 4 year olds) and participants who lived in a house with someone else who had a clinical P. falciparum episode during the same month (AOR: 3.43; CI: 1.52–7.72), after adjusting for other covariates.
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies demographic and household risk factors relevant to malaria transmission and clinical episodes.

fact: Clusters of non-participation in MDA were identified in three study villages, with the largest cluster in village TOT including 115 individuals.
source_span: There were significant clusters of non-participation in the MDAs in three of the study villages (TPN, HKT and TOT). The non-participation cluster in TOT made up a large portion of the western part of the village and included 115 individuals not participating in the MDA (out of 919 total individuals in TOT).
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on adherence patterns critical to interpreting the study's findings on MDA effectiveness and herd protection.

fact: Sporadic clinical P. falciparum episodes occurred in village TOT following MDA completion, followed by a small outbreak beginning approximately 12 months after MDA.
source_span: Sporadic clinical P. falciparum episodes occurred in village TOT following MDA (MDA was completed by M3), followed by a small outbreak beginning in M12.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the temporal pattern of malaria cases post-MDA, important for understanding the study timeline and outcomes.

fact: The combination of a persisting parasite reservoir and persistently high human biting rate likely explains the different malaria elimination outcomes between study villages.
source_span: The combination of a persisting parasite reservoir and persistently high HBR (from M13 – M18) in TOT likely explains the drastically different results between the study villages with regard to P. falciparum malaria elimination.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a key explanation for variation in intervention success, relevant to the study's significance.

fact: Community-based early diagnosis and treatment combined with MDA with high participation, targeted at the village scale or larger, appear effective at reducing prevalence, incidence, and transmission of P. falciparum.
source_span: Conversely, community based early diagnosis and treatment and MDA with high participation, targeted at the village scale or larger, appear effective at reducing prevalence, incidence, and transmission of P. falciparum.
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the practical implications and significance of the study's findings for malaria control strategies.

fact: Community-based early diagnosis and treatment combined with mass drug administration (MDA) with high participation at the village or larger scale effectively reduces prevalence, incidence, and transmission of Plasmodium falciparum.
source_span: Conversely, community based early diagnosis and treatment and MDA with high participation, targeted at the village scale or larger, appear effective at reducing prevalence, incidence, and transmission of P. falciparum (Landier et al., 2018b).
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding about the effectiveness of combined interventions central to the study's significance.

fact: Reactive case detection identifies additional clinical and uPCR-detected P. falciparum infections within houses and neighboring houses but only captures a small proportion of all infections and does not halt transmission.
source_span: Reactive case detection would have resulted in the detection of extra cases (of both clinical and uPCR-detected P. falciparum) when searching within houses and occasionally in neighboring houses, but these would have only been a small proportion of all infections within the villages (Parker et al., 2016) and would not have halted transmission.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains limitations of reactive case detection, motivating the study's focus on MDA and early diagnosis.

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) was conducted in four villages along the Myanmar-Thailand border, with two villages receiving early MDA and two receiving deferred MDA, to evaluate its impact on P. falciparum malaria.
source_span: The study site consisted of four villages (KNH, TPN, HKT, and TOT) along the Myanmar-Thailand border, in Kayin (Karen) State, Myanmar (Landier et al., 2017b)... MDAs were conducted in two villages at the beginning of the study (month 0, M0) and extended to the two control villages beginning in month 9 (M9).
selection_reasoning: This high-level description of the study design and setting is essential to understand the intervention and context.

fact: Ultrasensitive quantitative PCR (uPCR) was used to detect P. falciparum infections, most of which (86%) were subclinical, in the study villages.
source_span: Venous blood (3 mL) was drawn from each participant... and analyzed using a highly sensitive quantitative PCR (uPCR) assay with a limit of detection of 22 parasites per mL... Most (86%) uPCR-detected infections were subclinical (Landier et al., 2017a).
selection_reasoning: This method and finding are key to understanding how infections were detected and the prevalence of subclinical infections.

fact: A community-based malaria clinic (malaria post) was established in each village to diagnose malaria using rapid diagnostic tests and treat clinical infections with standard antimalarial drugs.
source_span: A community-based malaria clinic (referred to as a malaria post or MP) was established in each village at the beginning of the project... Village health workers were trained to diagnose malaria using rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) and to treat RDT positive infections with dose based on weight and age.
selection_reasoning: This describes a key intervention component relevant to early diagnosis and treatment.

fact: Clinical P. falciparum episodes persisted after MDA in one village (TOT) despite similar overall MDA adherence compared to another village (HKT) where elimination was successful.
source_span: In this study, the elimination efforts were successful in three out of four villages even though one of those villages (HKT) had a similar overall adherence to the village with P. falciparum remaining after MDA (TOT).
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights the complexity of MDA effectiveness and the importance of factors beyond overall adherence.

fact: Non-participation in MDA was associated with underdiagnosis of uPCR-detected infections and likely contributed to clusters of infections and resurgence of clinical episodes in the village TOT.
source_span: Individuals who did not participate in MDA also did not participate in blood screenings immediately after MDA (i.e. M3 in village TOT). uPCR-detected infections are therefore likely to be underdiagnosed for these individuals, and it is likely that such infections clustered and overlapped with the clusters of non-adherence to MDA... it is likely that these underdiagnosed infections, combined with the high HBR, led to a resurgence of clinical episodes.
selection_reasoning: This explains a key mechanism for persistence of infections and transmission despite MDA.

fact: Some P. falciparum infections are likely acquired outside the village, leading to complex spatial patterns of infection at the household level.
source_span: Some infections are likely to be acquired outside of the village, leading to complex spatial patterns in infections that are mapped at the house level.
selection_reasoning: This background fact is important for interpreting spatial clustering and transmission dynamics.

fact: Within-household clustering of P. falciparum infections may result from either transmission within the household or shared exposure outside the household among household members.
source_span: Within-household clustering can be the result of within-household transmission, or shared exposure outside of the household or village among household members.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies possible transmission mechanisms relevant to interpreting infection patterns.

fact: The study suggests that targeting MDA at spatial scales larger than a single village may be necessary when high prevalence villages are clustered across a landscape.
source_span: Most current MDA trials and programs in the GMS and elsewhere consider a single village or community as the target unit. In some cases, especially when high prevalence villages are spatially clustered across a landscape, it may be necessary to target units above the village level (i.e. groups of villages).
selection_reasoning: This implication is important for future MDA program design and policy.

fact: Radical cure for P. vivax was not provided in the study due to the absence of G6PD testing required to prevent hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals.
source_span: Radical cure for P. vivax was not provided because the absence of G6PD (Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) tests required to prevent hemolysis in G6PD individuals (Bancone et al., 2014; Chu et al., 2017).
selection_reasoning: This clinical limitation affects treatment and is relevant to understanding intervention scope.

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) was conducted with 3 days of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHA+P) plus a single low dose of primaquine on the third day, repeated over three months.
source_span: MDA consisted of 3 days of DHA + P , with a single low dose of primaquine on the third day , repeated over three months ( M0 , M1 , M2 for the first group and M9 , M10 , M11 for the control group ) .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key intervention used in the study, which is central to understanding the research design and findings.

fact: Follow-up blood surveys were conducted every three months after the initial MDA until month 18, with a final full blood survey at month 24.
source_span: Follow-up blood surveys were conducted in each village every third month after M0 until M18 . A final full blood survey was completed in each village at M24 .
selection_reasoning: This outlines the main method for monitoring the impact of the intervention over time, which is important for interpreting results.

fact: Mosquitoes were collected monthly using human landing catches at multiple indoor and outdoor sites in four study villages to estimate the human biting rate.
source_span: Mosquitoes were collected monthly using human landing catches to estimate the human biting rate ( HBR ) . Mosquito catching teams were based at five sites ( both indoors and outdoors ) within each of the four study villages ( total of 20 catch sites ) for five consecutive nights during the study period M0 through M20 .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key entomological method used to measure mosquito exposure, which is relevant to understanding transmission dynamics.

fact: The developing heart and lung engage in extensive crosstalk that is critical for their proper morphogenesis and maturation during embryogenesis.
source_span: The extensive crosstalk between the developing heart and lung is critical to their proper morphogenesis and maturation.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological importance of heart-lung interaction, motivating the study.

fact: There is a lack of models that investigate the critical cardio-pulmonary mutual interaction during human embryogenesis.
source_span: However , there remains a lack of models that investigate the critical cardio-pulmonary mutual interaction during human embryogenesis.
selection_reasoning: This identifies the knowledge gap and motivates the development of a new model.

fact: The authors developed a novel stepwise strategy to simultaneously induce both mesoderm-derived cardiac and endoderm-derived lung epithelial lineages from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) by temporally tuning WNT and nodal signaling without exogenous growth factors.
source_span: Here , we reported a novel stepwise strategy for directing the simultaneous induction of both mesoderm-derived cardiac and endoderm-derived lung epithelial lineages within a single differentiation of human-induced pluripotent stem cells ( hiPSCs ) via temporal specific tuning of WNT and nodal signaling in the absence of exogenous growth factors.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key methodological advance enabling co-differentiation of cardiac and pulmonary lineages.

fact: Using 3D suspension culture, the authors established concentric cardio-pulmonary micro-tissues (μTs) that include both cardiac and pulmonary components.
source_span: Using 3D suspension culture , we established concentric cardio-pulmonary micro-Tissues ( μTs ) , and expedited alveolar maturation in the presence of cardiac accompaniment.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the creation of a 3D model system that mimics heart-lung tissue organization.

fact: The presence of cardiac lineage cells within the micro-tissues promotes effective alveolar maturation of lung epithelial cells.
source_span: Using 3D suspension culture , we established concentric cardio-pulmonary micro-Tissues ( μTs ) , and expedited alveolar maturation in the presence of cardiac accompaniment.
selection_reasoning: This finding shows functional crosstalk and significance of co-culture for lung maturation.

fact: Withdrawal of the WNT agonist causes the cardiac and pulmonary components within each dual-lineage micro-tissue to segregate and initiates cardiac contraction.
source_span: Upon withdrawal of WNT agonist , the cardiac and pulmonary components within each dual-lineage μT effectively segregated from each other with concurrent initiation of cardiac contraction.
selection_reasoning: This describes a key dynamic developmental event modeled in vitro, relevant to tissue boundary formation.

fact: The multilineage differentiation model offers an experimentally tractable system for investigating human cardio-pulmonary interaction and tissue boundary formation during embryogenesis.
source_span: We expect that our multilineage differentiation model will offer an experimentally tractable system for investigating human cardio-pulmonary interaction and tissue boundary formation during embryogenesis.
selection_reasoning: This states the significance and potential applications of the model.

fact: During mouse embryonic development, WNT signaling from the second heart field induces pulmonary endoderm specification, which then signals back to the heart via SHH to regulate atrial septation.
source_span: During mouse embryonic development , WNT derived from the second heart field induces specification of pulmonary endoderm , which in turn secretes SHH that signals back to the heart and regulates proper atrial septation.
selection_reasoning: This background mechanistic fact supports the biological rationale for studying heart-lung crosstalk.

fact: Multipotent mesodermal progenitors located between the developing heart and lung contribute to pulmonary endothelium, pulmonary smooth muscle, and cardiomyocytes.
source_span: This inter-lineage crosstalk is partly mediated by the multipotent mesodermal progenitors located between the developing heart and lung , which have the potential for lineage contribution to pulmonary endothelium , pulmonary smooth muscle and cardiomyocytes.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides biological context for the cellular interactions involved in cardio-pulmonary development.

fact: Existing hiPSC differentiation protocols typically focus on generating either cardiomyocytes or pulmonary epithelium separately, often using stepwise strategies that mimic developmental signaling.
source_span: Much work has been done for directed differentiation of hiPSCs into either cardiomyocytes ... or pulmonary epithelium ... both of which often utilize stepwise differentiation strategies that recapitulate key developmental signaling events.

fact: bZIP transcription factors form dimers that bind DNA and regulate diverse cellular processes including metabolism and stress response.
source_span: bZIP proteins form a large and highly conserved group of eukaryotic TFs . They bind the DNA as dimers and are characterized by a basic region for specific DNA binding and a leucine zipper for dimerization ( Deppmann et al . , 2006; Reinke et al . , 2013 ) . They are involved in a multitude of cellular processes , including cell proliferation and differentiation , metabolism , stress response , and apoptosis ( Mayr and Montminy , 2001; Jakoby et al . , 2002; Motohashi et al . , 2002; Rodrigues-Pousada et al . , 2010; Tsukada et al . , 2011 ) .

fact: Phosphorylation can regulate bZIP transcription factors by affecting their activity, DNA binding, localization, stability, and interactions, but regulation of their dimerization is rarely reported.

Since the initial discovery that the mammalian bZIP cAMP response element binding protein ( CREB ) is regulated by reversible phosphorylation , many bZIP TFs were reported to be phosphorylated ( Holmberg et al . , 2002; Schuetze et al . , 2008; Tsukada et al . , 2011 ) . However , particularly in plants , the functional consequences of these phosphorylation events often remained unclear . ... It is also surprising that , while many examples for phosphorylation-dependent regulation of bZIP activity , DNA-binding , subcellular localization , stability , and interaction with regulatory proteins are known ( Schuetze et al . , 2008; Tsukada et al . , 2011 ) , reports on the regulation of dimerization are scarce .

fact: If biological diversity primarily reflects predictable adaptation, biology aims to explain how traits improve fitness; if it reflects chance sampling, biology focuses on invariant system characteristics; if it reflects contingency, biology must characterize historical constraints and opportunities.
source_span: For example , if diversity primarily reflects a predictable process of adaptation to distinct environments , then a central goal of biology would be to explain how the characteristics of living things help to execute particular functions and improve fitness ... By contrast , if diversity reflects chance sampling from a set of similarly fit possibilities , then the variation itself is of little interest because it does not affect biological properties or shape future evolutionary outcomes ... Finally , if diversity reflects contingency – a strong dependence of future outcomes on initial conditions or subsequent events , also known as path-dependence – then the outcomes of evolution would be predictable only given complete knowledge of the constraints and opportunities specific to each set of conditions ... the goal of biology would then be to characterize these constraints and opportunities , their mechanistic causes , and the historical events that shaped them .

fact: Kif2a regulates meiotic spindle size in Xenopus egg extracts by modulating microtubule dynamics.

fact: A physiological mechanism controlling spindle size was identified that maintains spindle orientation in very large cells of the early Xenopus laevis embryo.

fact: Larger spindles may resist rotation due to nonlinear frictional resistance in the viscous cytoplasm, helping maintain spindle orientation during metaphase.

fact: The embryo extract system combined with biochemical validation and experimental manipulation in developing embryos enables identification of molecular mechanisms controlling spindle architecture and cell division.

fact: Polyadenylation sites in RNA were identified by clustering 3′-end RNA-seq reads based on their polyA positions and applying a peak-finding algorithm to resolve closely spaced sites.
source_span: Most tag clusters spanned less than 24 bp , but if the polyA positions in a cluster spanned more than 40 bp , we applied a peak-finding algorithm as follows . For each genome coordinate in the region corresponding to the tag cluster , we defined the read count as the number of reads whose polyA position overlapped the coordinate . From these we first identified the genome coordinate ( posM ) with the greatest read count ( MaxHeight ) . We then delineated a window 40 bp upstream and 40 bp downstream of this coordinate . Within this window , we retained all coordinates with read counts greater than 10% of MaxHeight . Of these , we identified the most 5′ and 3′ polyA positions ( posL and posR ) . All reads in the tag cluster were then divided into three new candidate tag clusters: reads with positions 5′ to posL , reads with positions including and between posL and posR , and reads with positions 3′ to posR .

fact: Reads likely originating from internal priming at A-rich genomic regions were filtered out to improve the accuracy of polyadenylation site identification.

selection_reasoning: Filtering internal priming artifacts is important to ensure that identified polyadenylation sites reflect true biological 3′ ends.

fact: Tag clusters were further filtered to exclude those likely resulting from PCR duplicates or false mapping by comparing the precision of polyA positions to the precision of the other read ends.
source_span: We expected that for a given set of paired-end reads falling into a tag cluster , the characteristics of read ends originating from biological 3′-end processing should be distinct from the characteristics of read ends originating from fragmentation , reverse transcription , and ligation during RNA-seq library preparation . In particular , we reasoned that the polyA positions of a set of reads in a tag cluster with origin as a biologically relevant transcript would be less heterogeneous than the positions of the other mates of the reads . If the opposite were true , we considered the tag cluster to be a likely product of false mapping or PCR duplication . As such , we retained a tag cluster for analysis only if the precision of polyA positions across the reads of the unit was greater than the precision of the positions of the other mates .
selection_reasoning: This filtering step ensures that the data analyzed represent genuine biological signals rather than technical artifacts.

fact: Tag clusters with fewer than 50 total reads or poor reproducibility between biological replicates were excluded to ensure data reliability.
source_span: We also filtered out any tag cluster whose total read count across all samples amounted to fewer than 50 reads . For tag clusters with read counts between 50 and 100 , we calculated the Pearson correlation coefficient R between each pair of the two biological replicates across the six cell line samples , and eliminated the tag cluster from further analysis if the absolute value of R was less than 0 . 5 .
selection_reasoning: This quality control step is critical to maintain confidence in the identified polyadenylation sites.

source_span: For every tag cluster , the consensus sequence of the region 40 bp upstream from the polyA position was searched for a polyadenylation signal using the known hexamer motifs sorted by their abundance in the human genome from [30] . Polyadenylation signals with higher abundance were given higher priority when there was more than one instance in the 40 bp upstream window . In the absence of a match to these motifs , the 40 bp upstream window was searched for an A-rich stretch as follows .

The following antibodies were used to further characterize the OT-I response: APC-conjugated anti-CD44 and anti-KLRG1 , PE-Cy5-conjugated anti-CD62L , and PE-conjugated anti-CD127 ( all obtained from eBioscience ) . For intracellular staining , splenocytes were stimulated with the SIINFEKL peptide for 4 hours in the presence of Brefeldin A and recombinant IL-2 , and then stained with FITC-conjugated anti-CD45 . 1 and Pacific Blue-conjugated anti-CD8 . After fixation , cells were permeabilized and stained with PE-conjugated anti-granzyme B ( Invitrogen ) , PE-conjugated anti-Eomes and anti-IL-2 ( BD Biosciences ) . APC-conjugated anti-INFγ and PE-Cy7-conjugated anti-TNF were also used .
selection_reasoning: This fact details the immune phenotyping approach to characterize T cell activation and function, central to understanding the immune response.

fact: CD11c+ dendritic cells were isolated from spleens and analyzed for gene expression of HIF-1α, IL-10, IL-12p35, IL-12p40, IL-6, and TNF by real-time PCR.
source_span: Real-time PCR ( Stratagene mx3005p Real time PCR System ) was used to analyze transcripts levels of HPRT , HIF-1α , IL-10 , IL-12p35 , IL-12p40 , IL-6 , and TNF [19 , 54 , 88 , 89] . Total RNA was insolated using RNeasy ( Qiagen ) to perform real-time RT-PCR .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the molecular analysis of dendritic cell inflammatory and hypoxia-related gene expression, relevant to the study's mechanistic insights.

fact: Protein levels of HIF-1α in CD11c+ cells from infected and naïve mice were assessed by immunoblotting and normalized to β-actin.
source_span: Monoclonal anti-HIF-1α antibody Hif-1α67 ( Novus Biologicals , Littleton , CO , USA ) was used for immunoblot assays . Blots were stripped and reprobed with a polyclonal antibody against β-actin to confirm equal protein loading .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the investigation of HIF-1α protein regulation in dendritic cells during infection, a key mechanistic point.

fact: Bone marrow-derived dendritic cells were infected in vitro with PKH26-stained Leishmania donovani amastigotes to evaluate parasite survival and infection rate over time.
source_span: BMDC were generated as previously described [91] and seeded at 106 cells/ml onto 24-well plates . Cells were subsequently infected with PKH26-stained L . donovani amastigotes ( Sigma , staining done according to manufacturer’s instructions ) at a MOI of 5:1 . Infected cells were then harvested 24 , 48 , and 72 h later , fixed with 2% PFA , stained with Hoechst ( Invitrogen , staining done according to manufacturer’s instructions ) and cytospined on PBS/ 1% BSA-prepared slides . Mounted slides were than analyzed using a fluorescent microscope , to evaluate parasite survival and target infection rate .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key in vitro model to study dendritic cell infection dynamics, relevant to understanding host-pathogen interactions.

fact: Hif1αflox/flox Cd11c-Cre+ and Cre- mice were treated with anti-CD8 antibody to deplete CD8+ T cells before infection, and parasite burdens were measured at day 14 post-infection.
source_span: Hifflox/flox- Cd11c cre+ and cre- mice were treated bi-weekly with 0 . 2 mg of anti-CD8 antibody ( clone 2 . 43 ) , starting one day before infection . At day 14 p . i . , mice were sacrificed and parasite burdens were determined by limiting dilutions .
selection_reasoning: This fact relates to the functional role of CD8+ T cells in controlling infection, a key translational and mechanistic aspect.

fact: The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum is exposed to multiple selection pressures within the human host, and the host environment changes dramatically in severe malaria.
source_span: Within the human host , the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum is exposed to multiple selection pressures . The host environment changes dramatically in severe malaria , but the extent to which the parasite responds to—or is selected by—this environment remains unclear .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological context and motivation for studying parasite responses in severe malaria.

fact: Plasmodium falciparum is the leading cause of fatal malaria, responsible for over 400,000 deaths annually, primarily in sub-Saharan Africa.

source_span: Severe malaria due to P . falciparum can manifest as multiple , diverse clinical syndromes [2] , but a critical common feature is the sequestration of erythrocytes infected with mature parasites in the microvasculature ( reviewed in [3] ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key pathological mechanism relevant to severe malaria.

fact: Comparative genome-wide analyses of parasite isolates causing severe and uncomplicated malaria can identify genes associated with parasite virulence and pathology, informing therapy and vaccine design.
source_span: Comparative genome-wide analyses of parasite isolates that cause severe and uncomplicated malaria can be used to identify genes associated with parasite virulence and pathology . This knowledge could inform therapy and the design of vaccines targeting severe disease .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the rationale and significance of the comparative transcriptomic approach.

fact: Previous microarray studies showed no differences between parasites causing severe and uncomplicated malaria, but transcriptomic differences indicative of fundamental metabolic variations have been reported.

fact: The current study found a unique parasite transcriptional profile associated with severe malaria, involving deregulation of genes in central carbon metabolism, folate biosynthesis, histone methylation, chaperone function, and PfEMP1 surface expression.
source_span: We found a unique parasite transcriptional profile that was associated with severe malaria . While elements of this profile were congruent with reported profiles of clinical isolates [6 , 8] , these have not been previously linked with severe malaria phenotype . fact: PfEMP1 is the immunodominant variant surface antigen of Plasmodium falciparum, expressed on infected erythrocytes where it mediates adhesion to diverse host receptors.
source_span: PfEMP1 is the immunodominant , variant surface antigen of P . falciparum [9] . PfEMP1 is expressed on the surface of the infected erythrocyte ( IE ) , where it mediates adhesion to diverse host receptors .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines PfEMP1 and its role in parasite-host interactions.

fact: PfEMP1 binding to endothelial receptors leads to sequestration of infected erythrocytes in the microvasculature, contributing to malaria pathogenesis.
source_span: PfEMP1 binding to receptors on endothelium leads to the pathogenic sequestration of IEs in the microvasculature ( reviewed in [10] ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key pathogenic mechanism mediated by PfEMP1.

fact: PfEMP1 proteins are encoded by approximately 60 var gene copies per parasite genome, which show extreme diversity driven by immune pressure.
source_span: A parasite’s genome contains approximately 60 var gene copies that code for PfEMP1 [12] , and immune pressure has driven evolution of extreme diversity in PfEMP1s such that there is very little overlap in var repertoires [13–16] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides genetic background on PfEMP1 diversity relevant to immune evasion.

fact: Var genes can be classified into three broad groups (A, B, and C) based on upstream sequences, with group A var genes diverging in binding properties and being associated with severe malaria.
source_span: Even with such large sequence diversity , var genes can be classified into three broad groups based on their upstream sequence ( UPS; A , B , and C ) [12 , 17] . Group A var genes appear to have diverged from groups B and C in their binding properties [18] . Expression of group A and B var genes has been associated with clinical malaria in Papua New Guinea [19 , 20] , severe malaria in Africa [21] , and cerebral malaria in Africa [22–24] .
selection_reasoning: This fact links var gene classification to disease severity and geographic relevance.

selection_reasoning: This fact highlights molecular markers of severe malaria useful for vaccine target identification.

source_span: DBLβ5 from group B var genes and specific motifs in DBLβ1 and DBLβ3 from group A var genes bind intercellular adhesion molecule 1 ( ICAM1 ) [38–42] , and cerebral malaria has been associated with ICAM1 binding [43 , 44] and expression of group A carrying tandem CIDRα1-DBLβ1/3 domains [42].

source_span: DBLβ12 binds the host receptor gC1qR , and its expression is also associated with severe malaria [45].

source_span: Elevated expression of a number of DCs has also been associated with severe malaria; these included DC8 ( DBLα2-CIDRα1 . 1-DBLβ12-DBLγ4/6 ) [34 , 45–49] , DC13 ( DBLα1 . 7-CIDRα1 . 4 ) [32 , 49] , DC4 ( DBLα1 . 4-CIDRα1 . 6-DBLβ3 ) [39] , DC5 ( DBLγ12-DBLδ5-CIDRβ3/4 ) [48] , and DC6 ( DBLγ14-DBLζ5-DBLe4 ) [34].

source_span: The parasite biomass marker Histidine Rich Protein 2 ( HRP2 ) was present at higher concentrations in the plasma of patients with severe malaria than those with uncomplicated malaria ( p = 0 . 02 ).
selection_reasoning: This supports the clinical distinction between severe and uncomplicated malaria in the study cohort.

fact: None of the patients had severe malarial anaemia, suggesting that severe malaria in this cohort was associated with parasite sequestration rather than anaemia from repeated infections.
source_span: None of the patients had severe malarial anaemia ( defined as Hb < 5 g/dL in children <12 years old; Hb < 7 g/dL in adults; Table 1 ) [2] . These findings suggest that severe P . falciparum malaria in these patients was associated with sequestration rather than anaemia due to repeat infections [52].
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the pathological basis of severe malaria in the studied patients.

fact: A de novo assembly pipeline for var genes from RNAseq data was developed and validated using a P. falciparum ItG clone with a known var repertoire.
source_span: A pipeline for the de novo assembly of var genes from RNAseq data was developed and verified using a P . falciparum ItG clone ( ItG is the parent line of the It4 sequenced clone ) for which the var repertoire is known.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key methodological innovation enabling comprehensive var gene assembly.

fact: The var gene expression profiles obtained from RNAseq assemblies correlated significantly with quantitative PCR results (Pearson R = 0.88).
source_span: Expression profiles of the assembled transcripts were compared with those obtained by quantitative PCR ( qPCR ) and were found to correlate significantly ( Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0 . 88 ) ( Fig 1A ).
selection_reasoning: This validates the accuracy of the RNAseq-based var gene expression measurements.

fact: The assembly pipeline used (SoapDeNovo-Trans/Cap3) was robust to chimeric assemblies, sensitive to low-expressed transcripts, and produced minimal redundancy.
source_span: The pipeline used the SoapDeNovo-Trans/Cap3 method of [53] , which is robust to chimeric assemblies and minimises redundant transcripts ... with the SoapDeNovo-Trans/Cap3 pipeline chosen because it assembled the known samples correctly , was sensitive to low-expressed transcripts , and produced minimal redundancy.

fact: The assembly pipeline was applied separately to each of the 44 patient samples and also to a pooled sample combining all reads.

selection_reasoning: This describes the comprehensive approach to var gene assembly across samples.

fact: Significant differences in gene expression were identified between parasites from severe and uncomplicated malaria cases after accounting for parasite life cycle and other variations.
source_span: Significant differences were identified in the expression of genes between severe and uncomplicated cases of malaria . After accounting for library size , parasite life cycle , and other unwanted sources of variation , 358 genes were found to be differentially expressed after multiple testing correction ( p = 0 . 1 , limma/Voom pipeline [55 , 56] ) .
selection_reasoning: This is a core finding showing that parasite gene expression differs between severe and uncomplicated malaria, central to the study's main question.

fact: A mixture model was used to estimate the proportions of different parasite life cycle stages in each sample to control for life cycle effects in gene expression analysis.
source_span: A mixture model was used to account for parasite life cycle . A constrained linear model was fit using published data [57] to estimate the proportion of ring , early trophozoite , late trophozoite , schizont , and gametocyte stages present in each sample ( Fig 2A , S2 Data ) .
selection_reasoning: Describing the method to control for parasite life cycle is important to understand how differential expression was accurately assessed.

fact: Parasites from severe malaria cases formed two distinct transcriptomic clusters, suggesting severe malaria can be caused by parasites in different physiological states.
source_span: The severe malaria transcriptomes could be separated by profile of differentially expressed genes into 2 principal clusters—S1and S2 ( S3 Fig ) , which was consistent with previous reports of clinical isolates and severe malaria [6 , 7] . This suggests that severe malaria can be caused by parasites in different physiological states .
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights heterogeneity in parasite biology linked to severe malaria, relevant for understanding disease mechanisms.

fact: The 358 genes differentially expressed in severe malaria parasites were involved in diverse biological pathways, including glycolysis, histone methylation, folate metabolism, protein folding, the TCA cycle, pyrimidine metabolism, and GTPase regulation.
source_span: The 358 genes differentially expressed in severe malaria were from diverse functional pathways and revealed a distinct severe malaria parasite transcriptome ( S3 Fig , S1 Data ) . Biological pathways annotated as Gene Ontology ( GO ) biological process terms or Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes ( KEGG ) were ranked using a hypergeometric test , and those with p < 0 . 1 are considered . Terms relating to glycolysis , histone methylation , folate metabolism , and protein folding ranked highly and included genes down-regulated in severe malaria , whilst pathways relating to the tricarboxylic acid ( TCA ) cycle , nucleoside diphosphate ( pyrimidine ) metabolism , and regulation of guanosine triphosphatase ( GTPase ) activity included genes up-regulated in severe malaria ( Fig 3A , S3 Data ) .
selection_reasoning: Identifying key pathways altered in severe malaria parasites is central to understanding the biological changes linked to disease severity.

fact: Genes involved in PfEMP1 transport and var gene regulation were down-regulated in parasites causing severe malaria, suggesting reduced PfEMP1 surface presentation.
source_span: In addition , genes involved in PfEMP1 transport and a gene involved in regulation of var genes were down-regulated in severe malaria . This suggested that var gene expression was modulated but PfEMP1 surface presentation was reduced .
selection_reasoning: PfEMP1 is a key virulence factor, so changes in its expression and transport are important for understanding severe malaria pathogenesis.

fact: Parasites from severe malaria patients showed decreased transcription of genes involved in aerobic glycolysis, including significant down-regulation of aldolase, glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase, and mitochondrial dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase.
source_span: Parasites isolated from patients with severe malaria had significantly down-regulated genes included in the KEGG pathway ‘Glycolysis/gluconeogenesis’ . Significant decreases were observed in transcript levels of 3 glycolytic enzymes ( 0 . 52- to 0 . 62-fold the levels in parasites that caused uncomplicated malaria ) ( all adjusted p < 0 . 1 ) ( Fig 3B , Fig 3A , S1 Data , S3 Data ) . These were aldolase , glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehyrogenase , and mitochondrial dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase ( LPD1 ) that converts glycolytic pyruvate to acetyl coenzyme A ( acetyl-CoA ) .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking metabolic gene expression changes to severe malaria.

fact: The lactate transporter gene was also down-regulated in parasites causing severe malaria, supporting decreased aerobic glycolysis in these parasites.
source_span: The lactate transporter ( also known as the formate nitrite transporter [61] ) was also down-regulated in parasites causing severe malaria ( 0 . 33-fold p = 0 . 009 ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the metabolic shift observed in severe malaria parasites, relevant to the study's main conclusions.

fact: The transcriptional signature of parasites from severe malaria patients resembles a starvation-like response characterized by decreased glycolysis and increased TCA cycle enzyme expression.
source_span: Daily et al . [6] described a cluster of P . falciparum clinical isolates that exhibited a distinct , starvation-like response , characterised by decreased transcription of genes involved in glycolysis and increased transcription of genes encoding enzymes involved in the TCA cycle , which is similar to the transcriptional signature we observed from parasites linked to severe malaria samples ( S4 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This links the study's findings to previous work and provides biological context for the metabolic changes.

fact: Metabolite levels in plasma from severe and uncomplicated malaria patients were analyzed by untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry to investigate whether nutrient availability influenced parasite gene expression.
source_span: To determine whether nutrient availability was contributing to the reduced expression of genes encoding glycolysis enzymes by the parasites causing severe malaria , metabolite levels in plasma samples from the severe and uncomplicated malaria patients were analysed by untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry ( LC-MS ) analysis .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key method used to explore the cause of observed gene expression changes, relevant to the study's main question.

fact: Parasites isolated from patients with severe malaria showed reduced expression of genes encoding glycolysis enzymes compared to parasites from uncomplicated malaria.
source_span: To determine whether nutrient availability was contributing to the reduced expression of genes encoding glycolysis enzymes by the parasites causing severe malaria ...
selection_reasoning: This is a core finding about parasite metabolism differences linked to severe malaria.

fact: Metabolite analysis of plasma from severe and uncomplicated malaria patients identified 35 metabolites that differed significantly, including depletion of citrulline in severe malaria patients.
source_span: Thirty-five metabolite peaks differed significantly between the plasma of patients with severe and uncomplicated malaria ... which was depleted in the patients with severe malaria.
selection_reasoning: This finding links host metabolite changes to severe malaria and supports the study's investigation of metabolic differences.

fact: Low plasma citrulline in severe malaria likely contributes to hypoargininemia, impaired nitric oxide bioavailability, and endothelial dysfunction in affected patients.
source_span: Low citrulline is therefore likely to contribute to the hypoargininenia, impaired NO bioavailability and endothelial dysfunction found in both adults and children with severe malaria ...
selection_reasoning: This explains a clinically relevant mechanism connecting metabolite changes to disease pathology.

fact: Plasma glucose and lactate levels were similar in patients with severe and uncomplicated malaria, indicating that parasite glycolysis down-regulation in severe malaria is not due to reduced blood glucose availability.
source_span: The plasma levels of glucose and lactate were similar in patients with uncomplicated and severe malaria ... suggesting that the down-regulation of parasite glycolysis in the patients with severe malaria is not a direct response to reduced availability of blood glucose.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies that metabolic changes in parasites are not simply due to host glucose levels, refining understanding of parasite metabolism in severe malaria.

fact: Parasites from severe malaria patients did not show increased expression of key enzymes involved in glutamine utilization and mitochondrial respiration, suggesting they do not compensate for decreased glycolysis by increasing TCA cycle activity.
source_span: Key enzymes in glutamine utilisation were either down-regulated ... or unchanged ... indicating that these parasites are unlikely to exhibit a significant switch to mitochondrial respiration.
selection_reasoning: This finding addresses the parasite metabolic adaptation in severe malaria, a principal mechanistic insight.

fact: Overall, parasites associated with severe malaria may be metabolically less active than those from uncomplicated malaria patients.

fact: Genes involved in histone methylation and chromatin modification were down-regulated in parasites causing severe malaria.

selection_reasoning: This identifies epigenetic regulatory changes in parasites associated with severe malaria, relevant to gene expression control.

fact: Genes involved in folate biosynthesis and pyrimidine biosynthesis pathways were down-regulated in parasites from severe malaria patients, suggesting decreased nucleoside biosynthesis.

fact: Differential expression analysis at the var transcript level was performed using two distinct computational approaches to identify significant transcript differences.
source_span: Differential expression analysis at the var transcript level was performed using 2 distinct approaches . The first made use of the separately assembled transcripts by first aligning reads to the transcripts allowing for multiple mapping using Bowtie v0 . 12 . 9 [120] . The transcripts were then clustered using Corset v1 . 03 [89] . The resulting cluster read counts were analysed using the default DESeq2 pipeline [86] . An alternative strategy made use of the combined assembly transcripts . Reads were aligned and transcript level counts obtained using Subread and Featurecounts , respectively , before analysing differential expression using DESeq2 .
selection_reasoning: This describes the main analytical methods used to detect differential expression, which is central to the study's findings.

fact: HMMER3’s hmmsearch was used to annotate specific protein domains (NTS, DBL, and CIDR) in assembled transcripts to characterize var gene domain composition.
source_span: HMMER3’s hmmsearch v3 . 1b1 [91] was used to search the NTS , DBL , and CIDR domain models of [14] against the assembled transcripts from each sample . The most significant domain was annotated first and then successively less significant domains , with the requirement that 2 domains do not overlap .
selection_reasoning: Annotating var gene domains is key to understanding the molecular features analyzed and their differential expression.

fact: An E-value threshold of 1e-8 was applied during domain annotation to minimize spurious domain assignments in the var transcripts.
source_span: An E-value threshold of 1e-8 was chosen to minimise spurious annotations .
selection_reasoning: This threshold ensures the reliability of domain annotations, which supports the validity of downstream differential expression results.

fact: Read counts for annotated var gene domains were aggregated using both a previous domain classification and a novel hierarchical clustering approach to identify differentially expressed domain groups.
source_span: The resulting counts were then aggregated using the previous domain classification of [14] as well as a novel hierarchical approach . The annotated domains were hierarchically clustered using USEARCH [93] by first clustering by length and then by successively lower identity thresholds . The read counts for each domain are then aggregated up this hierarchical tree , and the default DESeq2 pipeline was used to identify differentially expressed nodes .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key methodological innovation to detect meaningful domain-level expression differences.

fact: An iterative multiple testing correction procedure was applied to select the most significant clusters of var gene domains while avoiding redundancy from overlapping domain groups.
source_span: After multiple testing correction [94] , we iteratively reject the null hypothesis ( p < 0 . 05 ) of the most significant node in the hierarchy before removing its ancestor and children nodes . This ensures that we select the most significant grouping of domains from which to form clusters .
selection_reasoning: This statistical approach is important to ensure robust identification of significant domain clusters, supporting the study's conclusions.

source_span: One promising , creative approach is to use adeno-associated virus ( AAV ) vector to deliver antibodies with potent and broadly neutralizing activity [3–7] . This method is an alternative to classical immunization and independent of the host immune system .

source_span: There are good reasons for believing that development of an effective preventive vaccine against HIV-1 is going to be a very difficult task . selection_reasoning: This background explains the motivation for exploring antibody delivery as a prevention strategy.

fact: The study delivered 5L7 IgG1 and 4L6 IgG1 monoclonal antibodies to rhesus monkeys using recombinant AAV vectors to assess protection against SIVmac239 infection.

fact: There was considerable variation between individual monkeys in the levels of delivered 5L7 IgG1 antibody, but these levels remained stable over months before viral challenge.
source_span: Considerable monkey-to-monkey variation was observed in the levels of 5L7 IgG1 that were achieved ... However , the levels in each individual monkey remained stable over the course of months leading up to the time of challenge .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important background on antibody expression variability and stability, relevant to interpreting protection outcomes.

fact: The 4L6 IgG1 antibody levels peaked 3–4 weeks after administration but then declined rapidly, coinciding with the development of anti-antibody immune responses.
source_span: In this experiment , the levels of delivered 4L6 mAb peaked 3–4 weeks after administration and then fell precipitously ... All six of the recombinant AAV-4L6 recipients had antibody responses to the delivered 4L6 mAb whose appearance coincided with the precipitous decline in 4L6 mAb levels .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key difference in antibody persistence and immune response that affects efficacy.

fact: Anti-antibody immune responses were mostly directed against the variable regions of the delivered 5L7 and 4L6 IgG1 antibodies, not the constant regions.
source_span: The anti-anti responses in the 5L7 IgG1 recipients ... were largely specific for 5L7 while the anti-anti responses in the 4L6 IgG1 recipients ... were largely specific for 4L6; since the 5L7 and 4L6 IgG1s have the exact same constant regions , these results indicate that the responses were mostly directed to the variable domains .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight explains the nature of immune responses limiting antibody persistence.

fact: Only one monkey, which had the highest sustained levels of 5L7 IgG1 antibody, resisted all six intravenous SIVmac239 challenges, showing apparent sterilizing immunity.
source_span: Only one monkey of the 18 resisted all six challenges: monkey 84–05 with the highest levels of delivered mAb ( averaging approximately 270 μg/ml of the 5L7 mAb through all of the challenges ) ... The absence of anti-gp41 antibody responses in 84–05 even following the 10x challenge is consistent with the apparent sterilizing immunity in this animal .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding demonstrating the protective potential of high-level 5L7 IgG1 expression.

fact: No significant difference in SIV acquisition was observed between control monkeys and those receiving 4L6 IgG1 antibody, likely due to low or undetectable antibody levels at challenge time.
source_span: Otherwise , no significant difference in the acquisition of SIV infection was observed among the test vs . control monkeys ... Given that levels of delivered 4L6 IgG1 mAb were driven to low or undetectable levels by the time of first challenge in most monkeys in this group , it is not surprising that plasma virion SIV RNA levels in the 4L6 mAb group ... were not significantly different from control monkeys .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses the lack of efficacy of 4L6 IgG1 due to antibody decline, important for interpreting results.

fact: The 5L7 IgG1 antibody group had significantly lower plasma SIV RNA loads at peak viremia and during chronic infection compared to control monkeys.
source_span: However , SIV plasma RNA loads in the 5L7 mAb group were significantly lower than those in the control group both at peak viremia ... and during chronic phase infection ... The differences were significant whether or not the undetectable viral loads of monkey 84–05 were included in the analyses .
selection_reasoning: This fact states a key efficacy outcome supporting the protective effect of 5L7 IgG1.

fact: Both 5L7 and 4L6 IgG1 antibodies lack detectable neutralizing activity against the challenge strain SIVmac239 but can neutralize a neutralization-sensitive derivative, SIVmac316.
source_span: Both the 5L7 and the 4L6 mAb IgG1s lack detectable neutralizing activity against the challenge strain SIVmac239 ... However , both the 5L7 and 4L6 mAbs had neutralizing activity against the neutralization-sensitive derivative of SIVmac239 called SIVmac316 .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the neutralization profile relevant to understanding the mechanism of protection.

fact: AAV vectors can provide long-term expression of delivered antibodies in muscle cells with little or no turnover, enabling prolonged protein production.
source_span: AAV vectors are ideally suited for this purpose. The only protein expressed from AAV vectors is derived from the inserted transgene put into it. As long as the protein is viewed as self, protein expression can continue for prolonged periods. In fact, there are already examples where proteins delivered by AAV vector have persisted at stable levels for years [4, 8, 9, 37], including animal 84–05 in our study. Since muscle cells exhibit little or no turnover, they are a preferred source for long-term delivery purposes.
selection_reasoning: This background explains why AAV vectors are used for antibody delivery and supports the study's approach and significance.

fact: The molecularly cloned SIVmac239 strain is difficult to neutralize and has been widely used as a challenge virus to test vaccine efficacy in monkeys.
source_span: The molecularly cloned SIVmac239 is a difficult-to-neutralize strain with many of the characteristics of a primary isolate. It has been extensively used as a challenge strain to gauge efficacy of vaccine approaches in monkeys, and it has generally proven quite difficult to achieve protection against [29, 30, 41–43].
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential disease context and explains the challenge model used in the study.

fact: Delivery of the 5L7 monoclonal antibody by AAV vector significantly delayed peak viral loads and lowered viral loads at peak and set point after SIVmac239 challenge in monkeys.
source_span: The presence of AAV-delivered 5L7 mAb in our experiments significantly delayed the time to peak viral loads and significantly lowered SIVmac239 viral loads both at peak viremia and at viral load set point.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding demonstrating the protective effect of the 5L7 antibody.

fact: The 5L7 monoclonal antibody provided protection against SIVmac239 challenge despite lacking detectable neutralizing activity against this virus.
source_span: The protective effects in the 5L7 mAb group occurred in the absence of any detectable neutralizing activity of the 5L7 mAb against the SIVmac239 molecular clone even out to 1 mg/ml. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of significant protective effects of a mAb in the absence of an ability to neutralize the challenge virus [46, 47].
