source_span: Recent studies have emphasized the importance of Fc-mediated effector functions in contributing to the protection afforded by mAbs capable of neutralizing the SHIV used for challenge [48–52]. ... Effector functions potentially contributing to the protective effects of the 5L7 IgG1 observed in our current study include but are not limited to ADCC activity and complement-mediated virolysis.
selection_reasoning: This explains a plausible mechanism underlying the observed protection despite lack of neutralization.

fact: The 5L7 monoclonal antibody circulating in monkey 84–05 exhibited extraordinarily high ADCC activity on a per microgram basis compared to purified 5L7 IgG1.
source_span: Along these lines, it is fascinating that the 5L7 mAb circulating in monkey 84–05 was not only present at extraordinarily high levels, it had extraordinarily high ADCC activity on a per μg basis.
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights a unique functional property of the antibody in the protected animal, relevant to understanding protection.

fact: Differences in post-translational modifications of the 5L7 monoclonal antibody, such as decreased core fucosylation or terminal sialylation, may explain the increased ADCC activity observed in monkey 84–05.
source_span: Because of the nature of the ADCC assay that was used, it seems likely that the extraordinarily high ADCC activity in the serum of this one animal results from differences in post-translational modifications of the 5L7 mAb. Decreased core fucosylation or terminal sialylation have been shown to dramatically increase Fc-mediated ADCC activity [58–62].
selection_reasoning: This provides a mechanistic insight into why the antibody in this animal had enhanced effector function.

fact: Immune responses to the delivered IgG1 antibody were detected in 9 of 12 rhesus monkeys and appeared to limit the levels of delivered antibody.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii is an obligate intracellular parasite that replicates inside a parasitophorous vacuole in mammalian cells.
source_span: Toxoplasma is an obligate intracellular parasite that replicates in mammalian cells within a parasitophorous vacuole ( PV ) that does not fuse with any host organelles .
selection_reasoning: This background fact defines the parasite and its intracellular niche, essential for understanding the study context.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii exploits host lipid droplets, which are fat storage organelles, to acquire nutrients necessary for its replication.
source_span: One mechanism developed by the parasite for nutrient acquisition is the attraction of host organelles to the PV . Here , we examined the exploitation of host lipid droplets ( LD ) , ubiquitous fat storage organelles , by Toxoplasma .
selection_reasoning: This states the main research question and biological focus of the study.

fact: Toxoplasma replication is reduced in host cells that are depleted of lipid droplets or have impaired triacylglycerol lipolysis or fatty acid catabolism.
source_span: We show that Toxoplasma replication is reduced in host cells that are depleted of LD , or impaired in TAG lipolysis or fatty acid catabolism .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking host lipid droplet metabolism to parasite replication.

fact: During infection, the number of host lipid droplets and the expression of lipid droplet-associated genes (ADRP, DGAT2) increase progressively until parasite replication begins.
source_span: In infected cells , the number of host LD and the expression of host LD-associated genes ( ADRP , DGAT2 ) , progressively increase until the onset of parasite replication .
selection_reasoning: This finding shows how the parasite infection alters host lipid droplet biology, relevant to the parasite’s nutrient acquisition.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii can access lipids stored in host lipid droplets and incorporates these lipids into its own membranes and lipid droplets.
source_span: Toxoplasma is capable of accessing lipids stored in host LD and incorporates these lipids into its own membranes and LD .
selection_reasoning: This is a key mechanistic finding demonstrating lipid transfer from host to parasite.

fact: Adding oleic acid to host cells stimulates lipid droplet formation and causes accumulation of large neutral lipid droplets inside Toxoplasma.
source_span: Exogenous addition of oleic acid stimulates LD biogenesis in the host cell and results in the overaccumulation of neutral lipids in very large LD inside the parasite .
selection_reasoning: This experimental manipulation supports the role of host lipid droplets in parasite lipid storage.

fact: Toxoplasma intercepts and internalizes host lipid droplets into the parasitophorous vacuole, where some remain associated with the host protein Rab7 and become wrapped by an intravacuolar network of membranes.
source_span: To access LD-derived lipids , Toxoplasma intercepts and internalizes within the PV host LD , some of which remaining associated with Rab7 , which become wrapped by an intravacuolar network of membranes ( IVN ) .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key mechanism of host lipid droplet internalization and processing by the parasite.

fact: Mutant Toxoplasma parasites impaired in intravacuolar network formation have a reduced capacity to take up lipids from host lipid droplets.
source_span: Mutant parasites impaired in IVN formation display diminished capacity of lipid uptake from host LD .
selection_reasoning: This finding links the intravacuolar network to the parasite’s ability to acquire host lipids.

fact: Parasites lacking an intravacuolar network-localized phospholipase A2 enzyme are less efficient at salvaging lipids from host lipid droplets in the parasitophorous vacuole.
source_span: Moreover , parasites lacking an IVN-localized phospholipase A2 are less proficient in salvaging lipids from host LD in the PV , suggesting a major contribution of the IVN for host LD processing in the PV and , thus lipid content release .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a specific enzyme important for lipid processing and uptake from host lipid droplets.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii contains endocytic-like structures that internalize lipid material originating from the parasitophorous vacuole lumen.
source_span: Interestingly , gavage of parasites with lipids unveils , for the first time , the presence in Toxoplasma of endocytic-like structures containing lipidic material originating from the PV lumen .
selection_reasoning: This novel observation reveals a parasite structure involved in lipid uptake, advancing understanding of the mechanism.

fact: Host lipid droplets are cytoplasmic organelles composed mainly of neutral lipids such as triacylglycerols and cholesteryl esters, surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer with associated proteins.
source_span: In mammalian cells , lipid droplets ( LD ) are cytoplasmic structures containing a diverse array of lipids and proteins . LD consist of an organic core , comprising neutral lipids ( mostly triacylglycerols ( TAG ) and cholesteryl esters ( CE ) with mixed fatty acid composition ) bounded by a monolayer of phospholipids [1] . Inserted onto the outer phospholipid monolayer are structural proteins ( e . g . , proteins of the perilipin family , such as Adipose differentiation-related protein ( ADRP ) or adipophilin ) , lipid biosynthetic enzymes ( e . g . , acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2 ( DGAT2 ) , and acyl-CoA synthetase ) , lipolytic enzymes ( e . g . , adipose tissue triacylglycerol lipase ( ATGL ) and membrane-trafficking proteins ( e . g . , Rab7 , Rab18 and ARF1 ) [2–4] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact defines lipid droplets and their components, necessary to understand their role in infection.

fact: Lipid droplets have diverse cellular functions including energy storage, lipid homeostasis, cell signaling during inflammation, innate immunity, and RNA metabolism.
source_span: LD display canonical lipid-related functions ranging from energy storage to lipid homeostasis . In addition , these structures are engaged in various cellular processes , depending on cell type and activation conditions , such as cell signaling during inflammation , innate immunity , RNA metabolism , cytoskeletal organization , nuclear transcription and histone modulation [5–7] .
selection_reasoning: This explains why lipid droplets are important beyond fat storage, relevant to infection biology.

fact: Several pathogens have evolved to exploit host lipid droplets to promote their survival by inducing lipid droplet formation, altering their structure, or transferring lipid droplet content to the pathogen compartment.
source_span: Unsprisingly , several pathogens have evolved to take advantage of host LD to favor their own survival: they target host LD for progeny assembly , or as part of an anti-immunity strategy [8–12] . Prominent pathogen-mediated changes to host LD include inducing LD formation , altering LD ultrastructure , modifying LD lipid and protein composition , relocating LD to the site of pathogen replication , and transferring LD content to the pathogen’s intracellular compartment .
selection_reasoning: This situates Toxoplasma’s strategy within a broader context of pathogen exploitation of host lipid droplets.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii infection increases the number of host lipid droplets in various cell types, including macrophages, skeletal muscle cells, fibroblasts, and epithelial cells.
source_span: Recent studies on Toxoplasma infecting macrophages and skeletal muscle cells showed an increased number of LD in the host cytoplasm up to 48 h post-infection [25 , 26] . To determine if a similar effect occurs in other cell types , human fibroblasts ( HFF ) and epithelial cells ( HeLa ) were infected in vitro with Toxoplasma , and LD biogenesis was monitored throughout infection .
selection_reasoning: This finding shows the generality of host lipid droplet induction by Toxoplasma infection.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii relies on host lipid droplet lipid content and lipolytic activities for its intracellular development in mammalian cells.
source_span: Our data reveal that host LD lipid content and lipolytic activities are important for the parasite’s development in mammalian cells .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the significance of host lipid droplets for parasite growth.

fact: Toxoplasma infection alters host neutral lipid homeostasis by changing lipid droplet abundance, intracellular distribution, and neutral lipid synthesis.
source_span: Toxoplasma infection has a pronounced impact on host cell neutral lipid homeostasis , through changes in host LD abundance , LD intracellular distribution and host neutral lipid syntheses .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the broader impact of infection on host lipid metabolism.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii internalizes host lipid droplets into its parasitophorous vacuole and salvages their lipid content for membrane incorporation or storage in its own lipid droplets.
source_span: that Toxoplasma internalizes host LD into the PV and salvages their lipid content for incorporation into membranes or , in case of excess , storage in its own LD .
selection_reasoning: This is a core mechanistic finding explaining how Toxoplasma exploits host lipids, central to the study's biological question.

fact: Host lipid droplet biogenesis is stimulated in Toxoplasma-infected mouse macrophages and skeletal muscle cells 24 and 48 hours post-infection.
source_span: It has been shown that host LD biogenesis is stimulated in Toxoplasma-infected mouse macrophages and skeletal muscle cells 24 h and 48 h post-infection ( p . i . ) [25 , 26] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes prior knowledge motivating investigation of LD changes in other cell types.

fact: In human fibroblasts infected with Toxoplasma, the number of host lipid droplets increases early in infection but declines after about 24 hours post-infection.
source_span: The number of mammalian LD steadily increased early in infection from a median of 23 LD in uninfected cells to 34 ( 1/PV ) , 51 ( 2/PV ) and 50 ( 4/PV ) in infected cells . However , once the PV contains 8 parasites , which corresponds to ~24 h p . i . , the host LD number abruptly declined to approximately 26 per cell .
selection_reasoning: This principal finding describes the dynamic changes in host LD number during infection, key to understanding host-parasite interactions.

fact: The expression of the host ADRP gene, which encodes a lipid droplet-associated protein, increases early during Toxoplasma infection and peaks around 9 hours post-infection before returning to baseline by 24 hours.
source_span: The expression of hsADRP transcripts increased by 1 . 5-fold at 5 h p . i . , as compared to uninfected cells , and continued increasing up to 9 h p . i . , then declined to levels similar to uninfected cells at 24 h p . i .
selection_reasoning: This molecular evidence supports the observed changes in host lipid droplets and is relevant to the infection timeline.

fact: Toxoplasma infection causes downregulation of host ACAT1 and DGAT1 gene expression, enzymes involved in cholesteryl ester and triacylglycerol synthesis, respectively, while DGAT2 expression increases at 9 hours post-infection.
source_span: A significant down-regulation of hsACAT1 expression throughout infection was observed with ~2 . 8-times fewer transcripts by 24 h p . i . ... Expression levels of hsDGAT1 were also reduced in infected cells ... While hsDGAT2 expression decreased slightly 5 h p . i . , it increased significantly by 1 . 6-times 9 h p . i . , as compared to uninfected cells .
selection_reasoning: This finding reveals specific host lipid metabolic pathway alterations during infection, important for understanding parasite manipulation of host lipids.

fact: Host lipid droplets cluster around the Toxoplasma parasitophorous vacuole early during infection and remain closely associated until parasite egress.
source_span: In infected cells , the vast majority of LD gathered around individual PV of Toxoplasma beginning early in infection , and this perivacuolar distribution of host LD was maintained throughout infection until parasite egress .
selection_reasoning: This spatial redistribution of host organelles is a key phenotypic hallmark of infection relevant to parasite-host interactions.

fact: Increasing host lipid droplet formation by adding oleic acid or overexpressing ADRP enhances the association of host lipid droplets with the Toxoplasma parasitophorous vacuole.
source_span: Upon exogenous addition of 0 . 2 mM OA ... we observed a pronounced increase in host LD association with the PV in HFF ... In HeLa cells overexpressing GFP-ADRP , PV were extensively enveloped with host LD harboring GFP-ADRP at their surface ... Under conditions of simultaneous OA addition and ADRP overexpression , LD became enlarged , which was more dramatic in infected cells with most of these oversized LD surrounding the PV .
selection_reasoning: This experimental manipulation demonstrates the generality and modifiability of host LD recruitment to the parasite vacuole, highlighting a key interaction.

fact: The attraction of host lipid droplets to the Toxoplasma parasitophorous vacuole is a general phenotype observed in multiple mammalian cell types infected in vitro.
source_span: These data suggest that the attraction of host LD to the PV is a general phenotype of Toxoplasma infection in vitro .
selection_reasoning: This broad relevance supports the significance of the host LD-PV interaction across cell types, important for translational implications.

fact: Toxoplasma infection causes host lipid droplets (LD) to cluster and enlarge around the parasitophorous vacuole (PV) in infected mammalian cells.
source_span: These data suggest that the attraction of host LD to the PV is a general phenotype of Toxoplasma infection in vitro ... We observed a substantial clustering of host LD at the PV, with LD often organized in multiple layers around the vacuole ... the size of host LD in OA-loaded cells was measured, revealing ... 1.04 ± 0.56 μm of LD in infected cells ... indicating an increase in size of the mammalian LD population upon Toxoplasma infection.
selection_reasoning: This is a core finding about how Toxoplasma alters host cell lipid droplet distribution and size, which is central to understanding host-parasite interactions.

fact: The accumulation of host lipid droplets around the parasitophorous vacuole increases progressively over time during Toxoplasma infection.
source_span: Throughout infection, an accumulation of host LD around the PV was observed. Early in infection (2 h), only ~2% of PV were positive, however, by 8 h p.i., the PV percent reached approximately 20. Between 8 h and 24 h, the percent of positive PV increased by 10% ... The addition of 0.2 mM OA amplified this phenomenon as by 24 h p.i., ~50% of PV were positive.
selection_reasoning: This temporal dynamic of LD relocation is a key mechanistic insight into the infection process.

fact: Host lipid droplets may support the intracellular development of Toxoplasma, as suggested by their redistribution to the parasitophorous vacuole and increased expression of host DGAT2 at the onset of parasite replication.
source_span: The redistribution of host LD to the PV and the increased expression of HsDGAT2 at the onset of parasite replication suggest that host LD may play a role in supporting the intracellular development of Toxoplasma.
selection_reasoning: This links host lipid metabolism to parasite growth, highlighting biological significance.

fact: Toxoplasma replication is significantly delayed in mutant mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF) lacking both DGAT1 and DGAT2 enzymes, which have few and small lipid droplets.
source_span: Toxoplasma replication rates were quantified ... in DGAT-deficient MEF, and a significant growth delay was observed ... The slower replication rate of parasites in DGAT-deficient MEF (D1D2KO) was further confirmed by tritiated uracil incorporation ... showing a growth reduction of ~40% compared to parasites replicating in WT MEF.
selection_reasoning: This experimental result demonstrates the functional importance of host lipid droplets for parasite growth.

fact: Parasites cultivated for multiple passages in DGAT-deficient MEF show a more pronounced replication defect than parasites exposed to DGAT-deficient MEF for only 24 hours.
source_span: Parasites maintained solely in DGAT-deficient MEF exhibited a growth reduction of ~60%, and this replication defect was more pronounced than that of parasites cultivated only 24 h in DGAT-deficient MEF.
selection_reasoning: This finding emphasizes the cumulative negative impact of host lipid droplet deficiency on parasite development.

fact: Toxoplasma may exploit host lipid droplets not only for their lipid cargo but also for associated lipid-metabolizing enzymes and energy substrates.
source_span: In addition to their lipid cargo, T. gondii may take advantage of host LD for their lipid-metabolizing enzymes and energy substrates.
selection_reasoning: This suggests a broader role of host lipid droplets in parasite metabolism and survival.

fact: Lipolysis of triacylglycerols stored in host lipid droplets releases fatty acids that can be used by Toxoplasma for lipid synthesis and membrane biogenesis.
source_span: Lipolysis is the biochemical pathway responsible for the catabolism of TAG, stored in LD, into glycerol and non-esterified fatty acids by lipases. The free fatty acids can subsequently be used as precursors for major lipid synthesis and membrane biogenesis.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why host lipid droplets are a valuable resource for the parasite.

fact: Toxoplasma lacks an ATGL homolog, the host enzyme that catalyzes the initial step in triacylglycerol hydrolysis in lipid droplets.
source_span: In LD, ATGL catalyzes the initial step in TAG hydrolysis, generating DAG and a fatty acid. No ATGL homolog is present in the Toxoplasma genome.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the parasite’s dependence on host lipolytic enzymes for accessing fatty acids.

fact: Inhibiting host ATGL lipase activity with Atglistatin reduces fatty acid mobilization in infected cells.
source_span: To examine whether Toxoplasma exploits some lipolytic activities associated with host LD, we incubated infected cells with Atglistatin, a specific inhibitor of ATGL. In cultured mammalian cells, up to 100 μM of Atglistatin inhibits lipolysis by reducing fatty acid mobilization.
selection_reasoning: This experimental approach tests the role of host lipolysis in parasite development, relevant to the study’s main question.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii lacks the gene encoding adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL), which catalyzes the initial step in triglyceride hydrolysis in host lipid droplets.
source_span: No ATGL homolog is present in the Toxoplasma genome.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why the parasite may rely on host lipolytic enzymes, motivating the study of host lipase inhibition effects on parasite replication.

fact: Inhibiting host ATGL lipase activity with Atglistatin reduces Toxoplasma gondii replication in infected cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source_span: Incubation of infected cells with Atglistatin at different concentrations for 24 h resulted in a significant decrease in parasite replication, proportional to the drug concentration.
selection_reasoning: This key experimental finding shows that host lipolysis supports parasite growth, a principal result relevant to the study's main question.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii lacks the genes encoding mitochondrial enzymes carnitine palmitoyltransferase-1 (CPT-1) and 3-ketoacyl coenzyme A thiolase (3-KAT), which are essential for fatty acid β-oxidation in host mitochondria.
source_span: T. gondii lacks both CPT-1 and 3-KAT genes.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the hypothesis that the parasite depends on host mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation rather than its own for energy metabolism.

fact: Inhibiting host mitochondrial fatty acid β-oxidation enzymes CPT-1 and 3-KAT with Etomoxir and Trimetazidine respectively decreases Toxoplasma gondii replication in infected cells.
source_span: Incubation of Toxoplasma-infected cells with Etomoxir or Trimetazidine at various concentrations results in decreased parasite replication, proportional to drug concentrations.
selection_reasoning: This finding indicates that host mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation contributes to parasite growth, a principal mechanistic insight.

fact: Inhibiting host ATGL, CPT-1, or 3-KAT activities causes disorganization of Toxoplasma gondii parasites within the parasitophorous vacuole and accumulation of lipid material in the vacuole lumen.
source_span: Microscopy observations of infected cells exposed for 24 h to 50 μM Atglistatin, 100 μM Etomoxir or 100 μM Trimetazidine reveal disorganized parasites within the PV and large lipidic material accumulated between the parasites.
selection_reasoning: This observation links host lipid metabolism inhibition to parasite structural and metabolic disruption, supporting the significance of host lipid metabolism for parasite viability.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii attracts host lipid droplets and mitochondria to its parasitophorous vacuole, suggesting it exploits host lipid stores and metabolic processes.
source_span: The redistribution and closeness of host LD to the PV membrane suggests that Toxoplasma may take advantage of mammalian LD for their lipid stores and/or metabolic properties.
selection_reasoning: This background and mechanistic fact explains the biological context and rationale for studying host lipid metabolism in parasite infection.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii can internalize fluorescent fatty acid analogs derived from host lipid droplets into its own lipid droplets and intracellular membranes over 24 hours of infection.
source_span: After 24 h of infection, we observed a fluorescent staining within the parasite, illustrating that Toxoplasma accumulated C4-BODIPY-C9 or lipids derived from it... The fluorescence staining was also observed on intracellular membranes.
selection_reasoning: This key experimental result demonstrates parasite uptake and utilization of host lipid droplet-derived lipids, central to the study's main claim.

fact: Using a non-metabolizable fluorescent lipid dye preloaded into host lipid droplets, Toxoplasma gondii was shown to internalize neutral lipids directly from host lipid droplets into its own lipid droplets.
source_span: BODIPY 493/503 staining was observed within the parasite, mostly accumulated within their LD... this data establishes that Toxoplasma is able to access lipids confined to host LD.
selection_reasoning: This finding provides direct evidence that the parasite accesses and stores host lipid droplet lipids, a principal mechanistic insight.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii sequesters host mammalian Rab14, Rab30, and Rab43 vesicles containing lipids into its parasitophorous vacuole (PV).
source_span: We previously demonstrated that T . gondii diverts and sequesters into the PV host mammalian Rab14 , Rab30 and Rab43 vesicles containing lipids [24] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes the parasite's known mechanism of accessing host lipids, which is central to the study's focus on lipid acquisition.

fact: Rab7 localizes at least in part to host lipid droplets (LD) and is involved in their recognition by Toxoplasma gondii.
source_span: We first confirmed that Rab7 localizes , at least in part , to LD by transfecting HFF with a plasmid containing mCherry-Rab7 and staining with BODIPY 493/503 . Partial colocalization ( PCC: 0 . 129 ) of mCherry-Rab7 and BODIPY 493/503 was observed , primarily on the surface of the LD ( yellow , positive difference from the mean ( PDM ) image ) ( Fig 6A ) .
selection_reasoning: Identifying Rab7 on host LD is key to understanding how Toxoplasma may selectively target these lipid stores.

fact: The number of host lipid droplets positive for Rab7 increases significantly upon addition of oleic acid (OA), especially in Toxoplasma-infected cells.
source_span: Upon the addition of OA , the number of foci containing the two fluorescent signals significantly increased; measurement of the fluorescence overlap was performed by counting the number of BODIPY 493/503 foci with or without mCherry-Rab7 in the presence or the absence of 0 . 2 mM OA , and a ~3-fold increase in yellow foci was calculated ( p < 0 . 005 in uninfected vs . infected cells ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding shows that lipid loading enhances Rab7 association with LD, which is relevant to parasite lipid acquisition.

fact: Rab7-positive host lipid droplets are sequestered inside the Toxoplasma parasitophorous vacuole (PV).
source_span: In all conditions , several GFP-Rab7 foci were observed inside the PV , as visualized in the orthogonal view of the z-stack . The percent of PV with intravacuolar GFP-Rab7 foci significantly increased in the presence of 0 . 2 or 0 . 4 mM OA added to the medium ( Fig 6C ) .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding showing that the parasite internalizes Rab7-associated host LD into its vacuole.

fact: Host lipid droplets positive for both Rab7 and neutral lipid stain BODIPY 493/503 are present inside the Toxoplasma PV, confirming that bona fide host LD are sequestered into the vacuole.
source_span: Intravacuolar foci stained for both mCherry-Rab7 and BODIPY 493/503 were observed in 3D reconstructed images , shown both as an orthogonal view of a z-stack and as individual z-slice images . This indicates that these yellow foci , which correspond to bona fide host LD , were sequestered into the PV .
selection_reasoning: This confirms the identity of the internalized structures as host lipid droplets, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Rab18-positive structures are also found inside about 40% of Toxoplasma PV, but their presence does not increase with oleic acid treatment.
source_span: In infected GFP-Rab18-expressing HFF , we also observed intravacuolar GFP-Rab18-positive structures ( S4A Fig ) inside ~40% of Toxoplasma PV ( S4B Fig ) . In contrast to GFP-Rab7 , there was no significant increase in the percent of PV containing Rab18 in the presence of excess OA .
selection_reasoning: This suggests Rab18 may play a role in LD uptake but is less responsive to lipid loading than Rab7.

fact: Host lipid droplets are found inside the Toxoplasma PV, often protruding into or surrounded by the PV membrane, as shown by ultrastructural studies using malachite green staining.
source_span: In many instances , we observed several host LD not only in close proximity to the PV membrane , but also protruding into the PV . In HFF infected with Toxoplasma for 24 h incubated with 0 . 2 mM OA , even more host LD were observed bulging against the vacuolar membrane ( Fig 7A , panel II ) . Examination of the PV content reveals the presence of LD inside the vacuole ( Fig 7B ) , some of them surrounded by the PV membrane ( Fig 7B , panel I ) .
selection_reasoning: This provides ultrastructural evidence supporting the internalization of host LD into the parasite vacuole.

fact: Host lipid droplets inside the Toxoplasma PV have similar ultrastructural features as those in the host cytoplasm, including a phospholipid monolayer and similar size and shape.
source_span: These LD displayed all the features of LD found in the host cytoplasm , including a thin phospholipid monolayer , and a similar size , electron-density and shape ( S5 Fig ) , confirming that host LD were translocated from the host cytosol to the intravacuolar space .
selection_reasoning: This confirms that the internalized structures are intact host lipid droplets, important for understanding parasite nutrient acquisition.

fact: The intravacuolar network (IVN), a tubule network secreted by Toxoplasma into the PV, wraps host lipid droplets inside the vacuole.
source_span: Interestingly , host LD internalized into the PV were wrapped by tubules of the IVN , as illustrated for 3 LD ( Fig 7B , panels II and III ) .
selection_reasoning: This suggests a structural mechanism by which the parasite may interact with and process host LD inside the PV.

fact: The IVN is proposed to be involved in nutrient uptake and parasite protein targeting to the PV membrane.
source_span: The PV lumen contains thin tubules organized in a dense network named the intravacuolar network ( IVN ) . The IVN is initially secreted by the parasite [57] and then expanded through the salvage of host lipids by the parasite via an unknown mechanism [58] . It has been proposed that this network may be involved in nutrient uptake [59] , or parasite protein targeting to the PV membrane [60] .
selection_reasoning: This background explains the functional significance of the IVN in parasite-host interactions.

fact: A Toxoplasma mutant lacking the IVN structural proteins GRA2 and GRA6 shows reduced ability to store lipids and form lipid droplets compared to wild-type parasites.
source_span: Quantification of the volume of the green fluorescent signal within individual parasites reveal significantly less staining ( ~50% reduction ) in the Δgra2Δgra6 mutant , as compared to WT parasites ( Fig 8A , panel II ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding links the IVN structure to parasite lipid storage capacity, a key functional insight.

fact: The Δgra2Δgra6 mutant parasite can scavenge host lipid droplet-derived neutral lipids but to a much lower extent than wild-type parasites.
source_span: Mutant parasites were capable of scavenging host LD-derived neutral lipids , albeit to a much lower extent than WT parasites , as evidenced by microscopic observations illustrating very spare and small LD ( Fig 8B , panel I ) . Quantification of the fluorescent signal within the mutant reveals BODIPY 493/503 intensity ~ 4-times lower than calculated for WT parasites ( Fig 8B , panel II ) .
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates the functional importance of the IVN in efficient host lipid acquisition.

fact: The phospholipase A2 enzyme TgLCAT, secreted by Toxoplasma into the PV and associated with the IVN, may mediate degradative or lipolytic activities to process host nutrient-enriched structures inside the PV.
source_span: We previously characterized the properties of a phospholipase A2 enzyme ( TgLCAT ) , a dense granule protein that is secreted by Toxoplasma into the PV and is associated with the IVN post-secretion [59] . One attractive hypothesis is that the IVN may serve as a platform for degradative or lipolytic activities mediated by TgLCAT , thus for the processing of host nutrient-enriched structures sequestered into the PV , to cover the
selection_reasoning: This suggests a mechanistic role for the IVN and TgLCAT in processing host lipids for parasite use.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii parasites lacking the TgLCAT enzyme show reduced ability to process host lipid droplets trapped in the parasitophorous vacuole, resulting in lower lipid availability for the parasite.
source_span: All together, these results suggest that the IVN and, at least, one lipase associated to this network are implicated in the processing of host LD trapped into the PV, which would result in lipid availability for the parasites.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key mechanism by which the parasite accesses host lipids, central to understanding parasite nutrition and virulence.

fact: The TgLCAT-deficient Toxoplasma mutant exhibits growth defects in vitro and in mice, while overexpression of TgLCAT increases parasite virulence in mice.
source_span: We previously generated a parasite mutant lacking TgLCAT (Δlcat), which exhibited growth defects both in vitro and in mice, and a parasite complemented strain overexpressing TgLCAT (Δlcat::LCAT), which was more virulent in mice than WT parasites [59].
selection_reasoning: This fact connects the enzyme TgLCAT to parasite growth and virulence, a principal finding with clinical and biological significance.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii can take up oleic acid stored in host lipid droplets proportionally to the concentration of oleic acid and infection time.
source_span: Tritiated material was incorporated into Toxoplasma proportionally to the OA concentrations and the infection times, revealing the avidity of the parasite to divert large amounts of lipids accumulated in its environment.
selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates the parasite's ability to salvage host lipids, a key aspect of its nutrient acquisition strategy.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii expresses two ACAT enzymes (TgACAT1 and TgACAT2) involved in producing cholesteryl esters for storage in lipid droplets, with TgACAT2 having broader fatty acid specificity and producing more cholesteryl esters.
source_span: Toxoplasma possesses two ACAT enzymes (TgACAT1 and TgACAT2) that are both involved in producing CE for storage in LD. While TgACAT1 preferentially utilizes palmitoyl-CoA, TgACAT2 has broader fatty acid specificity and produces more CE.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on the parasite's lipid metabolism machinery relevant to its lipid storage and utilization.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii has a single DGAT enzyme responsible for all triacylglycerol synthesis.
source_span: The parasite expresses only one DGAT, TgDGAT responsible for all its TAG synthesis.
selection_reasoning: This fact is important for understanding the parasite's lipid synthesis pathways.

fact: Exposure of intracellular Toxoplasma gondii to excess oleic acid leads to increased expression of TgACAT2 and TgDGAT enzymes after 24 hours, indicating activation of lipid storage pathways.
source_span: At 24 h p.i., a significantly increase in TgACAT2 (1.7-fold) and TgDGAT (1.8-fold) expression was observed.
selection_reasoning: This finding shows how the parasite responds to excess fatty acids by upregulating lipid storage enzymes, a principal adaptive mechanism.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii encodes a single stearoyl-CoA desaturase (TgSCD) enzyme potentially involved in synthesizing oleic acid from stearate.
source_span: Genome searches in T. gondii reveal the presence of a gene coding for a single SCD (Δ-9 fatty acid desaturase; TGME49_238950 in www.toxodb.org), potentially involved in the synthesis of stearate to oleate.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on the parasite's capacity for fatty acid modification, relevant to its lipid metabolism.

fact: The transcription of TgSCD in intracellular Toxoplasma gondii is upregulated in response to excess oleic acid, increasing by 1.65- and 2.7-fold at 0.2 mM and 0.4 mM oleic acid respectively.
source_span: TgSCD transcription was upregulated by 1.65- and 2.7-fold in the presence of 0.2 and 0.4 mM OA respectively.
selection_reasoning: This fact shows the parasite's regulatory response to fatty acid availability, important for understanding its lipid metabolism adaptation.

fact: Addition of oleic acid to fibroblast host cells increases transcription of genes involved in triacylglycerol synthesis and lipid droplet formation, such as hsADRP, hsDGAT1, and hsDGAT2.
source_span: Addition of 0.2 mM OA to the medium of a confluent layer of cells for 24 h resulted in an increase in transcription of hsADRP by 3.9-fold, hsDGAT1 by 1.7-fold, and hsDGAT2 by 1.9-fold, as compared to untreated cells.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on host cell lipid metabolism changes relevant to parasite infection and nutrient availability.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii has a gene coding for a single stearoyl-CoA desaturase (TgSCD) potentially involved in converting stearate to oleate.
source_span: Genome searches in T . gondii reveal the presence of a gene coding for a single SCD ( Δ-9 fatty acid desaturase; TGME49_238950 in www . toxodb . org ) , potentially involved in the synthesis of stearate to oleate .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the parasite's capacity for fatty acid modification, relevant to understanding lipid metabolism studied.

fact: The transcription of TgSCD in intracellular Toxoplasma gondii parasites is upregulated in response to excess oleic acid (OA).
source_span: TgSCD transcription was upregulated by 1 . 65- and 2 . 7-fold in the presence of 0 . 2 and 0 . 4 mM OA respectively , which is analogous to the response of adipocytes exposed to excess OA .
selection_reasoning: This shows a key regulatory response of the parasite to excess OA, central to the study's investigation of lipid metabolism.

fact: Exposure of intracellular Toxoplasma gondii parasites to excess oleic acid increases the production of neutral lipids, especially triacylglycerols (TAG) and cholesteryl esters (CE).
source_span: Higher amounts of TAG were detected for T . gondii incubated with excess OA , with an ~3- and ~4 . 5-fold increase for 0 . 2 and 0 . 4 mM OA , respectively ... higher quantities of CE were detected for T . gondii incubated with excess OA , with an ~1 . 5- and ~2 . 5-fold increase with 0 . 2 and 0 . 4 mM OA , respectively;
selection_reasoning: This principal finding links excess OA exposure to increased neutral lipid synthesis, a core result of the study.

fact: Oleic acid salvaged by Toxoplasma gondii is mainly converted into triacylglycerols and cholesteryl esters, consistent with upregulation of lipid-synthesizing enzymes TgACAT2 and TgDGAT.
source_span: In conclusion , OA salvaged by T . gondii is mainly converted to TAG and CE , which is consistent with the upregulation of TgACAT2 and TgDGAT in the presence of excess OA .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the metabolic fate of OA in the parasite, linking gene expression and lipid accumulation.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii parasites increase the number and size of lipid droplets in response to excess oleic acid exposure.
source_span: After incubation with 0 . 2 and 0 . 4 mM OA for 24 h , we detected up to 8 fluorescent puncta within the parasite ... some of these fluorescent puncta were as large as host LD , with a diameter up to ~0 . 6 μm .
selection_reasoning: This finding shows a cellular adaptation to store excess lipids, important for understanding parasite lipid handling.

fact: Electron microscopy revealed that Toxoplasma gondii accumulates many small lipid droplets rather than a few large ones when exposed to excess oleic acid.
source_span: We observed a gathering of many small LD ( up to 20 per parasite ) in the cytosol more frequently than isolated gigantic LD ... in response to excess OA , the parasite is able to stimulate LD biogenesis for the storage of large quantities of neutral lipids .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the nature of lipid storage structures formed under excess OA, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Excess oleic acid causes a dramatic expansion of the intravacuolar network (IVN) within the parasitophorous vacuole of Toxoplasma gondii-infected cells.
source_span: By contrast , in the presence of 0 . 2 mM OA , the IVN dramatically expands and occupies the entire vacuolar space available between parasites ... the extremely compacted structure of the IVN that is composed of remarkably long , intertwined tubules .
selection_reasoning: This finding links lipid availability to structural changes in the parasite's vacuole, relevant to parasite biology.

fact: Part of the oleic acid salvaged by Toxoplasma gondii is incorporated into the intravacuolar network, contributing to its expansion.
source_span: These findings suggest that part of the OA salvaged by Toxoplasma is incorporated into the IVN , contributing to the dramatic expansion of this network .
selection_reasoning: This connects lipid metabolism to vacuolar membrane remodeling, a significant mechanistic conclusion.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii forms a large plasma membrane invagination with a narrow neck at the anterior pole when exposed to excess oleic acid, which is distinct from the known micropore structure.
source_span: We noticed one very large invagination of the parasite’s plasma membrane ... This invagination was clearly distinct from the micropore ... by its larger size and more post-nuclear localization .
selection_reasoning: This novel structural observation may relate to endocytic processes, addressing a key question about macromolecule uptake.

fact: The large plasma membrane invaginations in Toxoplasma gondii exposed to excess oleic acid have a cytoplasmic coat resembling endocytic structures, suggesting they are involved in endocytosis rather than exocytosis.
source_span: The cytoplasmic surface of these invaginations was also coated with a radiating , bristle-like structure ... reminiscent of the coat of specialized invaginations involved in endocytosis ... indicating that these invaginations are not exocytic cups .
selection_reasoning: This suggests a mechanism for uptake of extracellular material, addressing a key unknown in parasite biology.

fact: Toxoplasma gondii salvages essential metabolites, including lipids, from host cells to replicate and produce infectious progeny.
source_span: Toxoplasma gondii needs to salvage many essential metabolites , including lipids , from host cells to replicate and produce infectious progeny [75].
selection_reasoning: This fact provides critical background on the parasite's metabolic needs and motivates the study of lipid acquisition.

fact: Toxoplasma exploits host lipid droplets by relocating them to the parasitophorous vacuole and salvaging neutral lipids stored in these structures.
source_span: In this study , we demonstrated that Toxoplasma exploits host LD by relocating them to the PV and salvaging neutral lipids stored in these structures.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding showing how the parasite accesses host lipid stores.

fact: Host lipid droplets are important for Toxoplasma infectivity, as parasite growth is reduced in mutant cells depleted of lipid droplets and partially recovers when transferred to normal cells.
source_span: Additionally , we provide evidence that host LD are important for parasite infectivity: first , Toxoplasma growth is reduced in mutant MEF largely depleted of LD via the genetic ablation of DGAT1 and DGAT2 ( D1D2KO ) ; and second , parasites repetitively cultivated in D1D2KO cells , partially regain their growth capability when transferred to WT MEF.
selection_reasoning: This fact links host lipid droplets to parasite growth and infectivity, highlighting biological significance.

fact: During Toxoplasma infection, the number and distribution of host lipid droplets change dynamically, with an initial increase and clustering around the parasitophorous vacuole coinciding with parasite replication.
source_span: During a Toxoplasma infection , the number of LD in the host cell fluctuates . Initially , the host LD population progressively increases , with a peak coincident with the first round of parasite replication ( ~8 h post-invasion ) . At this time , the global distribution of host LD is also prominently modified as many host LD cluster around the PV , and the transcription of host DGAT2 is concomitantly upregulated , suggesting a stimulation of TAG synthesis in LD .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes host cell lipid droplet dynamics relevant to parasite development.

fact: Host lipid droplets remain accumulated around the parasitophorous vacuole even after their number declines later in infection.
source_span: After that period of time , the host LD number declines and hsDGAT2 expression decreases but the vast majority of host LD remain accumulated around the PV .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights sustained host lipid droplet localization near the parasite, relevant for nutrient access.

fact: Toxoplasma may benefit from host lipid droplets not only for their lipid content but also for enzymatic activities associated with lipid droplets.
source_span: Toxoplasma may attract and retain host LD to its PV not just for their lipid content but also to take advantage of the enzymatic activities associated with LD .
selection_reasoning: This suggests a broader functional significance of host lipid droplets in parasite biology.

fact: The parasite is sensitive to inhibition of host adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) activity, implying that host lipolysis affects parasite growth.
