fact: Amacrine cells modulate transmission of different frequency components in visual input by acting on intrinsic properties of bipolar cells, including dendritic input tuning and synaptic terminal calcium dynamics.
source_span: The general picture that emerges is one in which amacrine cells modulate transmission of different frequency components in the visual input by acting on the background of at least two intrinsic properties varying between BCs: tuning of dendritic inputs summed at the cell body and the filter determining calcium dynamics in the synaptic terminal providing the output (Figure 3G) [62].
selection_reasoning: This integrates cellular and circuit-level mechanisms relevant to frequency tuning and signal processing.

fact: The synaptic filter that shapes bipolar cell output varies between different outputs because of variations in the intrinsic property of synaptic terminal volume.
source_span: The key new idea that we propose here is that this synaptic filter varies between different outputs because of variations in an intrinsic property of the synaptic compartment—its volume.
selection_reasoning: This is a central novel conceptual claim of the study linking terminal volume to functional diversity.

fact: The visual system separates signals encoding different stimulus aspects into parallel ON and OFF pathways beginning in distinct types of bipolar cells.
source_span: It has long been recognized that the visual system separates signals encoding different aspects of a stimulus for transmission through different pathways or “channels.” The most fundamental of these parallel representations is the separation of ON and OFF signals, which begins in distinct types of BC [63].
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological context and importance of studying bipolar cell diversity.

fact: More than ten morphologically distinct types of bipolar cells exist in the vertebrate retina, with probably more than 20 types in zebrafish, but their response property differences are not fully understood.
source_span: More than ten types of morphologically distinct BCs can be recognized in the vertebrate retina, and probably more than 20 in zebrafish [64], [65], but we still do not fully understand how these differ in their response properties.
selection_reasoning: This motivates the study by highlighting gaps in knowledge about bipolar cell functional diversity.

fact: Different synaptic terminals of a single bipolar cell can be functionally isolated, allowing divergence of different signals from one neuron.
source_span: More recent work indicates that it might be more fruitful to focus on the synaptic terminal as the fundamental unit of signal transmission, which would allow for divergence of different signals from the one neuron [11]. Implicit in this idea is the notion that the different synaptic outputs of a neuron are functionally isolated from each other, at least to some extent.
selection_reasoning: This conceptual framework underpins the study’s focus on terminal-level mechanisms.

fact: Connecting processes between bipolar cell terminals provide a sufficient diffusional barrier to keep calcium signals local to individual terminals.
source_span: Simultaneous measurements of calcium signals in connected terminals demonstrate that the answer is yes: connecting processes provide a sufficient diffusional barrier to allow calcium signals with different amplitudes and kinetics to remain local to individual terminals (Figure 3).
selection_reasoning: This experimental evidence supports the functional isolation of synaptic terminals.

fact: Presynaptic heterogeneity, including differences in synaptic terminal properties, has been observed in sensory pathways of insects, suggesting a conserved mechanism across species.
source_span: Such presynaptic heterogeneity has previously been observed in sensory pathways of insects, including cricket auditory afferents [67] and Drosophila olfactory receptor neurons [68].
selection_reasoning: This places the findings in a broader biological context, indicating relevance beyond vertebrates.

fact: The study used transgenic zebrafish expressing SyGCaMP2.0 and sypHy to image calcium dynamics and vesicle release in bipolar cell terminals in vivo.
source_span: Transgenic zebrafish expressing SyGCaMP2.0 and sypHy were maintained on a 14/10 h light/dark cycle at 28°C... Fish were imaged as described previously [13].
selection_reasoning: This high-level methodological fact is important to understand how the principal findings were obtained.

fact: Imaging was performed using multiphoton microscopy to measure calcium signals and vesicle release in the live zebrafish retina under controlled light stimulation.
source_span: Imaging was performed using a custom-built multiphoton microscope... Full-field light stimuli were delivered using an amber LED... The retina was imaged through an Olympus LUMPlanFI 40× water immersion objective.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key experimental approach enabling functional measurements in vivo.

fact: Optical measurements in the live retina produce a low-photopic background light level due to laser and fluorophore emission activating photoreceptors, which partially saturates rods and adapts cones.
source_span: Importantly, optical measurements in the live retina necessarily give rise to a background activation of photoreceptors... rods are typically saturated, and cones partially adapted, giving rise to a low-photopic background light-level.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains an important experimental consideration affecting interpretation of visual responses.

fact: The zebrafish retina is cone dominated, resulting in weaker background illumination from laser scanning compared to species like rabbits.
source_span: However , this background illumination was weaker than typically observed in e . g . , rabbit [70] , presumably as the zebrafish retina is cone dominated .
selection_reasoning: This background difference is important for understanding the visual system context and experimental conditions in zebrafish, which is likely a core background fact.

fact: Following activation of laser scanning in in vivo experiments, a 30-second wait was used before additional visual stimulation to allow retinal adaptation to background light levels.
source_span: Nevertheless , following activation of the laser scanning , we typically waited 30 seconds before commencing with additional visual stimulation to ensure the retina adapted to the background levels attributed to the laser .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key methodological step ensuring valid measurement of retinal responses under controlled adaptation conditions.

fact: Synaptic terminals in the zebrafish retina were detected and analyzed using image averaging and a filtering algorithm based on a Laplace operator followed by thresholding.
source_span: ROIs corresponding to terminals within these averaged images were defined using a filtering algorithm based on a Laplace operator followed by application of a threshold , as described in detail in [17] .
selection_reasoning: This high-level method for identifying synaptic terminals is central to the study's measurement approach.

fact: Terminal sizes in the zebrafish retina were similar across different fish, and terminal size influenced adaptation kinetics of synaptic responses.
source_span: Average terminal sizes were similar between different fish ( Figure S5A ) and the effects of terminal size on adaptation kinetics could be observed in individual fish ( Figure S5B ) as well as in data averaged over multiple fish ( Figure 6C ) .
selection_reasoning: Terminal size effects on adaptation kinetics are a key biological finding relevant to synaptic function.

fact: The SyGCaMP2 indicator showed larger estimated terminal sizes compared to sypHy or Synaptophysin-EGFP, likely due to its greater overall brightness.
source_span: However , the distribution of estimated terminal sizes in SyGCaMP2 was shifted to larger values , compared to sypHy or Synaptophysin-EGFP fish ( Figure S1H ) . This is likely explained by the greater overall brightness of SyGCaMP2 .
selection_reasoning: This fact relates to the interpretation of imaging data and the choice of fluorescent indicators, important for understanding measurement differences.

fact: The microscope used had a z-resolution of approximately 2 µm, sufficient to avoid underestimating terminal size and to exclude out-of-focus terminals from the signal.
source_span: The z-resolution of the microscope was ∼2 µm . Given an average radius of just above 1 micron per terminal , this resolution was therefore large enough to avoid underestimating the size of terminals traversed non-centrally by the optical plane , but small enough to avoid out-of-focus terminals contributing to the signal .
selection_reasoning: This technical fact supports the reliability of terminal size measurements, relevant to data validity.

fact: The fraction of total vesicles released per second (V'exo) in synaptic terminals was calculated from sypHy fluorescence signals using a formula involving fluorescence intensity and vesicle retrieval rate constants.
source_span: V′exo , the fraction of total vesicles in the terminal released per second , was calculated from the sypHy signal according to the equation: ( 1 ) where F is the average fluorescence intensity over the terminal at time t , Fmin is the intensity when the rate of vesicle release is at a minimum , and kendo is the rate-constant of vesicle retrieval .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key quantitative measure of synaptic vesicle release central to the study's findings.

fact: Goldfish retinal slices were used for whole-cell recordings from large synaptic terminals or bipolar cell somas to measure calcium dynamics with a low-affinity Ca2+ indicator.
source_span: Slices of goldfish retina were perfused with extracellular solution ... Whole cell recordings were obtained from “large” terminals ( diameter: 4–12 µm ) or from the soma of “mixed” BCs using 8–12 MΩ patch electrodes [71] ... and 100 µM of the hexapotassium salt of the low affinity Ca2+ indicator OGB-5N .
selection_reasoning: This high-level description of experimental preparation and measurement is central to the methods used to study synaptic calcium.

fact: Calcium indicator OGB-5N signals were imaged at 40 Hz and converted to estimates of absolute calcium concentration in bipolar cell terminals.
source_span: OGB-5N was imaged at 40 Hz using an electron multiplying charge coupled device ( EM CCD ) camera ( Hamamatsu C9100 ) . Subsequent image analysis was performed using ImageJ , Igor Pro , and Matlab . OGB-5N signals were quantified as changes in fluorescence relative to background fluorescence at each pixel ( ΔF/Fo ) and converted to estimates of absolute Ca2+ concentration: ( 2 )
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the key measurement and quantification approach for calcium dynamics, important for interpreting results.

fact: Resting calcium concentration in bipolar cell terminals is approximately 50 nM, which is much lower than the Kd of the calcium indicator OGB-5N (20 µM).
source_span: Since resting Ca2+ in bipolar terminals ( ∼50 nM [30] ) is much lower than the Kd of OGB-5N ( 20 µM ) we assumed that Frest = Fmin .
selection_reasoning: This background fact is important for understanding the calibration and interpretation of calcium imaging data.

fact: Marburg virus, Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), and Dengue virus activate and benefit from expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2).
source_span: Marburg virus , the Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus ( KSHV ) and Dengue virus all activate , and benefit from , expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes the known role of Nrf2 activation in viral infections, providing context for studying Nrf2's impact on HIV.

fact: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection had not been tested prior to this study.
source_span: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus ( HIV ) infection has not been tested .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the knowledge gap motivating the study.

fact: Sulforaphane (SFN), a compound produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage, mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression.
source_span: Sulforaphane ( SFN ) , produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage , mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression .
selection_reasoning: This explains the natural source and biological role of SFN as an Nrf2 activator, relevant to the study's intervention.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.
source_span: Here we show for the first time that SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding demonstrating cell-type specific antiviral activity of SFN.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines but not in other tested cell lines.
source_span: Similarly SFN blocks infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines , but not in other cell lines tested .
selection_reasoning: This finding extends the antiviral effect of SFN to macrophage-like cell lines, supporting the specificity of the effect.

fact: siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 increases HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduces the antiviral effects of SFN treatment.
source_span: siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduced the anti-viral effects of SFN treatment .
selection_reasoning: This supports the conclusion that SFN's antiviral activity is mediated through Nrf2.

fact: SFN treatment blocks HIV infection after viral entry but before the formation of 2-LTR circles, similar to the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.
source_span: We further found that , like the type I interferon-induced cellular anti-viral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2 , SFN treatment blocks infection after entry , but before formation of 2-LTR circles .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the stage of viral replication inhibited by SFN, important for understanding the mechanism.

fact: SFN does not upregulate the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during its inhibition of HIV infection.
source_span: Interestingly however , neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated .
selection_reasoning: This distinguishes SFN's mechanism from other known antiviral pathways.

fact: Nrf2 activation can potently block HIV infection, highlighting a novel way to trigger this inhibition.
source_span: This shows for the first time that Nrf2 action can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition .
selection_reasoning: This is a key conclusion emphasizing the significance of the findings.

fact: Highly active anti-retroviral treatment (HAART) is effective but has high financial costs, emergence of resistant viruses, and side effects, motivating the search for new therapeutic alternatives.
source_span: Highly active anti-retroviral treatment ( HAART ) is saving countless lives , however its application is accompanied by high financial costs , the emergence of resistant viruses and short- and long-term side-effects . A better understanding of how to activate cellular anti-viral defenses promises new therapeutic alternatives to overcome these limitations and to support prevention and cure strategies .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the clinical relevance and motivation for exploring Nrf2 activation as a therapeutic strategy.

fact: Macrophages play a critical role in HIV infection and pathogenesis by forming long-lived viral reservoirs and carrying virus into restricted compartments like the brain.
source_span: These cells play a critical role in HIV infection and pathogenesis , forming long-lived viral reservoirs [1 , 2] and carrying virus into restricted compartments like the brain [3] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important disease context explaining why targeting macrophages is significant.

fact: Most monocytes are largely refractory to HIV infection until they differentiate into macrophages, but a small subset may be readily infectable even in HAART-treated patients.
source_span: Most monocytes , precursors of macrophages , are largely refractory to HIV infection until they differentiate to replenish the macrophage pool [4 , 5] . A small but specific subset of these cells however may be readily infectable , even in HAART-treated patients [6–9] .
selection_reasoning: This fact further clarifies the infection dynamics relevant to macrophage targeting.

fact: Infected macrophages have been observed in both asymptomatic untreated patients and HAART-treated individuals.
source_span: Infected macrophages have been observed in asymptomatic , untreated patients [10] and in HAART-treated individuals [11] .
selection_reasoning: This supports the clinical importance of macrophage infection in HIV persistence.

fact: Macrophages can increase T cell infection and may exacerbate T cell depletion in HIV-infected individuals.
source_span: Importantly , macrophages can powerfully increase T cell infection [14] and may thereby exacerbate T cell depletion in infected individuals .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the pathogenic role of macrophages in HIV disease progression.

fact: SFN is absorbed in the human gut and reaches peak plasma levels within 90 minutes after consumption.
source_span: In humans SFN is absorbed in the gut and peak plasma levels are achieved within 90 minutes [16] .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the translational relevance of SFN as a dietary compound with systemic bioavailability.

fact: SFN activates Nrf2 by modifying KEAP1, preventing Nrf2 degradation and allowing it to translocate into the nucleus to initiate transcription of antioxidant response genes.
source_span: SFN and other Nrf2-activators modify KEAP1 to prevent engagement of Nrf2 [27] . As Nrf2 accumulates , it translocates into the nucleus , partners with musculoaponeurotic fibrosarcoma protein ( Maf ) and initiates transcription from antioxidant response elements ( ARE ) .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic fact explains how SFN activates Nrf2, relevant to understanding the antiviral effect.

fact: Unlike Marburg virus, Dengue virus, and KSHV which benefit from increased Nrf2 expression, HIV infection is blocked through Nrf2 activation.
source_span: Together this work shows that , in contrast to Marburg , Dengue and KSHV , HIV is blocked through Nrf2 and sets the stage for discovering the mechanism underlying this restriction .
selection_reasoning: This contrast highlights the novel and unique role of Nrf2 in HIV infection.

fact: Sulforaphane (SFN) blocks single-round HIV-1 infections in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages (hMDMs) but not in primary T cells.
source_span: Thus, SFN acts to block single-round HIV-1 infections in primary hMDMs but not in primary T cells.
selection_reasoning: This is a core finding about the cell-type specificity of SFN's antiviral effect, central to the study's main claim.

fact: SFN treatment markedly decreases HIV infection in monocytoid U937 and THP1 cells differentiated into macrophage-like cells but does not inhibit infection in HeLa, HEK293T, or GHOST cells.
source_span: We detected no inhibition of HIV infection after SFN treatment in HeLa, HEK293T or GHOST cells but SFN markedly decreased evidence of infection in U937 and THP1 cultures.
selection_reasoning: This fact expands on the breadth of SFN's antiviral action across different cell types, important for understanding its specificity.

fact: SFN reduces HIV infection in PMA-differentiated THP1 cells by 50% at concentrations between 2.5 and 5 μM.
source_span: Further titration of SFN in cultures of PMA-differentiated THP1 cells shows that infections can be reduced by 50% when cultures are treated with SFN in the 2.5 to 5 μM range.
selection_reasoning: This provides a key quantitative measure of SFN's antiviral potency in a relevant macrophage model.

fact: SFN does not block HIV infection by increasing levels of the antiviral protein SAMHD1 in U937 cells.
source_span: We immunoblotted lysates of mock- and SFN-treated U937 cells for SAMHD1 and found that while SAMHD1 was readily detected in THP1 lysates, it remained undetectable in U937 lysates under the conditions tested. This indicates that SFN does not block HIV by increasing SAMHD1 levels.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the mechanism of SFN action by ruling out SAMHD1 induction as the cause of antiviral activity.

fact: SFN-mediated impairment of HIV infection is not due to decreased cell viability as indicated by sustained metabolic activity in multiple cell types.
source_span: Overall these data indicate that SFN mediated impairment of HIV infection is not due to decreased cell viability as indicated by sustained metabolic activity.
selection_reasoning: This addresses a critical alternative explanation, supporting that SFN's antiviral effect is not cytotoxicity.

fact: The antiviral effect induced by SFN treatment in THP1-derived macrophages is reversible and the duration of infection block depends on the SFN dose.
source_span: These data show that the anti-viral effect induced by SFN treatment is reversible and that the SFN dose determines the duration over which the anti-viral state is maintained.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the dynamics and dose-dependence of SFN's antiviral state, important for therapeutic considerations.

fact: SFN blocks infection by both HIV-1 and HIV-2 in a manner that is not dependent on the reporter gene used to measure infection.
source_span: The loss of luciferase signal after SFN treatment in HIV-2-infected cultures paralleled that in the HIV-1-infected cultures... These results demonstrate that our observations, showing an SFN-mediated infection block, are not reporter-dependent.
selection_reasoning: This confirms the robustness of SFN's antiviral effect across virus types and measurement methods.

fact: The similarity of SFN's antiviral effect on HIV-1 and HIV-2 suggests that SAMHD1 is not responsible for the infection block because HIV-2 Vpx would be expected to overcome SAMHD1 restriction.
source_span: The similarity between the results for HIV-1 and HIV-2 further indicate that SAMHD1 is not responsible for the block because HIV-2 Vpx would be expected to at least partially overcome that restriction.
selection_reasoning: This provides mechanistic insight supporting that SFN acts independently of SAMHD1-mediated restriction.

fact: SFN pretreatment blocks HIV infection at or before reporter production from integrated proviruses.
source_span: We exploited the characteristics of VSV-G-pseudotyped, env (‒) reporter viruses to determine that SFN pretreatment blocks infection at or before reporter production from integrated proviruses.
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies the stage of viral replication targeted by SFN, key to understanding its antiviral mechanism.

fact: Continuous SFN treatment reduces replication of the dual-tropic, replication-competent HIV-1 strain 89.6 in primary human macrophages to background levels.
source_span: Both western blotting and antigen-capture ELISA were employed. The concentration of viral capsid in the cell supernatant increased steadily in the vehicle control, however in the AZT- and 10 μM SFN-treated samples it decreased from residual input levels to background levels.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates SFN's efficacy against a clinically relevant, replication-competent HIV strain in primary macrophages.

fact: SFN treatment does not reduce mitochondrial dehydrogenase activity in primary human macrophages during 14 days of continuous treatment, indicating no loss of cell viability.
source_span: Continuous SFN treatment did not reduce cellular dehydrogenase activity relative to the vehicle only control.
selection_reasoning: This supports the safety profile of SFN in primary macrophages during prolonged antiviral treatment.

fact: The HIV-1 89.6 envelope glycoprotein can mediate fusion between adjacent macrophages, allowing SFN to inhibit virus replication in these cell cultures.
source_span: The HIV-1 89 . 6 Env glycoprotein can mediate fusion between adjacent macrophages , making inhibition of virus replication by SFN and AZT readily apparent in the cell cultures ( Fig 5C ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the biological context in which SFN inhibits HIV replication, relevant to understanding the antiviral effect.

fact: Continuous treatment with 10 μM SFN for 14 days does not reduce mitochondrial dehydrogenase activity in macrophage cultures, indicating SFN is not toxic to these cells.
source_span: Continuous SFN treatment did not reduce cellular dehydrogenase activity relative to the vehicle only control ( Fig 5D ) .
selection_reasoning: Demonstrating SFN's lack of toxicity supports its potential therapeutic relevance.

fact: SFN significantly hinders infection by HIV-1 89.6 envelope glycoprotein-pseudotyped virus in single-round infections.
source_span: As in the experiments with the VSV-G-pseudotyped virus , SFN significantly hindered infection with the HIV-1 89 . 6 envelope glycoprotein-pseudotyped virus ( Fig 5E ) .
selection_reasoning: This shows SFN's antiviral effect extends to viruses bearing the HIV envelope, a key finding.

fact: SFN inhibits both single-round and spreading HIV infections, including those with HIV envelope glycoprotein and VSV-G-pseudotyped virus.
source_span: Overall , this set of experiments shows that SFN hinders both single-round and spreading infections . It further demonstrates that SFN interferes with infection of virus bearing the HIV envelope glycoprotein as it also interferes with VSV-G-pseudotyped virus .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the broad antiviral activity of SFN, central to the study's main claim.

fact: The SFN-mediated block to HIV infection is independent of exogenous reporter genes and cannot be reversed by the Nef protein.
source_span: Finally , it also supports that our observation of SFN-mediated HIV inhibition is independent from exogenous reporter genes and shows that the SFN mediated block cannot be reversed by the Nef protein , which was absent from the luciferase and GFP reporter viruses .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the mechanism and robustness of SFN's antiviral effect.

fact: SFN acts through the transcription factor Nrf2 to execute most of its known functions.
source_span: SFN acts through Nrf2 to execute the majority of its known functions [44–46] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact is necessary to understand the hypothesized mechanism of SFN's antiviral action.

fact: Other Nrf2 activators, dimethyl fumarate (DMF) and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), also block HIV infection in single-round macrophage infections with minimal toxicity.
source_span: We found that like SFN , DMF and EGCG hinder reporter virus expression in single-round HIV-1 infections of PMA-differentiated THP1 cells and exhibit minimal toxicity ( Fig 6A–6C and S2A–S2C Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the role of Nrf2 activation in blocking HIV infection, reinforcing the mechanism.

fact: EGCG blocks infection by VSV-G-pseudotyped HIV, indicating its antiviral effect is not due to blocking gp120/CD4 interaction.
source_span: Our observation that EGCG blocked VSV-G-pseudotyped virus eliminates the possibility that EGCG is thwarting a specific gp120/CD4 interaction in our system [48] .
selection_reasoning: This fact helps clarify the mechanism of EGCG and by extension Nrf2 activators in HIV inhibition.

fact: Pretreatment with SFN, DMF, or EGCG inhibits HIV reporter gene expression in macrophages, suggesting these compounds act before viral transcription.
source_span: While pretreatment with AZT , SFN , DMF or EGCG significantly inhibited luciferase activity , treatment after infection had much less or no impact . This suggests that each compound is likely acting before transcription in THP-1 infections , although we cannot rule out some impact after integration , especially for SFN .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the stage of viral replication targeted by these compounds, important for understanding their antiviral mechanism.

fact: SFN is a more potent inhibitor of HIV reporter activity than DMF or EGCG in pretreated macrophage cultures.
source_span: Neither DMF nor EGCG suppressed reporter activity to the same degree as SFN in pretreated cultures , perhaps because SFN is one of the most potent naturally occurring Nrf2 activators [49–52] or because SFN may also have an additional , albeit smaller , impact after proviral integration .
selection_reasoning: This highlights SFN's superior antiviral potency among tested Nrf2 activators.

fact: Depletion of Nrf2 in primary human macrophages increases HIV infection, indicating that basal Nrf2 levels restrict HIV replication.
source_span: In the absence of SFN , depletion of Nrf2 caused a significant increase in luciferase activity indicating that Nrf2 is detrimental to HIV infection in macrophages and that the basal level of Nrf2 that is present in macrophages is sufficient for establishing some anti-viral activity ( Fig 6D ) .
selection_reasoning: This provides direct evidence that Nrf2 restricts HIV infection.

fact: SFN treatment increases Nrf2 protein levels in primary human macrophages, partially counteracting siRNA-mediated Nrf2 depletion.
source_span: Specific siRNA transfection reduced Nrf2 protein levels , but SFN treatment restored Nrf2 expression to levels seen in untreated cultures .
selection_reasoning: This supports the mechanism that SFN enhances Nrf2 to block HIV infection.

fact: Nrf2 levels are inversely proportional to HIV infection levels in primary human macrophages, both with and without SFN treatment.
source_span: Importantly however , Nrf2 levels remained inversely proportional to infection levels even in the absence of SFN .
selection_reasoning: This fact strengthens the link between Nrf2 expression and HIV restriction.

fact: The Nrf2-dependent protein NQO1 levels correlate inversely with HIV infectability in macrophages, decreasing with Nrf2 depletion and increasing with SFN treatment.
source_span: If Nrf2 triggers expression of a protein or an RNA with anti-viral function , then we also expect levels of the Nrf2-dependent protein NQO1 to be inversely proportional to infectability . As expected in this scenario , NQO1 levels fell below constitutive quantities upon siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 and increased well above the base line in non-targeting siRNA-transfected cultures treated with 10 μM SFN .
selection_reasoning: This supports that Nrf2-dependent gene expression mediates the antiviral effect.

fact: Overall, HIV infection of primary human macrophages is restricted by Nrf2, and SFN enhances this restriction by increasing Nrf2 function.
source_span: Overall these data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in hMDMs that is enhanced , here , by SFN treatment .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the principal mechanistic conclusion of the study.

fact: Sulforaphane (SFN) blocks HIV-1 and HIV-2 infection in primary human macrophages by enhancing an Nrf2-dependent restriction.
source_span: Overall these data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in hMDMs that is enhanced , here , by SFN treatment . SFN blocks single-round HIV-1 and HIV-2 infections ( Fig 4 ) .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking SFN treatment to Nrf2-dependent inhibition of HIV infection in macrophages.

fact: The SFN-mediated block to HIV infection occurs after viral entry and reverse transcription but before 2-LTR circle formation and proviral integration in macrophages.
source_span: This limits the Nrf2-mediated block to steps that extend from attachment of the virus to the cell through transcription from the provirus . ... The vehicle- and SFN-treated samples showed similar levels of late reverse transcription product , indicating that SFN , unlike AZT , did not hinder replication steps from viral entry through reverse transcription ( Fig 7A ) . When we tested for 2-LTR circles ... we found that these were clearly decreased in the AZT and SFN samples relative to the vehicle controls ( Fig 7B ) . Alu-PCR , testing for integrated proviral sequences , also showed that these were similarly decreased in AZT- and SFN-treated cultures to levels that were significantly lower than in the vehicle-treated controls ( Fig 7C ) .
selection_reasoning: This defines the key mechanistic window of SFN's antiviral action, a core scientific claim.

fact: SFN increases Nrf2 protein levels and the expression of Nrf2-regulated antioxidant genes such as NQO1 and GCLM in macrophage-like cells.
source_span: As expected , SFN significantly increased levels of Nrf2 as well as of the Nrf2-regulated genes NQO1 and GCLM ( Fig 8 ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the mechanism by which SFN enhances Nrf2 activity, central to the study's main question.

fact: The antiviral restriction mediated by SFN in macrophages does not involve upregulation of the interferon-inducible antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2.
source_span: SFN did not significantly change levels of either SAMHD1 or MX2 . Conversely , IFNα treatment increased levels of MX2 as expected . SAMHD1 levels , despite some donor-to-donor variation , did not change significantly in response to IFNα , nor did the levels of Nrf2 , NQO1 or GCLM .
selection_reasoning: This distinguishes the SFN/Nrf2 antiviral mechanism from classical interferon responses, clarifying the unique pathway involved.

fact: Macrophages express sufficient basal levels of Nrf2 to partially restrict HIV infection even without SFN treatment.
source_span: Importantly , we found that macrophages express sufficient Nrf2 to maintain a partial restriction even in the absence of SFN .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the physiological relevance of Nrf2 in macrophage antiviral defense.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in macrophages regardless of whether viral entry is mediated by HIV Env or VSV-G glycoproteins, indicating a post-entry block.
source_span: We found that SFN counters infection whether viral entry is mediated through HIV Env or VSV-G glycoproteins ( Figs 1B versus 5E ) . This suggests a post-entry block as these glycoproteins engage different entry mechanisms .
selection_reasoning: This supports the conclusion that SFN acts after viral entry, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: SFN reduces the number of infected macrophages rather than suppressing viral transcription in already infected cells.
source_span: The fraction of those infected cells closely paralleled the population-wide reporter activity measured with the luciferase reporter virus . This indicates that the SFN-mediated block reduced the number of infected cells rather than suppressing transcription from similar numbers of infected cells .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the nature of the antiviral effect, important for understanding SFN's mode of action.

fact: SFN does not inhibit HIV infection in all cell types, indicating that its antiviral effect is macrophage-specific and dependent on Nrf2.
source_span: SFN does not block infection in all cell-types and ... the dependence in macrophages solely on Nrf2 also indicates that SFN is neither inhibiting HIV directly by modifying a viral component nor is it modifying and thereby inhibiting a cellular component that the virus needs for successful infection .
selection_reasoning: This fact is important for the translational relevance and specificity of SFN's antiviral action.

fact: Previous studies showed that dimethyl fumarate (DMF) and monomethyl fumarate (MMF) also attenuate HIV infection in macrophages by increasing Nrf2 levels, similar to SFN.
source_span: Our findings also put into perspective previous work that tested the neuroprotective effects of di- and monomethyl fumarate ( MMF ) . This study showed that DMF and MMF can attenuate spreading HIV infections in hMDMs [40] . ... DMF and MMF , like SFN , increase levels of Nrf2 [55] , suggesting that these compounds also block HIV in macrophages through Nrf2 .
selection_reasoning: This situates the current findings within the broader context of Nrf2-activating compounds as potential HIV inhibitors.

fact: The SFN-mediated antiviral restriction in macrophages is distinct from interferon-induced antiviral responses and does not involve known antiviral gene products regulated by Nrf2 in other cell types.
source_span: None of the genes known to be modulated by Nrf2 direct production of recognized anti-viral products [28] . It is however possible that Nrf2 initiates a different expression pattern in macrophages than it does in previously tested B lymphocyte-derived cell lines [28] .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the novelty and cell-type specificity of the antiviral mechanism discovered.

fact: Sulforaphane (SFN) blocks HIV infection in human macrophages more effectively at lower concentrations than dimethyl fumarate (DMF).
source_span: Interestingly , in our experiments SFN blocked infections more effectively at lower concentrations than DMF did [40] .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key comparative finding about the potency of SFN versus DMF in blocking HIV, central to the study's main claim.

fact: SFN and other Nrf2 stimulators can be used therapeutically to block HIV infection of macrophages and possibly other important HIV target cells.

fact: Retro (pseudo)genes originate through reverse transcription of mRNAs and insertion into the genome, creating intronless gene copies.
source_span: Retro ( pseudo ) genes are gene copies that originate through the process of reverse transcription of mRNAs and their subsequent insertion into the genome . This process , called retroposition is usually mediated by enzymes provided by retrotransposable elements and creates intronless copies of existing genes [1] .
selection_reasoning: Provides essential background on the biological mechanism underlying the study.

fact: Retrocopies were long considered nonfunctional 'junk DNA' due to lack of parental gene promoters, but recent findings show some are functional as protein-coding genes or regulatory RNAs.
source_span: Due to the lack of promoter sequence of their parental genes , retrocopies were long assumed to be nonfunctional and simply “junk DNA” . However , multiple findings challenged that view and a few mechanisms were proposed for retrogene transcription [2] . Functional retrocopies ( retrogenes ) may have an intact open reading frame and thus be protein-coding , but can also act as long noncoding RNAs [3] , sources of short interfering RNAs [4] and microRNA sponges [5] .
selection_reasoning: Explains the functional relevance of retrocopies, important for interpreting study implications.

fact: Retrogenes can undergo neofunctionalization more often than other gene copies due to loss of parental regulatory sequences and recruitment of new regulatory elements.
source_span: The loss of parental regulatory sequences and potential replacement with those recruited from the new locus of integration is believed to be the most possible reason that retrogenes are able to undergo neofunctionalization more often than other types of gene copies [6] and take part in the shaping of lineage- and species-specific features [7] .
selection_reasoning: Provides mechanistic insight into how retrocopies can gain new functions, relevant to evolutionary and functional significance.

fact: Retrogenes can replace their parental genes in some cases.
source_span: As recently shown , retrogenes can also replace their parental genes [8] .
selection_reasoning: Highlights an important functional role of retrogenes.

fact: Retrocopies serve as useful phylogenetic markers for studying evolutionary processes such as sex chromosome origin and retrotransposable element activity.
source_span: Apart from their functionality , retrocopies are also useful phylogenetic markers , providing insight into such evolutionary processes as sex chromosome origination [9] or changes in retrotransposable element activity and germ line gene expression [2] .
selection_reasoning: Explains the broader significance of retrocopies beyond gene function.

fact: Many retrogenes are important for health and disease, including tumor suppressors and genes involved in genetic disorders and viral resistance.
source_span: In recent years , numerous studies have shown that many retrogenes are vitally important and a number of them are involved in diseases . A good example is the RHOB gene ( ras homolog gene family member B [MIM: 165370] ) , a tumor suppressor that belongs to the Rho GTPases family [10] . A mutation in another retrogene , RNF113A ( ring finger protein 113A [MIM: 300951] ) , results in trichothiodystrophy [11] . On the other hand , insertion of the PPIA cDNA ( peptidyl-prolyl isomerase A [MIM: 123840] ) into the TRIM5 gene ( tripartite motif-containing protein 5 [MIM: 608487] ) confers resistance to HIV in owl monkeys [12] .
selection_reasoning: Demonstrates clinical and translational relevance of retrogenes.

source_span: Recent developments in sequencing technology allow researchers to move beyond the analysis of individual genomes from model organisms to the study of retrocopies within a population . selection_reasoning: Explains the rationale and opportunity for population-level retrocopy studies.

As a result , this approach allows only for the detection of retrocopies that originated relatively recently in evolutionary history and show little sequence divergence compared to their parental genes .
selection_reasoning: Identifies limitations in existing methods, motivating the new approach developed.

fact: Evolutionary events leading to older retrocopy variations in the human lineage have been less explored.

Presence or absence of a functional retrocopy might have far reaching biological implications . Due to lack of reliable experimental data , these issues have thus far been ignored; yet , this will most certainly change in the near future .

fact: A total of 214 insertions and deletions (indels) affecting 190 retrocopies were identified in human genomes.

fact: Retroduplication variants (RDVs) affect both expressed and non-expressed retrocopies, but deletions of expressed retrocopies tend to have low allele frequencies, suggesting they are new or slightly deleterious.
source_span: RDVs seem to affect both expressed and non-expressed retrocopies indiscriminately , but their allele frequency for most deletions of expressed retrocopies is relatively low ( < 2% ) , suggesting that they are new or slightly deleterious .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding about the evolutionary dynamics and potential functional impact of retrocopy deletions.

fact: Eleven ancestral transcriptionally active retrogenes undergoing deletions were experimentally confirmed to be expressed.
source_span: We experimentally confirmed the expression of 11 ancestral transcriptionally active retrogenes undergoing deletions .
selection_reasoning: This supports the functional relevance of some retrocopies affected by deletions.

fact: One retrogene, retro_hsap_4873, is deleted in over 10% of alleles in African populations, while the other 10 have very low deletion frequencies.
source_span: The frequency of their deletion is very low with the exception of retrogene retro_hsap_4873 , which is absent in over 10% of alleles in African populations .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a notable population-specific deletion with potential evolutionary or functional significance.

fact: The expression, ancient origin, and low deletion rate of most ancestral expressed retrocopies suggest possible functionality, though further studies are needed to confirm this.
source_span: The expression , ancient origin and low rate of deletion of the remaining 10 retrocopies may suggest some functionality , but further studies would be required to establish their function and the possible consequences of their deletion .
selection_reasoning: This points to the potential biological importance of these retrocopies, a key implication.

fact: Retrogenes have been reported to tend to be expressed in the testis, possibly due to hypertranscription in spermatogenic cells or insertion near germline-expressed genes.
source_span: Numerous studies revealed a tendency of retrogenes to be expressed in the testis [9 , 26] . It has been hypothesized that this specific transcription may be the result of the hypertranscription state observed in meiotic and postmeiotic spermatogenic cells [27] . Alternatively , retrocopies could be preferentially inserted into actively transcribed , and therefore open chromatin [28] . Since the retroposition occurs in the germ line , retrocopies may be primarily inserted into , or near to genes expressed in the germ line , which may enable or enhance their expression in testis .
selection_reasoning: This background explains the biological context and hypotheses about retrocopy expression patterns.

fact: Expression analysis across 16 human organs confirmed testis-specific expression for only one retrogene, indicating many retrogenes have broad expression patterns.
source_span: To verify the tendency of retrocopies to be expressed in testis , we performed expression analysis on 16 cDNA libraries from various human organs . Our findings confirmed testis-specific expression of only one retrogene . This supports results from our previous studies , showing that many retrogenes have broad expression patterns [8] .
selection_reasoning: This finding refines previous assumptions about retrogene expression, relevant to understanding their function.

fact: Nine retrogenes show statistically significant differential expression between human populations, mostly between African and European groups.
source_span: Overall , we detected 9 retrogenes that undergo statistically significant differential expression . Similar to inter-population differences in RDVs frequencies , retrogene expression differences tend to coincide with geographical locations , with most differences occurring between African and European populations .
selection_reasoning: This is a key finding linking retrocopy expression variation to population differences.

fact: Differences in retrogene expression between populations likely arise from variation in regulatory sequences, but other factors like DNA methylation cannot be excluded.
source_span: Observed differences most likely arise from different frequencies of short sequence variants ( SNPs and indels ) in the regulatory sequences of the retrogenes studied , but we cannot exclude more complicated scenarios , such as variation in DNA methylation .
selection_reasoning: This provides mechanistic insight into population expression differences, important for interpretation.

fact: The functional implications of population differences in retrogene expression are currently unknown and require further study.
source_span: At this point , we still know very little concerning the functional implications of discovered expression differences , and this will require further study .
selection_reasoning: This states a key limitation and future direction relevant to the study's significance.

fact: Sequences similar to human genome patches, alternative assemblies, and genomic contaminations from viruses, bacteria, and parasites were excluded from analysis to ensure data quality.
source_span: Sequences that showed similarity to human genome patches and alternative assemblies ( GRCh37 . p10 , HuRef ) , as well as genomic contaminations from viruses , bacteria and parasitic organisms were excluded from further analysis .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains data filtering to ensure accurate retrocopy identification, relevant for understanding the study's methodological rigor.

fact: The study used a stringent retrocopy identification pipeline from RetrogeneDB to detect and characterize retrocopies in assembled genomic regions.
source_span: Finally , we applied the retrocopy identification pipeline from RetrogeneDB [19] to detect and characterize retrocopies in assembled genomic regions . The pipeline takes a very stringent approach to identifying gene copies that originated via retroposition .
selection_reasoning: Describes the key method used to identify retrocopies, central to the study's main question and approach.

fact: Retrocopies were identified based on whole proteome alignment to the genome, requiring at least 150 bp length, over 50% alignment identity and protein coverage, and loss of at least two introns.
source_span: The retrocopy identification process is based on the alignment of the whole proteome to the genome , using LAST software [36] . Observed alignments must meet numerous criteria to be considered retrocopies , including a length of at least 150 bp on the genomic sequence , alignment identity and protein coverage greater than 50% , and the loss of at least 2 introns inferred from the alignment .
selection_reasoning: Provides a high-level description of the criteria defining retrocopies, important for understanding the study's detection strategy.

fact: Novel retrogenes and insertion-deletion variants were experimentally confirmed by PCR in the genomes of 17 individuals from diverse origins.
source_span: Novel retrogenes and indels were confirmed experimentally by PCR in the genomes of 17 individuals from various origins ( S3 Table ) from Coriell Cell Repositories .
selection_reasoning: Highlights experimental validation of key findings, supporting the reliability of detected novel retrogenes.

fact: Expression of retrogenes was analyzed across multiple human tissues using cDNA panels covering heart, brain, placenta, lung, liver, skeletal muscle, kidney, pancreas, spleen, thymus, prostate, testis, ovary, small intestine, colon, and peripheral leukocytes.
source_span: Expression of retrogenes was analyzed in Multiple Tissue cDNA Panels from Clontech—Human MTC Panel I and II ( catalog no . 636742 and 636743 respectively ) . This set of tissues contained the following: heart , brain , placenta , lung , liver , skeletal muscle , kidney , pancreas , spleen , thymus , prostate , testis , ovary , small intestine w/o mucosal lining , colon and peripheral leukocyte cDNA .
selection_reasoning: Describes the key method for assessing retrogene expression across diverse tissues, relevant to understanding functional implications.

fact: Retrogene expression was further analyzed using RNA-Seq data from 10 individuals in five human populations and 16 human tissues from public datasets.
source_span: In order to analyze retrocopy expression , RNA-Seq samples from 10 individuals for each of 5 populations ( CEU , GBR , FIN , TSI , YRI ) from the Geuvadis RNA sequencing project [18] were used , as well as data for 16 human tissues from the Illumina Bodymap 2 . 0 project .
selection_reasoning: Indicates the use of large-scale transcriptomic data to assess population and tissue-specific expression, a principal finding approach.

fact: Retrocopies with normalized expression of at least 1 read per million mapped reads were considered expressed.
source_span: Only retrocopies with a normalized expression value of at least 1 RPM ( reads per million mapped reads ) , were considered to be expressed .
selection_reasoning: Defines the expression threshold used to identify biologically relevant retrogene expression, important for interpreting results.

fact: Significant differences in retrocopy expression between human populations were identified using DESeq2, requiring at least a twofold change and adjusted p-value less than 0.05.
source_span: Furthermore , the DESeq2 package [23] was used to search for significant differences in retrocopy expression between analyzed populations , requiring at least a 2 fold expression change and adjusted p-value less than 0 . 05 .
selection_reasoning: Describes the statistical approach to detect population-specific expression differences, a key finding related to genetic diversity.

fact: Yaws is a re-emerging endemic treponemal infection caused by Treponema pallidum ssp. pertenue.
source_span: Yaws is a re-emerging endemic treponemal infection caused by Treponema pallidum ssp. pertenue [1].
selection_reasoning: This provides essential background on the disease studied.

fact: Early yaws disease is characterized by papillomatous and ulcerative skin lesions, while late-stage disease involves skin lesions, bone involvement, and rarely destructive lesions of the nasopharynx.
source_span: Early disease is characterised by papillomatous and ulcerative skin lesions, whilst late stage disease is characterised by skin lesions, bony involvement, and rarely progression to destructive lesions of the nasopharynx.
selection_reasoning: This background helps understand the clinical presentation relevant to the study.

fact: Azithromycin at a dose of 30 mg/kg (maximum 2 g) is effective in treating yaws and is central to the WHO yaws eradication strategy.
source_span: Azithromycin (30mg/kg, maximum dose 2g) has recently been shown to be effective in the treatment of yaws and is now central to WHO’s yaws eradication strategy [2, 3].

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) of azithromycin at a lower dose (20 mg/kg, maximum 1 g) was previously conducted in two regions of Ghana for trachoma control.

fact: Despite several rounds of azithromycin MDA for trachoma, ongoing reporting of yaws cases in Ghana raises concerns about possible azithromycin resistance or alternative causes of skin lesions.

fact: Haemophilus ducreyi, the causative agent of chancroid, is a common cause of non-genital skin lesions in countries where yaws is endemic, complicating yaws diagnosis.
source_span: The epidemiology of yaws has been further complicated by the discovery that Haemophilus ducreyi, the causative agent of the ulcerative sexually transmitted disease chancroid, is a common cause of non-genital skin lesions in several countries where yaws is endemic [12, 13].
selection_reasoning: This fact explains diagnostic challenges relevant to the study.

fact: The study conducted a cross-sectional survey in thirty communities in two districts of Ghana where azithromycin MDA for trachoma had previously been conducted.

fact: In these Ghanaian communities previously treated with azithromycin MDA for trachoma, there was no evidence of ongoing transmission of yaws.

fact: The majority of ulcerative skin lesions in the study remain unexplained by either Treponema pallidum ssp. pertenue or Haemophilus ducreyi.

fact: Azithromycin resistance has emerged in other treponemal infections such as syphilis, but has not yet been documented in yaws.
source_span: Although resistance has yet to be documented in yaws, azithromycin resistance has emerged in other treponemal infections, notably syphilis [6–9].
selection_reasoning: This contextualizes the concern about resistance relevant to the study.

fact: Ghana remains a major focus of yaws transmission in Africa despite previous control programs using penicillin in the mid-20th century.
source_span: In the 1950s–60s and 1980s, two large yaws control programmes using penicillin were conducted in Ghana, successfully reducing the burden of the disease, but yaws has subsequently re-emerged throughout the country and Ghana remains a major focus of transmission in Africa.

source_span: H. ducreyi DNA was detected in 9/98 (9.2%) ulcers (from eight children).

selection_reasoning: Important finding regarding antibiotic resistance relevant to treatment and control strategies.

source_span: Our study highlights the poor specificity of clinical case reporting and the urgent need to integrate serology into clinical surveillance systems.

source_span: This study is the first to report on the impact of testing multiple skin lesions from the same individual . Of those with multiple tested lesions , we identified some whose PCR results were concordant between lesions and others where PCR results were discordant between lesions: only testing one lesion may result in the false assumption that all of a patient’s lesions have the same aetiology.

fact: Negative TPPA testing in all individuals suggests minimal transmission of treponemal diseases in children in the studied community.
source_span: The negative TPPA testing in all individuals in our study however , suggests there is minimal transmission of treponemal diseases in children in this community.

fact: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) produced in the mitochondrial respiratory chain act as primary signals for cellular adaptation but can also cause cell damage under hypoxia/reoxygenation conditions relevant to systemic diseases and transplantation.
source_span: Reactive oxygen species ( ROS ) produced in the mitochondrial respiratory chain ( RC ) are primary signals that modulate cellular adaptation to environment , and are also destructive factors that damage cells under the conditions of hypoxia/reoxygenation relevant for various systemic diseases or transplantation .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential background on the dual role of ROS in cell signaling and damage, framing the study's motivation and disease relevance.

fact: The study extended a rule-based model of mitochondrial complex III to include the entire respiratory chain, proton translocation, transmembrane potential, TCA cycle reactions, and substrate transport to mitochondria.
source_span: To perform such an investigation we extended our rule-based model of complex III in order to account for electron transport in the whole RC coupled to proton translocation , transmembrane electrochemical potential generation , TCA cycle reactions , and substrate transport to mitochondria .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key methodological advance enabling comprehensive analysis of ROS production mechanisms.

fact: The extended model fits respiratory electron fluxes measured in rat brain mitochondria fueled by succinate or pyruvate and malate, and captures NAD+ reduction dynamics by reverse electron transport from succinate through complex I.
source_span: It fits respiratory electron fluxes measured in rat brain mitochondria fueled by succinate or pyruvate and malate , and the dynamics of NAD+ reduction by reverse electron transport from succinate through complex I .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the model's validity and relevance to physiological mitochondrial function.

fact: ROS production is associated with levels of specific radicals of individual electron transporters and their combinations in complexes I and III.
source_span: Our analysis revealed an association of ROS production with levels of specific radicals of individual electron transporters and their combinations in species of complexes I and III .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key mechanistic insight into how ROS generation relates to electron transport chain components.

fact: The phenomenon of bistability, previously found in complex III, also applies to the whole mitochondrial respiratory chain, allowing switching between low and high free radical states.
source_span: It was found that the phenomenon of bistability , revealed previously as a property of complex III , remains valid for the whole RC .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding explaining how mitochondrial ROS production can switch states, relevant to cell damage.

fact: Theoretical predictions of conditions causing a switch to a high free radical state in complex III were experimentally confirmed.
source_span: The conditions for switching to a state with a high content of free radicals in complex III were predicted based on theoretical analysis and were confirmed experimentally .
selection_reasoning: This fact validates the model's predictive power and experimental relevance.

fact: ROS generation begins with the formation of superoxide radicals from the interaction of molecular oxygen with free radicals such as semiquinone in the mitochondrial respiratory chain.
source_span: ROS generation starts with the formation of a superoxide radical ( O2− ) as a result of interaction between molecular oxygen and free radicals , e . g . semiquinone ( Q− ) : O2+Q−→O2−+Q [1] .
selection_reasoning: This provides a fundamental biochemical definition necessary to understand ROS production.

fact: Excess ROS released during stress conditions like hypoxia/reoxygenation can directly damage cells, contributing to problems in organ transplantation and systemic diseases such as Parkinson's disease and diabetes.
source_span: However , when released in excess under certain stress conditions such as hypoxia/reoxygenation , ROS can also directly damage cells [6] . This destructive function of the electron transport chain represents the main problem in organ transplantation [7] and in many systemic diseases , as diverse as Parkinson disease [8] and diabetes [9] .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the clinical and translational significance of understanding ROS production.

fact: Reverse electron transport from succinate through complex I to NAD+ is important for respiration and ROS production, but the detailed mechanism of ROS production upstream in the respiratory chain is not fully understood.
source_span: It is generally accepted that electron transport from succinate through complex I to NAD+ , the phenomenon known as reverse electron transport [14] , is important for respiration and ROS production [15] , [16] . However , the mechanism of ROS production as a result of electron transfer upstream in the respiratory chain is not understood .
selection_reasoning: This states a key knowledge gap motivating the study.

fact: Kinetic modeling is a useful method for investigating complex systems like the mitochondrial respiratory chain, but classical models have been limited to simplified scenarios requiring automated procedures for large system construction.
source_span: The solution to such problems requires not only improvements in experimental techniques and new experiments , but also modification of methods for theoretical analysis . Specifically , kinetic modeling , which is an efficient method for investigating complex systems , still needs to be adopted for the mitochondrial respiratory chain . In fact , kinetic modeling in its classical form has been used for analysis of mitochondrial respiration . However , even the most detailed models [19] could consider only simplified scenarios . Huge number of differential equations is necessary to describe the behavior of respiratory complexes , so an automated procedure is required for their construction .
selection_reasoning: This explains the methodological rationale for the modeling approach used.

fact: Previously developed rule-based methodology for automated construction of large differential equation systems was extended to describe mitochondrial respiratory complex III based on the Q-cycle mechanism.
source_span: Previously we developed a rule-based methodology for the automated construction of large systems of differential equations for analysis of 13C isotope tracing experiments in metabolic flux analysis [20]–[22] . We extended this methodology to the mathematical description of multienzyme complexes , specifically mitochondrial respiratory complex III based on a Q-cycle mechanism [23] .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the novel modeling approach foundational to the current study.

fact: Complex III exhibits bistability where two different steady states exist for the same parameters, and perturbations like succinate fluctuations or hypoxia can switch the system from low to high ROS producing states.
source_span: A detailed description of complex III operation revealed that in a certain range of parameters complex III has the property of bistability , where two different steady states exist for the same parameters and the system can reach one or the other , depending on its initial state . Perturbations , such as fluctuations in succinate concentrations or temporal hypoxia , can switch the system from low to high ROS producing steady state .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight explains how environmental changes can trigger damaging ROS increases.

fact: The extended model of the respiratory chain includes complex I, electron transport and proton translocation stoichiometry, transmembrane potential, proton leak, oxidative phosphorylation, the TCA cycle, and metabolite transport.
source_span: The extended model includes the following elements: a detailed mathematical description of complex I; the stoichiometry of electron transport and proton translocation by the respiratory chain; the transmembrane potential; proton leak; oxidative phosphorylation; the TCA cycle that produces NADH and succinate as substrates for complexes I and III; and the transport of TCA cycle metabolites .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the comprehensive scope of the model, important for understanding its capabilities.

fact: The model aims to analyze respiratory chain behavior under different forward and reverse flux conditions and to reveal characteristics like free radical content that are difficult to measure experimentally.
source_span: The objective of this extension to the whole respiratory chain and linked processes was to create a tool for analysis of the basic behavior of the respiratory chain , in particular under conditions defining different fluxes in the forward and reverse directions . The ultimate aim was to reveal characteristics that have not been measured , such as the content of various free radicals , and thus to provide an insight into the relationship between states of the respiratory chain operation and ROS production .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the study's main goal and significance in advancing understanding of ROS mechanisms.

fact: The study aimed to reveal characteristics of mitochondrial respiratory chain operation that have not been measured, such as the content of various free radicals, to provide insight into the relationship between respiratory states and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production.
source_span: The ultimate aim was to reveal characteristics that have not been measured , such as the content of various free radicals , and thus to provide an insight into the relationship between states of the respiratory chain operation and ROS production .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the main research goal and scientific motivation, which is essential background for the study.

fact: The model of the respiratory chain includes linked substrate transport and TCA cycle reactions and contains 51 parameters to simulate mitochondrial respiration and electron transport.
source_span: As described in the Methods section , the model of the respiratory chain and linked substrate transport and TCA cycle reactions contains 51 parameters .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a high-level description of the modeling approach used to study mitochondrial respiration.

fact: Respiration rates in mitochondria fueled by succinate or pyruvate/malate differ between state 3 (presence of ADP) and state 4 (absence of ADP), reflecting maximal respiratory capacity and proton leak compensation, respectively.
source_span: The rates of respiration in the presence of ADP ( state 3 ) or an uncoupler characterize the maximal capacity of the respiratory chain . In the absence of ADP ( state 4 ) , the respiration rate is characterized by proton leaks , which must be compensated by respiration . According to our measurements , the respiration rate is 480±40 and 170±30 ng atom O/min/mg protein in the uncoupled and in state 4 in succinate-fueled mitochondria , and 410±30 and 80±20 ng atom O/min/mg protein in mitochondria fueled by pyruvate and malate , respectively .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes key experimental measurements that define respiratory states and their physiological relevance.

fact: Succinate oxidation in state 4 leads to fast reduction of intramitochondrial NAD+ due to reverse electron transport, which is inhibited by rotenone, an electron transport complex I inhibitor.
source_span: If mitochondria fueled by succinate do not expend the energy of the transmembrane electrochemical potential on ATP synthesis ( state 4 ) , succinate oxidation results in fast reduction of intramitochondrial NAD+ . In the presence of rotenone , an inhibitor of electron transport in complex I , NAD+ reduction is characterized by NAD+-dependent reactions of the TCA cycle and in particular the forward respiratory flux resulting from succinate oxidation . In the absence of rotenone , reverse electron transport [14] also participates in NAD+ reduction , which makes the process much faster ( Figure 2A ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key mechanistic insight about reverse electron transport and its modulation by rotenone, central to understanding mitochondrial redox dynamics.

fact: Malate and pyruvate oxidation in the TCA cycle fuel complex I by reducing NAD+ to NADH, defining the characteristics of complex I respiration.
source_span: While succinate fuels complex III through succinate dehydrogenase , the oxidation of malate and pyruvate in the TCA cycle fuels complex I by reducing NAD+ to NADH . Respiration under such conditions defines the characteristics of complex I .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the biological basis for different substrate effects on respiratory complexes, important for interpreting experimental conditions.

fact: The model parameters were fitted by simulating multiple experimental data types simultaneously, adjusting free parameters within known ranges to reproduce measured NAD+ reduction dynamics and respiration rates under various conditions.
source_span: To evaluate the model parameters , we used a procedure that simulates all the different types of data listed above for the same set of parameters . The ratio of forward and reverse constants defined by a known midpoint potential or dissociation constant was kept fixed , and the conditions of substrate supply or membrane permeability for protons were changed in accordance with experimental conditions . The procedure fitted all the data by changing the free parameters within the order of magnitude indicated in [19] , summarizing and minimizing the deviations in several calculations that simulated measurements . Minimization was performed using a standard stochastic procedure in the global space of parameters as described in Methods . selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the comparative study between eukaryotic and archaeal nucleosomes and highlights the biological system used.

fact: Archaeal nucleosomes assemble into tetramers lacking N- and C-terminal tails, making them structurally distinct from eukaryotic octameric nucleosomes with histone tails.

fact: Despite fundamental structural differences, the association between nucleosome footprints and sequence evolution is strikingly conserved between humans and the archaeon Haloferax volcanii.

selection_reasoning: This novel model is a key conclusion that advances understanding of nucleosome evolution.

fact: Nucleosome repositioning is both necessary and largely sufficient to explain the association between current nucleosome positions and biased substitution patterns.

selection_reasoning: This finding highlights the causal direction between genetic and epigenetic changes, a major implication of the study.

fact: Nucleosomes preferentially form on DNA sequences that are more amenable to being wrapped around the histone core, influencing local epigenetic states.
source_span: Both in vitro and in vivo , nucleosomes are non-randomly positioned with regard to the underlying sequence , forming preferentially on stretches of DNA that – by virtue of their sequence composition – are more amenable to being wrapped around the histone core [1]–[3] . Consequently , changes at the sequence level during evolution can bring about changes in nucleosome positioning and occupancy [4] , [5] , providing a simple example of how genetic changes can locally alter epigenetic states .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the mechanistic basis for nucleosome positioning and its evolutionary consequences.

fact: Nucleosomes can influence sequence evolution by modulating mutation and repair dynamics and by exerting selective pressure on the underlying DNA sequence.
source_span: In short , nucleosomes can affect evolution at the sequence level by modulating mutation and repair dynamics ( thereby biasing the emergence of novel variants ) and by exerting selective pressure on the underlying sequence ( thereby altering fixation probabilities ) .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the biological mechanisms linking nucleosomes to genome evolution, important for understanding the study's rationale.

fact: Previous studies in eukaryotes have found biased nucleotide substitution patterns around nucleosomes, such as increased A:T to G:C substitutions near nucleosome centers in humans.

For example , A:T to G:C substitutions were found to be more common closer to the nucleosome mid-point in humans , whereas C:G to T:A changes were enriched outside the nucleosome [9] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides context on known substitution biases relevant to the study's comparative analysis.

fact: The assumption that current nucleosome positions correspond closely to ancestral positions may be incorrect, affecting interpretations of substitution patterns around nucleosomes.
source_span: Interpretation of these trends has up to now proceeded from the assumption that experimentally determined nucleosome positions correspond closely to ancestral positions and that , as a result , current positions are informative about the chromatin context in which substitutions occurred . However , if this assumption is wrong and nucleosomes are repositioned following a change at the sequence level , conclusions about the relationship between nucleotide substitutions and nucleosome positions might change dramatically ( Fig . 1 ) .
selection_reasoning: This motivates the study's investigation into causality between nucleosome positioning and sequence evolution.

fact: Calcium influx induced by PLY is the key event initiating glutamate release from astrocytes.
