fact: A curated list of known plant height genes from maize, sorghum, and rice was used to search for orthologous genes within the Setaria viridis QTL intervals.
source_span: A curated list of plant height genes cloned from maize, sorghum and rice was generated through literature review... The genomic coordinates of coding sequences of interest were extracted... to examine their location relative to the coordinates of the QTL.
selection_reasoning: This comparative genomics approach supports identification of candidate genes relevant to height.

fact: Height in the field was measured using two different methods: exact measurement of the uppermost leaf collar on a subset of plants and estimation of average height on all plants within a plot.
source_span: Height in the field was measured using two different methods of approximation. An analysis of variance indicates that on average, measuring the exact height to the collar of the uppermost leaf on the culm of a subset of three individuals within a plot (as performed in 2014) was approximately 5.8% more heritable than attempting to estimate the average height to the collar of the uppermost leaf on the culm of all plants within the plot (as performed in 2013).
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important context on phenotyping methods and their impact on heritability estimates.

fact: Five different automated methods of measuring plant height from 2-D images were used at the Bellweather Phenotyping Facility.
source_span: Five different automated methods of measuring plant height (height_above_bound, extent_y, centroid_y, ellipse_center_y, canopy_height) from 2-D images captured at the Bellweather Phenotyping Facility were...
selection_reasoning: This highlights the use of high-throughput phenotyping methods, relevant to the study's methodology.

fact: Plant height heritability was higher when measured as the height to the collar of the uppermost leaf on the culm of the tallest plant in a plot compared to measuring the average height of all plants in the plot.
source_span: plot ( as performed in 2014 ) was approximately 5 . 8% more heritable than attempting to estimate the average height to the collar of the uppermost leaf on the culm of all plants within the plot ( as performed in 2013 ) ( S1 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key methodological comparison affecting heritability estimates, relevant to understanding measurement approaches and their impact on genetic analysis.

fact: The increase in heritability of plant height between 2013 and 2014 was not due to environmental or management differences, as flowering time heritability did not increase between these years.
source_span: An increase in heritability between years was not observed for flowering time between the 2013 and 2014 field seasons , suggesting that the increase in heritability was not due to differences in environment or management ( S1 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the conclusion that observed heritability changes are due to measurement or genetic factors rather than environmental variation.

fact: Five automated methods of measuring plant height from 2-D images were evaluated, with three methods showing high correlation and high heritability.
source_span: Five different automated methods of measuring plant height ( height_above_bound , extent_y , centroid_y , ellipse_center_y , canopy_height—see definitions in methods ) from 2-D images captured at the Bellweather Phenotyping Facility were evaluated ( S1 Fig ) . Among these measurements , height_above_bound , extent_y and centroid_y were highly correlated ( R2 > 0 . 97 ) ( S2 Table ) and all three were highly heritable on average ( h2 > 0 . 85 ) and showed clear effects of water limitation ( S2 Fig , S3 and S4 Tables ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key phenotyping methods and their validation, which is central to the study's approach and findings.

fact: The mean value of height_above_bound from four rotational images was used as the primary plant height metric because it is simple, highly heritable, sensitive to treatment effects, and validated against manual measurements.
source_span: The mean value of height_above_bound based upon four rotational images was the primary metric used for the remainder of this study as it is intuitively simple to understand , highly heritable , strongly correlated with other height metrics , sensitive to treatment effects and previously validated against manual measurements [52] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the main measurement choice, important for understanding the study's methodology and data reliability.

fact: Plant height was evaluated in a Setaria viridis x Setaria italica recombinant inbred line population under diverse growing conditions including different water availability, planting density, day length, temperature, locations, and planting dates.
source_span: Height of individuals within the S . viridis ( A10 ) X S . italica ( B100 ) RIL population was evaluated under very diverse growing conditions . Variation resulted from different water availability and planting density treatments . In addition , day length and temperature varied between plant-outs at three locations ( Illinois field site , DDPSC growth chamber , Carnegie growth chamber ) and two different planting dates each year at the Illinois field site .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential background on the experimental design and environmental variables tested, framing the study's scope.

fact: Although mean and variance of final height differed significantly between grow outs, the coefficient of variation remained relatively constant across all experiments and treatments.
source_span: Although the mean and variance of final height differed significantly between grow outs ( Fig 1a ) , the coefficient of variation remained relatively constant across all replicated experiments and treatments ( Table 1 and S5 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact indicates stability in relative variation of height despite environmental differences, relevant to interpreting genetic effects.

fact: Heritability of final plant height within each trial and treatment exceeded 0.84, with an average heritability of 0.82 across all time points and environments.
source_span: Within each trial and treatment , the heritability of final plant height exceeded 0 . 84 ( S1 Table ) . The mean heritability of plant height in this population across all time points was 0 . 82 and tended to be higher in controlled environments ( average H2 = 0 . 86 at Bellweather and Carnegie , average H2 = 0 . 83 in field at Illinois ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the strong genetic control of plant height, a principal finding relevant to the study's genetic mapping goals.

fact: The proportion of height variance attributed to genotype increased as plants approached maturity.
source_span: Generally , the proportion of height variance attributed to genotype increased as the plant approached maturity ( Fig 1c and S6 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact reveals a dynamic genetic influence on height over development, important for understanding trait architecture.

fact: Water limitation and planting density treatments did not dramatically influence the heritability of plant height in this study.
source_span: The effects of water limitation and planting density treatments did not dramatically influence the heritability of plant height in this study ( S1 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies that environmental treatments affected height but not its genetic heritability, relevant for interpreting genotype-by-environment interactions.

fact: Genotype had the strongest effect on plant height under drought conditions, followed by trial location and treatment nested within location.
source_span: Within drought trials , genotype had the strongest effect on height , followed by trial location and treatment effect nested within location ( S7 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies the primary factors influencing height under drought, central to understanding genetic and environmental contributions.

fact: A significant positive correlation between final plant height and day of panicle emergence was observed in each field grow out, suggesting that variation in planting dates, day length, and temperature could explain some location differences.
source_span: Similar to the correlation of height and days to anthesis in maize [13] , a significant positive correlation between final height and day of panicle emergence was observed in each field grow out ( Table 1 ) , suggesting that different planting dates , with their different day lengths and temperatures could explain some of the trial location variation .
selection_reasoning: This fact links developmental timing to height variation, providing insight into environmental effects on the trait.

fact: Water limitation treatments varied widely between experiments, simulating several possible drought scenarios plants could experience.
source_span: The water limitation treatment varied widely between experiments , simulating several possible scenarios plants could experience .
selection_reasoning: This fact contextualizes the environmental treatments, important for interpreting the study's drought-related findings.

fact: Controlled growth experiments and the 2014 field experiment showed significant effects of drought on plant height, while the 2013 field experiment did not detect a significant drought effect due to late water withholding.
source_span: The controlled growth experiments all showed a significant effect of drought , as did the 2014 field experiment ( despite an end of season flood ) . In retrospect , water was not withheld early enough in the 2013 field experiment to detect a significant drought effect on height although soil probes showed a substantial difference in water availability within 3 weeks ( S8 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports key findings on drought impact on height, central to the study's investigation of environmental stress effects.

fact: Withholding water soon after germination in the Carnegie experiment caused the most pronounced height reduction observed among all grow outs.
source_span: The effect of withholding water completely soon after germination in the Carnegie experiment made the observed height effect the most pronounced of any grow out observed ( S5 Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the severity of early drought stress on height, a principal experimental finding.

fact: Plant height was less responsive to planting density than to water limitation, with most variance attributed to genotype and plot nested within treatment.
source_span: Height appears less responsive to planting density than water limitation , with most of the variance attributed to genotypic and plot nested within treatment followed by the variance attributed to year and lastly planting density ( S7 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the relative impact of environmental factors on height variation, important for understanding trait plasticity.

fact: Planting density had a significant effect on plant height by the end of the experiment in both 2013 and 2014 field trials.
source_span: Nonetheless , in both 2013 and 2014 , planting density had a significant effect on height by the end of the experiment .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports a significant environmental effect on height, relevant to the study's environmental treatment outcomes.

fact: The rank order of lines by phenotype showed that experimental location and environment type (controlled vs. field) strongly influenced plant height variation.
source_span: Using the rank order of lines by phenotype as a proxy for how similar the experiments are to each other , the effect of experimental location is apparent , as well as the difference between controlled environment and the field .
selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates the influence of environment on genotype performance, important for interpreting genotype-by-environment interactions.

fact: Planting density had a significant effect on plant height by the end of the experiment.
source_span: planting density had a significant effect on height by the end of the experiment .
selection_reasoning: This fact establishes an important environmental factor influencing the trait studied, relevant for understanding experimental conditions and results.

fact: The effect of experimental location and the difference between controlled environment and field conditions are apparent in plant height phenotypes.
source_span: Using the rank order of lines by phenotype as a proxy for how similar the experiments are to each other , the effect of experimental location is apparent , as well as the difference between controlled environment and the field .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the environmental variability impacting the trait, important for interpreting genetic findings across conditions.

fact: The well-watered treatment at Bellweather, the drought treatment at Carnegie, and the 2013 field density experiment represent the most divergent environments in this study.
source_span: The well-watered treatment at Bellweather , the drought treatment at Carnegie and the 2013 field density experiment are the most divergent environments encountered within this study .
selection_reasoning: Identifying key contrasting environments is important for understanding the range of conditions tested and their impact on plant height.

fact: A de novo genetic map was constructed and all phenotyped recombinant inbred lines (RILs) were genotyped to verify genetic stock identity.
source_span: We constructed a de novo genetic map and genotyped all phenotyped RILs to verify the identity of genetic stocks [68] .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key methodological step ensuring the genetic data quality and completeness for the study.

fact: The final genetic map consists of 217 individuals spanning 1,088 cM with 1,595 markers after filtering and alignment to the Setaria viridis genome.
source_span: the final genetic map consists of 217 individuals , spanning 1 , 088 cM , calculated using 1 , 595 markers ( S9 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a high-level description of the genetic resource used for mapping, relevant for understanding the study's genetic resolution.

fact: A total of 153 individual SNPs associated with plant height were identified across all time points and treatments in 12 experimental grow outs.
source_span: This procedure identified a total of 153 individual SNPs associated with height across all time points and treatments within the 12 experimental grow outs ( Fig 3 and S10 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding identifying genetic loci linked to the trait across diverse conditions.

fact: No significant epistatic interactions between QTL were detected for plant height.
source_span: No significant epistatic interaction between QTL was detected .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the genetic architecture as primarily additive, important for interpreting genetic effects.

fact: Clusters of linked SNPs were collapsed into 37 unique QTL locations associated with plant height.
source_span: Groups of closely linked QTL markers ( 10 cM radius ) were collapsed into the most frequently observed SNP marker in each cluster , resulting in 37 unique QTLs ( S11 Table and S6 Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the genetic mapping results into distinct loci, simplifying the genetic architecture.

fact: Seventeen of the 37 QTL were observed in at least three treatment groups, and twelve were observed in four treatment groups, indicating similar genetic architecture of height across environments.
source_span: A substantial proportion of these QTL were observed at least once in three ( 17/37 ) or four ( 12/37 ) treatment groups , suggesting that the genetic architecture of height is similar across all experimental treatments contrasts considered in this study ( S11 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the consistency of genetic effects across diverse environmental conditions.

fact: A static QTL model including 12 QTL locations identified in all treatment groups explained on average 53% of the additive genetic variance for final plant height.
source_span: A static QTL model including only the 12 QTL locations identified at least once in all treatment groups was fit at a time point representative of final plant size in each experiment . Across all experimental grow outs these 12 QTL explained between 25–64% of the additive genetic variance and 53% on average ( Fig 4 ) .
selection_reasoning: This quantifies the major genetic contribution to the trait, a key principal finding.

fact: The most frequently observed QTL (marker S5_41999990) was identified in all 12 experiments and explained the largest percentage of additive genetic variance, with the B100 allele associated with reduced plant height.
source_span: The most frequently observed QTL ( marker: S5_41999990 ) was identified in each of the 12 experiments and explained the largest percentage of additive genetic variance ( mean of 19% ) . The B100 allele at this QTL position is associated with reduced plant height .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key genetic locus with a consistent and strong effect on plant height.

fact: Nine of the twelve major QTL have the B100 allele associated with increased plant height.
source_span: The B100 allele at nine of these twelve positions are associated with increased plant height .
selection_reasoning: This provides insight into the direction of allele effects at major loci.

fact: Across all field trials, more QTL were shared between treatment blocks and years than were unique to any single treatment or year.
source_span: Across all field trials performed , the number of QTL shared between treatment blocks and across years is greater than the number of QTL unique to any treatment block across growth years or both treatment blocks within a single growth year ( Fig 5 and S7 Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the stability of genetic loci across environments and time.

fact: No QTL were detected exclusively in well-watered or water-limited conditions across any experiments.
source_span: No overlap between QTL detected exclusively in well-watered or water-limited conditions was observed between any of the experiments ( Fig 5a and S7 Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This indicates a lack of environment-specific QTL for water treatment, relevant for understanding genetic-environment interactions.

fact: A single QTL (marker S9_52254840) was uniquely identified within the high planting density treatment block in both years.
source_span: Within planting density experiments a single QTL ( marker: S9_52254840 ) was identified uniquely within the high planting density treatment block in both years ( Fig 5b and S7 Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a genetic locus potentially responsive to planting density.

fact: Most QTL detected in controlled environments (13 out of 16) were also detected in field environments.
source_span: A majority ( 13/16 ) of the QTL detected in controlled environments were also detected in field environments ( Fig 5c ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact shows overlap in genetic control of height across environment types.

fact: QTL analyses on numerical difference, relative difference, and ratio of plant heights between treatment blocks largely overlapped with QTL identified from plant height measurements within treatments.
source_span: The results from QTL scans performed on the numerical difference , relative difference and the ratio of plant heights measured between treatment blocks at all time points largely overlapped with the results from the QTL analysis performed on measured value of plant height within treatments ( S8 Fig and S12 Table ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the robustness of QTL findings across different analytical approaches.

fact: Most environmentally responsive QTL are due to relative differences in the timing of loci growth effects between treatments rather than unique loci.
source_span: While there are genetic loci that appear to be responsive to different environments , the majority of the environmentally responsive loci are due to relative differences in the timing of the loci growth affect between treatments .
selection_reasoning: This provides insight into the dynamic nature of genetic effects on height across environments.

fact: Plant height is a dynamic trait that changes at different rates throughout the plant life cycle.
source_span: Height is a dynamic trait that changes at different rates throughout the plant life cycle .
selection_reasoning: This background fact is important for understanding the temporal genetic analyses performed.

fact: Linkage mapping performed independently at each time point identified more QTL locations than function-valued analysis, but major QTL locations were consistent between methods.
source_span: Across all grow outs , linkage mapping analysis performed independently at each time point identified a larger number of QTL locations relative to the function-valued analysis . The positional locations of major QTL detected using each of these methods varied slightly , but in all cases it is likely that the same QTL are identified .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the reliability of QTL detection methods and the robustness of major loci.

fact: Plant height at early stages of development is strongly associated with a major QTL located at chromosome 5 position 100 cM (5@100) in Setaria.
source_span: In all experimental grow outs, plant height at early stages of development is strongly associated with a single major QTL located at 5@100.
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key genetic locus influencing early plant height, a core finding relevant to the study's genetic mapping of growth traits.

fact: The influence of the 5@100 QTL on plant height diminishes over time while the contribution of other QTLs at 2@91 and 9@35 increases during plant development.
source_span: In the dataset with the highest temporal resolution (Bellweather), the proportional contribution of this QTL diminishes over time while the contribution of other QTL located at 2@91 and 9@35 increase.
selection_reasoning: This describes the dynamic genetic control of plant height over time, a principal finding about developmental genetics.

fact: Water-limited plants exhibit slightly decreased average and maximal growth rates and a significant delay in the day of maximal growth rate compared to well-watered plants.
source_span: Water-limited plants exhibit slightly decreased average and maximal rates of growth. In addition, the day at which maximal growth rate is achieved is significantly delayed in water-limited plants.
selection_reasoning: This fact links environmental treatment (water limitation) to growth dynamics, important for understanding treatment effects.

fact: QTLs associated with maximal and daily growth rates are essentially the same as those detected for plant height, but their greatest influence occurs earlier in development.
source_span: QTLs associated with maximal and daily growth rate are essentially identical to those detected for height, although the time at which these QTL exhibit the greatest influence appears shifted toward earlier time points in the experiment.
selection_reasoning: This connects genetic loci controlling growth rate and height, highlighting timing differences, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: A simple additive QTL model comprising loci on chromosomes 2, 5, and 9 (2@91, 5@100, and 9@35) explains much of the variation in plant height in Setaria.
source_span: The SLOD based function-valued QTL analysis of our highest resolution dataset identified a simple, additive, QTL model comprised of loci on chromosomes 2, 5 and 9 (2@91, 5@100 and 9@35) which provides a framework to link many of the experiments.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main genetic architecture model derived from the study, central to the article's conclusions.

fact: Early in development, the B100 allele at 5@100 is associated with shorter plants, but later the B100 alleles at 2@91 and 9@35 increase plant height at maturity.
source_span: Early in plant development, individuals that inherit the B100 allele at position 5@100 will be shorter than those that inherit the A10 allele. The effects of this locus are then counterbalanced by the influence of the QTL at position 2@91 and later by 9@35 where the B100 allele increases plant height at maturity.
selection_reasoning: This fact details allele-specific effects over time, important for understanding genetic contributions to growth.

fact: The genetic model with 5@100 driving early growth and B100 tall QTLs at 2@91 and 9@35 driving later growth explains observed variation in most experiments.
source_span: In most of the experiments, a fairly simple model with the 5@100 QTL driving early growth and several B100 tall QTLs taking over later explains the observed variation.
selection_reasoning: This provides a coherent developmental genetic model linking genotype to phenotype over time.

fact: Differences in plant height observed between controlled environment and field settings may be explained by the timing of QTL effects and environmental constraints such as pot size.
source_span: This chronological genetic model of plant height may in part explain the differences in plant height observed when parental lines are grown in controlled environments versus field settings. Experiments performed in controlled environmental settings potentially end before the effects of the B100 alleles at positions 2@91 and 9@35 can fully materialize or may reflect limitations in growth due to pot size constraints.
selection_reasoning: This fact links genetic findings to experimental context and explains observed phenotypic differences, important for interpretation and significance.

fact: Pot size does not dramatically limit vertical growth during the first 35 days after planting in controlled environment experiments.
source_span: The results of a glass house experiment designed to test these factors, suggests that the pot size used during in the Bellweather trial does not dramatically limit vertical growth given the duration of this experiment (experiment ends prior to 35 days after planting).
selection_reasoning: This addresses a potential confounding factor in growth experiments, relevant for interpreting results.

fact: Plant height in Setaria is controlled by multiple genetic loci that act throughout development and are influenced by environmental factors such as water availability and planting density.
source_span: The results of 12 coordinated grow outs of a Setaria RIL population in three different experimental locations suggest that plant height is specified as a functionally continuous developmental process that is under strong and robust genetic control but can be influenced by both water availability and planting density.
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the core finding about genetic and environmental control of plant height, central to the study's main question and significance.

fact: Water limitation delays the maximal growth rate of Setaria plants by approximately three days but does not reduce the maximal growth rate itself.
source_span: As expected [40–42], more aggressive water limitation treatments led to a greater reduction in plant height. However, no significant difference in the maximal plant growth rate was observed, rather it was delayed by approximately 3 days in water limited plants.
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights a key environmental effect on growth dynamics, relevant to understanding how water stress impacts plant height.

fact: Setaria plants grown at lower planting densities are taller than those grown at higher densities, contrary to the expected shade avoidance response.
source_span: Another surprising finding was that RILs planted at lower planting densities were taller than their densely planted counterpart, counter to the expectation that the shade avoidance response would result in increased plant height in densely grown stands [42, 72] and may reflect resource limitations that inhibit growth of densely planted stands.
selection_reasoning: This fact reveals an unexpected environmental effect on plant height, important for interpreting growth responses under different planting conditions.

fact: The most influential genetic locus affecting plant height in Setaria (5@100) colocalizes with the ortholog of the rice SD-1 gene, a gibberellin 20-oxidase enzyme involved in growth regulation.
source_span: The QTL of greatest influence on plant height (5@100) colocalizes with the S. viridis ortholog of rice SD-1 (semi-dwarfing), a putative gibberellin 20-oxidase enzyme [36].
selection_reasoning: Identifying a major QTL and its candidate gene provides a key mechanistic insight into genetic control of height, central to the study's genetic findings.

fact: Twelve genetic loci consistently influence plant height across different environmental treatments, indicating a core genetic program underlying height determination in Setaria.
source_span: Twelve genetic loci are found in each of the four different treatment regimens and are responsible for the strongest effects in every experiment, although many smaller effect QTL were identified across individual time points in multiple independent replicated trials.
selection_reasoning: This fact emphasizes the robustness and consistency of key genetic factors controlling height, important for understanding genetic architecture.

fact: Alleles increasing plant height early in development are mostly inherited from the shorter A10 parental line, while alleles increasing height later in development are mostly inherited from the taller B100 parental line.
source_span: The alleles that increase plant height are found in both parental lines, with the allele of largest positive effect (5@100) inherited from the shorter A10 parental line. The effects of this locus are realized early, as growth rate approaches its maximum value. Later in development, the number of loci that contribute to plant height increases. A vast majority of the loci that increase plant height late in development are inherited from the B100 parent.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the temporal genetic contributions from parental lines, key to understanding the genetic dynamics of height.

fact: Trial location strongly influences plant height in Setaria, likely due to environmental factors such as day length and temperature affecting flowering time.
source_span: Trial location was the most influential variable affecting plant height after genotype which may be the result of differences in day length and temperature influencing flowering time.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the importance of environmental context on height variation, relevant for interpreting genotype-by-environment interactions.

fact: Flowering time is positively correlated with plant height at maturity in all field trials of Setaria.
source_span: In all field trials, flowering time was positively correlated with plant height at maturity.
selection_reasoning: This relationship links developmental timing to final height, important for understanding growth and yield traits.

fact: High-throughput phenotyping platforms enable frequent, non-destructive measurements of plant height, providing temporal resolution of genetic effects on growth.
source_span: As demonstrated here, using platforms with high frequency and non-destructive measurements of plant height provides temporal resolution of QTL effects.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the methodological advance that allowed detailed temporal genetic analysis, relevant to the study approach.

fact: Several candidate genes for plant height QTL in Setaria were identified by colocalization with orthologs of known height genes from other grasses, including maize and rice.
source_span: Several promising candidate genes were identified for two of the three major QTL identified during this study. The QTL of greatest influence on plant height (5@100) colocalizes with the S. viridis ortholog of rice SD-1... Two potential candidate genes appear to colocalize with QTL on 9@35. The S. viridis orthologs of maize Kn1 and maize D8 are located within the 1.5 LOD confidence interval of this QTL.
selection_reasoning: This fact connects genetic findings in Setaria to known genes in related species, supporting biological relevance and candidate gene identification.

fact: Alleles from the wild parent act early in development to increase plant height, while alleles from the domesticated parent act later in development.
source_span: Temporal analysis revealed that alleles from the wild parent act early in development , while alleles from the domesticated parent act later .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the timing and parental origin of genetic effects on plant height, a core finding about genetic contributions.

fact: The number of genetic loci contributing to plant height increases later in development, with most late-acting loci inherited from the domesticated B100 parent.
source_span: Later in development , the number of loci that contribute to plant height increases . A vast majority of the loci that increase plant height late in development are inherited from the B100 parent .
selection_reasoning: This describes the developmental dynamics of genetic control over plant height, central to the study's main question.

fact: Environmental factors influence the effects of late-appearing genetic loci on plant height, causing variability between experiments.
source_span: The dynamics of the late-appearing genetic loci are clearly dependent upon environmental factors as they are more variable between experiments .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the environmental modulation of genetic effects, important for understanding gene-environment interactions.

fact: The balance of early alleles favoring height from the wild parent and later alleles from the domesticated parent may reflect domestication effects on growth habit.
source_span: The balance of early alleles favoring height coming from the wild parent and later alleles coming from the domesticated parent may reflect the results of domestication on growth habit , with the wild parent favoring rapid growth and flowering while the domesticated favors longer growth cycles and larger plants .
selection_reasoning: This provides biological context linking genetic findings to domestication and growth strategies, important background.

fact: The peak genetic locus at position 5@100 is closely linked to the SD-1 gene ortholog, suggesting SD-1 is responsible for the early growth rate phenotype.
source_span: The close linkage of the 5@100 peak LOD score marker with the ortholog of SD-1 strongly suggests that this gene is responsible for the phenotype , but confirmation will require further experiments .
selection_reasoning: Identifying a candidate gene underlying a major QTL is a key mechanistic insight relevant to the study's conclusions.

fact: Several other QTLs for plant height have candidate orthologs nearby, but some QTLs lack known candidate genes, indicating novel height-altering loci.
source_span: Several other promising candidates were found for other QTLs , but several have multiple possible candidates , while others are within linkage disequilibrium , but farther away from the peak LOD SNP . Several QTLs have no known candidate orthologs within their confidence intervals , suggesting that they result from novel height altering loci .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the discovery of both known and novel genetic factors affecting plant height, important for genetic understanding.

fact: Despite differences in genotype rankings and parental height between field and controlled environments, the detected QTL largely overlap.
source_span: Despite stark differences in rank order among genotypes and the relative height of the parents observed within field and controlled environments , the QTL detected largely overlap .
selection_reasoning: This supports the robustness of genetic loci across environments, a principal finding about genetic architecture.

fact: Temporal QTL modeling explains conflicting observations of plant height across experiments conducted at different developmental time windows.
source_span: The temporal QTL model provides the explanation for these conflicting observations across experiments conducted at different time windows .
selection_reasoning: This fact shows the value of temporal analysis in resolving experimental discrepancies, a key methodological insight.

fact: Adding temporal analysis to phenotyping greatly improves the ability to detect and interpret factors underlying complex traits like plant height.
source_span: These results demonstrate that adding temporal analysis to phenotyping can greatly improve our ability to detect and interpret the factors underlying complex traits .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal methodological conclusion with broad significance for trait analysis.

fact: The dense genetic marker map created in this study can be combined with diverse germplasm to fine map causal variants and identify markers useful for breeding programs.
source_span: The dense marker map created for this study can be combined with diverse germplasm studies to fine map causal variants and identify tightly linked markers for use in breeding programs .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the translational potential of the study's resources for crop improvement.

fact: The genetic and environmental components of plant height in Setaria were dissected by combining field and controlled environment analysis with quantitative genetics.
source_span: By combining field and controlled environmental analysis with quantitative genetics we were able to dissect the genetic and environmental components of plant height in Setaria .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the high-level approach used to address the main research question.

fact: The genetic components determining plant height in the Setaria RIL population show strong genetic canalization but their contributions vary with time and environment.
source_span: The identity of genetic components that determine plant height within this RIL population exhibits a strong degree of genetic canalization , but the contribution of these loci is influenced by temporal and environmental factors .
selection_reasoning: This fact captures a key biological insight about genetic stability and environmental modulation.

fact: The approaches used in this study should be applicable across diverse species and traits for improving food and biofuel crops.
source_span: These approaches should be applicable across diverse species and traits for improvement of both food and biofuel crops .
selection_reasoning: This states the broader significance and potential impact of the study's methods.

fact: High-throughput phenotyping systems combined with temporal genetic analysis can be used to better understand plant adaptation.
source_span: This approach can be used to dissect all of the traits that can be measured in a high throughput manner by emerging phenotyping systems to better understand plant adaptation .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the future utility of the study's approach for plant biology.

fact: In Drosophila melanogaster females, heterochromatic homology ensures the segregation of achiasmate chromosomes during meiosis I.
source_span: Heterochromatic homology ensures the segregation of achiasmate chromosomes during meiosis I in Drosophila melanogaster females
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological system and the key phenomenon under study.

fact: Achiasmate 4th chromosomes in Drosophila melanogaster females do not undergo crossing over but are still segregated efficiently by a distributive system.
source_span: However, in Drosophila melanogaster females, the 4th chromosomes are always achiasmate ... Nonetheless, Drosophila females can segregate these achiasmate chromosomes with high efficiency, demonstrating the existence of a system (termed the distributive system) to segregate homologous chromosomes that fail to recombine
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important context about the unique meiotic behavior of achiasmate chromosomes relevant to the study.

fact: Heterochromatic regions on achiasmate chromosomes are necessary and sufficient for their proper segregation during female meiosis in Drosophila melanogaster.
source_span: Heterochromatic regions on the achiasmate chromosomes are both necessary and sufficient for the proper segregation of achiasmate homologs
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies the key chromosomal regions involved in segregation, central to the study's focus.

fact: For schistosomiasis, the study recommends using sub-district implementation units for MDA to better target treatment and avoid overtreating or undertreating subpopulations.
source_span: In the case of schistosomiasis , a disease that is very focal in nature , and for which treatment medication is costly and in limited supply , we feel that it would be more appropriate to use the sub-district as implementation units to determine needs for treatment because a district-based approach may result in overtreating or undertreating subpopulations within the district [23] .

fact: Using the WHO protocol would have resulted in tens of thousands of people in highly endemic areas not receiving treatment and others not in need being treated, as shown in Senegal.

fact: LubX E3 ubiquitin ligase activity is required for the temporal degradation of SidH in host cells.
source_span: In cells infected with the L . pneumophila lubXI39A mutant, similar levels of 3× FLAG-SidH were detected at all time points and the protein was not polyubiquitinated, indicating that LubX E3 ubiquitin ligase activity is required for the temporal degradation of SidH.

fact: Legionella pneumophila strains defective in lubX show increased lethality to Drosophila flies compared with wild-type or sidH mutant strains, despite having lower bacterial counts in surviving flies.

fact: LubX functions as a metaeffector by regulating the stability and function of another Legionella pneumophila effector, SidH, within host cells.
