selection_reasoning: This describes a key methodological advance enabling precise measurement of telomere features.

fact: Crossing American and European S. paradoxus strains produced offspring with a continuum of telomere lengths, consistent with multiple quantitative trait loci (QTLs) controlling telomere length.
source_span: Crossing the American and European strains resulted in F1 spores with a continuum of telomere lengths consistent with what would be predicted if many quantitative trait loci ( QTLs ) were involved in length maintenance .
selection_reasoning: This finding supports a complex genetic basis for telomere length variation.

fact: Variation in telomere position effect (TPE) is quantitative but only weakly correlated with telomere length.
source_span: Variation in TPE is similarly quantitative but only weakly correlated with telomere length .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the relationship between two telomere-related phenotypes, important for understanding telomere biology.

fact: Genotyping of F1 segregants identified several QTLs associated with telomere length and silencing variation, including known candidate genes and regions without previously known telomeric genes.
source_span: Genotyping F1 segregants indicated several QTLs associated with telomere length and silencing variation . These QTLs include likely candidate genes but also map to regions where there are no known genes involved in telomeric properties .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the genetic complexity and novel loci involved in telomere regulation.

fact: Reciprocal hemizygosity tests validated that YKU80 and TLC1 are telomere-length QTLs in the two S. paradoxus subpopulations.
source_span: We validated by reciprocal hemizygosity that YKU80 and TLC1 are telomere-length QTLs in the two S . paradoxus subpopulations .
selection_reasoning: This confirms specific genes as key genetic determinants of telomere length variation.

fact: Sequence divergence within the Ku heterodimer likely causes negative epistasis in one allelic combination (American-YKU70 and European-YKU80), resulting in very short telomeres.
source_span: Furthermore , we propose that sequence divergence within the Ku heterodimer generates negative epistasis within one of the allelic combinations ( American-YKU70 and European-YKU80 ) resulting in very short telomeres .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight explains how genetic interactions affect telomere length.

fact: Telomeres are nucleoprotein structures at chromosome ends that protect chromosomes from DNA repair enzymes and are replenished by telomerase.
source_span: Telomeres are active nucleo-protein sites that constitute the ends of chromosomes in most eukaryotic species [1] . Telomeric DNA is G-rich and highly species specific in sequence . The telomeric DNA is bound by a number of proteins that together form a tight structure that effectively hides chromosome ends from DNA repair enzymes . Telomeric sequences are elegantly replenished by telomerase , a specialized reverse transcriptase .
selection_reasoning: This background information is essential to understand the biological importance of telomeres and telomerase.

fact: Telomere length is species- and chromosome-specific and plays an important role in normal cell function.
source_span: Telomere length is both species and chromosome specific and appears to play an important role in the normal functioning of a cell .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides biological context for why telomere length variation matters.

fact: Saccharomyces cerevisiae has been used by humans for thousands of years and may not be an ideal model for studying natural variation of complex traits compared to S. paradoxus, which has had no such human interaction.
source_span: S . cerevisiae has been used for thousands of years by humans . Selection and domestication issues have been previously invoked [9] , [10] to argue that S . cerevisiae may not be a good model for studying natural variation of complex traits . In contrast , S . paradoxus has had no such interaction with humans .
selection_reasoning: This explains the rationale for focusing on S. paradoxus to study natural telomere length variation.

fact: S. paradoxus consists of three major geographic subpopulations: European, Far Eastern, and American, which differ in subtelomeric structures and sequence variation.
source_span: Sequence analysis in this species supports the presence of three major geographic subpopulations: European , Far Eastern and American [8] , [11]–[14] . Subtelomeric structures are also highly variable between S . paradoxus subpopulations as illustrated by the documented paucity of the Y′ element in Far Eastern isolates [8] . The overall sequence variation found in S . paradoxus ( up to 4 . 5% ) is much greater than in any S . cerevisiae analysed ( ∼0 . 7% ) [14] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact contextualizes the genetic and geographic diversity relevant to telomere length variation.

fact: Saccharomyces paradoxus strains from different geographic populations show reproducible and strain-dependent differences in telomere length.
source_span: These results indicate that the telomere length variation in S . paradoxus was reproducible and strain background dependent.
selection_reasoning: This establishes the core biological variation motivating the study and justifies genetic analysis.

fact: The genetic background explains 98% of the variability in telomere length phenotype in Saccharomyces paradoxus, making it a strong candidate for quantitative trait locus (QTL) analysis.
source_span: Altogether , the genetic background explains 98% of the variability in the phenotype , making it a good candidate for a QTL study considered below.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the genetic basis of telomere length variation and the rationale for further genetic mapping.

fact: Telomere length differences between CBS (European) and YPS (American) strains were confirmed at two specific chromosome ends using a URA3 marker.
source_span: Consistent with the initial screening , the single VII-L telomere revealed a significant difference in length between the strains: 201±15 bp in CBS and 438±29 in YPS ... Similarly , telomere length at XV-R showed the expected length difference between the two isolates: 189±53 bp in CBS and 416±43 bp in YPS.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key experimental approach and confirms the main phenotype measured.

fact: Sequencing of telomeres at the nucleotide level showed that the conserved core telomeric sequence length is similar between CBS and YPS strains, indicating a conserved mechanism sensing critically short telomeres.
source_span: The fact that we found no significant differences between the average length of the conserved sequence between CBS and YPS indicates that cells sense critically short telomeres by a conserved mechanism that recognises a specific telomere length.
selection_reasoning: This provides mechanistic insight into telomere length regulation relevant to the main findings.

fact: The minimal telomere length detected in Saccharomyces paradoxus was as short as 14 base pairs, indicating the extent of telomere attrition before telomerase action.
source_span: It is worth noting that the minimal telomere length detected , inferred from the measure of maximum internal resection ( Figure 2 , length of black bars ) , was as short as 14 bp.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key biological limit relevant to telomere maintenance.

fact: Deletion of telomere length regulatory genes MRE11 and YKU70 caused severe telomere shortening in both CBS and YPS strains, while deletion of RIF1 and PIF1 caused telomere elongation.
source_span: MRE11 and YKU70 deletions normally result in severe telomere shortening whereas RIF1 and PIF1 mutants have extra long telomeres.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes key genetic perturbations and their effects on telomere length, central to understanding telomere regulation.

fact: The CBS strain showed growth defects when YKU70 or MRE11 were deleted, indicating partial intolerance to mutations causing very short telomeres.
source_span: Growth defects were observed in both yku70Δ and mre11Δ in the CBS but not in YPS strain background , indicating that the CBS strain could only partially tolerate mutations that result in a very short telomere phenotype.
selection_reasoning: This fact links telomere length regulation to cellular fitness and strain-specific phenotypic consequences.

fact: Deletion of YKU70 in the CBS strain did not significantly alter telomere length, suggesting a strain-specific difference in Ku heterodimer function.
source_span: Interestingly , deletion of yku70 in CBS did not seem to alter telomere length.
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key difference in telomere regulation mechanisms between strains.

fact: Loss of Ku function in the YPS strain caused a large increase in single-stranded telomeric G-overhangs, while the CBS-yku70Δ mutant showed a smaller but significant increase, indicating that Ku protects chromosome ends in both strains.
source_span: As expected , the loss of Ku function in the YPS strains resulted in an almost 7-fold increase in G-overhang . Interestingly , we observed a more than 3-fold increase in G-overhang in the CBS-yku70Δ mutants suggesting that the Ku heterodimer does , in fact , protect the chromosome ends in the CBS strain.
selection_reasoning: This provides mechanistic evidence about telomere end protection relevant to strain differences.

fact: The severe telomere shortening caused by mre11Δ in the CBS strain was associated with extra telomeric repeat fragments likely resulting from recombination events.
source_span: In contrast to yku70Δ , mre11Δ resulted in the dramatic loss of telomeric repeats in CBS with extra bands appearing at 1 . 2–1 . 3 kbp on the Southern blot ... These extra TRFs could be a result of recombination events.
selection_reasoning: This links genetic mutation effects to telomere structure changes and potential compensatory mechanisms.

fact: The Ku heterodimer retains some conserved functions in the CBS strain despite partial defects.
source_span: These phenotypes clearly indicate that the Ku heterodimer is not fully defective in CBS strain and some functions are evolutionary conserved.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the functional status of Ku in the studied strain, relevant to telomere biology.

fact: The YPS mre11Δ strain shows increased G-overhang levels at telomeres, while the CBS mre11Δ strain does not due to severe telomere length loss.
source_span: A similar pattern of increased level of G-overhang was observed at the telomeres in the YPS mre11Δ strains. No differences were detected in the CBS mre11Δ, because the severe loss of telomere length made further analysis of G-overhangs not possible.
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights strain-specific telomere phenotypes linked to mre11 deletion, important for understanding telomere regulation.

fact: The rif1Δ and pif1Δ mutants do not significantly affect telomeric G-tails in either CBS or YPS strains.
source_span: The rif1Δ and pif1Δ mutants did not show any significant effect on the G-tails of either strain as expected.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies which mutations do not influence telomere overhangs, refining the focus on relevant genetic factors.

fact: CBS and YPS strains have large differences in telomere length, making them suitable for segregation analysis.
source_span: The large difference seen in telomere length between CBS and YPS made these strains ideal candidates for segregation analysis.
selection_reasoning: This motivates the choice of strains for genetic analysis of telomere length.

fact: F1 hybrids of CBS and YPS strains have intermediate telomere lengths between the parental strains.
source_span: F1 hybrids of YPS and CBS were created with telomere lengths that were intermediate between those of the parents.
selection_reasoning: This establishes the genetic basis for studying telomere length inheritance.

fact: The high sequence divergence (3.71%) between CBS and YPS strains causes partial reproductive isolation with only 35% gamete viability.
source_span: It is worth noting that the extremely high sequence divergence (3.71%) between the CBS and YPS strains resulted in partial reproductive isolation with only 35% of the gametes being viable.
selection_reasoning: This contextualizes the genetic background and challenges in hybrid analysis.

fact: Genotype analysis of 84 F1 spores at 113 loci showed no evidence of genetic incompatibility causing reproductive isolation between CBS and YPS strains.
source_span: Genotype analysis ruled out genetic incompatibility as a possible mechanism of reproductive isolation between the European and American S. paradoxus genes as there are no combinations of CBS and YPS genes located on different chromosomes that are underrepresented among the segregants.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies that reproductive isolation is not due to gene incompatibility, important for interpreting segregation results.

fact: The average number of crossing over events per meiosis in CBS/YPS hybrids is about 33.5, which is about one third of that observed in S. cerevisiae crosses.
source_span: We estimated from the genotype data an average of 33.5 crossing over events (CO) per meiosis... This CO count is about one third of the CO per meiosis previously detected in a cross between S. cerevisiae isolates.
selection_reasoning: This provides insight into recombination frequency differences relevant to genetic mapping.

fact: The high sequence divergence between CBS and YPS strains accounts for the reduced crossing over frequency observed.
source_span: The very high sequence divergence between the CBS and YPS strains accounts for the CO reduction observed.
selection_reasoning: This explains a key genetic mechanism affecting recombination in the study.

fact: After 200 generations, the 84 hybrid progeny showed a continuous range of telomere lengths averaging close to the hybrid parent length.
source_span: The 84 hybrid progeny were propagated for 200 generations and phenotyped for telomere length... Telomere length analysis revealed a continuum of values... with an average in the segregants (325 bp) remarkably close to the length measured in the hybrid (347 bp).
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates quantitative inheritance of telomere length in hybrids.

fact: Some F1 spores exhibited transgressive segregation with telomere lengths longer or shorter than either parent.
source_span: We found transgressive segregation in 14 F1 spores that had telomeres longer or shorter than the parental telomeres.
selection_reasoning: This indicates complex genetic interactions affecting telomere length.

fact: The donor of the tagged telomere does not affect telomere length, indicating no epigenetic or cis-regulatory effects on telomere length regulation.
source_span: Segregation of the nearby subtelomeric marker proved that the telomere donor had no effect on telomere length. This indicates that there is no epigenetic effect on telomere length regulation and also that no cis elements are involved.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the genetic versus epigenetic control of telomere length.

fact: Four chromosomal intervals on chromosomes II, III, XII, and XIII are significantly associated with telomere length variation by linkage analysis.
source_span: Four intervals in chromosomes II, III, XII and XIII were significantly associated with telomere length by linkage analysis.
selection_reasoning: This identifies key genomic regions controlling telomere length.

fact: The chromosome II interval includes the RNA template of telomerase, TLC1, and likely contains multiple linked QTLs affecting telomere length.
source_span: The interval on chromosome II spans a large section (~300 Kb), likely to contain multiple linked QTLs... and includes the RNA template of telomerase, TLC1.
selection_reasoning: This links a known telomerase component to telomere length variation.

fact: The chromosome XIII interval peaks on the YKU80 gene, a known telomere length regulator.
source_span: The chromosome XIII interval peaks on YKU80.
selection_reasoning: This highlights a specific gene associated with telomere length differences.

fact: The five loci detected explain 56% of the total telomere length variance in the hybrid progeny.
source_span: Using the normal model, the 5 loci detected... explain 56% of the total telomere length variance.
selection_reasoning: This quantifies the genetic contribution to telomere length variation.

fact: There is no overlap between the telomere length QTL intervals found in CBS/YPS and those previously reported in S. cerevisiae strains.
source_span: It is worth mentioning that there is no overlap between the intervals found here and the ones previously reported in a linkage analysis between two S. cerevisiae strains.
selection_reasoning: This indicates species- or strain-specific genetic control of telomere length.

fact: The four major QTLs have significant additive effects on telomere length, with no significant epistatic interactions detected.
source_span: The four major QTLs described above exhibit significant additive effects... We found no significant novel epistatic interaction effects.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the genetic architecture of telomere length regulation.

fact: The YKU80 marker is strongly linked to telomere length, with spores carrying the YPS allele having longer telomeres than those with the CBS allele.
source_span: The segregant analysis suggested that the YKU80 marker was strongly linked with the telomere length phenotype... with length averages of 370 bp and 276 bp for the spores carrying the YPS or the CBS allele respectively.
selection_reasoning: This supports YKU80 as a key gene influencing telomere length.

fact: Deletion of the YPS allele of YKU80 in a CBS/YPS hybrid causes telomere shortening compared to deletion of the CBS allele.
source_span: We found a telomere shortening effect (78 bp) in the hybrid when the YPS allele of YKU80 was deleted compared to the deletion of the CBS allele.
selection_reasoning: This experimentally validates the functional effect of YKU80 alleles on telomere length.

fact: Deletion of one copy of YKU80 in the diploid parental strains does not affect telomere length, ruling out haploinsufficiency for YKU80.
source_span: Deletion of one copy of YKU80 in the diploid parental strains showed no telomere length variation, ruling out haploinsufficiency.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the genetic mechanism of YKU80 dosage effects.

fact: Deletion of one copy of TLC1 in parental diploid strains causes telomere shortening, indicating that RNA telomerase template abundance limits telomere length maintenance.
source_span: Both parental diploid strains suffered telomere shortening when one copy of TLC1 was deleted indicating that the abundance of RNA telomerase template molecules is a limiting factor in telomere length maintenance.
selection_reasoning: This identifies TLC1 dosage as a key factor in telomere length regulation.

fact: The haploinsufficiency effect of TLC1 deletion is more pronounced in the CBS strain than in the YPS strain.
source_span: The haploinsufficiency effect was more visible in the CBS with 81 bp reduction (42% of total length) than in YPS with 66 bp reduction (14%).
selection_reasoning: This shows strain-specific differences in telomerase RNA template sensitivity.

fact: In the CBS/YPS hybrid, deletion of the YPS allele of TLC1 results in shorter telomeres than deletion of the CBS allele.
source_span: Deletion of the YPS allele resulted in shorter telomeres when compared to the deletion of the CBS allele with 101 bp (29%) and 38 bp (11%) reduction, respectively.
selection_reasoning: This validates allele-specific effects of TLC1 on telomere length in hybrids.

fact: There is no significant epistatic interaction between YKU80 and TLC1 loci, but they have significant additive effects on telomere length.
source_span: Two-locus analysis provided no evidence for a significant epistatic interaction between YKU80 and TLC1, however, the two loci showed a significant additive effect.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the combined genetic effects of two major telomere length regulators.

fact: YKU70 and YKU80 genes are required for heterodimerization and end binding, and are essential for both telomere protection and non-homologous end joining (NHEJ).
source_span: YKU70 and YKU80 genes are required for heterodimerization and end binding , and are essential for both telomere protection and NHEJ .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological role of YKU70 and YKU80, which is central to understanding their impact on telomere length and genome stability.

fact: Deletion of the YPS allele of YKU80 results in shorter telomeres compared to deletion of the CBS allele, indicating allele-specific effects on telomere length.
source_span: Deletion of the YPS allele resulted in shorter telomeres when compared to the deletion of the CBS allele with 101 bp ( 29% ) and 38 bp ( 11% ) reduction , respectively
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights allele-specific contributions to telomere length, a key phenotype studied in the article.

fact: There is a significant additive effect but no significant epistatic interaction between YKU80 and TLC1 loci on telomere length.
source_span: Two-locus analysis provided no evidence for a significant epistatic interaction between YKU80 and TLC1 , however , the two loci showed a significant additive effect
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the genetic relationship between two important telomere-related loci, relevant to the study's genetic analysis.

fact: A detrimental epistatic interaction between CBS-YKU80 and YPS-YKU70 alleles in F1 hybrids causes very short telomeres comparable to complete YKU deletions.
source_span: Interestingly , we detected a detrimental interaction between the CBS-YKU80 and YPS-YKU70 in the F1 hybrid resulting in very short telomeres ( Figure 5C ) comparable in length to telomeres in ykuΔ ( yku70Δ/yku70Δ or yku80Δ/yku80Δ ) hybrid strains .
selection_reasoning: This principal finding reveals a key genetic interaction affecting telomere length, central to the article's conclusions.

fact: Loss of heterodimerization between Yku70 and Yku80 proteins is a possible mechanism underlying the negative epistasis observed between CBS-YKU80 and YPS-YKU70 alleles.
source_span: Loss of heterodimerization is one of the possible mechanisms for the negative epistasis of the CBS-YKU80 and YPS-YKU70 alleles .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight helps explain the genetic interaction affecting telomere length.

fact: Sequence divergence in YKU80 is greater within S. paradoxus species than between species, while YKU70 shows less divergence within species and more between species.
source_span: YKU80 on the other hand is more divergent within the S . paradoxus species and less divergent between the species . Comparing amino acid identities , YKU80 is more divergent than YKU70 within the S . paradoxus species and less divergent between species
selection_reasoning: This evolutionary analysis provides context for the genetic variation affecting telomere length.

fact: Telomere position effect (TPE) is evolutionarily conserved between Saccharomyces species, as shown by TPE observed at the VII-L telomere in the YPS strain.
source_span: TPE was observed at the VII-L telomere ( 61 . 1±28% of the colonies FOA resistant ) in YPS indicating that this mechanism is evolutionarily conserved between Saccharomyces spp .
selection_reasoning: This background and significance fact links telomere length to gene silencing, relevant to the study's broader implications.

fact: Telomere length negatively regulates expression of nearby genes by recruiting Rap1p and the SIR complex, explaining absence of silencing in the CBS strain with short telomeres.
source_span: The short length of telomeric tract can explain the absence of silencing in the CBS strain , as telomere length negatively regulates the expression of nearby genes by recruiting Rap1p and the SIR complex
selection_reasoning: This fact connects telomere length to functional consequences on gene expression, important for understanding phenotypic effects.

fact: There is only a weak correlation between telomere position effect (TPE) and telomere length in F1 segregants, with some spores having long telomeres but no TPE.
source_span: Our results indicate only a very weak correlation between TPE and telomere length ( r = 0 . 36 ) with many of the spores exhibiting no TPE ( Figure 4B and Figure 6B ) . Spores with long telomeres and no TPE were found .
selection_reasoning: This finding nuances the relationship between telomere length and gene silencing, a key phenotype.

fact: Linkage analysis identified several genetic markers associated with the telomere position effect (TPE) phenotype, though these associations are weaker than those for telomere length.
source_span: Linkage analysis indicates several markers associated with the TPE phenotype ( Figure 4C ) . Because the TPE measurements are strongly non-normal , we used a nonparametric method for assessing the strength of a QTL ( Table S2B ) . TPE phenotype does not exhibit strong genetic associations compared to telomere length . There are two significant QTLs at the 5% significance cutoff on chromosomes IV and IX . The strong QTLs for length on chromosomes II and XIII are also associated with high levels of TPE , but are not significant at the 5% level .
selection_reasoning: This genetic mapping result is relevant to understanding the genetic basis of TPE, a secondary phenotype studied.

fact: Telomere length varies widely among Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains, with a threefold difference observed between European and American subpopulations of S. paradoxus.
source_span: We detected a massive 3-fold telomere length variation between the strains: ∼150 bp in CBS432 and ∼450 bp in YPS138.
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes the biological variation motivating the study and is central to understanding the research question.

fact: The study screened 112 Saccharomyces strains to investigate telomere length variation and its genetic basis within a natural population.
source_span: To obtain a broad picture of the extent of variation of this trait within a natural population and to investigate the mechanisms behind telomere length regulation we screened 112 Saccharomyces strains.
selection_reasoning: This high-level method description explains the scope and approach of the study.

fact: The researchers selected two representative S. paradoxus strains, CBS432 and YPS138, from European and American subpopulations respectively, for detailed telomere length analysis.
source_span: We selected two strains, CBS432 and YPS138 as representative of the European and American subpopulations respectively, and accurately measured telomere length at individual telomeres.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key experimental design choice relevant to the main findings.

fact: Natural sequence variants in the YKU80 and TLC1 genes contribute to part of the telomere length variation observed among individuals.
source_span: We confirmed that part of the variation in telomere length among individuals is due to natural sequence variants within YKU80 and TLC1.
selection_reasoning: Identifying specific genes linked to telomere length variation is a principal finding central to the study.

fact: High sequence divergence in the Ku heterodimer causes a negative epistatic interaction that produces extremely short telomeres in certain allele combinations.
source_span: We also show that high sequence divergence in the Ku heterodimer results in a negative epistatic interaction producing extremely short telomeres in one allele combination.
selection_reasoning: This key mechanistic insight explains how genetic interactions affect telomere length, a core scientific claim.

fact: Negative epistasis is widespread in progeny from crosses between the highly diverged CBS and YPS parental strains, contributing to low fitness under multiple conditions.
source_span: We have evidence that negative epistasis is widespread in progeny obtained from the highly diverged parental strains CBS and YPS explaining their low fitness when exposed to a multitude of conditions.
selection_reasoning: This finding has significance for understanding genetic incompatibility and fitness consequences in natural populations.

fact: Widespread negative epistasis between diverged subpopulations may prevent hybridization between European and American S. paradoxus populations where they coexist.
source_span: This widespread epistasis could prevent hybridization between the European and American population of S. paradoxus in geographic regions where the two populations coexist but do not interbreed.
selection_reasoning: This implication links genetic findings to population-level reproductive isolation, highlighting biological and evolutionary significance.

fact: Telomere length and telomeric position effect (TPE) are quantitative traits controlled by multiple genetic loci, some shared and some distinct.
source_span: As predicted by the phenotype distribution, both telomere length and TPE variation seem to be controlled by multiple QTLs... Some of the QTLs, like YKU80, are shared between the two phenotypes but many others only affect one of the phenotypes explaining the weak correlation between the two traits.
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a principal finding about the genetic architecture of telomere-related traits.

fact: The CBS strain lacks telomeric position effect (TPE) while the YPS strain exhibits high TPE, indicating extreme variation in this telomeric trait between subpopulations.
source_span: We also phenotyped the segregants for an additional quantitative telomeric trait, TPE, that also exhibits extreme variation in the CBS (no TPE) and YPS (high TPE) strains.
selection_reasoning: This background and finding about TPE variation is important for understanding the phenotypic differences studied.

fact: Several candidate genes within QTL intervals on chromosomes IV and XIII, including RVB1, SIR4, and YKU80, are implicated in controlling telomeric position effect and telomere length variation.
source_span: Chromosome IV QTL was mapped within a 31 Kb region... with several possible candidates for the QTL (HST4, ATC1, REF2, RVB1)... Similarly, we mapped the QTL interval in chromosome XIII... that peaks at YKU80.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights key genetic loci identified as controlling telomere-related traits, central to the study's genetic mapping results.

fact: Inactivation of the Ku heterodimer in the CBS strain does not affect telomere length but increases the length of the G-overhang, indicating natural variants affect specific Ku functions.
source_span: One surprising finding in the CBS strain was that inactivation of the Ku heterodimer did not affect telomere length per se but increased the length of G-tail.
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight about Ku protein function variants is a notable finding relevant to telomere biology.

fact: Negative epistasis is widespread in progeny from highly diverged parental strains CBS and YPS, explaining their low fitness under multiple conditions.
source_span: We have evidence that negative epistasis is widespread in progeny obtained from the highly diverged parental strains CBS and YPS explaining their low fitness when exposed to a multitude of conditions ( Warringer J and Liti G , unpublished results ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides key background and a principal finding about genetic incompatibility affecting fitness, central to the study's focus on epistasis.

fact: Widespread negative epistasis between diverged subpopulations can prevent hybridization between European and American populations of S. paradoxus where they coexist.
source_span: This widespread epistasis could prevent hybridization between the European and American population of S . paradoxus in geographic regions where the two populations coexist but do not interbreed [12] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the biological significance and evolutionary impact of negative epistasis in natural populations, relevant to the study's motivation.

fact: The two S. paradoxus strains used to generate F1 segregants have nearly 10-fold higher sequence divergence than any previously used S. cerevisiae strains in linkage analysis, likely causing strong epistatic interactions.
source_span: Indeed , the two S . paradoxus strains used in this study to generate the F1 segregants have a level of sequence divergence almost 10-fold higher than in any other S . cerevisiae strains previously used in linkage analysis [22] , [39] , which is consequently likely to result in strong epistatic interactions .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key experimental system and rationale for expecting strong epistasis, important for understanding the study design and findings.

fact: High sequence divergence between parental strains reduces crossover number during meiosis, decreasing gamete viability and linkage analysis resolution.
source_span: The high sequence divergence also has a dramatic impact on gamete viability resulting from the reduced number of CO . This reduction in CO also decreases the resolution of the linkage analysis , requiring a low number of markers to generate the initial genotypes and to map the recombination breakpoints .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key biological consequence of divergence affecting the genetic analysis, relevant to interpreting results.

fact: Segregants analyzed were derived from the same meiotic event to ensure genuine meiotic products without aneuploidies, providing reliable information on phenotype inheritance.
source_span: We analysed segregants from the same meiotic event to ensure that the gametes are genuine meiotic products , with no aneuploidies , and provide important information on phenotype inheritance .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a critical methodological approach ensuring data quality and relevance to inheritance studies.

fact: Geographic subpopulations of the same species have evolved dramatic differences in telomeric properties, though the reasons remain unclear.
source_span: Why geographic subpopulations of the same species have evolved dramatic differences in telomeric properties remains unclear .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background motivation for studying telomeric differences, relevant to the biological context.

fact: Macrophages need to be activated after an infectious challenge to efficiently clear infectious pathogens.
source_span: Following an infectious challenge , macrophages have to be activated in order to allow efficient clearance of infectious pathogens , but how macrophage activation is coupled to increased clearance remains largely unknown .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential background on the biological context and motivation for the study.

fact: Inflammatory stimuli reprogram macrophages from receptor-mediated phagocytosis to macropinocytosis, enabling rapid transfer of internalized cargo to lysosomes in a receptor-independent manner.
source_span: We here describe that inflammatory stimuli induced the reprogramming of the macrophage endocytic machinery from receptor-mediated phagocytosis to macropinocytosis , allowing the rapid transfer of internalized cargo to lysosomes in a receptor-independent manner .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding describing the key mechanism discovered in the study.

fact: Protein kinase C-mediated phosphorylation of the macrophage protein coronin 1 activates phosphoinositol-3-kinase activity necessary for macropinocytic uptake.
source_span: Reprogramming occurred through protein kinase C-mediated phosphorylation of the macrophage protein coronin 1 , thereby activating phosphoinositol ( PI ) -3-kinase activity necessary for macropinocytic uptake .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies the molecular mechanism underlying the macrophage reprogramming.

fact: Expression of a phosphomimetic form of coronin 1 is sufficient to induce PI3-kinase activation and macropinocytosis even without inflammatory stimuli.
source_span: Expression of a phosphomimetic form of coronin 1 was sufficient to induce PI3-kinase activation and macropinocytosis even in the absence of inflammatory stimuli .
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates the causal role of coronin 1 phosphorylation in switching uptake modes.

fact: Macrophages primarily clear microbes through receptor-mediated phagocytosis involving various cell surface receptors.
source_span: The main mechanisms via which macrophages can internalize and clear microbial material occurs through receptor-mediated phagocytosis . This process , making use of different cell surface receptors , including Fc receptors , complement receptors , scavenging receptors as well as several lectin receptors , ensure the uptake of particulate material into phagosomes followed by delivery of the cargo to lysosomes [1] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the normal macrophage clearance mechanism relevant to understanding the study.

fact: Pathogenic mycobacteria can survive inside macrophage phagosomes by blocking phagosome-lysosome fusion, preventing their degradation.
source_span: Once internalized into phagosomes , pathogenic mycobacteria have evolved to withstand lysosomal degradation by effectively blocking phagosome-lysosome fusion thereby surviving within macrophage phagosomes instead of being degraded in lysosomes prior to cytosolic escape [3]–[10] .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the challenge macrophages face in clearing certain pathogens, motivating the study.

fact: During acute infection, the phagocytic capacity of macrophages may be insufficient to internalize and destroy enough bacilli to control infection.
source_span: Also , during an acute infection , the phagocytic capacity of macrophages may become limiting in being able to internalize and destroy sufficient numbers of bacilli in order to curb the infection [11] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains why alternative uptake mechanisms might be necessary.

fact: Macropinocytosis is a receptor-independent, non-saturable uptake mechanism that allows macrophages to internalize large amounts of cargo.

fact: Perceptual decisions in many visual tasks rely on information encoded in neural responses in the primary visual cortex (V1).

fact: Accurate perceptual judgments require the brain to pool sensory responses efficiently by decoding population neural responses into a reliable decision variable.
source_span: To form accurate perceptual judgements , the brain thus needs to pool sensory responses efficiently , decoding the population response into a reliable decision variable .

fact: Optimal population decoding in two-alternative visual discrimination tasks involves evaluating the likelihood of only the two relevant stimuli with high precision.
source_span: In two-alternative discrimination tasks , only two stimulus alternatives need to be considered . An optimal decoder aiming to maximize accuracy therefore calculates a ratio of likelihoods by reading out the likelihood function precisely at two specific locations that correspond to the two possible stimulus alternatives .
selection_reasoning: This defines the theoretical ideal decoding strategy that the study tests against actual perceptual behavior.

fact: It is unclear whether the likelihood ratio in two-alternative discrimination tasks can be computed with arbitrarily high precision by the brain.
source_span: While the use of a likelihood ratio decision variable has been demonstrated in various perceptual tasks [12] , [14]–[16] , it remains unclear to what extent the likelihood ratio can be computed with arbitrary high precision .
selection_reasoning: This knowledge gap motivates the main research question addressed by the study.

fact: The study induced an asymmetry in the likelihood function of spatial frequency by embedding gratings in spectrally filtered noise.
source_span: Using spectrally filtered noise , we induced an asymmetry in the likelihood function of spatial frequency .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key experimental manipulation used to probe perceptual decoding.

fact: Filtered noise backgrounds dramatically alter the perception of grating spatial frequency, with low-pass filtered noise decreasing perceived frequency and high-pass filtered noise increasing it.
source_span: Embedding a grating in low-pass filtered noise causes the perceived spatial frequency of the grating to decrease , while high-pass filtered noise increases perceived grating spatial frequency .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal empirical finding demonstrating the perceptual bias induced by the noise manipulation.

fact: Observers evaluate likelihoods of a broad range of irrelevant spatial frequencies and discard prior knowledge of stimulus alternatives when performing two-alternative discrimination.
source_span: Nevertheless , we find a significant shift in perceived grating frequency , indicating that observers evaluate likelihoods of a broad range of irrelevant frequencies and discard prior knowledge of stimulus alternatives when performing two-alternative discrimination .
selection_reasoning: This finding challenges the assumption of precise likelihood read-out and optimal decoding.

fact: The observed perceptual bias indicates that observers read out the likelihood function with low precision, failing to sample it only at the two relevant stimulus values.

fact: A population code model with broad read-out functions (as broad as 4 octaves) accounts for all behavioral measurements, suggesting imprecise likelihood read-out.

selection_reasoning: This modeling result supports the interpretation of suboptimal, imprecise decoding.

fact: The study measured grating detectability and discriminability in the presence of filtered visual noise using a two-alternative two-interval discrimination task.
source_span: We measured the effect of filtered noise on perceived spatial frequency in a two-alternative two-interval discrimination task .
selection_reasoning: This describes the high-level experimental method used to obtain the key findings.

fact: Low-pass filtered noise significantly decreased perceived grating spatial frequency from 5.5 cycles per degree to an average of 3.8 cycles per degree.
source_span: In the former conditions ( hereafter referred to as the main conditions ) , low-pass noise significantly decreased perceived standard grating spatial frequency ( parametric Monte-Carlo test , for all observers , see methods ) from 5 . 5 cycles per degree ( c/deg ) to an average of 3 . 8 c/deg ( s . e . m . = 0 . 63 ) .
selection_reasoning: This quantifies the main perceptual bias induced by low-pass noise, a principal empirical result.

fact: High-pass filtered noise significantly increased perceived grating spatial frequency to an average of 7.2 cycles per degree.
source_span: Conversely , high-pass filtered noise increased perceived spatial frequency ( parametric Monte-Carlo test , for all observers ) to an average of 7 . 2 c/deg ( s . e . m . = 0 . 64 ) .
selection_reasoning: This quantifies the main perceptual bias induced by high-pass noise, complementing the low-pass noise effect.

fact: Embedding a grating in low-pass filtered noise decreases its perceived spatial frequency.
source_span: Embedding the comparison grating in low-pass filtered noise decreased its perceived spatial frequency ( parametric Monte-Carlo test , for all observers ) , requiring an average comparison frequency of 6 . 6 c/deg ( s . e . m . = 0 . 61 ) to match the 5 . 5 c/deg standard grating embedded in broadband noise .
selection_reasoning: This is a core perceptual finding about how noise filtering affects spatial frequency perception, central to the study's main question.

fact: Embedding a grating in high-pass filtered noise increases its perceived spatial frequency.
source_span: Perceived grating frequency increased in high-pass filtered noise ( parametric Monte-Carlo test , for all observers ) , resulting in a matching frequency of 4 . 2 c/deg ( s . e . m . = 0 . 62 ) .
selection_reasoning: This complements the previous fact and is a key finding about the direction of perceptual bias caused by noise filtering.

fact: Detection thresholds for a 5.5 c/deg grating are much higher when the grating is embedded in broadband noise compared to no noise.
source_span: Embedding the grating in the broadband noise backgrounds used in our discrimination task increases the detection threshold contrast to an average of 10 . 3% ( s . e . m . = 0 . 005% ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact shows how noise affects grating visibility, important for understanding the perceptual context of the study.

fact: Detection thresholds for a 5.5 c/deg grating are lower in notched noise, where a frequency band around 5.5 c/deg is removed, compared to broadband noise.
source_span: We also determined grating visibility in the presence of filtered notched noise , i . e . , broadband noise from which a 4-octave-wide notch centred around 5 . 5 c/deg has been removed . The average detection threshold in the latter condition equalled 1 . 3% ( s . e . m . = 0 . 26% ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights how selective noise filtering affects detection thresholds, relevant to the study's investigation of noise effects.

fact: Detection and discrimination of gratings depend on the responses of V1 neurons that are sharply tuned to spatial frequency.
source_span: Detection and discrimination of gratings presumably depend on the responses of V1 neurons , which are relatively sharply tuned to spatial frequency [17]–[19] .

fact: A computational model based on the normalization model of V1 simple cells was implemented to simulate neural responses to gratings embedded in filtered visual noise.

fact: The model incorporates Gabor-like excitatory receptive fields tuned to spatial frequency, nonlinear response transduction, and broadly-tuned contrast gain control inhibition.
source_span: Our model provides a description of the contrast response of typical V1 neurons , incorporating Gabor-like linear excitatory receptive fields tuned to spatial frequency [21] , nonlinear response transduction [22] and the inhibitory effects of broadly-tuned contrast gain control [23] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the model's biological plausibility and mechanisms, important for understanding the study's significance.

fact: Broadband noise shifts the contrast response function of V1 neurons towards higher contrasts and lower response rates, indicating inhibition of informative neural responses.

fact: The model predicts that filtered noise can either excite or inhibit neurons depending on whether the noise stimulates the neurons' excitatory receptive field or gain control mechanism.
source_span: Extending the logic of the normalization model to filtered noise , our model predicts either excitation or inhibition depending on whether the noise stimulates the neurons' excitatory receptive field or gain control mechanism .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight is central to explaining the differential perceptual effects of low-pass and high-pass noise.

fact: Population responses simulated by the model are asymmetric in low-pass and high-pass filtered noise, reflecting selective activation of neurons tuned to frequencies below or above 5.5 c/deg.

fact: The estimated read-out functions in human observers are broader than optimal, with a width of about 4.2 octaves, indicating limited precision in spatial frequency decoding.

fact: Many outer membrane protein genes in H. pylori contain SSRs in their promoter or coding regions, contributing to hypermutable loci that mediate stochastic switching and help the bacteria adapt to fluctuating host environments.
source_span: SabA is just one , of many outer membrane proteins in H . pylori , which have SSRs in its inter- and intragenic sequences . Intragenic CT-tracts have been reported for loci encoding BabA , BabB , SabB , OipA and HopZ , and we show that a set of them also harbor T- or A-tracts in their promoter regions , respectively . Taken together , all the SSR regions found in a genome create multiple contingency loci of hypermutable DNA that via different mechanisms blindly mediate causal and heritable genotypes , and contribute to stochastic switching . This cost-beneficial approach meets the need to control gene expression at various levels and can despite the lack of specific trans-acting regulators pilot persistent infections in fluctuating host environments through production of heterogeneous bacterial populations of best-fit phenotypes .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the biological and clinical importance of SSR-mediated gene regulation in H. pylori persistence and adaptation.
