fact: Establishment success responds most strongly to propagule pressures between 10 and 100 individuals, with low probability at the lower end and high probability at the upper end of this range.
source_span: Establishment success responded most strongly to propagule pressures between 10 and 100 individuals ( Fig 3 ) .
selection_reasoning: Identifies the critical range of propagule sizes relevant for management and biological interpretation.

fact: The positive effect of propagule pressure on establishment success was consistent across all subsets of data analyzed.
source_span: In the first quantitative systematic review of the effect of propagule pressure on establishment success , we have presented consistent evidence that alien populations founded by more individuals are more likely to establish . Indeed , we have shown that the mean propagule pressure effect is clearly positive and that this was a feature of every subset of the data we analysed .
selection_reasoning: Confirms the robustness and generality of the main finding.

fact: The shape of the relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success informs understanding of small-population dynamics and the effectiveness of biosecurity policies.
source_span: The details of the propagule pressure relationship with establishment success are as important to the management of invasions , and to our understanding of small-population dynamics , as is the direction of the relationship . The shape of the relationship informs at what sizes populations are most subject to stochastic and other factors that increase extinction risk ... and it informs the risk-reduction payoff associated with reducing alien species releases via biosecurity policy ...
selection_reasoning: Explains the significance and practical implications of the findings.

fact: Management needs to reduce alien species releases to very low levels, essentially single digits, to have confidence that establishment is unlikely, but only complete exclusion guarantees no establishment.
source_span: This result suggests that it does not take many individuals to found an alien population and that management needs to reduce alien species releases to very low levels ( essentially into single figures ) to have some confidence that establishment is unlikely . Even then , the risk is not eliminated ... —only complete exclusion of an alien can guarantee no establishment .
selection_reasoning: Provides a clear translational implication for invasive species management.

fact: The propagule pressure effect on establishment success is equally positive across different spatial scales and types of evidence, including experimental, observational, and proxy-based studies.
source_span: The effect of propagule pressure on establishment success manifests equally , as positive , within local experimental tests ... and global compilations ... We also found the propagule pressure effect to be just as strong when studies used proxies for propagule pressure rather than direct measurements of the number of individuals released .
selection_reasoning: Demonstrates the generality and robustness of the effect across study designs and scales.

fact: Heterogeneity in effect sizes was most consistently explained by whether analyses were univariate or multivariate, with multivariate analyses producing weaker effects of propagule pressure.
source_span: The moderator variable that most consistently explained variation in effect size was whether analysis was univariate or multivariate ... Multivariate analyses produced noticeably weaker effects of propagule pressure in the full dataset ...
selection_reasoning: Identifies a key methodological factor influencing effect size estimates, relevant for interpreting results.

fact: There is consistent support for a positive relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success of alien populations.
source_span: In conclusion , we find consistent support for a positive relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success despite a priori expectations that the effect magnitude ( or sign ) of this relationship will vary according to a variety of biological and methodological factors.
selection_reasoning: This is the principal finding and core scientific claim of the study.

fact: The effect size of propagule pressure on establishment success varies primarily due to different analytical approaches rather than biological or methodological factors.
source_span: There is heterogeneity in effect sizes , but this is primarily associated with different analytical approaches.
selection_reasoning: This explains variation in the main relationship and is important for interpreting results.

fact: Studies that directly measure the number of individuals released show the strongest positive relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success when propagule pressure is categorized into large discrete bins rather than treated as a continuous variable.
source_span: We also found that if analysis is restricted only to those studies that could directly measure the number of individuals released ( i . e . , that analyse propagule size ) , then the positive relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success is strongest when large step changes across ranges of propagule pressures are discretised , compared with continuous ( either linear or log-transformed ) measures.
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key methodological insight relevant to measuring the main effect.

fact: Increasing the range of release sizes beyond approximately 100 individuals weakens the measured effect of propagule pressure on establishment success.
source_span: Effect sizes also weakened as the range of release sizes ( i . e . , propagule size ) increases ... Effect sizes were strongest for studies where minimum to maximum release sizes spanned around 100 individuals or fewer.
selection_reasoning: This finding clarifies the conditions under which propagule pressure effects are most detectable.

fact: Small propagules are highly likely to fail to establish, but the probability of establishment success approaches a maximum by the time about 100 individuals have been released.
source_span: Small propagules are highly likely to fail to establish , but the average probability of success is already close to its maximum value ( always <1 ) by the time 100 individuals have been released.
selection_reasoning: This biological insight explains the observed pattern in propagule pressure effects.

fact: There is no evidence that the influence of propagule pressure on establishment success is notably larger in New Zealand than in other parts of the world.
source_span: However , there is no evidence that the influence of propagule pressure in driving establishment success in New Zealand is notably larger than elsewhere in the wold.
selection_reasoning: This addresses geographic generality and relevance of the findings.

fact: Vertebrate and invertebrate studies tend to show larger effect sizes of propagule pressure on establishment success than plant studies.
source_span: Although we found some evidence that vertebrate and invertebrate studies have larger effect sizes than plant studies ...
selection_reasoning: This biological difference is relevant for understanding variation in the main effect.

fact: The ability of many successful alien plant species to reproduce asexually or vegetatively may reduce the impact of small population sizes on their establishment success compared to most animal species.
source_span: Perhaps because the ability of many successful alien plant species to reproduce asexually or vegetatively may mitigate the effects of small population sizes relative to most animal species—there was no clear effect of any of the other groupings.
selection_reasoning: This provides a mechanistic explanation for observed differences between taxa.

fact: There is no evidence of publication bias affecting the observed relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success.
source_span: There was no evidence for publication bias , and the propagule pressure effect is remarkably consistent in both size and shape.
selection_reasoning: This supports the robustness and reliability of the main findings.

fact: Reducing propagule pressure to very low levels is a clear policy and management target for slowing invasion rates of alien species.
source_span: In a field that seeks to address one of the more pressing issues of global change ( invasive species ) , this result is encouraging as it provides a clear policy and management target for slowing invasion rates: reduce propagule pressure , ideally to single figures or zero , regardless of any other feature of the invasion.
selection_reasoning: This states the practical significance and application of the study's findings.

fact: Propagule pressure is often used as a proxy for other variables that influence alien population establishment success, such as annual fecundity.
source_span: This effect may result because propagule pressure is acting in part as a proxy for variables that explain variation in alien population establishment success ( e . g . , annual fecundity ).
selection_reasoning: This background fact helps explain why propagule pressure is important and how it relates to other biological factors.

fact: Propagule pressure is a key factor influencing the establishment success of introduced species.
source_span: We calculated a ( statistical ) population-level effect size of propagule pressure on establishment success using information from all 96 relationships given by the 43 study/dataset groups.
selection_reasoning: This fact captures the main biological relationship studied and is central to the article's core scientific claim.

fact: The study analyzed 56 peer-reviewed papers from 1986 to 2016 that statistically examined the relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success.
source_span: This left a total of 56 studies ( years 1986–2016 inclusive ) reporting statistical analyses of the relationship between propagule pressure and establishment success.
selection_reasoning: This provides a high-level description of the data source and scope, important for understanding the study's evidence base.

fact: Establishment success was universally reported as a binary outcome of success or failure in the analyzed studies.
source_span: We relied on author assessments of establishment success for the populations they tracked, which were universally reported as a binary outcome ( success, failure ).
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the key outcome measure used across studies, important for interpreting results.

fact: Most studies used logistic- or probit-type regression analyses to relate propagule pressure to establishment success.
source_span: The majority of studies (41 out of 56) conducted a logistic- or probit-type regression analysis between establishment success and propagule pressure.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main analytical approach, relevant for understanding how conclusions were drawn.

fact: A Bayesian multilevel meta-analysis was conducted to estimate the overall effect size of propagule pressure on establishment success, accounting for heterogeneity among studies.
source_span: We conducted a Bayesian multilevel meta-analysis to estimate the overall statistical population-level effect size. This approach allowed us to estimate the heterogeneity in effect size for the random effects: among studies and among relationships within a study.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key method used to synthesize evidence and address variability, central to the study's findings.

fact: Moderator variables such as taxon, spatial scale, methodology, number of predictors, and propagule pressure components were evaluated to explain heterogeneity in effect sizes.
source_span: These candidate models fitted to the full dataset included the following moderators ( singly, or at most in pairs ): (i) ‘Taxon’, (ii) ‘Spatial scale’, (iii) ‘Methodology’, (iv) ‘Number of predictors’, and (v) ‘Transform’. There were two additional moderator variables... ‘Propagule pressure’ and ‘Propagule size’.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the investigation into factors influencing variation in the relationship, important for understanding the robustness and context-dependence of findings.

fact: The majority of excluded studies were removed because they used genetic methods to infer propagule pressure or focused on geographical spread rather than initial establishment.
source_span: The majority of these papers (70%) were excluded because they used genetic methods to deduce propagule pressure or because they evaluated the role of propagule pressure in the geographical spread of an alien species and not at initial establishment.
selection_reasoning: This explains the study's focus and rationale for data selection, important background for interpreting the meta-analysis.

fact: Publication bias was assessed by examining asymmetry in residual effect sizes from the highest-ranked meta-analysis model.
source_span: We investigated for evidence of publication bias ( visually and statistically ) by examining the degree of asymmetry in the residual effect sizes from the highest-ranked model fitted to the full dataset.
selection_reasoning: This addresses the reliability and validity of the meta-analytic findings, a key consideration in evidence synthesis.

fact: Selective reporting of results can lead to publication bias in meta-analyses.
source_span: Selective reporting of results can lead to ‘publication bias’ [73].
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why investigating publication bias is important in the study.

fact: The study investigated publication bias by examining asymmetry in residual effect sizes from the highest-ranked model fitted to the full dataset.
source_span: We investigated for evidence of publication bias ( visually and statistically ) by examining the degree of asymmetry in the residual effect sizes from the highest-ranked model fitted to the full dataset ( Table 1 ).
selection_reasoning: This describes a key methodological approach relevant to the study's validity.

fact: The highest-ranked model included the moderator variable 'number of predictors' and random effects among author/dataset and within-study variation, plus measurement error.
source_span: This model includes the moderator variable 'number of predictors' and random effects among author/dataset and within-study variation, plus the measurement error ( see Results ), as the data points in the funnel plot.
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the model structure used to assess publication bias, important for understanding the analysis.

fact: A modified Egger’s regression based on meta-analytic residuals weighted by inverse precision was used to statistically examine publication bias.
source_span: Nakagawa and Santos [63] present a modified Egger’s regression based on these meta-analytic residuals weighted by their inverse precision, and we use this approach statistically to examine publication bias.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the specific statistical method used to detect publication bias, relevant to the study's rigor.

fact: Some studies experimentally evaluated how increasing propagule size affects establishment probability by varying founding numbers of individuals across replicate populations.
source_span: Some studies have used an experimental approach to evaluate how incrementally increasing propagule size served to alter establishment probability. Each experiment consisted of a series of populations held in either constant or systematically altered environments. The treatment applied is the varying of founding numbers of individuals across replicate populations, with the range of founder sizes determined by the researchers.
selection_reasoning: This describes the experimental approach central to the study's main question about propagule pressure and establishment.

fact: Establishment probability was defined as the number of experimental populations that remained extant after more than one generation out of the total initially constructed.
source_span: Establishment probability in this context is the number of experimental populations that remained extant ( successful ) after a predefined time frame ( >1 generation ) out of the total number of experimental populations initially constructed.
selection_reasoning: This definition is necessary to understand the main outcome measured in the experiments.

fact: Eleven studies provided raw data that were combined into a single analysis evaluating variation in the shape of the propagule pressure effect on establishment probability.
source_span: Eleven of these studies provided sufficient raw data for us to extract and combine 14 relationships into a single analysis that evaluates the specific variation in the shape of the propagule pressure effect.
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the data synthesis approach central to the study's findings.

fact: A Bayesian generalized linear mixed model with a logit link and binomial variance function was used to evaluate the effect of propagule pressure on establishment probability, accounting for differences between experiments as a random effect.
source_span: We used a Bayesian generalised linear mixed model with a logit link and binomial variance function to evaluate the slope of the effect of propagule pressure on establishment probability, accounting for average differences in establishment success between experiments ( a random effect ).
selection_reasoning: This describes the key statistical method used to analyze the main relationship studied.

fact: The analysis also examined random differences in the slope of the relationship between propagule pressure and establishment probability across experiments.
source_span: We also examined evidence for random differences in the slope of the relationship across experiments.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the investigation of variability in the main effect, important for understanding generalizability.

fact: Propagule pressure was log10 transformed and centered for the analysis.
source_span: Propagule pressure was log10 transformed and centred for this analysis.
selection_reasoning: This methodological detail is relevant to interpreting the statistical modeling of the main effect.

fact: No evidence for overdispersion in the binomial proportions was found after accounting for random effects.
source_span: We found no evidence for overdispersion in the binomial proportions after accounting for the random effects.
selection_reasoning: This supports the validity of the statistical model used to analyze establishment probability.

fact: Mechanistic mathematical modeling and sensitivity analysis can be used to identify fragile points in human biochemical cascades that may serve as therapeutic targets despite model uncertainty.
source_span: In this study, mathematical modeling and sensitivity analysis were used to explore the working hypothesis that mechanistic models of human cascades, despite model uncertainty, can be computationally screened for points of fragility, and that these sensitive mechanisms could serve as therapeutic targets.
selection_reasoning: This fact states the main research question and approach, which is central to the article's purpose and abstract.

fact: A validated mathematical model of the human coagulation cascade, including 92 proteins and 148 protein–protein interactions, was used to test the hypothesis about points of fragility.
source_span: We tested our working hypothesis by screening a model of the well-studied coagulation cascade, developed and validated from literature. The model, composed of 92 proteins and 148 protein–protein interactions, was validated using 21 published datasets generated from two different quiescent in vitro coagulation models.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key method and model system used to address the study question.

fact: Simulated platelet activation and thrombin generation profiles from the model matched experimental data with a high correlation, supporting the model's validity.
source_span: Simulated platelet activation and thrombin generation profiles in the presence and absence of natural anticoagulants were consistent with measured values, with a mean correlation of 0.87 across all trials.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the reliability of the model predictions, which is critical for the study's conclusions.

fact: Sensitivity analysis identified factor X/activated factor X (fX/FXa) activity and thrombin-mediated platelet activation as fragile mechanisms in the coagulation cascade, while factor IX (fIX/FIXa) and factor VIII (fVIII/FVIIIa) activities were robust.
source_span: In the absence of anticoagulants, fluid and surface phase factor X/activated factor X (fX/FXa) activity and thrombin-mediated platelet activation were found to be fragile, while fIX/FIXa and fVIII/FVIIIa activation and activity were robust.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the principal findings about which mechanisms are sensitive and which are robust, central to the study's claims.

fact: Both anti-fX/FXa and direct thrombin inhibitors are important anticoagulant drug classes, with anti-fX/FXa inhibitors approved for preventing venous thromboembolism and treating deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
source_span: Both anti-fX/FXa and direct thrombin inhibitors are important classes of anticoagulants; for example, anti-fX/FXa inhibitors have FDA approval for the prevention of venous thromboembolism following surgical intervention and as an initial treatment for deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
selection_reasoning: This fact connects the model findings to clinical relevance and therapeutic applications.

fact: Experimental evidence supports the model prediction that factor IX (fIX/FIXa) activity is robust and less sensitive to perturbation.
source_span: Both in vitro and in vivo experimental evidence is reviewed supporting the prediction that fIX/FIXa activity is robust.
selection_reasoning: This fact validates a key model prediction with experimental data, reinforcing the study's conclusions.

fact: Coagulation is a critical biological process involving serine proteases and platelets that is essential for stopping bleeding but can cause serious complications if dysregulated.
source_span: Coagulation, mediated by a family of serine proteases (factors) and a key group of blood cells (platelets), both of which are normally inactive in the circulation, is directly relevant to human health...
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological and clinical importance of the coagulation cascade, motivating the study.

fact: Disorders of insufficient coagulation include haemophilia A, haemophilia B, and von Willebrand disease, while excessive clotting contributes to coronary artery diseases and complications after surgery.
source_span: Insufficient coagulation is manifested in disorders such as haemophilia A (1 in 5,000 live births), haemophilia B (1 in 30,000 live births), or von Willebrand disease (1 in 1,000 live births). Conversely, unwanted clotting can be a serious complication following surgical intervention and is directly involved in coronary artery diseases...
selection_reasoning: This fact provides clinical context for why understanding coagulation mechanisms is important.

fact: The coagulation cascade involves two pathways, intrinsic and extrinsic, that lead to thrombin activation and clot formation, with the extrinsic pathway considered the main mechanism in blood.
source_span: There are two pathways that lead to activation of the master protease thrombin and eventually to a clot—the intrinsic and extrinsic cascades. It is generally believed that the extrinsic cascade is the main mechanism of thrombinogenesis in the blood.
selection_reasoning: This fact defines key biological concepts necessary to understand the study's focus.

fact: Thrombin plays a central role in coagulation by activating platelets, converting fibrinogen to fibrin, and amplifying coagulation through positive feedback loops.
source_span: Thrombin, in addition to playing a key role in platelet activation, catalyzes the conversion of fibrinogen... to fibrin... Thrombin also activates upstream coagulation factors, thereby forming a strong positive feedback that ensures rapid activation.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the biological significance of thrombin, a key molecule studied in the model.

fact: Three natural inhibitors—TF pathway inhibitor (TFPI), antithrombin III (ATIII), and activated protein C (APC)—regulate thrombin formation and coagulation activity.
source_span: Three control points that inhibit thrombin formation are considered in the model. TF pathway inhibitor (TFPI)... Antithrombin III (ATIII)... The FIIa–TM complex catalyzes the conversion of protein C (PC) to activated PC (APC); APC attenuates the coagulation response...
selection_reasoning: This fact describes key regulatory mechanisms included in the model, important for understanding the system's control.

fact: The model accurately predicted thrombin concentration profiles following tissue factor–FVIIa addition to synthetic plasma, consistent with in vitro observations.
source_span: The predicted thrombin concentration profiles following the addition of TF–FVIIa to synthetic plasma were quantitatively consistent with in vitro observations.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the model's predictive validity, a key methodological claim.

fact: The strength of tissue factor–FVIIa input influences the initiation phase of thrombin generation but not the maximal rate of thrombin formation, which is dominated by surface reactions.
source_span: Decreasing the TF–FVIIa input prolonged the initiation phase as it slowed the rate of generation of FXa and thrombin in the bulk. However, TF–FVIIa input strength did not influence the maximal rate of thrombin formation because this is surface dominated.
selection_reasoning: This fact reveals a mechanistic insight from the model relevant to coagulation dynamics.

fact: Increasing TF pathway inhibitor (TFPI) concentration delays thrombin initiation and reduces thrombin amplification by sequestering factor Xa and TF–FVIIa complexes.
source_span: Increased TFPI concentration lead to a longer initiation delay and a decreased rate of FIIa amplification. TFPI delayed initiation through interaction with free FXa and TF–FVIIa in an FXa-dependent manner; sequestering FXa reduced flux through the initial FXa-dependent route of FIIa generation.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes how a natural anticoagulant modulates coagulation, supporting the model's biological relevance.

fact: Tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI) delays the initiation of thrombin (FIIa) formation by interacting with free factor Xa (FXa) and the TF–FVIIa complex in an FXa-dependent manner.
source_span: TFPI delayed initiation through interaction with free FXa and TF–FVIIa in an FXa-dependent manner; sequestering FXa reduced flux through the initial FXa-dependent route of FIIa generation.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key mechanism by which TFPI modulates thrombin generation, central to understanding its anticoagulant role.

fact: Increased TFPI concentration leads to a longer delay before thrombin generation starts and decreases the rate of thrombin amplification.
source_span: Increased TFPI concentration lead to a longer initiation delay and a decreased rate of FIIa amplification.
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights the dose-dependent effect of TFPI on thrombin formation, a principal result relevant to anticoagulant regulation.

fact: Antithrombin III (ATIII) inhibits thrombin formation differently than TFPI by irreversibly inactivating thrombin (FIIa) and reversibly binding to FIXa, FXa, and TF–FVIIa.
source_span: ATIII reversibly binds FIXa , FXa , and TF–FVIIa , and irreversibly inactivates FIIa . ATIII produced a different thrombin generation profile when compared with TFPI.
selection_reasoning: This fact contrasts the mechanisms of two key anticoagulants, essential for understanding their distinct roles in coagulation control.

fact: The combination of TFPI and ATIII completely stops thrombin formation following TF–FVIIa addition.
source_span: The combination of TFPI ( 2 . 5 nM ) and ATIII ( 3 . 4 μM ) , consistent with the experiment , completely quenched FIIa formation following TF–FVIIa addition.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates the synergistic anticoagulant effect of TFPI and ATIII, a principal finding with therapeutic implications.

fact: Activated protein C (APC) is generated from protein C (PC) via thrombomodulin (TM)-dependent and TM-independent routes, with the TM-dependent route catalyzing APC formation at a rate 400 times greater than the thrombin-only route.
source_span: APC was generated from PC via TM-dependent and -independent routes; the TM-dependent route catalyzes the conversion of PC to APC at a rate 400-fold greater than the thrombin route alone.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important background on APC generation mechanisms, relevant to anticoagulant pathways studied.

fact: Simulations of APC generation and thrombin inhibition in the presence of TM matched experimental data well for TM concentrations up to 1 nM but were less accurate at higher TM concentrations.
source_span: The correlation between model and experimental data for APC was approximately 96% for TM values ≤ 1 nM . However , the average correlation between the predicted and measured FIIa profile for TM ≤ 1 nM was 67% . Simulations of the TM 10 nM case failed to quantitatively capture both APC and FIIa formation; the correlation between model and experiment for APC in the presence of 10 nM TM was 49% , while 57% of the FIIa dynamics were correctly described.
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the model's performance in simulating APC and thrombin dynamics, a key methodological and validation result.

fact: In vivo thrombin signal amplification requires the surface of activated platelets, and simulations of platelet activation and thrombin formation were consistent with cell-based coagulation assay data.
source_span: In vivo , amplification of the thrombin signal requires the surface of activated platelets . Preliminary simulations of simultaneous platelet activation and thrombin formation were found to be consistent with the results of the cell-based coagulation assay of Roberts and coworkers.
selection_reasoning: This fact links the biological context of platelet surfaces to thrombin amplification and validates the model against experimental data.

fact: The model identified that the most fragile mechanisms controlling thrombin formation involve binding or activation of factor X (fX/FXa) and platelet activation by thrombin (FIIa).
source_span: The top 25 fragile mechanisms for the control ( case A ) are shown in Table 3; four of the top five fragile mechanisms involve the binding or activation of fX/FXa , with the fifth being platelet activation by FIIa.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights key sensitive points in the coagulation network, important for understanding regulation and potential therapeutic targets.

fact: TFPI primarily influences thrombin formation through FXa-specific interactions with the TF–FVIIa complex, altering the sensitivity of multiple mechanisms related to FXa and factor IX (fIX).
source_span: TFPI was found to influence thrombin formation primarily through the FXa-specific interaction with TF–FVIIa; there were 13 mechanisms whose OSSC values changed significantly in response to TFPI , nine of which become more robust , while two become more fragile.
selection_reasoning: This fact details the molecular influence of TFPI on coagulation, central to the study's mechanistic insights.

fact: ATIII has a more pronounced effect on thrombin generation than TFPI alone, mainly through direct interactions with FXa and thrombin (FIIa).
source_span: While ATIII had a more pronounced effect on FIIa generation than TFPI alone , only four mechanisms were significantly affected by ATIII . ATIII influenced thrombin formation through direct interaction with FXa and FIIa.
selection_reasoning: This fact contrasts the potency and mechanism of ATIII relative to TFPI, a key comparative finding.

fact: Antithrombin III (ATIII) influences thrombin formation by directly interacting with factor Xa (FXa) and factor IIa (FIIa), reducing the sensitivity of FXa affinity for factor IX (fIX) in the fluid phase.
source_span: ATIII influenced thrombin formation through direct interaction with FXa and FIIa; ATIII reduced the sensitivity of the affinity of FXa for fIX in the fluid phase , while the on rate governing the binding of FXa and FIIa with ATIII was found to be of increased importance .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key mechanism by which ATIII modulates coagulation, central to understanding anticoagulant effects.

fact: The combination of tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI) and ATIII produces distinct effects on coagulation mechanisms that are not equivalent to the sum of their individual effects.
source_span: The predicted mechanism of action of anticoagulant combinations is not equivalent to the union of the individual treatment cases . The combination of TFPI + ATIII ( case D ) resulted in 14 statistically significant shifts relative to the control .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the complexity and significance of combined anticoagulant therapies, relevant for therapeutic strategies.

fact: Fondaparinux selectively binds ATIII and enhances its natural inhibitory effect against factor Xa by approximately 300-fold, interrupting thrombin generation and clot formation without directly inactivating thrombin.
source_span: Fondaparinux increases the natural inhibitory effect of ATIII against FXa approximately 300-fold [48 , 49]; selective inhibition of FXa by fondaparinux interrupts thrombin generation and clot formation without inactivating thrombin itself [50 , 51] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the clinical relevance and mechanism of a widely used anticoagulant drug.

fact: Direct thrombin inhibitors (DTIs), such as ximelagatran, reduce thrombin generation and platelet activation in humans, demonstrating anticoagulant effects.
source_span: Sarich et al . have explored the DTI ximelagatran in healthy male volunteers [57] . Thrombin generation , platelet activation , and the thrombin–antithrombin complex were monitored in shed blood collected from skin incisions in 120 healthy male volunteers following oral administration of ximelagatran . Oral ximelagatran showed a rapid and statistically significant decrease in all endpoints relative to control .
selection_reasoning: This supports the clinical significance of DTIs as anticoagulants affecting key coagulation processes.

fact: Factor IX (fIX) and its activated form (FIXa) contribute to coagulation but are more robust to inhibition compared to factor Xa and thrombin, as significant reduction in fIX/FIXa activity is required before coagulation times are affected.
source_span: Feuerstein et al . found that fIX/FIXa activity could be reduced by as much as 2 . 5-fold before any significant change in the aPTT was observed; only after >90% of the fIX/FIXa activity was eliminated was there a 3 . 5- to 4-fold increase in aPTT .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the relative robustness of fIX/FIXa in coagulation, important for understanding therapeutic targeting.

fact: In a canine coronary thrombosis model, inhibition of fIX/FIXa with a competitive inhibitor reduced coronary thrombus formation without increasing bleeding, suggesting that direct TF-FVIIa-mediated activation of factor X is the primary mechanism of factor X activation in bleeding wounds.
source_span: Animals that received saline or bovine fIX developed a coronary occlusion due to a fibrin/platelet thrombus in approximately 1 h; conversely , FIXai decreased coronary thrombus occlusion in a dose-dependent manner . However , FIXai administration was not accompanied by increased bleeding at abdominal and chest-wall incision sites , leading Benedict et al . to conclude , consistent with the earlier work of Weiss and Lages [63] , that direct TF-FVIIa–mediated activation of fX may be the primary mechanism of fX activation in blood obtained from bleeding wounds .
selection_reasoning: This provides translational insight into coagulation mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets.

fact: The activation of platelets by thrombin (FIIa) via protease-activated receptors is a key amplification mechanism in coagulation that becomes less important when TFPI and ATIII are combined as anticoagulants.
source_span: The activation of platelets by FIIa via the protease-activated receptor family of surface receptors became less important , but the retention of FXa and the affinity of the surface FVa–FXa complex increased in importance .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights changes in coagulation amplification pathways under combined anticoagulant treatment.

fact: Anti-factor Xa (anti-fX/FXa) and direct thrombin inhibitors (DTIs) are important classes of anticoagulants currently under clinical development and use.
source_span: Anti-fX/FXa and direct thrombin inhibitors ( DTIs ) are two important classes of anticoagulants ( see Table 5 for a sampling of current clinical trials involving anti-fX/FXa strategies and DTIs ) .
selection_reasoning: This situates the study within the context of clinically relevant anticoagulant drug classes.

fact: Animals that received saline or bovine factor IX developed coronary occlusion due to a fibrin/platelet thrombus in approximately 1 hour.
source_span: Animals that received saline or bovine fIX developed a coronary occlusion due to a fibrin/platelet thrombus in approximately 1 h;
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on the disease model and the pathological outcome relevant to the study of coagulation and thrombosis.

fact: Administration of activated factor IX inhibitor (FIXai) decreased coronary thrombus occlusion in a dose-dependent manner without increasing bleeding at incision sites.
source_span: FIXai decreased coronary thrombus occlusion in a dose-dependent manner . However , FIXai administration was not accompanied by increased bleeding at abdominal and chest-wall incision sites ,
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding demonstrating the therapeutic potential of FIXai to reduce thrombosis without increasing bleeding risk.

fact: Direct tissue factor-factor VIIa (TF-FVIIa) mediated activation of factor X is likely the primary mechanism of factor X activation in blood from bleeding wounds.
source_span: Benedict et al . to conclude , consistent with the earlier work of Weiss and Lages [63] , that direct TF-FVIIa–mediated activation of fX may be the primary mechanism of fX activation in blood obtained from bleeding wounds .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight is key to understanding coagulation activation pathways relevant to the study.

fact: Sensitivity analysis of the coagulation network shows that inhibitors can affect multiple mechanisms beyond their direct targets, indicating complex network responses.
source_span: The naive perspective that a specific inhibitor influences only its target and nothing else is not consistent with our sensitivity analysis . Consider the sensitivity results for TFPI; 13 different mechanisms were predicted to change significantly relative to the control .
selection_reasoning: This finding highlights the complexity of anticoagulant effects and is important for interpreting inhibitor actions.

fact: Shifts in sensitivity coefficients provide insight into the mechanism of action and network response to anticoagulants but do not predict clinical performance or practical patient outcomes.
source_span: However , while shifts in sensitivity coefficients might be a useful predictor of the network response , they are not predictors of clinical performance . No information about practical issues in patients , e . g . , bioavailability , therapeutic window , unexpected toxicities , etc . , was gained from sensitivity analysis of the network in isolation .

fact: Type-III ATPases enhance secretion efficiency when secretion substrate concentrations are limited but are not essential for the type-III protein export process.
source_span: Our data support a role for type-III ATPases in enhancing secretion efficiency under limited secretion substrate concentrations and reveal the dispensability of ATPase activity in the type-III protein export process .
selection_reasoning: This conclusion clarifies the functional role of ATPases, balancing their importance and dispensability.

fact: Bacterial flagella enable motility through liquids and viscous environments and contribute to pathogenesis by promoting host interactions, adherence, biofilm formation, and invasion.
source_span: Many bacteria move by rotating a rigid , helical organelle , the flagellum ... The flagellum ... enables bacteria to move through liquids ( swimming ) and highly viscous environments or surfaces ( swarming ) ... flagellar motility contributes to bacterial pathogenesis by promoting bacteria-host interactions , adherence , biofilm formation and invasion of eukaryotic cells .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why flagellar motility is biologically and medically important.

fact: The flagellar-specific type-III secretion system (fT3SS) exports flagellar building blocks and shares core components evolutionarily and functionally related to virulence-associated type-III secretion systems (vT3SS).
source_span: Export of the building blocks of the flagellum is mediated by a flagellar-specific type-III secretion system ( fT3SS ) , whose core cytoplasmic and inner-membrane export apparatus components ... are evolutionarily and functionally related to the virulence-associated type-III secretion systems ( vT3SS ) of pathogenic Gram-negative bacteria .
selection_reasoning: This fact links the flagellar and virulence secretion systems, providing rationale for studying both.

fact: The cytoplasmic ATPase complex composed of FliI, FliH, and FliJ regulates substrate entry and ATP hydrolysis in the flagellar type-III secretion system.
source_span: Functionally associated with the fT3SS is a cytoplasmic ATPase complex composed of the FliI , FliH and FliJ proteins ... FliH interacts with the N-terminal region of FliI and prevents its ATPase activity until the export apparatus is competent to utilize ATP hydrolysis in the export process .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the ATPase complex's regulatory role, important for understanding the mechanism.

fact: Elimination of the proton motive force inhibits flagellar type-III secretion, indicating that PMF is essential for secretion.
source_span: However , it was demonstrated that elimination of the proton motive force ( PMF , consisting of the protein gradient ΔpH and the membrane potential Δψ ) inhibited flagellar type-III secretion .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the critical role of PMF in secretion, central to the study's energy source question.

fact: Suppressor mutations that increase proton motive force or flagellar substrate levels can restore flagellar assembly and motility in mutants lacking the ATPase complex.
source_span: We demonstrate that flagellar ATPase activity is not essential for secretion by the isolation and characterization of spontaneous suppressor mutants that assemble flagella in a ΔfliHI genetic background ... One linkage group included the clpXP operon ... The third group of motile revertants were linked to the ATP synthase structural genes ( atp ) ... ATP synthesis , flagellum assembly and flagellar rotation are all dependent on the PMF and it has been previously described that a null mutation in atp increases the PMF ... Increased PMF could thus restore proper flagellar assembly and function if the fT3SS is primarily PMF-dependent .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the genetic basis for bypassing ATPase requirement, supporting the main findings.

fact: Flagellum assembly and flagellar rotation depend on the proton motive force (PMF).
source_span: flagellum assembly and flagellar rotation are all dependent on the PMF
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the energy dependency of flagellar function, which is central to the study.

fact: A null mutation in the atp gene increases the proton motive force (PMF).
source_span: a null mutation in atp increases the PMF [29], [30]
selection_reasoning: This fact provides the basis for the experimental manipulation of PMF to study flagellar assembly.

fact: Increased PMF can restore proper flagellar assembly and function if the flagellar type-III secretion system (fT3SS) is primarily PMF-dependent.
source_span: Increased PMF could thus restore proper flagellar assembly and function if the fT3SS is primarily PMF-dependent.
selection_reasoning: This hypothesis motivates the study and links PMF to flagellar assembly via the fT3SS.

fact: Deletion of the FOF1 ATPase (atpA) restores motility in fliI, fliHI, and fliHIJ deletion mutants to varying degrees of wildtype motility.
source_span: The absence of the FOF1 ATPase restored motility of a fliI deletion mutant to about 5% of the wildtype, of a fliHI deletion mutant to about 25% of the wildtype and of a fliHIJ deletion mutant to about 11% of the wildtype
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding showing that ATPase deletion can compensate for loss of flagellar ATPase components.

fact: Deletion of atpA in an otherwise wildtype background causes a pronounced growth defect but does not affect free-swimming velocity.
source_span: In an otherwise wildtype background, deletion of atpA resulted in a pronounced growth defect (Fig. S3), however did not affect the free-swimming velocity (Fig. S4).
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the physiological impact of atpA deletion and its specific effect on motility.

fact: Deletion of the FlgM anti-σ28 factor or a FlgM-resistant σ28 mutant increases flagellar class 3 gene expression and motility in fliHIJ deletion backgrounds.
source_span: Similarly, a deletion of the FlgM anti-σ28 factor, or a FlgM-resistant σ28 mutant (FliAH14D) results in an increase of flagellar class 3 gene expression... the flgM deletion and the FlgM-resistant σ28 mutant raised motility levels up to 24–35% of the wildtype.
selection_reasoning: This identifies a regulatory mechanism that can partially restore motility in ATPase-deficient mutants.

fact: The atpA mutation substantially increases motility in clpX null and FlgM-resistant σ28 mutant backgrounds to approximately 41–54% of wildtype motility.
source_span: the apparent PMF increase of the atpA mutation did substantially increase motility in the clpX null and fliAH15D backgrounds to approximately 41–54% of the wildtype
selection_reasoning: This shows a synergistic effect of increased PMF and regulatory mutations on motility restoration.

fact: Inactivation of the ATP synthase by atpA deletion increases PMF by about 20%, which enhances fT3SS export capability and bypasses the FliHIJ ATPase requirement for flagellar function.
source_span: We thus concluded that a 20% increase in PMF by inactivation of the ATP synthase [29], [30] substantially enhances fT3SS export capability and thereby bypasses the FliHIJ ATPase requirement for flagellar function.
selection_reasoning: This is a key mechanistic conclusion linking energy metabolism to flagellar assembly.

fact: Induction of the PMF-dependent TetA tetracycline/proton antiporter counteracts the motility restoration caused by atpA deletion in fliHIJ deletion mutants by draining the PMF.
source_span: Induction of the TetA efflux pump counteracted the suppressor phenotype of the atpA deletion of various fliHIJ deletion mutants in a motility assay... high levels of TetA tetracycline/proton antiporter activity drained the PMF and thereby negatively affected protein export via the fT3SS.
selection_reasoning: This experimentally confirms the role of PMF in supporting flagellar protein export and motility.

fact: Flagellar filament assembly requires a functional and efficiently working flagellar type-III secretion system (fT3SS).
source_span: Flagellar filament assembly will only occur in the presence of a functional and efficiently working fT3SS.
selection_reasoning: This fact defines a critical biological requirement for flagellar assembly.

fact: Deletion mutants of fliI, fliHI, and fliHIJ are non-flagellated, but the atpA deletion increases the frequency of functional flagella formation in these mutants.
source_span: Deletion mutants of fliI, fliHI and fliHIJ were non-flagellated... the absence of atpA in a fliHI deletion mutant increased the frequency of flagella formation to about 10% of the bacteria.
selection_reasoning: This finding links increased PMF to partial restoration of flagellar assembly in ATPase-deficient mutants.

fact: Mutations that increase flagellar substrate levels, such as flgM deletion, clpX deletion, or FlgM-bypass fliAH14D allele, increase the frequency of flagellated bacteria in fliHIJ mutant backgrounds.
source_span: Mutations in flgM, clpX and the fliAH14D (FlgM-bypass) allele result in increased secretion substrate levels... null mutations of flgM, clpX or fliAH14D increased the frequency of bacteria able to produce at least one flagellum up to 35% of the population.
selection_reasoning: This identifies a mechanism by which increased substrate availability can compensate for ATPase loss.

fact: The combination of flgM deletion and atpA deletion enhances flagellar assembly frequency to a maximum of 74% in the fliHI mutant background.
source_span: The deletion of flgM and atpA enhanced the frequency of flagellar assembly to a maximum of 74% of the population in the fliHI mutant background.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates a strong synergistic effect of regulatory and energy metabolism mutations on flagellar assembly.

fact: The absence of ATP synthase increases flagellar filament formation in clpX and fliAH14D mutant backgrounds to 55% and 36%, respectively.
source_span: The absence of the ATP synthase increased flagellar filament formation in the clpX or fliAH14D backgrounds to 55% and 36%, respectively.
selection_reasoning: This supports the role of increased PMF in enhancing flagellar assembly across different genetic backgrounds.

fact: Increased PMF due to atpA deletion leads to a significant increase in secreted flagellin in flgM, clpX, or fliAH14D mutant backgrounds.
source_span: A significant increase in secreted flagellin was also observed in the flgM, clpX or fliAH14D mutant backgrounds under conditions when the PMF was apparently elevated by the atpA deletion.
selection_reasoning: This provides biochemical evidence for enhanced flagellar protein export linked to PMF increase.

fact: Flagellar filaments formed in fliHIJ mutants with increased PMF or regulatory mutations are as long or longer than wildtype filaments.
source_span: We additionally measured the lengths of flagellar filaments... and observed that the average lengths of flagellar filaments of the various fliHIJ mutants is as long or longer than the wildtype filament lengths.
selection_reasoning: This indicates that restored flagella are structurally comparable to wildtype, supporting functional relevance.

fact: The absence of ATP synthase increases flagellar filament formation in certain mutant bacterial backgrounds.
source_span: The absence of the ATP synthase increased flagellar filament formation in the clpX or fliAH14D backgrounds to 55% and 36%, respectively.
selection_reasoning: This finding links ATP synthase activity to flagellar assembly, a core biological mechanism relevant to the study.

fact: Deleting the atpA subunit, which increases the proton motive force (PMF), leads to increased secretion of flagellin in specific bacterial mutants.
source_span: A significant increase in secreted flagellin was also observed in the flgM, clpX or fliAH14D mutant backgrounds under conditions when the PMF was apparently elevated by the atpA deletion.
selection_reasoning: This shows a key relationship between PMF and flagellar protein secretion, central to the study's main question.

fact: Flagellar filament lengths are increased in mutants lacking components of the FliHIJ ATPase complex or when PMF is increased or secretion substrates are in excess.
source_span: The average lengths of filaments were also increased in an otherwise wildtype background if an excess of secretion substrates (e.g. by deleting the negative regulator flgM) was provided or the PMF was increased by deletion of the atpA subunit.
selection_reasoning: This supports the role of PMF and substrate availability in flagellar filament assembly, a principal finding.

fact: Proton flux through the FlhA protein is essential for flagellar type-III secretion, whereas ATP hydrolysis by the FliHIJ complex is not essential.
source_span: No secretion of flagellin was detected under either condition, demonstrating that the proton flux through FlhA is essential for flagellar type-III secretion in contrast to ATP hydrolysis by the FliHIJ complex.
selection_reasoning: This identifies a critical mechanism distinguishing proton flux and ATP hydrolysis in the secretion process, a core scientific claim.

fact: The FliH component of the ATPase complex functions as an inhibitor of the type-III export process.
source_span: These results demonstrate that FliH functions as an inhibitor of the type-III export process.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the regulatory role of FliH, important for understanding the ATPase complex's function.

fact: Significant type-III secretion can occur without both the negative regulator FliH and the ATPase FliI if excess substrate is provided.
source_span: However, significant export can occur in the absence of both the negative regulator FliH and the ATPase FliI if excess substrate is provided.
selection_reasoning: This finding challenges the necessity of ATP hydrolysis for secretion, a key conclusion.

fact: ATPase activity is universally dispensable for protein export via bacterial type-III secretion systems, as shown using a catalytically inactive InvC mutant in the Spi1 vT3SS.
source_span: The results demonstrate that ATPase activity is universally dispensable for protein export via bacterial type-III secretion systems.
selection_reasoning: This generalizes the main finding across different bacterial secretion systems, increasing its significance.

fact: The primary function of the type-III secretion system (T3SS) export gate is substrate unfolding and translocation, while the ATPase complex facilitates substrate delivery and efficient unfolding.
source_span: It is reasonable to assume that the export gate itself has a primary function in substrate unfolding and translocation. We speculate that the function of the ATPase complex in substrate unfolding and chaperone release is secondary to assure a highly efficient export process.
selection_reasoning: This proposes a mechanistic model explaining the roles of the export gate and ATPase complex, central to the study's interpretation.

fact: Increasing the proton motive force (PMF) can compensate for the lack of ATPase activity in type-III protein export by shifting the equilibrium of substrate unfolding and translocation.
source_span: Increasing PMF thus shifts the equilibrium of the spontaneous process.
selection_reasoning: This explains how energy sources other than ATP hydrolysis support secretion, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: FliJ and FliH components of the ATPase complex act in different pathways of the type-III export process, with FliJ activating Δψ-driven export and FliH localizing substrates for efficient unfolding.
source_span: The observation that export of a FlgE-Bla reporter construct was similarly increased in both the fliHI and fliJ mutant strains indicated that the FliHI and FliJ components of the ATPase complex acted in different pathways of the type-III export process.
selection_reasoning: This details distinct functional roles within the ATPase complex, important for understanding the export mechanism.

fact: The FliHI and FliJ components of the ATPase complex act in different pathways of the type-III protein export process in bacteria.
source_span: that export of a FlgE-Bla reporter construct was similarly increased in both the fliHI and fliJ mutant strains indicated that the FliHI and FliJ components of the ATPase complex acted in different pathways of the type-III export process .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the distinct roles of key ATPase components in the bacterial type-III secretion system, which is central to the study's investigation of protein export mechanisms.

fact: FliJ interacts with FlhA of the export gate and activates efficient membrane potential (Δψ)-driven type-III protein export.
source_span: A possible scenario would be that FliJ – which interacts with FlhA of the export gate – activates the efficient Δψ-driven type-III protein export as suggested by Minamino et al .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a key mechanism by which FliJ facilitates protein export, relevant to understanding the molecular basis of the secretion process.

fact: FliH binds to both the ATPase FliI and the cytoplasmic C-ring, localizing secretion substrates to the export gate for efficient unfolding by FliI before translocation.
source_span: FliH binds to both the ATPase FliI and the cytoplasmic C-ring , thereby localizing secretion substrates to the export gate for efficient unfolding by FliI prior to a Δψ or ΔpH-driven translocation process .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the role of FliH in substrate preparation for export, a key step in the type-III secretion mechanism.

fact: In the absence of FliJ, the inner membrane export apparatus functions as a less-efficient ΔpH-driven protein-proton antiporter, with secretion facilitated by substrate unfolding via the FliHI complex.
source_span: In the absence of FliJ , the inner membrane export apparatus can still function as a less-efficient ΔpH-driven protein-proton antiporter and the secretion process is facilitated by substrate unfolding via the FliHI complex .
selection_reasoning: This highlights an alternative export pathway compensating for the loss of FliJ, important for understanding the flexibility of the secretion system.

fact: In fliHI mutant strains, substrate unfolding does not occur, but the export gate operates in a highly efficient Δψ export mode that may energize substrate unfolding.
source_span: The non-essential substrate unfolding is not occurring in a fliHI mutant strain , however the export gate operates in the highly-efficient Δψ export mode , which might be able to energize substrate unfolding as well .
selection_reasoning: This fact reveals how the export system adapts to the absence of FliHI, relevant to the study of mutant phenotypes and export efficiency.

fact: The switch from early to late (flagellin-like) substrate secretion is a bottleneck in the process of bacterial flagellar bioassembly.
source_span: The switch from early to late ( flagellin-like ) substrate secretion is a bottleneck in the process of flagellar bioassembly .
selection_reasoning: This identifies a critical regulatory step in flagellar assembly, central to the biological context of the study.

fact: Deletion mutants lacking the fliHIJ complex can assemble single flagellar filaments of wildtype lengths or longer despite impaired flagellar protein export.
source_span: The importance of this step in flagellar bioassembly was evidenced by the fact that we observed assembly of single flagellar filaments of wildtype lengths and longer in our fliHIJ deletion mutants ( Fig . 6 ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates that flagellar filament assembly can occur under mutant conditions, indicating alternative mechanisms or compensations.

fact: The inner membrane ring complex, the C-ring, and integral membrane components of the flagellar type-III secretion system assemble normally in the absence of the fliHIJ complex.
source_span: It has been demonstrated before that the inner membrane ring complex , the C-ring and integral membrane components of the fT3SS assemble normally in the absence of the fliHIJ complex [38] , [39] .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports that structural assembly of secretion system components is independent of the FliHIJ ATPase complex, relevant to understanding mutant phenotypes.

fact: Completion of the hook-basal-body structure triggers a secretion substrate specificity switch in the flagellar export apparatus.
source_span: Only upon completion of the hook-basal-body structure , the secretion apparatus undergoes its secretion substrate specificity switch .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key regulatory checkpoint in flagellar assembly and secretion.

fact: In the absence of the FliHIJ complex, flagellar protein export is strongly impaired, making hook-basal-body completion and the switch to filament-type secretion rare events.
source_span: In the absence of the FliHIJ complex , flagellar protein export is strongly impaired and thus HBB completion and the switch to filament-type secretion is a rare event .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the critical role of the FliHIJ complex in efficient flagellar assembly and export.

fact: A mechanism exists that localizes late flagellar substrates to the single hook-basal-body in a late-export-competent state, allowing filament lengths as long or longer than wildtype in fliHIJ mutants.
source_span: However , there appears to exist a mechanism for localization of the available late flagellar substrates to the single hook-basal-body that is in a late-export-competent state since we observed filament lengths that were as long or longer than the wildtype in our fliHIJ mutants ( Fig . 6 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact suggests compensatory localization mechanisms enabling filament assembly despite export defects.

fact: Increasing the proton motive force (PMF) likely assists efficient export of late secretion substrates and can overcome the requirement of the FliHIJ ATPase complex for late substrate secretion.
source_span: An increase in PMF then likely assists in efficient export of late secretion substrates and thereby overcomes the requirement of the FliHIJ ATPase complex for late substrate secretion – similar to the related scenario where excess substrates bypass the requirement of the FliHIJ ATPase complex .
selection_reasoning: This finding reveals how energetic conditions can compensate for ATPase complex deficiencies in protein export.

fact: The cytoplasmic components of the bacterial type-III secretion system share strong homology with components of the FOF1 ATP synthase, suggesting an evolutionary relationship.
source_span: As mentioned above , the cytoplasmic components of the type-III secretion system share strong homology to components of the FOF1 ATP synthase and it has been proposed that the flagellum was derived from a proto FOF1 ATP synthase where ATP hydrolysis might have energized the export process .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides evolutionary context linking the secretion system to ATP synthase, important for understanding the origin and function of the system.

fact: A proto F1-ATPase was likely added to a primordial proton-powered type-III export system, enhancing the efficiency of bacterial protein export in flagella and injectisomes.
source_span: The present results would indicate that a proto F1-ATPase was added to a primordial type-III export system ( which might have been proton-powered ) with the evolutionary benefit of facilitating the export process . This made the bacterial type-III secretion apparatus to the highly efficient protein-export system of the contemporary flagellum and injectisome .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the evolutionary significance and functional enhancement of the ATPase complex in bacterial secretion.

fact: Bacterial type-III protein export involves ATPase complexes that bind substrate proteins, shuttle them to the base of the growing structure, energize chaperone release and substrate unfolding in an ATP-dependent manner, and present substrates to the membrane export apparatus for proton motive force-dependent secretion.
source_span: A reasonable , general proposal for the export mechanism of bacterial type-III secretion systems is that the respective ATPase complexes bind to substrate proteins , shuttle the substrates to the base of the growing structure , energize chaperone release and substrate unfolding in an ATP-dependent manner and present the substrate to the membrane-embedded export apparatus components for efficient PMF-dependent secretion .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the core mechanistic model of type-III protein export, central to the study's conclusions.

fact: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent arbovirus causing an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections annually.
source_span: Dengue virus ( DENV ) is the most prevalent arbovirus leading to an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections every year .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential background on the global burden and importance of dengue virus infection.

fact: DENV infection can cause a range of clinical manifestations from mild dengue fever (DF) to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).
source_span: DENV can cause a spectrum of clinical manifestations , ranging from mild dengue fever ( DF ) to more life threatening forms such as dengue hemorrhagic fever ( DHF ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the disease spectrum and clinical relevance of the study.

fact: The mechanisms triggering the transition from mild dengue fever (DF) to severe dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) at the critical phase of infection are not well understood.
source_span: The clinical symptoms of DHF become evident typically at the critical phase of infection ( 5–7 days after onset of fever ) , yet the mechanisms that trigger transition from DF to DHF are not well understood .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the main knowledge gap motivating the study.

fact: The study performed mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection.
source_span: We performed a mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of infection .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key method used to investigate metabolic differences related to disease severity.

fact: Twenty-nine metabolites were differentially expressed between DF and DHF patients at the critical phase, including bile acids, purines, acylcarnitines, phospholipids, and amino acids.
source_span: There were 29 differentially expressed metabolites identified between DF and DHF at the critical phase . These include bile acids , purines , acylcarnitines , phospholipids , and amino acids .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the principal finding of metabolic differences linked to disease severity.

fact: Bile acids were up to fivefold higher in DHF patients compared to DF patients at the critical phase and correlated with elevated liver enzymes AST and ALT, indicating liver injury in DHF.
source_span: Bile acids were observed up to 5 fold higher levels among DHF compared to DF patients and were significantly correlated to the higher levels of aspartate transaminase ( AST ) and alanine transaminase ( ALT ) , suggestive of liver injury among DHF .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies a key metabolic marker linked to liver damage in severe dengue.

fact: Uric acid, the most abundant antioxidant in blood, was 1.5 fold lower in DHF patients compared to DF patients, suggesting decreased antioxidant defense and increased oxidative stress in DHF.
source_span: Uric acid , the most abundant antioxidant in the blood , was observed to be 1 . 5 fold lower among DHF compared to DF patients . This could result in decreased capacity of endogenous antioxidant defense and elevated oxidative stress among DHF patients .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides insight into a possible mechanism contributing to DHF pathogenesis.

fact: At the recovery phase, levels of eight metabolites, including the bile acid chenodeoxyglycocholic acid, remained significantly altered in DHF patients, indicating prolonged liver impact.
source_span: In the recovery phase , the levels of eight metabolites were still significantly higher or lower among DHF patients , including chenodeoxyglycocholic acid , one of the bile acids observed at the critical phase . This indicates potential prolonged adverse impact on the liver due to DENV infection in DHF patients .
selection_reasoning: This fact shows that metabolic alterations and liver effects persist beyond the acute phase in severe dengue.

fact: The study identified altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF during both critical and recovery phases, providing insights into host-virus interactions and DHF pathogenesis.
source_span: Our study identified altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF in the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection and provided insights into the different host and DENV interactions between DF and DHF .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the overall significance and contribution of the study.

fact: Dengue is a re-emerging disease endemic in tropical and subtropical regions, with over half the world’s population at risk of infection.
source_span: Dengue is a re-emerging disease caused by four closely related serotypes of dengue viruses ( DENV ) and it is endemic in the tropical and sub-tropical regions of the world . An estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections occur annually , with over half of the world’s population living at the risk of infection [1] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides epidemiological context emphasizing the public health importance of dengue.

fact: There is currently no specific treatment for dengue, and management of DHF patients is primarily supportive.
source_span: As yet , there is no specific treatment for dengue and the management of DHF patients is primarily supportive .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the clinical relevance and unmet medical need addressed by the study.

fact: Dengue illness progresses through three phases: febrile (day 0–4), critical (day 5–7), and recovery (day 21–28), with DHF symptoms typically emerging during the critical phase.
source_span: Dengue is a dynamic disease . After the incubation period , the illness begins abruptly and is followed by the three phases—febrile ( day 0–4 post onset of fever ) , critical ( day 5–7 post onset of fever ) and recovery ( day 21–28 post onset of fever ) . DF patients would recover uneventfully after 5–7 days of acute illness , but for DHF patients , the initial febrile period is followed by a rapid onset of vascular leakage , thrombocytopenia and hemorrhage at the critical phase .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the clinical timeline and critical window relevant to disease progression and study focus.

fact: The pathological differences between DF and DHF suggest differential virus-host interactions and involvement of both viral and host immune factors in disease severity.
source_span: The pathological difference between DF and DHF suggest differential virus-host interaction in the susceptibility to the disease , and both viral and host immune factors are likely involved .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides biological rationale for investigating metabolic differences between DF and DHF.

fact: Metabolomics provides a global investigation of metabolites reflecting cellular regulatory processes and can reveal metabolic pathways related to disease processes.
source_span: Metabolomics is a rapidly emerging field in systems biology that refers to the global investigation of metabolite pool in biological systems in response to biological stimuli or perturbations [7] . Metabolites are the end products of cellular regulatory processes and form a direct link between molecular changes and phenotypes , and by providing a snapshot of an organism’s metabolic status , metabolomics holds the promise of finding metabolites or metabolic pathways related to disease processes [8 , 9] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the rationale for using metabolomics to study dengue pathogenesis.

fact: Previous metabolomics studies identified potential marker metabolites to predict DHF at the early febrile phase of dengue infection.
source_span: In our previous study , we investigated serum metabolome difference between adult DF and DHF patients enrolled from a prospective dengue study at early febrile phase of DENV infection and found potential marker metabolite to predict DHF at early phase of the infection [14] .
selection_reasoning: This fact situates the current study in the context of prior work and highlights the novelty of studying critical and recovery phases.

fact: The majority of differentially expressed metabolites between DF and DHF at the febrile phase differ from those identified at the critical phase, indicating distinct molecular changes at different disease stages.
source_span: Interestingly , the majority of identified differentially expressed metabolites between DF and DHF in the febrile phase were different from those identified in the critical phase , showing that metabolomics study could capture the distinct molecular changes in DF and DHF patients at different phases of DENV infection .
selection_reasoning: This fact emphasizes the dynamic nature of metabolic changes during dengue progression.

fact: Dengue fever (DF) and dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) patients were classified according to the WHO 1997 and 2009 dengue guidelines.
source_span: DF and DHF patients were classified according to the WHO 1997 and 2009 dengue guidelines [2 , 16].
selection_reasoning: Classification of patient disease severity is essential background for understanding the study population and outcomes.

fact: Dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) diagnosis requires fever or history of fever, hemorrhagic tendencies, thrombocytopenia, and evidence of plasma leakage.
source_span: To fulfill the case definition of DHF , all four of the following criteria must be present , namely: fever or history of fever , hemorrhagic tendencies , thrombocytopenia and evidence of plasma leakage [16].
selection_reasoning: Defining DHF clinical criteria is important for understanding the disease context and study focus.

fact: Hematocrit increase of over 20% compared to convalescence phase values is a common clinical index of plasma leakage and DHF diagnosis.
source_span: Hematocrit increase of over 20% of the values at convalescence phase is considered a common clinical index of plasma leakage and DHF diagnosis.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key clinical measurement used to identify severe dengue cases.

fact: The study cohort included both dengue fever (DF) and dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) patients recruited at different phases of dengue infection, with DENV2 as the predominant dengue virus type.
source_span: The PADS cohort comprised of both DF and DHF patients recruited at different phases of dengue infection and DENV2 is the predominant DENV type.
selection_reasoning: Describing the study cohort and viral type is important background for interpreting findings.

fact: Immune status of dengue patients was determined based on anti-DENV IgG and IgM seropositivity or seronegativity.
source_span: Based on the anti-DENV IgG and IgM seropositivity or seronegativitiy , immune status of the patients was determined.
selection_reasoning: Determining primary versus secondary infection status is key to understanding patient immune responses.

fact: Anti-DENV IgM seropositivity and IgG seronegativity indicated that 40–52% of DF and 22–41% of DHF patients were primary dengue cases, with the remainder being secondary cases.
source_span: Anti-DENV IgM seropositivity and IgG seronegativity indicated that 40–52% of DF and 22–41% of DHF are primary cases , and the remaining are secondary cases.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important epidemiological context about infection types in the cohort.

fact: A significant proportion of dengue patients had severe thrombocytopenia, with 12–16% of DF patients and 59–76% of DHF patients having platelet counts below 50×10³/μL at any point during infection.
source_span: 12–16% DF patients and 59–76% DHF patients had platelets <50×103/μL at any point as determined during their daily routine total blood count.
selection_reasoning: Thrombocytopenia is a key clinical feature relevant to disease severity and outcomes.

fact: Dengue viral infection was confirmed by RT-PCR, NS1 antigen detection, or virus isolation and typing using DENV type-specific monoclonal antibodies.
